hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Plymouth From a Two-Generation Family Firm
hero.subheadline: MJ Kitchen & Bath designs and installs kitchens and baths from its new Plymouth showroom, with Wood-Mode, Showplace and Pioneer cabinetry on display. Matt and Mike Jenkins lead a team of designers, a project manager and lead carpenters.
trust_badges: Began as MJ Cabinet Designs in 2009

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling in Plymouth, MI: stained wood base cabinets and island under white painted upper cabinets, by MJ Kitchen & Bath

intro.h2: A Plymouth showroom where your new kitchen gets planned
paragraphs: MJ Kitchen & Bath handles kitchen remodeling in Plymouth from the first sketch to the last cabinet pull. The company began in 2009 as MJ Cabinet Designs, building custom kitchens for local builders, then added full remodeling for homeowners and took its current name in December 2019.

In June 2026 the team opened a larger showroom at 620 Ann Arbor Road, just across the street from the old one. Inside are kitchen and bath displays of Wood-Mode, Showplace and Pioneer cabinets, plus a selection center for tile, quartz and granite, flooring and hardware, so you can compare finishes side by side before you commit.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Plymouth and the rooms around it

items.name: Kitchen remodeling
items.blurb: The team designs and installs the whole kitchen: cabinets, counters, tile, sinks, lighting and flooring. You see floor plans, elevation drawings and color renderings before work starts, and MJ's own cost guide puts same-layout kitchen remodels at $50,000 and up.

image.alt: Remodeled kitchen with black lower cabinets, a natural wood range hood, white island and black countertops by MJ Kitchen & Bath

items.name: Bathroom remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, powder rooms, Jack-and-Jill layouts and busy family bathrooms. Popular requests include curbless walk-in showers, freestanding soaking tubs, radiant-heat floors and vanities with pull-out storage. MJ says most bath remodels are finished in 3 to 6 weeks.

image.alt: Primary bathroom with a freestanding soaking tub and a glass-enclosed shower lined in white subway tile

items.name: Semi-custom and custom cabinetry
items.blurb: Choose from Wood-Mode, crafted in Pennsylvania, Showplace from South Dakota and Pioneer from Michigan. Beyond kitchens, MJ builds cabinets for laundry rooms, mudrooms, wet bars, coffee bars and home offices, and its own carpenters install what it sells.

image.alt: Kitchen with green glass-front cabinets, a light wood island with seating and brass pendant lights

items.name: First-floor remodels
items.blurb: For bigger plans, MJ redesigns the first floor around a larger kitchen, with possible structural changes, fine custom cabinetry and new hardwood throughout. These projects start at $150,000 and often add a wet or dry bar, a powder room refresh or a new fireplace mantel.

image.alt: Open kitchen with light wood cabinets and a black island with stools that flows into a dining area

why_choose_us.h2: Why Plymouth homeowners keep calling MJ back

items.title: One family, two generations
items.text: Mike Jenkins has worked in cabinetry for more than 30 years and founded the company. Matt Jenkins leads remodeling sales, and Ryan Jenkins is one of the lead carpenters.

items.title: Clients come back for the next room
items.text: Rebecca A. hired MJ for her kitchen, then brought the same team back for two bathrooms the following year and for the last bathroom after that.

items.title: A project manager on every job
items.text: Your designated project manager and crew seal off nearby rooms to cut dust, clean up every day and finish with a punch list before they call the job done.

items.title: Ranked with the nation's largest
items.text: Qualified Remodeler ranked MJ 394th in its 2026 Top 500, one of only 32 kitchen and bath firms on the list. Matt was also a finalist for the 2025 Fred Case Award.

about.h2: From MJ Cabinet Designs to MJ Kitchen & Bath
about.text: Mike Jenkins spent more than 30 years in the cabinetry trade before opening MJ Cabinet Designs in 2009, building luxury custom kitchens and baths with local builders. As homeowners asked for more, the company added start-to-finish remodeling and became MJ Kitchen & Bath in December 2019. Today Mike (Owner, Cabinet Sales) and his fellow owner Matt Jenkins (Owner, Remodeling Sales) run it as a two-generation family business, with in-house designers, a project manager and lead carpenters. In the August 2026 issue of Qualified Remodeler, Matt described the goal as creating “an experience people can’t stop talking about.”

image.alt: Wood-Mode cabinetry display with a stone backsplash inside the MJ Kitchen & Bath showroom at 620 Ann Arbor Road, Plymouth

process.h2: Five steps from first call to final punch list

steps.title: Quick inquiry and ballpark
steps.text: Fill out the short inquiry form and the team calls back to review your project, give an initial ballpark estimate and outline next steps.

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: A team member visits to take exact measurements, listen to your wish list and share layout ideas that make the most of the space.

steps.title: Design and proposal at the showroom
steps.text: You review floor plans, elevation drawings, a detailed scope of work and a clear written estimate with the team in the Plymouth showroom.

steps.title: Selections with an interior designer
steps.text: Pick cabinets, counters, backsplash, flooring and hardware from showroom samples, then see your choices in color renderings before anything is ordered.

steps.title: Construction and wrap-up
steps.text: MJ secures permits and orders materials, then your project manager and crew build it, clean up daily and close out a punch list.

service_area.h2: Serving Plymouth, Canton, Northville and Ann Arbor
service_area.text: MJ Kitchen & Bath works from its showroom at 620 Ann Arbor Road in Plymouth, between Main Street and Lilley Road. The team remodels kitchens and baths for homeowners in Plymouth, Canton, Northville, Ann Arbor and Livonia, along with nearby Metro Detroit communities. Not sure your street is covered? Call (734) 354-9633 or stop in. The showroom is open weekdays from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Saturdays by appointment, and evening appointments are available.

faq.h2: Questions Plymouth homeowners ask before they remodel

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Plymouth?
items.a: MJ's own cost guide, based on its projects in Plymouth, Northville, Canton, Ann Arbor and Livonia, lists three levels. Same-layout remodels start at $50,000, expanded remodels with wall removal start at $100,000, and first-floor remodels start at $150,000. Final cost depends on cabinet line, layout changes, material choices and the age of the home.

items.q: How long will my kitchen or bathroom be under construction?
items.a: MJ estimates 6 weeks or more of construction for a same-layout kitchen and 8 weeks or more for larger kitchen projects, counted from the start of construction. Most bathroom remodels take 3 to 6 weeks. Design, selections and ordering are all completed before construction begins, though permits or material lead times can shift dates.

items.q: Can I see cabinets in person before I choose?
items.a: Yes. The showroom at 620 Ann Arbor Road has kitchen and bath displays of Wood-Mode, Showplace and Pioneer cabinetry, plus samples of tile, quartz and granite, flooring and hardware. Appointments are preferred, Saturday visits are by appointment, and customer parking is in front and along the west side of the building.

items.q: Do you handle design, or do I need my own designer?
items.a: MJ has its own design team. After an in-home measure you receive floor plans, elevation drawings and a written estimate, then you work with an interior designer on finishes and get color renderings of your selections. If you already have an interior designer or builder, MJ works with them too.

items.q: Will you take on a bathroom-only project?
items.a: Yes. The team remodels primary baths, guest and powder rooms, Jack-and-Jill layouts and high-traffic family bathrooms. Features it installs include curbless walk-in showers with Euro-style glass doors, freestanding soaking tubs, radiant-heat floors, built-in benches and vanities with pull-out storage for hair tools.

final_cta.h2: Visit the new showroom, then plan your kitchen
final_cta.text: Call the MJ team or book a free consultation at the Plymouth showroom on Ann Arbor Road.

hero.h1: Remodeling Contractor in Sterling Heights With Design Done First
hero.subheadline: Majestic Home Solutions finishes basements and remodels kitchens and baths across Macomb and Oakland counties. Founder Zayne Roumaya started the company in 1995, and you can see your space in 3D renderings before construction begins.
trust_badges: Full waiver of lien at final payment

image.alt: Finished basement bar with a backlit stone-look counter, clear stools and herringbone floor, built by Majestic Home Solutions, a remodeling contractor in Sterling Heights

intro.h2: Plan every detail on screen before the first wall comes down
paragraphs: Majestic Home Solutions is a family-owned remodeling contractor in Sterling Heights that has worked on Southeast Michigan homes since 1995. Many of its Google reviews mention finished basements, and the same crew takes on kitchens and bathrooms, from tear-out to the last piece of trim.

What sets the process apart is how much gets settled up front. Design meetings happen over Zoom at a time that suits you, and an optional Design Agreement buys extra hours with the design team for 3D renderings in Chief Architect and material picks. If you move ahead, that fee is applied to your project total.

services.h2: A remodeling contractor in Sterling Heights for basements, kitchens and baths

items.name: Basement finishing
items.blurb: Turn bare concrete into a home office, guest room, theater, gym, play space, extra bathroom or bar. Published packages start at $65,000 for 750 to 850 square feet, and add-ons such as a wet bar or a full bathroom are priced on the same page.

image.alt: Finished basement in Troy, MI with a shuffleboard table, a bar with seating and an open lounge area

items.name: Kitchen remodeling
items.blurb: Stock or custom cabinets, countertops, backsplash, lighting and appliance installs, planned around your budget. Published kitchen packages run $35,000, $45,000 and $55,000 for small to large kitchens that keep the existing floor, with more layout change allowed at each level.

image.alt: Remodeled kitchen with navy lower cabinets and island, white upper cabinets, glass pendant lights and a stainless range hood

items.name: Bathroom remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites and guest baths with custom marble, mosaic or ceramic tile, new vanities and options like heated floors, towel warmers and rain shower heads. Full bathroom packages for a standard 5 by 9 room are listed at $10,000, $12,000 and $15,000, before fixture and tile material.

image.alt: Clinton Township primary bathroom remodel with a dark double vanity, white counter, two framed mirrors and vanity light bars

items.name: Custom bars and built-ins
items.blurb: Wet bars, dry bars, entertainment centers and built-in cabinets are a regular part of Majestic basements. One Auburn Hills family has worked with the company for over 20 years and recently updated an entertainment center the team built for them long ago.

image.alt: Rochester Hills basement bar with dark cabinets, a stone-look counter, stacked stone wall and pendant lights

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons Macomb and Oakland homeowners hire Majestic

items.title: An 18-month labor warranty
items.text: Majestic offers an 18-month warranty on all of its labor. If something comes up after the job, you call the office and the team takes care of it.

items.title: Prices in writing, no hidden costs
items.text: Proposals break out every material and labor cost, and the company publishes package pricing for basements, kitchens and baths so you can budget before the first meeting.

items.title: Calls returned within one business day
items.text: Communication is guaranteed: calls and emails are returned within 1 business day or sooner, and BuilderTrend daily logs show progress between your updates.

items.title: Proof everyone got paid
items.text: At final payment you receive a full waiver of lien, which shows that every subcontractor and supplier on your project has been paid in full.

about.h2: Founded by craftsman Zayne Roumaya in 1995
about.text: Zayne Roumaya, an experienced craftsman, founded the company as “Majestic” in 1995, working on carpentry, deck design and remodeled basements, kitchens and baths. In 2005 it was reorganized into the family-owned Majestic Home Solutions, LLC, and its focus moved toward high-end design for basement finishing, kitchen remodels and bath refurbishments. Homeowners meet Zayne on the job too: Andre A. named him and Chris in his review after his basement was finished in early 2024. Every new hire passes a background check and skills evaluation, and licensed staff take continuing education courses to stay current on code.

process.h2: Dreaming to post-construction in five steps

steps.title: Dreaming
steps.text: At the first consultation you share inspiration photos, needs and budget while the team takes preliminary measurements and photos for your project file.

steps.title: Designing
steps.text: You review a preliminary plan and estimate, then sign a design agreement or contract. The agreement adds design hours for Chief Architect 3D renderings and selections.

steps.title: Pre-construction
steps.text: You get a BuilderTrend account for selections, schedules, change orders and daily logs, and every material is ordered and on site before work starts.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Each trade starts with a walk-through, crews follow detailed checklists, and a punch list walkthrough happens before the final payment is collected.

steps.title: Post-construction
steps.text: Your 18-month limited warranty begins, and the team comes back to photograph the finished space and talk through how the project went.

service_area.h2: Towns served across Macomb and Oakland counties
service_area.text: Majestic is based in Sterling Heights at 42886 Mound Rd and works across Macomb and Oakland counties. The towns it lists include Rochester, Rochester Hills, Oakland Township, Shelby Township, Auburn Hills, Lake Orion, South Lyon and Troy, and its project photos show work in Novi, Northville, Royal Oak and Clinton Township too. Not sure you are inside the area? Call (248) 917-3422 to check your address.

faq.h2: What to know before you finish a basement or remodel

items.q: How much does a finished basement cost?
items.a: Majestic publishes three packages for qualifying homes built in 1985 or later: Bronze at $65,000 for 750 to 850 square feet, Silver at $85,000 for 850 to 1,000 square feet, and Gold at $100,000 for 1,000 to 1,100 square feet. Upgrades such as a wet bar, full bathroom or extra room are priced separately.

items.q: What is a Design Agreement?
items.a: It is an optional first step that covers a virtual design consultation, material selections and renderings of your space, with a set number of revisions. Fees start at a $2,500 minimum for projects under $100,000 and rise with project size. If you go ahead with construction, the fee is deducted from your project total.

items.q: Do I have to take time off work for design meetings?
items.a: No. Majestic holds its design meetings and consultations over Zoom at a time that works for you, so you can review material selections and renderings from home or the office. Once your design is approved, you receive a full construction spec and contract with no hidden costs.

items.q: Is financing available?
items.a: Majestic's kitchen and bathroom pricing guides state that financing is available at 18% added to the total price. Packages are set at standard options, and estimates are done in person or from required photos you send. Problems found behind walls can add cost, so ask about them during your estimate.

items.q: What warranty do you offer?
items.a: Majestic gives an 18-month warranty on all of its labor. If an issue comes up, call the office and the team will take care of it. At final payment you also receive a full waiver of lien, so you know the subcontractors and suppliers on your job have been paid.

final_cta.h2: Start with a free design consultation
final_cta.text: Call the Majestic team in Sterling Heights or ask for your free estimate online.

hero.h1: Design-Build Remodeling in Gaithersburg, MD, Run by the Owners
hero.subheadline: Husband-and-wife team Alex and Carolina Reyes design, permit and build complete kitchens, baths and basements under one contract. Alex is on site every day.

image.alt: Design-build remodeling Gaithersburg MD: primary bath with freestanding soaking tub, marble-tiled walk-in shower and navy double vanities with backlit mirror

intro.h2: One Gaithersburg team from first sketch to final punch list
paragraphs: AC Remodeling is a family-owned firm that has offered design-build remodeling in Gaithersburg, MD since 2009. The same team draws your kitchen, bath or basement, prices it, pulls the permits and builds it under a single contract. The owners run every job, so the people at your first meeting are the people on your project.

The firm takes complete remodels only, not repairs or handyman work. Clients point to the same details again and again: a 3D rendering and written proposal before demolition, one project manager, a written update each week, and a crew that shows up on time and cleans up every day. That is how the firm earned 5.0 stars across 55 Google reviews.

services.h2: Design-build remodeling in Gaithersburg, MD: kitchens, baths and basements

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom and semi-custom cabinetry, mostly painted maple, with quartzite or engineered quartz tops and layered lighting on dimmers. Wall removals, beams and new plumbing fall under one permit. Plan on 3 to 5 weeks of design, 3 to 6 weeks for permits and ordering, then 6 to 9 weeks of building.

image.alt: White kitchen remodel in Bethesda, MD with marble island, brass hardware and hardwood floors

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary and hall baths taken back to the studs. Showers get a Schluter or equal waterproofing system and are flood-tested before tile goes up. Low-threshold showers, blocking for grab bars and comfort-height fixtures are offered for living in place. Construction usually runs 4 to 6 weeks.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel in Rockville, MD with open linen shelving, frameless glass shower and marble-look porcelain floor

items.name: Basement Remodeling
items.blurb: Moisture, insulation, electrical and plumbing are handled before the walls close. Then the space is planned around how you will use it: a wet bar, gym, guest suite with proper egress, theater or office, drawn in 3D and built by one crew under one permit.

image.alt: Finished basement remodel in Montgomery County with wall-mounted TV, white built-in cabinetry and warm wood counters

items.name: Design-Build
items.blurb: Design, engineering, permits and construction stay with one accountable team. Designers work beside the crews who build, so your selections are priced against real costs early. The design retainer is credited toward your construction contract when you go ahead with the build.

image.alt: Bethesda, MD kitchen built from a 3D design, with a large quartzite island, fluted glass pendants and stained wood base

why_choose_us.h2: Why Montgomery County homeowners hire AC Remodeling

items.title: The owners run your job
items.text: Alex Reyes is on site every day managing construction quality, and Carolina Reyes joins every client meeting. There is no layer of middle management between you and the owners.

items.title: Licensed in Maryland and DC
items.text: MHIC License #127743 and DCRA License #420220000070 appear on every page of the site. The firm is also an EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm and an NKBA member.

items.title: Recognized by Houzz for years
items.text: AC Remodeling holds 17 Best of Houzz awards for design and service, covering 2014 to 2021 and 2024 to 2026.

items.title: Prices shown up front
items.text: Google reviewers say they got all prices upfront with no unexpected costs. During the build you get one project manager, a shared schedule and a written progress report every week.

about.h2: Meet Alex and Carolina Reyes
about.text: Alex Reyes and his wife, Carolina, founded AC Remodeling in Gaithersburg in 2009. They kept the firm small on purpose so the owners could stay close to every project instead of chasing volume. Alex, a licensed contractor and self-described perfectionist, is on site daily and holds materials and detailing to his own standard. Carolina, the managing director, leads design and turns your wish list into a plan the crew can build on budget. Design assistant Melissa Rojas walks clients through showroom visits and selections, down to the last tile and fixture.

image.alt: Alex Reyes, President and CEO of AC Remodeling in Gaithersburg, MD

process.h2: How a project moves from idea to finished room

steps.title: Initial consultation
steps.text: A no-obligation meeting in your home or by video to cover your goals, lifestyle, timeline and investment range, with an honest look at what your space allows.

steps.title: Design and planning
steps.text: After you sign a design agreement and retainer, designers measure your space, draw the layout and show it in 3D renderings until you are confident in it.

steps.title: Material selection
steps.text: Carolina or Melissa goes with you to trusted suppliers to choose cabinets, counters, tile, lighting and fixtures that suit your style and budget.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: A dedicated project manager runs the build, protects the rest of your home, keeps the site clean and sends you regular progress updates.

steps.title: Final review
steps.text: A detailed walkthrough confirms every finish meets the standard, followed by a deep clean, a care guide and your warranty handoff.

service_area.h2: Where our crews work in Maryland and DC
service_area.text: AC Remodeling serves Montgomery County, Howard County and Northwest Washington, DC from its office and shop in Gaithersburg. Being close means deliveries stage locally and the project manager can stop by between visits. Permits are filed with Montgomery County DPS and, inside city limits, with the City of Gaithersburg. The towns below are where the firm works most, from Kentlands townhomes to Potomac colonials.

faq.h2: Questions Gaithersburg homeowners ask before they call

items.q: Do you offer free estimates?
items.a: No. AC Remodeling does not offer free estimates. Every project starts with a no-obligation consultation, in your home or by video, about your goals, timeline and investment range. Design then begins with a signed design agreement and a retainer, and that retainer is credited toward your construction contract if you build with the firm.

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take in Montgomery County?
items.a: The firm's kitchen timeline has three stages: 3 to 5 weeks for measurements, 3D plans and selections, 3 to 6 weeks for county permits and cabinet ordering, then 6 to 9 weeks of construction. Final detailing, a deep clean and the warranty handoff follow. Bathrooms run shorter, with 4 to 6 weeks of construction.

items.q: Do you pull the permits?
items.a: Yes. Permit administration is handled in-house. The team coordinates with Montgomery County DPS and, for homes inside city limits, the City of Gaithersburg, and it holds MHIC License #127743 in Maryland and DCRA License #420220000070 in Washington, DC. Code and structural questions are worked into the design from day one.

items.q: Can you remodel a bathroom in a high-rise condo?
items.a: Yes. Recent Google reviews come from a penthouse owner and from a high-rise condo building in North Bethesda, where the team renovated a primary bath and closets. In reply to one review the owners wrote that navigating high-rise condo renovations with minimal disruption is what they strive for across Bethesda.

items.q: Will you take on a small repair or partial update?
items.a: No. AC Remodeling does not take minor repairs, handyman tasks or partial updates. The firm focuses on complete remodels such as custom kitchens, primary suites and finished basements, where one accountable team can manage design, permits and construction from start to finish under a single contract.

final_cta.text: Call (240) 632-1660, Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, or request a consultation online and the team will reply within one business day.

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost in Vancouver, WA?

items.q: Do you work on both sides of the river?

intro.h2: Quality should not take forever
paragraphs: 3 Day Cabinet Pros and More does kitchen remodeling in Machesney Park, IL, and across the Stateline area with one focus: quality cabinets installed quickly. Most cabinet installs take one to two days, and most projects go from first visit to finished kitchen in two to three weeks.

Founder Liam McCormack believes a long timeline is a sign of a problem, not a sign of care. So every job is planned before work starts, with a detailed scope, a clear budget breakdown and your door, finish and hardware choices locked in. The crew installing your cabinets works for Liam, and has for an average of five-plus years.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Machesney Park, IL: cabinets, refacing and countertops

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: New cabinets from three lines, Essential, Signature and Luxury, plus countertops, sinks and backsplashes, all planned with a detailed design and cost breakdown before a start date is set. image.alt: Remodeled kitchen with gray shaker cabinets, stainless gas range, tan vertical tile backsplash and white counters

items.name: Cabinet Refacing
items.blurb: If your cabinet boxes are solid, refacing gives you new doors, drawer fronts, hardware and veneers without tearing everything out. It looks like a full replacement for a fraction of the $30,000 to $50,000 a tear-out can cost, and Liam will tell you honestly which option fits.

image.alt: Refaced kitchen cabinets in light gray shaker style with navy arabesque tile backsplash and stainless appliances

items.name: Countertops
items.blurb: Precise templating comes first, then fabrication and installation by a countertop partner the team has worked with for more than two years. 3 Day Cabinet Pros coordinates every trade and owns the result, so there is no finger-pointing between the contractor and the fabricator.

image.alt: Kitchen with cream shaker cabinets, granite countertops, white subway tile and stainless gas range

why_choose_us.h2: What makes this crew different

items.title: Your installers are employees
items.text: The people who install your cabinets work for 3 Day Cabinet Pros full time and have been with the company an average of five-plus years. No crew pulled from a list.

items.title: Known partners for specialty trades
items.text: Plumbing, electrical and countertops go to licensed specialists who have worked alongside the team for at least two years, so there are no strangers in your home.

items.title: What you approve is what you get
items.text: Doors, drawer fronts, hardware and finish are chosen before your start date is scheduled. No substitutions, and you know the full price before work begins.

items.title: Problems handled out loud
items.text: When something comes up on a job, Liam shares the facts, skips the blame and works out a plan with you. Fixing it is always the company's responsibility.

about.h2: Liam McCormack learned the trade by doing it
about.text: Liam McCormack grew up in a family of entrepreneurs and was fixing plumbing and hanging entry doors at age 12. He left college after a year, went back to the trades and built 3 Day Cabinet Pros and More from the relationships he made with clients and crews. Early on, a rushed sink hookup by a crew member led to a trap that leaked across the floor. The damage was small but the lesson stuck: slow down to do it right, especially when it is not easy. Today Liam wants every client to feel they could invite him over for dinner.

faq.h2: Bathroom questions from Conejo Valley homeowners

items.q: Is All Exclusive Construction licensed and insured?
items.a: Yes. The company holds California Contractor License #1120170 and describes itself as licensed, bonded and insured. hero.h1: Design-Build Remodeling in Ann Arbor With Transparent Pricing

intro.h2: You see the real cost of every fixture
paragraphs: Ann Arbor Remodeling is a full-service firm for design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, taking on everything from bathroom renovations to complete home remodels and additions. Every project is designed from scratch, and the team handles the first design concept, permits and construction all the way through final inspection.

Pricing works differently here. Instead of hiding markups in line items, the contract shows what the company pays its trade partners and the direct cost of your finish materials. If a toilet costs them $478, that is the number you see. Owner Justin Kolic wants the company on the same side of the table as its clients.

services.h2: Design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, from kitchens to additions

items.name: Kitchen remodeling
items.blurb: Custom kitchens planned around how your family cooks, with cabinetry design, material selections and lighting layouts worked out with your designer. The company's directional pricing puts a medium-size kitchen remodel with mid-level finishes at $125k to $175k.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with navy lower cabinets, white upper cabinets, double stainless wall ovens and white zigzag wall tile

items.name: Bathroom remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites and hall baths, built by a lead carpenter who stays on your job until it is finished. The newest finished project, the Huron River Primary Suite, pairs a freestanding tub with wood-look tile. Hall bathroom projects are listed at $50k to $55k.

image.alt: Huron River primary suite bathroom with a freestanding tub, wood-look wall tile, black countertop and floating wood vanity

items.name: Basement finishing
items.blurb: Basements fall under the Lead Carpenter System, so the same person is on site each weekday, coordinating trade partners and inspectors. On the company's pricing guide, a 1500-square-foot basement with a bathroom and bar starts at $200k.

image.alt: Finished lower level with white built-in cabinets, open shelving, a wood support post and light wood-look flooring

items.name: Additions, sunrooms and screen porches
items.blurb: Additions begin with a discovery day at your home, opening drywall to confirm conditions so the schedule holds. The team also builds sunrooms and screen porches that connect indoors and out. A 200-square-foot kitchen addition starts at $300k.

image.alt: Sunroom addition with exposed wood beams, two skylights, a ceiling fan and windows on three sides

items.name: Custom woodworking
items.blurb: With its own wood shop and carpenters, the company builds bookcases, fireplace built-ins and mantels, built-in cabinetry and even custom tables, so the storage, shelving and trim in your remodel are made for that exact room.

image.alt: Custom walnut built-in bookcase and cabinet run beside an exposed brick wall

why_choose_us.h2: How Justin's team runs a job

items.title: Transparent contracts
items.text: Your contract lists what the company pays trade partners and the direct cost of your finishes, with no hidden markups tucked into the line items.

items.title: One lead carpenter, one project
items.text: On kitchens, baths and basements, a hands-on lead carpenter manages only your job and is typically on site from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

items.title: Daily logs you can check
items.text: Daily logs, progress photos and change orders post to BuilderTrend, so you know where things stand even if you are across the country.

items.title: Cleaner air while you live there
items.text: Crews set up zip walls and air scrubbers to limit dust and contaminants, which matters when your family stays home during construction.

about.h2: A future teacher who chose the trades
about.text: Justin Kolic decided to become a remodeler in 2003 while studying to be a teacher. He finished an associate degree, took construction management classes at WCC and earned his Michigan Residential Builders license in 2006. He started Ann Arbor Remodeling LLC in 2013. Justin hires for character, following the ideas in The Ideal Team Player, and builds skills on the job. Two of today's team members, a lead carpenter and an estimator, were clients before they joined, and his former WCC instructor now leads pre-construction.

steps.title: Conceptual design
steps.text: After the Project Design Agreement, you meet your designer for a detailed measure, then review 2 to 3 concept designs with cost ranges for each.

steps.title: Design development
steps.text: Your designer walks you through cabinetry, materials, plumbing fixtures, lighting and electrical layouts while preparing the final drawing set for permits.

steps.title: Pre-construction
steps.text: You review the contract, plans and final scope, permits are applied for, and you meet the project manager who will run your job.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Your project manager shares progress, schedule and changes in Buildertrend and holds milestone meetings, and your designer returns for paint, tile and cabinet install reviews.

service_area.h2: Based on Jackson Plaza in Ann Arbor
service_area.text: The office is at 251 Jackson Plaza E in Ann Arbor, open Monday through Friday from 10 AM to 5 PM. faq.h2: Questions about pricing, process and the lead carpenter

items.q: What will my remodel cost?
items.a: The company shares directional prices based on mid-level finishes: a hall bathroom at $50k to $55k, a large primary bathroom at $100k to $160k+, a medium kitchen at $125k to $175k, a 1500-square-foot basement with bath and bar from $200k, and a 200-square-foot kitchen addition from $300k. Your exact cost comes from design and a detailed scope.

items.q: Why do you show your actual costs?
items.a: Ann Arbor Remodeling uses a transparent pricing model. Its construction contracts break out what it pays trade partners and the direct cost of your finish materials, without hidden markups. The company says this puts it on the same side of the table as you and makes talks about scope or material changes more relaxed.

items.q: What is a lead carpenter?
items.a: A lead carpenter is a hands-on project manager who runs one project at a time and is on site from start to finish, typically Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. They are your main contact, keep the work area clean, coordinate inspectors and oversee trade partners. Additions and larger projects use a project manager system instead.

items.q: Can we live at home during the remodel?
items.a: Many clients do. The Lead Carpenter System is used for kitchen, bath and basement projects where families stay in the house, and crews set up zip walls and air scrubbers to limit the spread of dust. Daily logs and progress photos in BuilderTrend keep you informed even when you are away.

items.q: How does the design phase work?
items.a: After you sign a Project Design Agreement and pay a deposit, a kickoff meeting introduces your designer and covers a detailed measure. You then see 2 to 3 concept designs with cost ranges, refine one through design development, and receive final drawings for permits before you sign the construction contract.

final_cta.h2: Tell Justin's team what you want to build
final_cta.text: Call or text (734) 368-1221, or email info@annarborremodeling.com, to start the conversation.

hero.h1: Condo Remodeling in Chicago, From Board Approval to Final Walkthrough
hero.subheadline: Assembly Squad is pre-approved in 300+ Chicago buildings. One design-build team handles your alteration agreement, permits, freight elevator and construction under one fixed-price contract.

intro.h2: Condo remodeling in Chicago, planned around your building's rules
paragraphs: Condo remodeling in Chicago is mostly about the building. Before a wall comes down there is an alteration agreement, insurance certificates, elevator bookings and work-hour rules. Assembly Squad has handled that paperwork since 2013, and today 75% of its completed projects are condominium renovations.

The firm is a licensed design-build general contractor, so one team covers design, permits, materials, construction and the final walkthrough. You meet your designer at the Lincoln Park studio, pick real materials, and get a fixed-price proposal. Then a dedicated project manager runs the job and sends daily photo updates while you get on with your week.

services.h2: What we renovate in Chicago homes and condos

items.name: Condo Remodeling
items.blurb: Gut renovations and single-room updates in high-rises, lofts and greystone conversions. The team prepares alteration agreements, insurance certificates, drawings, neighbor notices and board presentations, then works within building hours. Typical condo budgets run $25,000 to $250,000+, depending on scope.

image.alt: Galley kitchen remodel at The Chandler, 450 E Waterside Dr, Lakeshore East Chicago, with white shaker cabinets, quartz counters and breakfast bar with city view

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom cabinetry, quartz countertops, new appliances and full layout changes for condos, two-flats and single-family homes. Kitchens are the firm's most requested service, with typical budgets from $25,000 to $150,000+. You see 3D renderings and choose every material before construction starts.

image.alt: Bucktown kitchen remodel at 1757 N Paulina St with two-tone green and cream cabinetry, Calacatta quartz and fluted tile backsplash

items.name: Bathroom Renovation
items.blurb: Walk-in shower conversions, custom vanities, heated floors and tile work designed around condo plumbing stacks and building waterproofing rules. Bathroom budgets typically run $15,000 to $55,000. Recent work includes lofts in the West Loop and high-rise units in Lakeshore East.

image.alt: Bathroom renovation at Gotham Lofts, 420 S Clinton, West Loop Chicago, with oak double vanity, brass mirrors and stone top

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Family rooms, home offices, wet bars, ADUs and legal rental units, with waterproofing included in the scope. Typical basement budgets run $30,000 to $100,000+. Permits and inspections are part of every project, so you are not left dealing with the city alone.

image.alt: Lincoln Park basement remodel in Chicago finished as an entertainment suite

items.name: Whole Home Renovation
items.blurb: Complete gut rehabs covering the kitchen, every bathroom, flooring, plumbing and electrical. The team works on Chicago greystones, vintage two-flats, single-family homes and condo conversions, and as an EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm it can work in pre-1978 homes. Typical budgets start around $85,000.

image.alt: Wicker Park whole-home remodel in Chicago, kitchen with navy island, stainless steel appliances and gold accents

items.name: Illinois-Made Custom Cabinets
items.blurb: Since 2024 the firm has offered Illinois-made custom cabinetry for kitchens, baths and built-ins. Lead times run 4 to 6 weeks instead of the 16 weeks the firm saw on imports, with no tariff exposure. Full-size displays are open to see at the Lincoln Park studio.

image.alt: Wicker Park kitchen in Chicago after a full gut remodel, with custom cabinets in an open-concept layout

why_choose_us.h2: Why condo owners choose Assembly Squad

items.title: 300+ buildings already approved
items.text: The firm is pre-approved in more than 300 Chicago buildings and reports zero HOA complaints in 13 years. Alteration agreements, insurance certificates and elevator scheduling are part of every condo job.

items.title: A fixed price before anything is ordered
items.text: You get a detailed estimate within 48 hours and a fixed-price proposal after design. If you ask for a change mid-project, it is priced and signed in writing first.

items.title: See it at the Lincoln Park studio
items.text: The 2,500 sq ft showroom at 2315 N Southport Ave holds 500+ cabinet, countertop, tile, hardware and flooring samples, plus free 3D renderings of your project.

items.title: Licensed, insured and warrantied
items.text: License #TGC098779, $2M liability insurance, an A+ BBB rating and a 2-year written workmanship warranty on all Assembly Squad labor.

about.h2: Founded by Viktor Aharon after 22+ years in remodeling
about.text: Viktor Aharon spent more than 22 years in remodeling watching homeowners juggle contractors, chase permit updates and make decisions nobody prepared them for. In 2011 he built the first Assembly Squad as an app to help people plan and manage a renovation. By 2013 it had become a design-build general contracting company with one rule: one team, one contract, one fixed price. Viktor asks whether you are building a forever home or planning a five or six year stay, then plans the work to balance daily enjoyment with resale value.

image.alt: Viktor Aharon, founder and CEO of Assembly Squad Remodeling in Chicago

process.h2: Four steps, about twelve weeks

steps.title: Week 1: Free consultation
steps.text: The team visits your home or condo, reviews building requirements and talks through your plans. A detailed estimate follows within 48 hours, in person or virtual.

steps.title: Weeks 2 to 4: Design and approvals
steps.text: 3D renderings, material picks at the Lincoln Park studio and a fixed-price proposal, while the firm handles HOA paperwork, permits and landmark approvals.

steps.title: Weeks 4 to 12: Construction
steps.text: Crews work within building hours, coordinate elevators and keep the site clean. Your project manager sends daily photo updates.

steps.title: Final week: Walkthrough
steps.text: A punch-list inspection, touch-ups and your warranty paperwork, including the 2-year workmanship warranty on all Assembly Squad labor.

service_area.h2: Chicago neighborhoods and North Shore towns we serve
service_area.text: Assembly Squad works across Chicago, the North Shore and nearby suburbs, roughly 40 miles out from the Loop. Downtown and Near North jobs are mostly high-rise condos and lofts. West and Northwest Side work leans toward two-flats, bungalows and loft conversions. On the North Shore the team builds premium kitchens, primary baths and basements. Every area gets the same free consultation and fixed-price proposal.

faq.h2: Chicago condo remodeling questions, answered

items.q: Who deals with my condo board and building management?
items.a: Assembly Squad does. HOA coordination is included on every condo project: alteration agreements, certificates of insurance, architectural drawings, neighbor notifications and board presentations. The firm is pre-approved in 300+ Chicago buildings and says it has had zero HOA complaints in 13 years. Call (312) 544-9150 to check whether your building is on the list.

items.q: What does a condo kitchen or bathroom cost in Chicago?
items.a: The firm publishes typical ranges: $25,000 to $150,000+ for kitchens, $15,000 to $55,000 for bathrooms and $25,000 to $250,000+ for condo remodels, with full condo gut renovations often at the high end. Your exact number comes in a fixed-price proposal after design, and the first estimate is free.

items.q: How long will my renovation take?
items.a: The standard plan runs about twelve weeks. Week one is the consultation and estimate, weeks two to four cover design, HOA paperwork and permits, and construction runs from week four to week twelve. City permit processing typically takes two to three weeks and is built into that schedule.

items.q: Can I see materials before I sign?
items.a: Yes. The Lincoln Park design studio at 2315 N Southport Ave is a 2,500 sq ft showroom with 500+ cabinet finishes, countertop slabs, tile, hardware and flooring samples. It is open Monday to Friday 9 am to 6 pm and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm by appointment, and 3D renderings are free.

items.q: Do you work outside the city?
items.a: Yes. Since 2025 the firm has brought the same design-build service to the North Shore, including Winnetka, Lake Forest, Highland Park, Glencoe and Evanston. It also works in suburbs such as Hinsdale, Glenview and Arlington Heights, within about 40 miles of the Loop, with the same free in-home consultation.

final_cta.h2: Ready to talk about your building and your plans?
final_cta.text: Call Viktor's team at (312) 544-9150 for a free consultation, or visit the Lincoln Park studio by appointment.

intro.h2: The owner sits at the table for every design decision
paragraphs: Craft Home Remodeling offers bathroom remodeling in San Diego from a small office in Rancho Bernardo. Founder Joey Dahan works with each client on the design, so you can reach a finished look without signing a separate design contract.

That hands-on approach shows up in the reviews. Clients say Joey listens closely, gives honest advice and keeps the job on schedule. One kitchen client spent close to a year refining details with him. Projects range from guest baths and powder rooms to spa-style primary suites, and the same team also remodels kitchens and complete homes from Scripps Ranch to La Jolla.

services.h2: Bathrooms, kitchens and whole homes in San Diego County

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Primary suites, guest baths and powder rooms, from walk-in glass showers and freestanding tubs to floating oak vanities and custom tile. Joey helps you choose fixtures and finishes so the room feels designed, not just updated. Recent baths include projects in Scripps Ranch and Sorrento Valley.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel in Sorrento Valley, San Diego with wavy white tile shower and oak vanity

items.name: Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: Kitchen remodels are the work clients mention most in Google reviews. Expect custom cabinetry, stone or quartz counters, smarter storage and layouts that improve the way you cook. Past kitchens include a two-tone navy and white kitchen in La Jolla and a walnut and marble kitchen in Encinitas.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel in La Jolla, CA with white shaker cabinets, navy island, brass pulls and floating wood shelves

items.name: Complete Home Renovations
items.blurb: Whole-house remodels that bring kitchens, baths, living areas and finishes together under one plan, including additions and ADUs. Craft has completed full-home projects in Rancho Santa Fe, Solana Beach, Del Mar and Encinitas, and one client's living room work included a new gas fireplace.

image.alt: Complete home remodel in Rancho Santa Fe, CA with open kitchen, light oak cabinets and quartz waterfall island

about.h2: Meet Joey Dahan, founder and owner

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Ann Arbor, Designed and Built Under One Roof
hero.subheadline: Founder Jef Forward and his in-house designers and carpenters have remodeled Ann Arbor homes for over 27 years. You see three concept layouts at three price points before anything gets built.
trust_badges: NARI Regional Contractor of the Year 2022 and 2023

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Ann Arbor: vaulted wood plank ceiling, wall of windows, gray island and stainless double wall ovens

intro.h2: Designers and builders who share one office on Jackson Road
paragraphs: Forward Design Build Remodel has handled kitchen remodeling in Ann Arbor for over 27 years, and its own site calls kitchens its specialty. The same company draws your plans, prices them and builds them, so the designer and the lead carpenter talk every day instead of passing drawings between two firms.

Before you commit to a direction, the team sketches three possible layouts for your home, each at a different price point inside your budget. You pick one, then refine it with material samples and 3D renderings. The site lists typical Ann Arbor kitchen budgets of $100,000 to $250,000, so you know the range before the first meeting.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Ann Arbor, plus baths, whole floors and additions

items.name: Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: Simple redesigns or full rebuilds that remove walls to open a closed-in kitchen to the living area. Each plan starts with your list of priorities, moves through material selections and 3D modeling, and ends with a complete plan the crew can build with confidence.

image.alt: Remodeled Ann Arbor kitchen with white shaker cabinets, dark-base island with four gray stools and exposed ceiling beams

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Primary baths and en-suite bathrooms, from spa-style showers to double vanities. Forward remodels hall baths and powder rooms only as part of a larger project. Its bathroom page lists primary bath remodels at $75,000 to $200,000, depending on the size of the space.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel in Ann Arbor with navy walls, white subway tile, dark oak double vanity and black-framed mirrors

items.name: Rekindle Remove-and-Replace
items.blurb: Made for kitchens and baths whose layout already works. Rekindle keeps walls, plumbing and electrical where they are and replaces cabinetry, countertops, tile, flooring, lighting and fixtures. You get interior renderings, a simple scope of work and a budget before work begins.

image.alt: Kitchen update with green full-height cabinets, speckled granite island, black sink and faucet, and wood base cabinets

items.name: Whole-Home and Historic Remodels
items.blurb: When a first floor needs real change, the Reimagine service removes or moves walls, adds rooms and relocates plumbing and electrical. Forward also lists historic home remodeling, and one Google reviewer hired the team to prepare a modest 1956 ranch for aging in place.

image.alt: Historic home kitchen remodel with walnut lower cabinets, open wood shelving, white counters and a stainless refrigerator

items.name: Additions and Custom Homes
items.blurb: Home additions and new custom homes follow the same design-build steps, from concept layouts through a final inspection walk-through. The portfolio includes a dog-friendly custom farmhouse design in Ann Arbor with a covered wood porch and an open, airy layout.

image.alt: Home addition in Ann Arbor with a covered wood porch, board-and-batten siding and an orange front door

why_choose_us.h2: What sets Forward apart before, during and after the build

items.title: Three concepts, three price points
items.text: Step one ends with floor plans of your existing home and three sketched layouts, each at a different price point within your budget, plus a written evaluation of scope, time and cost.

items.title: Award-winning kitchens and baths
items.text: NARI named Forward a Regional Contractor of the Year for a mid-century modern kitchen in 2022 and for its Modern Barn Bath in 2023. The firm also lists 14 Houzz awards and a Guildmaster award.

items.title: A place to stay during construction
items.text: Clients can rent Terra Knoll, the firm's furnished home on Ann Arbor's west side, while their own house is torn up. The site lists it at $3,500 a month with utilities included.

items.title: A written warranty and a service team
items.text: Your warranty period starts when construction is complete, and you get it in writing. Forward keeps a warranty manager on staff and a Home Care and Repair team for small fixes and finish updates.

about.h2: Meet founder Jef Forward
about.text: Jef Forward started the company more than 27 years ago with a passion for both architecture and building, and chose design-build as the way he wanted to serve homeowners. He still leads it as President and Creative Director, and was a runner-up for the Fred Case Remodeling Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2019. Forward keeps designers, project consultants, carpenters, a warranty manager and a service team in-house at 8110 Jackson Rd., where clients can visit the showroom by appointment. Every build gets its own Project Manager, Project Designer and Project Coordinator, who meet with you on a regular schedule until the final walk-through.

image.alt: Jef Forward, President and Creative Director, meeting on a job site with lead carpenter Jeff

process.h2: How the Forward design-build process works

steps.title: Clarify your vision
steps.text: After you sign a design agreement, the team reviews your goals, researches your home and local codes, and sketches three layouts at three price points.

steps.title: Shape the design
steps.text: Materials, colors and fixtures are chosen, drawings grow into 3D renderings, and the scope and budget are updated so you can see what drives the cost.

steps.title: Confirm and build
steps.text: A pre-construction meeting sets communication and dust control rules. Your Project Manager meets with you regularly, and the crew leaves the work area clean.

steps.title: Walk-through and warranty
steps.text: A final inspection walk-through checks every detail. Your written warranty period begins as soon as construction is complete.

faq.h2: Ann Arbor kitchen and bath questions, answered

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost in Ann Arbor?
items.a: Forward's kitchen page lists typical custom kitchen remodels in Ann Arbor at $100,000 to $250,000. Your number depends on size, finishes and whether walls or plumbing move. The first design step shows three concept layouts at three price points inside your budget, so you can compare before you commit.

items.q: Will you remodel just a powder room or hall bath?
items.a: Not on its own. Forward does not take on single hallway bath or powder room remodels, but it will remodel those rooms as part of a larger project. A primary bathroom remodel runs $75,000 to $200,000 depending on the size of the space, not counting a walk-in closet.

items.q: My kitchen layout works. Do I need a full redesign?
items.a: Maybe not. The Rekindle service is for kitchens, baths and interiors where no walls, plumbing or electrical locations move. The team picks fixtures and materials with you, shows interior renderings, and sets a simple scope and budget. Projects that move walls or add rooms go through the Reimagine service.

items.q: Where can we live while the work is going on?

seo.og_description: See your new kitchen in photorealistic 3D before anything is ordered, then have it built by the same family-owned crew. Serving Bergen, Passaic, Morris and Essex.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Wayne, NJ, Drawn and Built by One Team
hero.subheadline: Devin Hamlett draws and renders every project himself, then runs the build with the company's own crew. You walk through your new kitchen in 3D before a single wall comes down.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling near Wayne, NJ: Hackensack kitchen with blue Shaker cabinets, white marble hexagon backsplash and brass faucet

intro.h2: See the finished room first, then decide
paragraphs: Most kitchen remodeling in Wayne, NJ runs through three hires: a designer, a round of bids, then a builder. Hamlett Renovations keeps all of it under one contract. The team laser-measures your room, draws two or more layouts and renders the result in photorealistic 3D, so you can change it on screen before anything is ordered.

The price is then built line by line against the drawings you approved, with allowances named for anything still to be picked. Hamlett even posts its ranges: $35,000 to $60,000 for a refresh that keeps the layout, and $60,000 to $140,000 for a full design-build kitchen.

services.h2: Kitchen Remodeling in Wayne, NJ, Plus the Rest of the House

items.name: Kitchen Design & Build
items.blurb: Custom cabinetry, countertops and islands, with cabinets chosen in person at a partner showroom. When the layout changes, a design phase from $5,000 comes first and is credited in full toward construction. A full kitchen build typically takes 10 to 14 weeks.

image.alt: Remodeled kitchen in Paramus, NJ with white raised-panel cabinets, glass-front uppers and a sink under the window

items.name: Bathroom Design & Build
items.blurb: Tile showers, vanities and full renovations, with waterproofing done properly. A refresh that keeps the layout runs $12,000 to $22,000, and a full design-build bathroom runs $22,000 to $40,000. Most bathrooms are finished in 2 to 4 weeks.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel in Clifton, NJ with marble-look wall tile, tub and shower combination and black floating shelves

items.name: Additions & Whole-Home
items.blurb: Room and second-story additions and in-law suites, from feasibility and zoning through framing and finish. When a job moves structure, a licensed New Jersey architect reviews and seals the drawings inside Hamlett's own contract. Additions start at $120,000.

image.alt: Home addition great room in North Jersey with wood plank ceiling, stone fireplace and tall windows

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Unfinished basements turned into real living space, starting with a moisture check before anything else is built. Most basement projects take 4 to 8 weeks and run $30,000 to $80,000 or more, with permits and inspections included.

image.alt: Finished basement in Paramus, NJ with white wainscoting, gray brick accent wall and wood-look plank floor

items.name: Decks & Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Composite and wood decks, porches, paver patios and retaining walls, set on footings below the frost line so they hold up through North Jersey winters. Deck estimates are free, and most outdoor builds take 1 to 3 weeks.

image.alt: New composite deck with black metal railing in a North Jersey backyard

why_choose_us.h2: Why North Jersey homeowners pick Hamlett

items.title: You walk through it before you sign
items.text: Kitchens, baths, basements, additions and decks are rendered to scale. You see the finished room in 3D, and change it, before you sign a construction contract.

items.title: One contract, the company's own crew
items.text: Hamlett self-performs framing, carpentry and finish work, so the people who start your job are the people who finish it. Long-time trade partners handle mechanical, electrical and plumbing.

items.title: Prices out in the open
items.text: Ranges for kitchens, baths and additions are published on the site. If you decide not to build, the drawings and renderings are yours to keep and you owe nothing further.

items.title: A clean house at the end of the day
items.text: Google reviewer Mae A. wrote that the workspace was clean at the end of each day. Daily cleanup, permits and inspections are listed as always included on kitchen and bath jobs.

about.h2: Devin Hamlett runs the job; Shawn Brinster runs the numbers
about.text: Devin Hamlett started Hamlett Renovations in 2019 working in the field, and he still runs the jobs. He draws and renders every project himself, walks you through the options and is on your site daily while it is being built. Co-owner Shawn Brinster handles estimating, scheduling, materials and the money. He builds the number your project is priced against and keeps the job supplied and on schedule. You deal with one of them directly, never a salesperson who hands you off after signing. The family-owned firm holds New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor license #13VH12093400 and carries general liability and workers' compensation.

process.h2: Four steps from first call to final walkthrough

steps.title: Consultation
steps.text: Devin walks the space, laser-measures it and talks through how you actually use it. There is no charge, and the visit takes 60 to 90 minutes.

steps.title: Design and renderings
steps.text: Measured drawings, layout options, selections and 3D renderings. From $5,000 for kitchens and $2,500 for bathrooms, credited toward construction. Skipped when the layout stays put.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Priced line by line against the approved drawings, then built by Hamlett's own crew with permits pulled, inspections scheduled and one point of contact.

steps.title: Warranty
steps.text: The team hands the space over, walks every drawer and detail with you, and backs the work with a 1-year workmanship warranty.

service_area.h2: Based in Wayne, building across four counties
service_area.text: Hamlett's shop is in Wayne, and its crews work in Bergen, Passaic, Morris and Essex County. Recent jobs include kitchens in Teaneck, Hackensack, Paramus and Montclair, bathrooms in Maywood, Clifton and North Haledon, and decks in Westwood, Glen Rock and Hawthorne. Franklin Lakes is about six miles from the Wayne shop. If your town is not on the list, ask; the team will tell you honestly whether it covers your street.

faq.h2: Kitchen and bath questions we hear in Wayne

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost in Wayne and Bergen County?
items.a: Hamlett publishes its ranges. A refresh that keeps the layout runs $35,000 to $60,000. A full design-build kitchen, with walls or plumbing moving and new cabinetry, runs $60,000 to $140,000. Cabinetry line and door style move the number most, followed by countertop material and slab count.

items.q: How long will my kitchen or bathroom be out of use?
items.a: A kitchen refresh that leaves walls, plumbing and appliance spots alone runs 3 to 6 weeks. A full design-build kitchen runs 10 to 14 weeks, and cabinet lead time is usually the biggest variable, so cabinets are ordered early. Most bathrooms take 2 to 4 weeks.

items.q: Do I have to pay for the first meeting?
items.a: No. The consultation is no charge and takes 60 to 90 minutes in your home. A paid design phase only applies when the layout is changing, and that fee is credited in full toward construction. If you decide not to build, you keep the drawings and renderings.

items.q: Are you licensed and insured in New Jersey?
items.a: Yes. Hamlett holds New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor license #13VH12093400, carries general liability and workers' compensation, and pulls its own permits in the towns it works in. Structural drawings are reviewed and sealed by a licensed New Jersey architect inside Hamlett's contract.

items.q: I already have architect plans. Can you still help?
items.a: Yes. For a plan review, the team renders your existing drawings in 3D, flags what will not build or will blow the budget, and gives you a real construction number against the design you own. The review costs $1,500, credited toward construction.

final_cta.h2: Ready to see your kitchen before it is built?
final_cta.text: Book a design consultation and the team calls back the same business day.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeler in Inver Grove Heights for Design and Build

intro.h2: Challenging designs, finished down to the last detail
paragraphs: McDonald Remodeling is a kitchen remodeler in Inver Grove Heights founded in 2000 and based on Cahill Avenue. As a full-service design/build firm, it handles both the design and the construction, so one company is responsible for the plan and for the finished room.

The team calls challenging design its specialty, and its planning backs that up. Your home is measured and modeled in 3D, layouts are tested before a hammer is lifted, and every task is scheduled down to the day. Clients from Shoreview to Cottage Grove point to that daily schedule as the reason they hired McDonald.

services.h2: Kitchens first, then any room that needs a rethink

items.name: Kitchens
items.blurb: Smart layouts, custom cabinetry and materials picked for beauty and daily use. Recent kitchens include a Bloomington main floor with sage green and wood cabinets, a Lakeville update that blends existing oak with new finishes, and a 100-plus-year-old St. Paul home reworked for modern living.

image.alt: Bloomington kitchen and main floor remodel with sage green and wood cabinets, brass pendants and a gold velvet sofa in the open living area

items.name: Bathrooms
items.blurb: Spa-like primary suites, powder rooms and accessible baths with custom storage and finishes chosen for daily use. items.title: Scheduled down to the day
items.text: Tasks are scheduled day by day before construction starts. A Shoreview couple thought it was a sales pitch until every milestone was met, and their neighbors noticed too.

items.title: A guest in your home

items.title: Awards judged by the industry
items.text: Recent honors include a 2026 Regional Chrysalis Award for a kitchen, 2026 Best of Houzz for Service and Design, and ROMA awards from Housing First Minnesota.

about.h2: Led by owner and CEO Chris Wylie, with roots back to 1976
about.text: Chris Wylie is the owner and CEO of McDonald Remodeling, the design/build firm founded in 2000 and based on Cahill Avenue in Inver Grove Heights. Its values of quality design and craftsmanship trace back to 1976, when Jim McDonald built his first home. Today the firm has a dedicated interior design studio with designers such as Alisa Dragt-Hoffman and Emily Thull, plus project managers and construction superintendents. Its mission is remodeling and design rooted in honesty, integrity, creativity and meticulous attention to detail, and its employees give hundreds of volunteer hours each year.

process.h2: Four phases, each with a timeframe you can plan around

steps.title: Discovery (about 1 to 2 weeks)
steps.text: A home visit to talk through your ideas, their benefits and challenges, ending with a well-reasoned view of what is possible and an approximate budget.

steps.title: Design (about 1 to 2 months)
steps.text: Under a design agreement, the team measures your home, tests layouts in 3D software and delivers a detailed proposal with a fixed-price contract.

steps.title: Refinement (about 1 to 2 months)
steps.text: Design and selection meetings with the interior designers settle wood finishes, cabinetry, fixtures, paint, tile and flooring until every element is chosen.

steps.title: Construction (depends on scope)
steps.text: Tasks are scheduled down to the day, your project manager keeps you informed, and the job closes with a thorough walkthrough of the finished space.

intro.h2: A Manheim crew that listens before it builds
paragraphs: ALL Renovation & Design has handled kitchen remodeling in Lancaster, PA and across southcentral Pennsylvania since 2006. The office is on Penryn Road in Manheim, and the same team takes on baths, basements, additions and outdoor kitchens. Founder Amos Lapp built the company on the careful detail work he learned growing up in an Amish family.

The method is plain. Cabinets, tile and fixtures are all chosen before demolition, so the crew never stalls waiting on a decision. You then sign a written Project Plan that lists your start date, expected length and final cost. Past clients say they felt heard, and one Lititz couple just finished their fourth project with the firm.

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling

why_choose_us.h2: Four reasons clients hire ALL again and again

items.title: Workmanship covered for up to 10 years

about.h2: Meet Amos Lapp, founder of ALL Renovation & Design
about.text: Amos Lapp founded ALL Renovation & Design LLC in 2006 with one goal: to serve clients through a high level of craftsmanship in every area of construction and remodeling. He comes from an Amish background and still enjoys the hard work and small details that bring a project to life. Longtime client George S. remembers when Amos was a one-man team. Today the company has its own designers, cabinetmakers, carpenters and finishers, and clients often name them in reviews, from designer Ronda to carpenter Mike P. The firm marked its 20th year with a press release in 2026.

image.alt: Amos Lapp, founder of ALL Renovation & Design in Manheim, PA

process.h2: How a project moves from phone call to final walkthrough

steps.title: Phone conversation
steps.text: A 10 to 20 minute call covers your plans, goals and budget. If the fit looks right on both sides, the team books a visit to your home.

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: Staff walk the house, take measurements and check for structural limits. If scope, budget and timeline line up, you get a preliminary concept with a realistic budget.

steps.title: Design agreement and Project Plan
steps.text: A signed design agreement and a small non-refundable payment start design and permits. The Project Plan then lists every selection, the start date, duration and final cost.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: The crew seals off the work area and keeps the rest of your home livable. Expect updates at least twice a day on progress and the next day's work.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: You walk the finished space together with the team. If anything is not right, staff are called in to fix it on the spot.

faq.h2: Common questions before a Lancaster County remodel

items.q: Is your estimate free?
items.a: The first three steps cost nothing: a phone conversation, an in-home consultation and a preliminary estimate or solution for your project. ALL prefers this to a quick free quote because it gives a more accurate cost, so the number does not jump later. Full design work starts with a signed design agreement and a small non-refundable payment.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: ALL guarantees its workmanship against defects for up to 10 years from the date the work is performed. If you run into a problem with work the team completed, they will come back and fix it. Ask during your consultation how the guarantee applies to your specific project.

items.q: How long will my remodel take?
items.a: Real remodels take weeks, not the hour you see on a TV show. The most common planning mistake ALL sees is expecting too short a timeline. Your written Project Plan states the start date and expected duration, and because every selection is made before construction, the crew is not held up waiting on choices.

items.q: When is the best time of year to start?
items.a: The best time is whenever the work disrupts your life the least. Winter suits interior jobs like kitchens and baths because they do not depend on weather. For an addition, spring or late summer into fall works well. The team has scheduled around teachers who wanted work done in summer.

items.q: Where do I pick out cabinets, tile and fixtures?
items.a: A designer walks you through selections in the ALL showroom, at a vendor's showroom or in your home. Reviewers often mention designer Ronda's help with lighting and finishes. Everything is chosen and written into the Project Plan before construction begins, along with colors, allowances and final costs.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Bethesda, Designed and Built Under One Roof
hero.subheadline: Boss Design Center shows you a photorealistic 3D rendering of your new kitchen, locks every selection into a fixed-rate contract, then builds it. Visit the Bethesda showroom or the McLean design campus.
trust_badges: Licensed in MD, DC and VA (Class A)

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Bethesda: Greentree Road kitchen with white oak cabinets, a pale blue island, white counters and white cone pendants with brass trim

intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Bethesda that starts with a rendering, not a guess
paragraphs: Boss Design Center handles kitchen remodeling in Bethesda from its showroom at 7220 Wisconsin Avenue. It is a design-build firm, so the designer who draws your kitchen stays involved until the job is done. Before any wall comes down, you see a photorealistic 3D rendering of the finished room.

Every tile, cabinet and fixture is picked before construction starts, which lets the firm write a fixed-rate contract with no allowances. Its own kitchen projects run $80,000 to $250,000. You can touch cabinet doors, counters and tile in person at the Bethesda showroom or the McLean design campus on Chain Bridge Road. One Google reviewer wrote that Talha and his crew get things done correctly the first time.

services.h2: What the Boss team designs and builds

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Traditional, transitional, modern, coastal and French-inspired kitchens, plus German-made cabinetry with handleless and designer-series options. Structural changes are welcome, as the firm's Arlington kitchen project shows. You choose cabinets, counters, backsplash and hardware in the showroom, not from catalog photos.

image.alt: Arlington, VA kitchen remodel with light oak cabinets, purple-veined stone counters, a woven rattan pendant and a breakfast table by French doors

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Small baths, modern and classic baths, and primary suites. You see the room in a 3D rendering and revise it until it is right, then pick tile, vanities and fixtures in person. Your project manager runs the daily work and meets with you every week.

image.alt: Bethesda, MD bathroom on Edgemoor Lane with ribbed wood-look wall tile, a frameless glass shower, heated towel rail and floating oak vanity

items.name: Whole Home Remodeling
items.blurb: For growing families, empty nesters, historic houses and new homes that need to feel like yours. One design idea carries through every room, and a single accountable team handles the kitchen, the baths, the basement and the spaces in between.

image.alt: Reston, VA whole house remodel with a two-story great room, exposed timber ceiling beams, a loft railing and an iron ring chandelier

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: A dark lower level that feels more like a root cellar can become real living space. The crew opens walls, checks what is behind them and handles the permits, then finishes the basement under the same fixed-rate contract and weekly updates as a kitchen.

image.alt: Boss Design crew member checking an opened basement wall at the start of a basement finishing project

items.name: Aging-in-Place Remodeling
items.blurb: Certified Aging-in-Place Specialists on staff plan barrier-free showers, grab bars that look like fixtures, comfort-height toilets, pull-out shelving and wider doorways. The goal is a safer home with no institutional look, and it starts with a free home assessment.

image.alt: McLean, VA bathroom with a frameless glass walk-in shower, built-in bench, black fixtures and a herringbone wood-look tile wall

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons homeowners near Bethesda pick Boss

items.title: A price that holds
items.text: Selections are made before construction begins, so there are no allowances. The firm puts it plainly: if your project starts at $200,000, it ends at $200,000.

items.title: Two showrooms to shop in person
items.text: See cabinet doors, counters and tile at 7220 Wisconsin Avenue in Bethesda or at 1389 Chain Bridge Road in McLean, by appointment Monday through Saturday.

items.title: Licensed in all three jurisdictions
items.text: Boss holds a Virginia Class A contractor license plus Maryland and Washington, DC contractor licenses. It is bonded and insured, with an A+ BBB rating and NKBA membership.

items.title: A written warranty
items.text: Every project includes a 5-year warranty on structural work and a 1-year warranty on finishes, fixtures, cabinetry, countertops, tile, plumbing, electrical and hardware.

about.h2: Led by architectural designer Talha Gursoy
about.text: Talha Gursoy leads design at Boss Design Center, and the firm's careers page lists its President as Taha A. Gursoy. He holds a Bachelor's and a Master's degree in Architecture and has more than ten years in design-build work, focused on interior design and construction. Homeowners often meet him first. One wrote that at the first visit he did not ask about budget right away but simply listened, and that his renderings matched the finished kitchen. Talha also writes the firm's blog, with plain guides on Virginia permits, fixed-rate contracts and German versus American cabinets.

image.alt: Talha Gursoy, architectural designer and President of Boss Design Center in Bethesda, MD

process.h2: From first visit to final punch list

steps.title: Free in-home consultation
steps.text: A remodeling planner visits your home, looks at the space and talks through your ideas, budget and timeline. There is no cost and no obligation.

steps.title: Design and 3D rendering
steps.text: The designer measures the existing structure, then presents a photorealistic rendering with a scope budget and projected timeline. This stage typically takes one to two months.

steps.title: Selections and fixed-rate contract
steps.text: You choose cabinets, counters, backsplash, fixtures and paint colors in the showroom. With every detail set, the contract price is fixed.

steps.title: Permits and preparation
steps.text: The team applies for permits, orders materials and introduces your project manager. Expect about four to six weeks from contract to start.

steps.title: Construction and walkthrough
steps.text: Building typically takes three to four months, with weekly in-person meetings and online updates. A full punch list is finished before the job closes.

service_area.h2: Where Boss works in Maryland, Virginia and DC
service_area.text: From the Bethesda showroom, the team remodels homes in Chevy Chase, Potomac, Kensington, Rockville, Silver Spring, Cabin John and nearby Maryland towns. The McLean design campus serves Arlington, Alexandria, Vienna, Great Falls, Fairfax, Falls Church, Reston and out to Leesburg and Ashburn. In the District, project photos on the site come from Georgetown, Kalorama, Cleveland Park, Wesley Heights and Capitol Hill.

faq.h2: Questions Bethesda homeowners ask Boss

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel with Boss cost?
items.a: The firm says its own kitchen projects run $80,000 to $250,000. Your number depends on size, layout changes and the finishes you pick. Because every detail is chosen before construction, the contract is fixed-rate with no allowances, so the price you sign is the price you pay.

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: Design and selections typically take one to two months. Permits and ordering add about four to six weeks from contract to start, and construction typically runs three to four months. The firm's own guide puts a full kitchen at about six to eight months from first consultation to finish.

items.q: Do you handle the permits?
items.a: Yes. Your project manager and crew apply for the permits you need and file them with your local jurisdiction. Boss holds contractor licenses in Maryland, Virginia and Washington, DC, including a Virginia Class A license, the top tier, which has no project value limit.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: Each project includes a 5-year warranty on structural work and a 1-year warranty on finishes, fixtures, cabinetry, countertops, tile, plumbing, electrical and hardware. Before the job is called finished, the team works through a full punch list with you and completes every item on it.

items.q: Can I see materials before I commit?
items.a: Yes. The Bethesda showroom at 7220 Wisconsin Avenue, Suite 110, and the McLean design campus at 1389 Chain Bridge Road are open Monday through Saturday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., by appointment. Call (301) 200-9991 to book a time to look at cabinets, counters and tile.

final_cta.h2: See your new kitchen before the first wall comes down
final_cta.text: Call the Bethesda showroom to book a free in-home consultation and start on your rendering.
