faq.h2: Questions Poway homeowners ask Kitchen Barn

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. The kitchen and whole-home pages invite you to contact Kitchen Barn for a free consultation, and the bathroom page calls it a complimentary consultation. Call (888) 454-6465 to make an appointment. The team talks through your goals first, then plans the design with you at the Poway showroom.

items.q: How fast can an express kitchen or bath be finished?
items.a: The Express Kitchen and Bath page lists about one week for the home consultation, one week of showroom design, two to three weeks for expedited cabinets to arrive and about one week to install. By those phases, an express project runs roughly five to six weeks, depending on the cabinet line you choose.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: The home page says Kitchen Barn's cabinet lines carry product warranties for customers. The site does not spell out a separate written warranty on labor, so ask for those terms in writing when you review your proposal. That way you know what each part of the project covers.

items.q: Can I see cabinets and finishes before I decide?
items.a: Yes. Design review and sign-off take place at the showroom at 13771 Danielson St in Poway. You compare cabinet lines, countertops, moldings, flooring, fixtures and hardware in person. Reviewers say the team showed them how different options would look, which made each choice easier.

items.q: Do you remodel more than kitchens?
items.a: Yes. Despite the name, the firm handles bathrooms, laundry rooms, family rooms and whole-home remodels. One client had the kitchen, family room and guest bath done together, and another had cabinets built for a full new home in Ramona. The firm's blog also covers doing a whole-home remodel in phases.

hero.h1: Design-Build Remodeling in Kirkland, WA, Led by a Designer
hero.subheadline: ARIID was started by interior designer Ariana Adireh Anderson so her plans would reach the job site intact. One licensed team designs, permits and builds your kitchen, bath or addition.

image.alt: Design-build remodeling Kirkland WA: dark-cabinet kitchen with a granite island, brass faucet, mirrored backsplash and sculpted glass pendants

intro.h2: Why a design studio started its own build company
paragraphs: ARIID Build & Remodel offers design-build remodeling in Kirkland, WA, and it grew out of a design firm. Ariana Adireh Anderson ran Ariana Designs & Interiors for years and kept seeing projects lose their magic between the drawing board and the job site. So she started a construction company with one job: protect the design and build it right.

Today the same team handles the drawings, the city permits and the construction, with the sister design studio choosing finishes and furniture. The firm calls it Design. Build. Furnish. For you, it means one contract, one schedule and one person to call when a question comes up mid-project.

services.h2: Design-build remodeling in Kirkland, WA: kitchens, baths and more

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: The team studies where your stove, sink, refrigerator and oven sit today, then looks for dead space in nearby halls, closets or under stairs. Plans cover custom cabinetry and storage, counters, appliance coordination, a layered lighting plan and any structural work.

image.alt: White kitchen remodel on the Eastside with a quartz waterfall island, open wood shelves and black-and-glass pendant lights

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: From primary bath overhauls to guest bath refreshes, ARIID handles layout, tile selection, plumbing coordination and construction. Every bathroom gets proper exhaust ventilation to stop moisture and mold, plus storage built in as cabinets, shelves or shower niches.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with a white stone double vanity, wall-mounted black faucets, wood cabinet base and large black-framed mirror

items.name: Whole-Home Remodeling
items.blurb: For homes where the kitchen, primary bath and main floor all need work at once. Designer and builder work as one team, so trades are sequenced together. ARIID plans with you early if you will need to live elsewhere during demolition.

image.alt: Remodeled living room with a linear gas fireplace in a tall tile wall, gray sectional sofa and starburst light fixture

items.name: Home Additions and New Builds
items.blurb: Main-floor expansions, second-story additions, ADUs and custom new homes. ARIID handles zoning, building code and HOA review, secures permits, manages inspections and prepares clear estimates covering materials, labor, permits and contingencies, so you see the full cost before construction begins.

image.alt: Modern two-story home built by ARIID with large black-framed windows, white siding and a covered outdoor room among tall evergreens

items.name: Aging in Place
items.blurb: Changes that let you stay home safely without the home looking clinical: grab bars, roll-in or curbless showers, comfort-height fixtures, non-slip floors, lower counters, lever handles, wider doorways and better lighting. It starts with an accessibility assessment of your current layout.

image.alt: Accessible bathroom remodel with a fold-down teak shower seat, handheld shower on a slide bar, tiled niches and a floating wood shelf

why_choose_us.h2: What you get with ARIID that a builder alone can't offer

items.title: A designer runs the company
items.text: Founder and CEO Ariana Adireh Anderson is also Head of Design, with over 20 years in the industry. Her sister firm, Ariana Designs & Interiors, picks finishes and furnishings so the build matches the plan.

items.title: Licensed, accredited and recognized
items.text: ARIID is a Washington State licensed contractor (License #ARIIDBL767NB), BBB accredited with an A+ rating, an NKBA member and a Master Builders Association member, with National NKBA Design Awards in 2021 and 2024.

items.title: Permits handled for you
items.text: A Google reviewer wrote that permits and code compliance went exactly as outlined at the first meeting. ARIID submits at the earliest design stage and manages the city review through each cycle.

items.title: Clean, careful crews
items.text: Reviewers mention a crew that kept the work area clean through a basement project while the family lived at home, and a team that showed up on time and cleaned up after itself.

about.h2: Meet Ariana Adireh Anderson, founder and Head of Design
about.text: Ariana Adireh Anderson founded ARIID Build & Remodel and serves as its CEO and Head of Design. She brings over 20 years of industry experience and still leads Ariana Designs & Interiors, the design studio that ARIID grew out of. The build company exists because she watched good designs get watered down by the time crews built them. Nick Anderson serves as President and oversees operations. Design-build project manager Isabel Valenta guides each job from first consultation to final install through site visits and subcontractor coordination, and customer concierge Line Beaudette keeps scheduling and communication on track.

image.alt: ARIID designer measuring a dark tile fireplace wall during an in-home design visit on the Eastside

process.h2: From first walk-through to final reveal

steps.title: Site visit and assessment
steps.text: The team walks your home, reviews existing conditions and your goals, and checks which parts of the work will need building permits.

steps.title: Design in 3D
steps.text: Designers draw the layout and show it in 3D visualizations, then help you choose cabinetry, tile, fixtures and lighting that fit your budget.

steps.title: Estimate and permits
steps.text: You get a detailed estimate before work starts. ARIID prepares drawings and specifications for permitting and handles the city review.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: A design-build project manager coordinates subcontractors, visits the site and checks quality against the approved plans, with regular updates to you.

steps.title: Final walk-through and furnishing
steps.text: The project closes with a final walkthrough. If you want it, the sister design studio can furnish and style the finished rooms.

service_area.h2: Building across Kirkland and the Eastside
service_area.text: ARIID works from an appointment-only office at 1018 Market St, Suite C, in Kirkland. Its Kirkland page names Houghton, South Rose Hill, Totem Lake, Juanita, Norkirk and Moss Bay among the neighborhoods it serves. Beyond Kirkland, the site lists Bellevue, Mercer Island, Medina, Clyde Hill, Yarrow Point, Redmond, Sammamish, Issaquah and Seattle, and it handles permits in each city as part of the job.

faq.h2: What Kirkland homeowners ask ARIID before a remodel

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
items.a: ARIID's kitchen page puts a full Eastside kitchen remodel at about $65,000 to $175,000 or more. Mid-range updates that keep the layout run $65,000 to $95,000. Major changes with a new layout, custom cabinets and premium appliances run $120,000 to $200,000. You get a detailed estimate after a site visit.

items.q: How long will my kitchen remodel take?
items.a: Plan on 3 to 5 months from design kick-off to final walkthrough. Design and permitting take 4 to 6 weeks for standard scopes, and construction runs 6 to 10 weeks. Custom cabinets take 8 to 12 weeks to arrive, so ARIID builds that lead time into the schedule on day one.

items.q: Do I need a permit to remodel my kitchen?
items.a: Yes, if the work touches electrical, moves plumbing, changes structure or adds new vent openings. New counters, refinished cabinets or appliance swaps usually do not need one. ARIID checks permit needs at the first assessment and manages the whole permit process as part of its design-build scope.

items.q: Will we have to move out during a big remodel?
items.a: It depends on scope. When the kitchen and primary bathroom are torn out at the same time, clients usually live elsewhere for 6 to 10 weeks. ARIID talks through relocation planning at kick-off and orders the construction so the stretch when your home is unlivable stays as short as possible.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom safer for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. ARIID installs grab bars, roll-in showers, walk-in tubs, comfort-height fixtures and non-slip floors. A bathroom conversion with a curbless shower, grab bars and ADA-height fixtures typically runs $35,000 to $75,000 on the Eastside. Grab bars in existing tile need no permit, but structural changes do.

seo.og_description: A Danville design-build firm founded in 1961, with in-house designers, a dedicated project manager on every job and a 5-year workmanship warranty.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Danville, CA from a Third-Generation Builder
hero.subheadline: Chris Gayler leads the design-build firm his grandfather founded in 1961. Designers, project managers and carpenters work under one roof, and every project gets a fixed-cost budget before construction starts.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling by a Danville, CA design-build firm: contemporary Lafayette kitchen with light oak flat-panel cabinets and a long island

intro.h2: A family process built to hit the date and the number
paragraphs: Kitchen remodeling in Danville, CA has been the Gayler family's trade for more than six decades. George Gayler took over his father's firm in 1980 and built the Gayler Process, a design-build system that links design and construction so nothing gets lost between the two. His son Chris runs it today from a showroom on Hartz Way.

The firm says every project has been delivered on time and on budget since 1999. That starts with a fixed-cost budget estimate and a design you approve in 3D before work begins. After the last walkthrough, a 5-year workmanship warranty and scheduled check-ins keep the team in touch.

services.h2: Kitchen Remodeling in Danville, CA, from Concept to Cleanup

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Kitchens planned for how your family cooks and gathers: large islands, custom pantries, multiple work stations and accessible storage. You see a 3D rendering of the final floor plan and pick finishes with the firm's interior designer before construction.

image.alt: San Ramon, CA kitchen addition with walnut island, white quartz countertop and white Shaker cabinets

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites and compact powder rooms, inside the existing footprint or expanded. Gayler designs for aging in place and universal access, with curbless showers, heated floors, soaking tubs and wet rooms when you want them.

image.alt: Aging-in-place primary bathroom in Danville, CA with curbless marble shower, grab bars and fold-down teak seat

items.name: Whole House Remodeling
items.blurb: For older homes that need more than one room. The design and construction teams plan the whole house together, so layout, finishes and schedule stay in step from demolition to the final deep clean. One project manager keeps it all on one calendar.

image.alt: Whole-home remodel in Danville, CA with white kitchen, charcoal island, glass pendant lights and oak floors

items.name: Home Additions & ADUs
items.blurb: Main-floor expansions, second stories, bump-outs, garage conversions and detached accessory dwelling units. You begin with an in-home consultation, then get conceptual drawings and a cost versus budget analysis before any detailed design work, so you know early whether the idea fits your budget.

image.alt: Kitchen inside a family ADU in Alamo, CA with white cabinets, stainless range and wood floors

items.name: Outdoor Living Spaces
items.blurb: Outdoor kitchens, covered pavilions, decks and screened porches planned around how you entertain. The team works through flooring, lighting, structure, electrical and plumbing so the finished space works as a true extension of the house, not an afterthought.

image.alt: Outdoor pavilion bar in Danville, CA with timber roof, woven bar stools and a pool beyond

why_choose_us.h2: The record behind the name

items.title: On time and on budget since 1999
items.text: Gayler gives fixed-cost budget estimates and states that every project since 1999 has finished on time and on budget. Past clients send 60% of its work.

items.title: Five years of workmanship coverage
items.text: The 5-year workmanship warranty is five times the one-year industry standard, the firm says, and it comes with scheduled follow-ups plus a binder of every manufacturer warranty.

items.title: Licensed builders in-house
items.text: The firm has four licensed contractors, architectural designers on staff and trades who average 26.7 years of experience. Each job gets a dedicated project manager.

items.title: Rated by clients, not just judges
items.text: GuildQuality named Gayler a Guildmaster with Highest Distinction four years running, 2023 to 2026, and Nextdoor neighbors voted it a 2026 Fave in General Contractor.

about.h2: Chris Gayler, third generation at the helm
about.text: Chris Gayler's grandfather founded the company in 1961. His father George took it over in 1980, a year after earning his contractor's license, and grew it with Chris's mother Darlene, who joined in 2000. Chris has worked in the business since 2003 and took over in January 2020. A UC Santa Barbara graduate, he brings his own contractor's license, a communications degree and a tech background. He serves on the boards of the San Ramon Rotary and the Valley Education Foundation. His goal, in his words, is to leave things in even better shape than he found them.

image.alt: Chris Gayler and his father George Gayler reviewing floor plans

process.h2: How a Gayler kitchen comes together

steps.title: A phone call
steps.text: You share your vision, the team answers questions and explains the design-build steps. If it looks like a good fit, an in-home visit is scheduled.

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: The team walks your space, reviews the current layout, talks cabinetry, countertops, lighting and flooring, and takes precise measurements and photos.

steps.title: Concept and preliminary estimate
steps.text: After you sign a design agreement and fill out a design questionnaire, the designers prepare a conceptual floor plan, a preliminary estimate and a clear scope of work.

steps.title: Final design in 3D
steps.text: You see a 3D rendering, choose finishes with the interior designer and receive the final construction estimate before signing the construction agreement.

steps.title: Build, clean and walk through
steps.text: A dedicated project manager runs the job with 24/7 online schedule access, the site is cleaned daily, and a final walkthrough checklist closes it out.

service_area.h2: Serving the Tri-Valley and Lamorinda from Hartz Way
service_area.text: The office and showroom sit at 825 Hartz Way in Danville, open Monday through Friday. From there, Gayler works across the Tri-Valley and Lamorinda: Alamo, Diablo and San Ramon close to home, Pleasanton, Dublin and Livermore to the south and east, and Walnut Creek, Lafayette, Orinda and Moraga over the hill. Recent jobs include an ADU in Alamo, a kitchen addition in San Ramon and a whole-home remodel in Danville.

faq.h2: Before you call: common Danville remodeling questions

items.q: What does the 5-year warranty cover?
items.a: Gayler backs its workmanship for five years, which it describes as five times the one-year industry standard, and schedules follow-ups after you move back in. At the final walkthrough you also get a binder holding the manufacturer warranties for every product used, from cabinets and countertops to backsplash and flooring.

items.q: Can you plan a kitchen or bath for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. Accessibility and aging in place are among the most common requests the design team hears. A recent Danville primary bathroom was built around them, with a curbless shower, grab bars and a fold-down seat. Universal design can be part of any bathroom or kitchen plan.

items.q: Can we stay in the house during the remodel?
items.a: Often, yes. One San Ramon couple wrote that they lived and worked at home through their 12-plus-week primary bathroom remodel, and that the crew left the house clean and safe every day. The team cleans the job site at the end of each workday to keep disruption down.

items.q: How will I know where my project stands?
items.a: Every project is assigned a dedicated project manager, and you get real-time, 24/7 access to your schedule and project details through the firm's online scheduling software. Changes to the original plan and timeline are shared as they happen, so you are not left guessing.

items.q: How do you keep a remodel on budget?
items.a: Gayler builds the design and the estimate together. You get a preliminary estimate with the concept plan, then a final construction estimate once finishes are chosen, before you sign. For additions, conceptual drawings come with a cost versus budget analysis so you can adjust scope early.

final_cta.h2: Talk kitchens with a Gayler designer
final_cta.text: Call the Danville office, open weekdays 8 am to 4 pm, or request a personal in-home consultation.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Santa Barbara With a Fixed Price Up Front
hero.subheadline: Owner Kiel Kellow's in-house designers and builders plan your kitchen side by side, then give you one fixed construction price before anyone breaks ground.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Santa Barbara area: Montecito kitchen with a white oak island, marble countertops, glass pendants and a skylight

intro.h2: Designers and builders at the same table
paragraphs: Kellow Construction handles kitchen remodeling in Santa Barbara and Montecito as a design-build firm, so the people drawing your kitchen work beside the people who will build it. Owner Kiel Kellow is a design-focused builder who believes estimating and design should always go hand in hand.

That belief runs the whole job. Cabinetry, countertops, tile, hardware and lighting are picked before you sign the construction contract, and the price that follows is one fixed number. A single project manager then runs the work from demo to punch list. On site, superintendent Rudy brings more than two decades of supervising local remodels.

services.h2: Design-build services across Santa Barbara and Montecito

items.name: Kitchen Design and Remodel
items.blurb: Your in-house designer works with your project manager from concept through construction, so the kitchen on paper is one the team knows it can build on budget. Layouts, finishes and details are settled early, whether the house is a historic craftsman bungalow or a modern hillside home.

image.alt: Remodeled Santa Barbara kitchen with white cabinets, a farmhouse sink, a professional range and a patterned tile backsplash under a plaster hood

items.name: Bath Design and Remodel
items.blurb: Primary suites, guest baths, small modern baths and historic restorations, plus Spanish-style tilework drawn from Santa Barbara's own architecture. Layout, plumbing, tile and fixtures are planned and priced before construction begins, so fewer surprises turn up once the walls are open.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel with a double vanity, marble top, brass faucets, freestanding tub and herringbone floor

items.name: Whole House Remodels
items.blurb: For gut renovations, phased remodels and big layout changes, the team treats the house as one system. Structural changes, systems upgrades and work across kitchens, baths, living areas and bedrooms are planned together. One client's 1888 former barn was rebuilt from roof to foundation.

image.alt: Whole-house interior renovation in Santa Barbara with exposed ceiling beams, wide windows and an open dining area

items.name: Home Additions
items.blurb: Additions are designed to feel like they were always part of the house. Kellow carries them from the first sketch through permits, construction and close-out, using the same design-build team and the same fixed-price contract it uses for every remodel.

image.alt: New framing and vaulted roof structure during a Kellow Construction remodel in Santa Barbara

why_choose_us.h2: What you get when one team designs and builds

items.title: One number before you build
items.text: Kellow works on a fixed-price, single-number construction contract. Every selection and detail is priced first, so you know exactly what you are building and what it costs before ground breaks.

items.title: Senior attention on big projects
items.text: The firm describes itself as big enough for complex, high-end projects and small enough that homeowners still get senior attention. Your designer works full time with your project manager and field crew.

items.title: Permit experience close to home
items.text: The team has worked through Santa Barbara permitting, Montecito overlay regulations and Hope Ranch project requirements across dozens of projects. That shapes the feasibility and timeline advice you get from the first conversation.

items.title: A rare green credential
items.text: Kellow says it is the only contractor in California holding the Earth Advantage Sustainable Homes Professionals designation, part of its aim to shrink both its own carbon footprint and its clients'.

about.h2: Meet owner Kiel Kellow and his crew
about.text: Kiel Kellow grew up between Tillamook County, Oregon and Bainbridge Island, Washington. He sharpened his carpentry while living aboard his 1934 wooden sailboat, working on boats, high-end custom homes and in a cabinet shop. In Portland he became a lead carpenter for an award-winning design/build firm before starting his own company. Today he leads Kellow Construction from Santa Barbara. Office manager Emily Kellow, born and raised in town, runs contracts, accounting and insurance. Project manager Jason brings more than 15 years of carpentry, and designer Tara holds a BFA in Interior Architecture.

image.alt: Kiel Kellow, owner of Kellow Construction in Santa Barbara, CA

process.h2: Five steps from first talk to fixed price

steps.title: Initial consultation
steps.text: A no-pressure talk about your home, goals, vision and investment range, and whether the design-build process is the right fit for both sides.

steps.title: Design phase 1
steps.text: The team studies your existing home, priorities, constraints and permit issues, and lines up scope with budget while there is still room to adjust.

steps.title: Design phase 2
steps.text: With a Design Agreement signed, in-house designers develop plans, layouts, materials, fixtures and finishes, with builders checking cost and constructability along the way.

steps.title: Documents, permits and fixed price
steps.text: Technical drawings, engineering and permits come next. Once scope and selections are defined, you get a fixed-price construction contract instead of a rough estimate.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Your project manager and site superintendent build from the plans and selections made in design, with regular updates and clear accountability until the final details.

service_area.h2: Remodeling from Goleta to Carpinteria
service_area.text: Kellow Construction is locally owned and based on East Micheltorena Street in Santa Barbara. The team works in Santa Barbara, Montecito, Goleta and Carpinteria and has handled projects in Hope Ranch. Inside the city, past work and local knowledge cover the Mesa, the Riviera and the Upper East Side, where homes run from Spanish Colonial and craftsman bungalows to modern hillside builds.

faq.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Santa Barbara: your questions answered

items.q: Will I know the full price before construction starts?
items.a: Yes. Kellow does not ask you to commit to construction based on a rough estimate. Design, drawings, selections and pricing happen first. Once the scope is fully defined, you get a fixed-price, single-number construction contract, so you know exactly what is being built and what it costs before ground breaks.

items.q: Do you work on historic homes?
items.a: Yes. The team works across Santa Barbara styles, from Spanish Colonial and Santa Barbara bungalows to contemporary coastal homes, and offers historic bathroom restorations. Past clients include the owners of an 1888 former barn and a 1920s craftsman, who wanted the house updated while keeping its original character.

items.q: What if I already have an architect or designer?
items.a: Most clients have Kellow manage the design, but the firm also works with outside architects and interior designers. Its Iterative Design Process brings them into a shared loop that keeps ideas buildable and on budget. Kellow says it enjoys partnering with design pros who care about cost, quality and detail.

items.q: Do you handle permits?
items.a: Yes. As the design comes together, the team prepares the technical drawings and specifications, coordinates consultants and engineering, and guides the project through permitting. It has worked through Santa Barbara's permit process and Montecito overlay regulations many times, which helps set a realistic timeline early.

items.q: Is there a warranty on the work?
items.a: Yes. Kellow offers what it calls a comprehensive warranty, so the team is still there for you long after the project is finished. The site does not list the length or terms, so ask for the written warranty during your consultation and review it before you sign the construction contract.

final_cta.text: Call 805-225-3310, Monday to Friday from 7 am to 3:30 pm, or schedule a consultation online. Every project starts with a conversation about your goals and investment range.

intro.h2: Kitchen and bath remodeling in Warwick, built on 37 years of Rhode Island homes
paragraphs: RIKB Design Build has handled kitchen and bath remodeling in Warwick since it opened its doors in 1989. The family-owned firm plans, designs and installs every project itself, which gives it tighter control over scheduling, quality and cost than a contractor who hands off parts of the job.

Before you commit, you can stand inside full-size kitchen and bath displays at 139 Jefferson Boulevard. Open the drawers, feel the countertop finishes, compare tile and fixtures. Several RIKB design consultants are Certified Kitchen & Bath designers and Certified Aging in Place Specialists, so a bath can be planned for the years ahead, not just for today.

services.h2: Rooms the RIKB team plans and builds

items.name: Kitchens
items.blurb: Simple cosmetic updates, pull-and-replace kitchens or a fully custom room, in traditional, contemporary or modern styles. Designers work on the layout, storage and countertop choice first, because those small decisions often make the biggest daily difference.

image.alt: Burrillville, RI kitchen remodel with white shaker cabinets, a stained wood island with white top, dark ceiling beams and glass globe pendants

items.name: Bathrooms
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and closets turned into powder rooms. The designers ask questions you may not have thought of, then help you choose materials that fit your budget, from a simple cosmetic refresh to a spa-like retreat.

image.alt: Providence, RI bathroom with a white freestanding tub, brass tub filler, green tile shower behind black steel-framed glass and dark slate floor

items.name: Aging in Place
items.blurb: Certified Aging in Place Specialists plan baths and kitchens that work as your needs change, such as zero-entry showers and fold-down shower seats. RIKB has also won a Qualified Remodeler Master Design Bronze award for an accessible bathroom.

image.alt: Bristol, RI primary bathroom with a zero-entry shower, navy wall tile, a fold-down teak shower seat and basketweave mosaic floor

items.name: Additions, Basements and Whole Homes
items.blurb: Home additions, finished basements, multi-room renovations, game rooms and bar areas. RIKB won a Chrysalis regional award for an addition under $250k and a PRO New England Gold award for an entire house, so larger projects are routine here.

image.alt: Rhode Island living room remodel with a white fireplace surround, coffered ceiling and a wall of windows facing the water

items.name: Mudrooms, Pantries and Built-ins
items.blurb: The smaller rooms that make a house run: mudrooms, laundry rooms, pantries, home offices, built-ins and coffee bars. Each one gets the same design consultant, 3D planning and installation crew as a full kitchen remodel would.

image.alt: North Kingstown, RI coffee bar with a white glass-front cabinet, gold faucet, scrolled tile panel and white subway backsplash

why_choose_us.h2: What you get with a Warwick firm that has done this since 1989

items.title: A five-year guarantee
items.text: Every project is covered by RIKB's Quality Assurance and Five-Year Workmanship Warranty, on top of the manufacturer warranties that come with many of the products installed.

items.title: Licensed and insured in three states
items.text: Rhode Island Reg. #3984, Massachusetts #164199 and Connecticut HIC.0673137, with liability insurance up to $2 million per project and full workers' compensation for all staff.

items.title: Materials checked before install
items.text: All materials are ordered, received and inspected at RIKB's own facility first, and you meet your installation team to review every detail before construction begins.

items.title: Recognized for service
items.text: A 2026 Guildmaster Award with Distinction, Qualified Remodeler Top 500 in 2025 and 2026, and Providence Business News Best Places to Work for 2018 through 2026.

about.h2: A family-owned team led by Tanya Donahue
about.text: Tanya Donahue is Owner and President of RIKB Design Build, the family-owned company that started in Warwick in 1989 as Rhode Island Kitchen & Bath. From the start, the firm has hired people with a passion for remodeling and kept training them. Design consultants earn CKD and CAPS credentials, and the company is EPA LeadSafe certified. Homeowners remember the people by name: designers Kelly May, Erika and Stephanie, and project manager Jamie all come up in reviews. RIKB also donates used building materials and supports the Rhode Island Community Food Bank, collecting food at its seminars.

image.alt: Tanya Donahue, Owner and President of RIKB Design Build in Warwick, RI

process.h2: Imagine, Conceptualize, Collaborate, Build

steps.title: Imagine
steps.text: The team starts with questions about how you live, then visits your home to measure and talk through ideas with your budget in mind.

steps.title: Conceptualize
steps.text: At the design center you see concepts in 3D modeling software. A Project Development Agreement sets the chosen concept and budget.

steps.title: Collaborate
steps.text: Your designer turns the concept into detailed plans and walks you through cabinetry, countertops, plumbing fixtures, flooring and lighting until construction documents are final.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Materials are received and inspected at RIKB's facility, you meet the installation crew, and trained craftspeople complete the work in your home.

service_area.h2: Remodeling across Rhode Island and just over the line
service_area.text: The design center sits on Jefferson Boulevard in Warwick, and the crews work throughout Rhode Island, southeastern Massachusetts and eastern Connecticut. Recent project photos come from Providence's East Side, East Greenwich, Bristol, Barrington, Warren, Portsmouth, Newport, Tiverton, Narragansett, North Kingstown, Glocester and Burrillville. Over the years the team has remodeled many historic and coastal homes, keeping character details and choosing durable materials.

faq.h2: Common questions for the RIKB design team

items.q: Do you work outside Rhode Island?
items.a: Yes. RIKB serves homeowners throughout Rhode Island, southeastern Massachusetts and eastern Connecticut from the Warwick design center. It is licensed in all three states: Rhode Island Reg. #3984, Massachusetts #164199 and Connecticut HIC.0673137. Call to confirm your town falls inside the service area.

items.q: How long will my remodel take?
items.a: It depends on size and scope. Smaller projects may take just a few weeks, and larger renovations or additions take longer. Because design and product selections are final before work begins, delays stay low. One client wrote that a complete kitchen was finished in the promised three and a half weeks.

items.q: What does the warranty cover?
items.a: Every project is guaranteed for five full years under RIKB's Quality Assurance and Five-Year Workmanship Warranty. That is on top of manufacturer warranties on many installed products. RIKB also carries liability insurance up to $2 million per project and workers' compensation for every staff member.

items.q: Can you remodel an older or coastal home?
items.a: Yes. The team has remodeled many historic and character-filled homes, keeping the architectural details while updating how the rooms work. It has also finished projects in coastal communities, where it chooses durable materials and plans layouts around natural light and water views.

items.q: Can I visit the design center first?
items.a: Please do. The 3,000+ square foot design center at 139 Jefferson Boulevard is open weekdays 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Saturdays 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., with off-hours appointments on request. RIKB also hosts complimentary remodeling seminars there, and you can book a virtual consultation.

final_cta.text: Call to book a consultation, in person on Jefferson Boulevard or virtually with a design consultant.

intro.h2: Small team, direct line to the owner
paragraphs: A+ Custom Builders handles bathroom remodeling in Seekonk, MA and the towns along the Massachusetts and Rhode Island line. Founder Greg DeSilva started the company in January 2018 after years in commercial construction in Boston. The work is done by his in-house team, not handed off to outside crews.

Homeowners who review A+ keep naming the same things: steady communication with Greg, a clean and respectful crew, and bathrooms that come out beautiful. Before you even book a visit, you can run the online cost calculator to see a ballpark range for your project, with no salesperson and no credit card.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Seekonk, MA and more

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Full bathroom renovations, master baths and guest half baths. Popular requests include walk-in tiled showers with glass enclosures, double vanities, heated tile floors and freestanding soaking tubs. Recent work includes a Swansea master bath on Dillon Lane and an Edgewood guest bath in Seekonk.

items.name: Decks, Patios and Pavilions

faq.h2: Common questions for A+ Custom Builders

items.q: Can I see a price before anyone comes to my house?
items.a: Yes. The cost calculator on the A+ site gives you a ballpark range for your bathroom, kitchen, basement or outdoor project in a few minutes. No credit card is needed. It asks for your contact details at the end, and A+ promises not to spam you with emails or calls.

items.q: Is the quote free?
items.a: Yes. A+ offers a free quote and estimate. Fill out the short form, or call or text Greg's office at (401) 225-7875. The website lists hours of Monday through Sunday, 7am to 6pm, so you can reach the team on weekends too.

items.q: Who actually does the work?
items.a: An in-house A+ team. The company says it does not outsource the work, so the crew you meet is the crew that builds. Greg DeSilva stays involved, and Google reviewers describe him answering questions and concerns throughout their bathroom remodels.

items.q: What do Seekonk homeowners ask for in a new bathroom?
items.a: The most requested upgrades A+ sees are walk-in tiled showers with glass enclosures, double vanities, heated tile floors, freestanding soaking tubs, better lighting and ventilation, and custom linen storage or shelving. The team helps you pick tile, vanities and fixtures during the design step.

items.q: Do you work in Rhode Island?
items.a: Yes. Besides Seekonk, Rehoboth and the South Coast, A+ serves East Providence and Barrington, and its kitchen portfolio includes a remodel in Warren, Rhode Island. On the Massachusetts side, finished projects in Swansea and Westport show how far along the South Coast the crew already works.

seo.og_title: AZ New Bath: family-run bath and shower remodels from Peoria to Prescott
seo.og_description: Brothers Jon and Jeremy Sands have remodeled Arizona bathrooms since 2007, with low-maintenance porcelain, quick installs and a lifetime warranty.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling Peoria AZ: Most Showers Done in 1 to 2 Days
hero.subheadline: AZ New Bath is a licensed, brother-run contractor that does bathrooms only. Most shower remodels take 1 to 2 days, you keep running water and a toilet throughout, and every remodel carries a lifetime warranty.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Peoria AZ: marble-look porcelain slab walls, wood double vanity, oval mirrors and brass sconces

intro.h2: Bathrooms are the whole business
paragraphs: AZ New Bath is a general contractor that does one job only: the bathroom remodeling Peoria AZ homeowners call about, from a single shower to a full overhaul. Crews also work across the Valley and up to Prescott and Sedona. Brothers Jon and Jeremy Sands started the company in 2007 and still answer calls, write estimates, source materials and install.

Their focus is materials that stand up to Arizona heat and hard water and take little scrubbing, such as large porcelain slabs with fewer grout lines. Jobs move fast. A shower remodel averages 1 to 2 days, and the company promises it will never leave you without running water or a toilet. One reviewer summed it up as an "amazing family company."

services.h2: Bath and shower remodels from the Peoria crew

items.name: Full Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: A complete overhaul from the first sketch to the final touches: tubs and showers, flooring, vanities, mirrors, medicine cabinets and lighting. Design consultants help pick every piece, down to the tile and showerheads. The company's own schedules put a complete primary bath at around two weeks.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel in Arizona with a freestanding tub, glass shower with bench seat and white double vanities

items.name: Shower Remodels
items.blurb: New wall surfaces, fixtures, niches and glass, installed clean and dust-free. Depending on size and scope, a shower can be finished in as little as one day, and the average is 1 to 2 days. All products used carry a lifetime warranty.

image.alt: Shower remodel with white marble-look porcelain walls, a hex mosaic accent stripe, niche and matte black rain head

items.name: Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: The old tub comes out and a walk-in shower goes in, built to your layout and finishes. It frees up floor space and removes the step-over that makes tubs risky for anyone with limited mobility. AZ New Bath handles everything from removal to the finished shower.

image.alt: Before and after of a tub-to-shower conversion by AZ New Bath in the Phoenix area

items.name: Porcelain Installation
items.blurb: Large porcelain slabs for shower walls, floors and vanity tops give a high-end look with fewer grout lines to clean. Buying directly from suppliers, without middlemen, keeps the price competitive, and the team helps you match slabs to your style and budget.

image.alt: Porcelain slab shower in white and gray veining with a frameless glass panel, handheld shower and patterned tile floor

items.name: Accessible Walk-In Showers
items.blurb: Walk-in showers and walk-in tubs for seniors and anyone with mobility needs, with options such as ramps, folding seats, grab bars and easy wheelchair access. Each one is still fully custom, so safety features sit inside a bathroom that looks finished rather than clinical.

image.alt: Accessible walk-in shower with a fold-down seat, black grab bar, recessed niche and pebble tile floor

why_choose_us.h2: Why West Valley homeowners call AZ New Bath

items.title: You keep a working bathroom
items.text: The company states it will never leave you without running water or a toilet. Most shower jobs wrap up in 1 to 2 days, so the disruption is short.

items.title: Lifetime warranty, satisfaction promised
items.text: Every remodel comes with a lifetime warranty on products and services. The team says it will keep working with you until you are 100% happy with the result.

items.title: Samples come to your home
items.text: A Google reviewer wrote that Wayne explained everything, showed the options and "had samples with him in person," which made picking the shower much easier.

items.title: Price match and 0% financing
items.text: AZ New Bath offers a price match guarantee and 0% financing, with transparent pricing and no hidden fees. Inquiries get a reply within 24 hours.

about.h2: Two brothers, one trade, since 2007
about.text: Jonathan Sands and his brother Jeremy started AZ New Bath during the 2007 recession. They saw that tile and cultured marble looked good at first but were hard to keep clean, so they built the business around low-maintenance products at a fair price. Jon is the owner and licensed contractor, and the brothers still work in the business every day. Evelyn Johnson schedules your consultation, design consultants Jay and Wayne guide selections, and installers like Chris and Daniel do the build.

image.alt: Jonathan Sands, owner and licensed contractor at AZ New Bath in Peoria, AZ

process.h2: How your bathroom gets done

steps.title: Call or request a quote
steps.text: Evelyn sets up your free, no-obligation in-home consultation. The team aims to answer every inquiry within 24 hours.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.text: A consultant looks at the space and helps pick the right materials and products for how you use the bathroom and what you want to spend.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: Jay or Wayne brings samples and maps out the layout, from tile and porcelain to showerheads, lighting and storage.

steps.title: Order
steps.text: Materials are ordered directly from suppliers. Choosing items that are in stock helps keep the schedule short.

steps.title: Installation
steps.text: Jon and the install crew build the bathroom, keep the work area clean and do a final inspection before handing it back.

items.q: How long will my bathroom remodel take?
items.a: It depends on scope. AZ New Bath says shower remodels average 1 to 2 days and can be done in as little as one day. In an October 2026 post built from its own project schedules, the company put a complete primary bathroom remodel at around two weeks. Moving plumbing or special-order materials can add time.

items.q: Will I be without a working bathroom?
items.a: No. The company states that it will never leave you without running water or a toilet during a remodel. Crews also keep the work area clean as they go, and the site notes that its renovations are safe for pets. That makes it easier to stay in your home while the work is done.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: AZ New Bath offers a lifetime warranty on all of its remodels, covering products and services. It also guarantees satisfaction and says it will work with you until you are 100% happy. The company is licensed, bonded and insured under Arizona ROC #264481.

items.q: Do you offer financing or price matching?
items.a: Yes. The company's Phoenix bathroom remodel page lists 0% financing and a price match guarantee, along with transparent pricing and no hidden fees. Your quote is free and comes with no obligation, so you can compare it with other contractors before you decide.

items.q: Can you make a shower safer for an older parent?
items.a: Yes. AZ New Bath often installs walk-in showers and walk-in tubs with accessibility features for seniors and people with disabilities. Options include ramps, folding seats and easy wheelchair access. A tub-to-shower conversion removes the high step into the tub, which lowers the risk of a slip.

hero.eyebrow: Largo, FL · Prices posted up front
hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Largo, FL, With the Price on the Page
hero.subheadline: Owner Justin Eichler runs a family-owned design-build company that orders your cabinets before demolition and gives you one project manager from first call to final walkthrough. Kitchens start at $28,000.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Largo FL: white shaker cabinets with copper pulls, white quartz counters, black marble-look floor tile and stainless appliances

intro.h2: Built for homeowners who were burned before
paragraphs: Bayshore Remodels offers kitchen remodeling in Largo, FL and across Pinellas, Hillsborough and Pasco counties from its office on Starkey Road. The company was set up for people who have been burned by a contractor: a deposit and then progress payments, a written scope broken out by trade, and changes approved in writing before extra work starts.

Prices are public. A small kitchen starts at $28,000, a full kitchen at $36,000 and a hall bath at $15,500. Bayshore also tells you when it is not the right fit. If you need only one trade, like an interior paint job, Justin will refer a sub he trusts.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Largo, FL and four more ways to update

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: You approve detailed renderings first, then your cabinets are delivered before demolition so the room never sits gutted. Most small kitchens run $28k to $36k and take 3 to 5 weeks on site; semi-custom to custom kitchens run $50k to $85k and up.

image.alt: Opened-up Largo kitchen remodel with white shaker cabinets, white quartz counters and wide-plank vinyl floors

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Hall baths from $15,500, tub-to-shower conversions from $23,000 and primary baths from $32,000. Fixtures and materials are on site before demolition, a 3D rendering comes first, and most bathrooms take 2 to 4 weeks once work starts.

image.alt: Belleair bathroom with walnut vanity, white quartz top, brass faucet and a blue tile walk-in shower with hex mosaic floor

items.name: Cabinet Refacing
items.blurb: New shaker, raised-panel, flat or beadboard doors and drawer fronts on the cabinet boxes you already have, with soft-close hinges and drawer slides standard. A medium kitchen usually lands at $10k to $12.5k, and most are done in 5 to 7 working days.

image.alt: Kitchen refaced with Delft blue shaker doors, white counters and a breakfast bar that looks out to the pool

items.name: Cabinet Refinishing
items.blurb: Doors and drawers go to a dedicated spray shop for a water-based commercial-grade coating while your kitchen is sealed off with dust barriers and air scrubbers. Smaller kitchens start at $5,000, and you keep a custom touch-up bottle for later.

image.alt: Refinished kitchen with an Indigo Baltic island, cream perimeter cabinets, butcher-block counter and blue patterned tile

items.name: Whole Home Remodeling
items.blurb: Kitchen, baths, floors, paint and built-ins on one contract and one schedule, with permits and inspections handled by the team. Full remodels start at $150,000. The flagship Belleair Beach renovation covered 1,950 square feet for $255,000.

image.alt: Whole-home remodel with open white kitchen, navy island, vaulted great room and new light vinyl plank floors

why_choose_us.h2: Why Pinellas homeowners pick Bayshore

items.title: Materials before demolition
items.text: Cabinets, tile and fixtures are ordered and on the way before anything is torn out, so your kitchen never sits gutted while you wait for a delivery truck.

items.title: Your estimate is the price
items.text: Written estimates are free, broken out by trade and good for 30 days. If crews find rot or bad wiring, they stop, show you and price it in writing first.

items.title: Warranty in writing
items.text: One year on remodeling labor and workmanship, two years on interior and exterior painting, and a touch-up visit within 30 days of completion. Products carry the manufacturer warranty.

items.title: Specialists for every stage
items.text: Demolition, licensed plumbing, licensed electrical, drywall, tile, cabinet install, countertops and paint are each done by someone with at least 10 years in that one trade.

about.h2: Justin Eichler and a promise to his dad
about.text: Justin Eichler grew up in a small town as his dad's right-hand man, and the two of them talked about starting a remodeling business one day. After his father passed away, Justin focused on making that shared plan real. Bayshore Remodels has served Tampa Bay since 2021 and lists more than 200 completed projects. It is family owned and run on plain rules: tell the truth, price fairly and keep your word. The company also supports Rescue Dogs Dream, an all-volunteer dog rescue from Justin's hometown.

image.alt: Justin Eichler, owner of Bayshore Remodels in Largo, FL

process.h2: How a Bayshore project runs

steps.title: A quick call
steps.text: The office calls or texts within one business day to hear what you want to change, your timeline and a ballpark budget.

steps.title: Free consultation at home
steps.text: A free 30-minute visit with the owner to measure the space, check what is behind the work and talk through your options.

steps.title: Written estimate
steps.text: Broken out by trade and good for 30 days. Smaller jobs usually get one within a day; design projects take a few days.

steps.title: Design, select, order
steps.text: Every kitchen gets a 3D rendering, and bathrooms can too. All selections are made and materials confirmed before any work starts.

steps.title: Build and walkthrough
steps.text: Specialists handle each stage in order. Then you walk the room together, close out the punch list and get the warranty in writing.

service_area.h2: Where Bayshore works around Tampa Bay
service_area.text: The office is at 2101 Starkey Rd in Largo, in the middle of Pinellas County. Crews work across Pinellas, Hillsborough and Pasco, from St. Petersburg and Clearwater north to Wesley Chapel and Lutz, plus Belleair and the beach towns. Select Sarasota and Lakewood Ranch projects are taken on when the job makes sense. Not sure your street qualifies? Call and the office will tell you.

faq.h2: Straight answers for Largo homeowners

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Largo?
items.a: Bayshore's published ranges: a small kitchen in the existing layout runs $28k to $36k, a full kitchen with new flooring $36k to $50k, and semi-custom to custom work $50k to $85k and up. Cabinets and counters are included; appliances, light fixtures and faucets are your selections. Your written estimate sets the actual price.

items.q: How long will my bathroom take?
items.a: Once work starts, a hall bathroom takes about 2 to 3 weeks and a primary bathroom 3 to 4 weeks. Permitted projects include inspection days in the schedule. Because the fixtures and tile are on site before demolition, the room is not left torn apart while you wait for parts.

items.q: Should I refinish, reface or remodel my cabinets?
items.a: Refinishing keeps your doors and changes the color, from $5,000. Refacing puts new doors and drawer fronts on the boxes you already have, from $7,000, and runs about $2,000 to $2,500 more than refinishing on a medium kitchen. If the layout has to change, a full remodel is the better fit.

items.q: What happens if you find a problem behind the wall?
items.a: Rot behind a dishwasher, two layers of old flooring or wiring that is not to code turn up on plenty of remodels. When the crew finds something, they stop, show you and price it in writing before any extra work happens. Every change is approved in writing first.

items.q: Can I supply my own materials?
items.a: Yes. Your own tile, vanity, faucets or fixtures are welcome, as long as they are on site before the trades need them. Bathroom starting prices cover the work, and most of what you pick out is budgeted separately as your selections, so you can see both numbers clearly.

final_cta.h2: Get a real number for your kitchen
final_cta.text: Call (813) 489-1552 or send the short form. The office replies within one business day to set up your free 30-minute consultation.

intro.h2: Planned with military precision, designed by Carol
paragraphs: C&S Remodeling has handled bathroom remodeling in San Antonio since Scott and Carol Kressner started the company in 2015. It is still family-owned and family-run today, and it is both veteran-owned and woman-owned.

Scott's military and IT background shapes the schedule and the job site, while Carol leads design. Design, 3D renderings, plumbing, electrical and finish work all stay inside one company, so the crew builds from the same plan you approved on screen. Google reviewers mention bathroom and primary bathroom remodels more than any other type of job, and recent owner replies credit Scott, Carol and Joe by name.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in San Antonio, plus kitchens and additions

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Full bathroom rebuilds handled in-house, from demolition and rough-in plumbing and electrical to waterproofing, tile and fixtures. A typical mid-range bath takes two to four weeks. C&S lists budget updates at $8,000 to $15,000, mid-range remodels at $15,000 to $35,000 and luxury rebuilds above $35,000.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel in San Antonio with a black-framed glass shower, marble-look wall tile and a wood shaker vanity

items.name: Walk-In Showers and Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: Dated tubs come out for custom walk-in showers, or stay as freestanding tubs and combined tub-shower units. Primary bath remodels often add multiple shower heads, dual vanities and heated floors, and the waterproofing is done with San Antonio's humidity in mind.

image.alt: Walk-in shower in a San Antonio bathroom remodel with marble-look porcelain walls, matte black fixtures and a glass block window

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: C&S kitchen remodels run from roughly $25,000 for a small kitchen to $85,000, and full renovations usually take four to eight weeks. Quartz is the most requested countertop. Every kitchen starts with an in-home visit and an itemized written estimate before any work is scheduled.

image.alt: San Antonio kitchen remodel with flat-panel white cabinets, a veined quartz waterfall island, blue glass backsplash and black range hood

items.name: Custom Cabinets and Vanities
items.blurb: C&S builds its own cabinets, so it also takes cabinet-only jobs, from refacing to full replacement. The in-house shop means two to six weeks of lead time, one team that measures, builds and installs, and a protective topcoat on every bathroom cabinet to handle humidity.

image.alt: Custom navy bathroom vanity with brass pulls, white quartz top and round mirror built by C&S Remodeling in San Antonio

items.name: Whole-Home Remodeling and Additions
items.blurb: For bigger plans, the same team handles whole-home renovations and additions such as family rooms, sunrooms and in-law suites, keeping design, construction, plumbing and electrical under one company. One recent client hired C&S to remodel large parts of a first home before moving in.

image.alt: Open living area in a whole-home remodel by C&S Remodeling with wood-look floors and a two-story wall of windows

why_choose_us.h2: Why homeowners pick Scott and Carol's crew

items.title: See it before it's built
items.text: Complimentary 3D renderings come with every remodeling project, so you can compare layouts, materials and features while changes still happen on a screen instead of on your walls.

items.title: Prices you can plan around
items.text: C&S publishes real cost ranges for bathrooms and kitchens and starts every job with a detailed written estimate. One reviewer chose C&S after comparing several San Antonio bids.

items.title: One connected team
items.text: Design, carpentry, plumbing, electrical and finish work stay with one company, so the people building your bathroom work from the plan you approved, not someone else's notes.

items.title: Owners close to the work
items.text: Scott and Carol are part of the team you hire. Scott's military and IT training keeps schedules honest, and Carol works with you directly on vanity, cabinet and tile choices.

about.h2: Meet founders Scott and Carol Kressner
about.text: Scott and Carol Kressner founded C&S Remodeling in 2015, and the business is still family-owned and family-run. Scott brings a military and IT background to project management, which shows in organized job sites and timelines that hold. Carol brings the design eye, working with homeowners on vanity styles, cabinet finishes and tile so the technical work serves a room that feels personal. Together they lead a veteran-owned and woman-owned company from an office on Poss Road in San Antonio. Their cabinet shop builds the boxes in-house, and the blog answers practical questions, such as whether a bathroom can be remodeled in one week.

image.alt: C&S Remodeling team photo in San Antonio, TX

process.h2: Four steps from first visit to final walkthrough

steps.title: Free consultation
steps.text: The team visits your home, measures the space and talks through what works, what doesn't, your style and the scope you have in mind.

steps.title: Design and 3D rendering
steps.text: Carol and the design team develop the plan and a complimentary 3D rendering, so you can test layouts and materials before anything is ordered.

steps.title: Construction by one team
steps.text: Once you approve the design, C&S runs demolition, rough-in, waterproofing, tile and finishes with one coordinated crew and a clear timeline.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: You walk the finished space with the team and review every detail. If something needs attention later, C&S returns at your request.

faq.h2: Bathroom remodel questions we hear in San Antonio

items.q: How many weeks will my bathroom be out of service?
items.a: Most San Antonio bathroom remodels take two to four weeks. A typical mid-range job moves through demolition, rough-in plumbing and electrical, waterproofing and tile, then lighting, mirrors, hardware and a final quality check. Larger or custom bathrooms can take longer, and you get a clear timeline during planning.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost with C&S?
items.a: C&S publishes its ranges: about $8,000 to $15,000 for budget updates like a new vanity, toilet and lighting, $15,000 to $35,000 for mid-range remodels with new tile and a custom vanity, and beyond $35,000 for luxury rebuilds. Every project starts with a detailed written estimate and a complimentary 3D rendering.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. C&S partners with several financing providers to offer flexible payment options for bathroom and kitchen remodels. Ask about current terms during your free consultation, and the team will help you find a plan that fits your budget before any work is scheduled.

items.q: Can you fix mold or water damage during a remodel?
items.a: Yes, and a remodel is the right time to do it. C&S works with licensed remediation specialists when needed, then installs moisture barriers and ventilation correctly so the problem does not come back. San Antonio's humidity makes careful waterproofing especially important behind shower walls.

items.q: Are the 3D renderings really included?
items.a: Yes. Every remodeling project includes complimentary 3D renderings at no added cost. They let you compare layouts, materials and features before construction starts and give you, the designer and the crew one shared picture to work from. Detailed selections still come later, but the big decisions get made on screen.

final_cta.text: Call (210) 485-5424 or schedule a free consultation, and the C&S team will visit, measure and talk through your bathroom, kitchen or addition.

intro.h2: Old house nerds with a design-build plan
paragraphs: Kitchen remodeling in Portland gets tricky when the house is a hundred years old. Rooms are small, walls hide surprises, and the trim is worth saving. Craftsman Design and Renovation has spent over 25 years on exactly these homes, from Laurelhurst bungalows to a 1940 Tudor near Mt Tabor.

The team calls itself a group of old house nerds who geek out on original woodwork and the perfect rafter tail. On a 1902 kitchen in Northwest Portland, they replicated stained wood, v-groove wainscot and leaded glass transoms, then set a soapstone counter at the center. The goal on every job is the same: a room that works for today and looks like it was always there.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Portland, plus baths, basements and additions

items.name: Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: After a design agreement, the designers draft concept drawings so you can see the layout and how your budget is spent before building starts. Most kitchens include custom cabinetry and shelving, new counters and flooring, a decorative backsplash, and new overhead and task lighting.

image.alt: 1913 Hawthorne kitchen remodel in Portland with blue painted cabinets, quartzite countertops, skylight and stainless range

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: New fixtures, glass shower enclosures, vanities and counters, custom cabinetry, flooring, lighting, and upgrades to ventilation and plumbing. The team drafts the plans, sources unusual materials when a period look calls for them, and handles the carpentry and finish work itself.

image.alt: 1910 Kings Hill bathroom in Portland with pedestal sink, recessed medicine cabinet, white subway tile and black-and-white mosaic border

items.name: Whole House Remodels
items.blurb: A study of your home and nearby houses from the same era guides the design, so every room reads as one whole. Work can happen all at once or in phases, with each phase planned so it sets up the next.

image.alt: 1916 Richmond Craftsman whole house remodel in Portland with sage green cabinets, wood-trimmed windows and a farmhouse sink

items.name: Basement Remodels
items.blurb: Turn a laundry and storage level into a family room, office, guest suite, wine cellar or extra bathroom. The design keeps the new space in step with the rest of your older home while adding the square footage you need.

image.alt: 1950 Laurelhurst Rambler basement remodel with stone fireplace wall, teal sofa, recessed lights and daylight windows

items.name: Additions and Exteriors
items.blurb: Bump-outs, sunrooms, porches, garages and full additions designed to look original to the house, with siding, trim and rooflines matched to the era. Award-winning examples include a 1935 Tudor Revival sunroom and a 1906 Craftsman addition.

image.alt: 1906 SE Portland cottage addition with green siding, covered front porch and restored foursquare roofline

why_choose_us.h2: Proof from the trade and from neighbors

items.title: A long run of NARI awards
items.text: NARI Contractor of the Year awards for kitchens in 2015, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023, and the 2025 NARI Remodeler of the Year for the 1911 Modern English Kitchen.

items.title: Fixed-cost construction agreement
items.text: Selections, drawings and the Health and Safety Plan are approved before you sign a fixed-cost construction agreement, so the price is set before the crew arrives.

items.title: Lead carpenter you talk to weekly
items.text: Your lead carpenter meets with you each week on status and schedule. The work area is sealed off from the house and left broom clean every day.

items.title: Guildmaster for service
items.text: Guild Quality named the firm a Guildmaster in 2017 and every year from 2019 to 2023, based on client surveys about service.

about.h2: From an attic office to SE 27th Avenue
about.text: Wade Frietag started Craftsman Design and Renovation in the attic of his 1905 Craftsman home, out of a love for Portland's historic houses. The firm moved to SE Division Street in 2004, above Rejuvenation on SE Grand in 2012, and to SE Belmont in 2015. Today Bill Myles, a Certified Remodeler, owns the company. His team includes designers Erika Rice and Stephanie Capretto, both CKBD, project manager Ryan Murphy and lead carpenters Pete Kelly and Nathan Maszy, both CLC. Clients have called them forensic architects for the way they read an old house.

image.alt: Bill Myles, owner of Craftsman Design and Renovation in Portland, OR

service_area.h2: Where in Portland we remodel
service_area.text: The office is at 837 SE 27th Ave, in the middle of the older neighborhoods the team loves most. Their project list runs through Mt Tabor, North Tabor, Laurelhurst, Hawthorne, Richmond, Sellwood, Eastmoreland, Irvington, Alameda, Grant Park, Rose City and Northwest Portland, with award-winning work in Lake Oswego and Raleigh Hills. If your house was built before most of your neighbors were born, call and ask.

faq.h2: Common questions about remodeling an older Portland home

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel with you usually cost?
items.a: The firm's FAQ page lists kitchen remodels in the $150,000 to $250,000 range. Your number depends on scope, structure and finishes. A flexible design retainer and a realistic target budget come first, then a preliminary estimate during design and a fixed-cost construction agreement before building starts.

items.q: Will my remodel match the rest of my 1910s house?
items.a: That is the core of the work. On a 1902 kitchen the team replicated stained wood, v-groove wainscot and leaded glass transoms. For whole houses, they compare your home with others built in the same era to guide the design, then blend in what you need today.

items.q: Are you licensed in Oregon?
items.a: Yes. Craftsman Design and Renovation is registered with the Oregon Construction Contractors Board as CCB#131520. Owner Bill Myles holds the Certified Remodeler designation, two designers are Certified Kitchen and Bath Designers, and two lead carpenters are Certified Lead Carpenters. Ask to see the registration before you sign.

items.q: Can we live at home during construction?
items.a: Many clients do. The construction area is sealed off to cut noise and dust in the rest of the house, the site is left broom clean at the end of every workday, and staff follow a written Health and Safety Plan that you review before the contract.

items.q: How do I start?
items.a: Call (503) 239-6200 or request a consultation online. The first meeting can be in your home or online, and it is a chance for both sides to see if the project is a good fit before you sign a design agreement.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Santa Barbara, Designed and Built In-House
hero.subheadline: Founder Jerry Jaimes and a team of nearly 20 designers, tradespeople and project managers handle your remodel from first sketch to final cleaning. You get one point of contact, not a string of subcontractors.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Santa Barbara: Italian Villa style kitchen with maple cabinets in a warm Amaretto finish, quartzite island with seating, wood ceiling beams and glass pendants

intro.h2: One plan and one team for your Santa Barbara remodel
paragraphs: ELITE Remodels offers kitchen remodeling in Santa Barbara the way a good hotel runs a stay: one team looks after everything. Designers, material selection, permits, construction and professional cleaning all sit under one roof at the design center on Las Positas Road. One person at ELITE stays your contact from start to finish.

Their tagline sums up what clients are buying: no chasing contractors, no surprise costs, no chaos in your home. Past clients from Hope Ranch to Solvang say their kitchens came in on time and on budget, and many come back for a bathroom next. On Google the firm holds 4.9 stars across 165 reviews.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths and the rooms around them

items.name: Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: Full kitchen design and build, from moving appliances and adding walk-in pantries to cabinetry, stone counters, tile, plumbing and electrical. Styles range from Modern Mediterranean and Santa Barbara Spanish to Mid-Century Modern and Modern Farmhouse. You see the design rendered before construction starts.

image.alt: Modern Mediterranean kitchen in Santa Barbara with arched marble range alcove, light oak cabinets, white stone island and leather counter stools

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Bathrooms taken past a finish update into a calm, spa-like room: new layout where it helps, walk-in showers, tubs, tile, vanities, lighting and plumbing. Google reviewers mention bathroom remodels more than any other project, including primary baths and a guest bath done in true Santa Barbara Spanish style.

image.alt: Santa Barbara bathroom remodel with charcoal gray vanity, white counter, matte black wall faucets and frameless glass shower with gray subway tile

items.name: REFRESH by ELITE
items.blurb: For cosmetic and finish-level work that wraps up in weeks, not months: partial kitchen or bath refreshes, tub-to-shower conversions, new counters and backsplashes, cabinet refacing and vanity swaps. Same designers, same craftspeople and the same 5-year craftsmanship warranty as a full remodel.

image.alt: Recessed shower niche with blue and cream patterned tile framed by tan stacked tile in a Santa Barbara bathroom

items.name: Built-ins, Fireplaces and Additions
items.blurb: The team goes beyond the kitchen and bath when a home needs it: built-in cabinetry and shelving, fireplace surrounds, closet systems, laundry rooms, new flooring and additions. A Goleta couple had ELITE handle construction, flooring and painting alongside their kitchen, two baths and fireplaces.

image.alt: Walnut floating shelves beside white cabinetry with blue accent tile in a Santa Barbara kitchen remodel

why_choose_us.h2: Why Santa Barbara County homeowners pick ELITE

items.title: Everything under one roof
items.text: Design, materials, planning and construction stay with one in-house team. One client said everything was decided, purchased and in place before demolition, so the build ran smoothly from demo to finish.

items.title: A showroom you can walk into
items.text: The design center at 2267 Las Positas Rd is open weekdays and Saturdays. You can touch finishes, meet a designer and see your plan before anything is ordered.

items.title: Covered for five years
items.text: ELITE backs its work with a 5-year craftsmanship warranty, and its craftsmen are insured and bonded. The warranty applies to smaller REFRESH projects as well as full design-build remodels.

items.title: Clients come back
items.text: Several past clients started with a bathroom and hired ELITE again for the kitchen right after. Google reviewers point to the designers, the friendly crew and tile work.

about.h2: Meet founder Jerry Jaimes and the ELITE designers
about.text: Jerry Jaimes started ELITE nearly 20 years ago as a small home-repair business and grew it into a full design-and-build firm. A stay at a five-star hotel, where every staff member focused on service, shaped what he calls a concierge approach to remodeling. Today his in-house team of nearly 20 includes designers, licensed tradespeople and project managers. Designer Grace Gambetta is a fifth-generation Santa Barbara native who grew up on her father's job sites. Designer Jane spent nearly 20 years in custom wood flooring and specializes in custom cabinet design.

image.alt: Portrait of Jerry Jaimes not used; no clearly labeled owner photo on the site

steps.title: Reach out
steps.text: Call, send the project form or drop by the showroom. The team replies to online requests within one business day.

steps.title: Design your space
steps.text: A designer starts with your goals and shows you the finished room on screen before construction begins.

steps.title: Choose and order everything
steps.text: Pick cabinets, stone, tile and fixtures at the design center so materials are bought and ready before demolition.

steps.title: Build and clean up
steps.text: The insured, bonded in-house crew handles permits through construction and finishes with a professional cleaning.

service_area.h2: Serving Santa Barbara, the coast and the Santa Ynez Valley
service_area.text: ELITE works across Santa Barbara County, from Carpinteria and Summerland up through Montecito, Hope Ranch and Goleta, and over the pass to Solvang, Santa Ynez, Los Olivos and Buellton. Recent projects include kitchens on the Mesa, the Riviera and in San Roque. The design center is in Santa Barbara, so most clients stop in to choose tile, stone and cabinet finishes in person.

faq.h2: Common questions about remodeling with ELITE

items.q: Will I be juggling a designer and a builder on my own?
items.a: No. ELITE's in-house team covers design, materials, project management and construction. A single ELITE contact guides you from the opening sketch through the last cleanup, so there is no chasing separate trades or passing messages between a designer and a builder.

items.q: Is REFRESH by ELITE or a full remodel right for me?
items.a: REFRESH covers cosmetic and finish-level work like new counters, backsplashes, vanities or a tub-to-shower conversion. If your project moves walls, changes the layout, adds square footage or needs construction drawings, a full design-build remodel is the better fit. Schedule a consultation and the team will tell you which one.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: ELITE provides a 5-year craftsmanship warranty. It applies to full design-build remodels and to smaller REFRESH projects alike. The craftsmen who do the work are part of ELITE's own insured and bonded in-house team rather than outside crews brought in for your job.

items.q: Can I visit the showroom?
items.a: Yes. The design center is at 2267 Las Positas Rd in Santa Barbara. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm and Saturday from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. Dropping in is a good way to meet a designer and see finishes before you plan.

items.q: Will my remodel stay on budget?
items.a: Staying on budget is the point clients raise most in their testimonials. Kitchens in Summerland, on the Riviera and in Rancho Embarcadero came in on budget, and one owner said there were no surprises. Planning and buying materials before demolition is a big part of how the team keeps costs steady.

final_cta.h2: Bring your ideas to the design center
final_cta.text: Call (805) 869-2391 or fill in the project form; ELITE answers online requests within one business day.
