seo.og_title: Kitchen Remodeling in Homewood, AL | ELM Construction LLC
seo.og_description: One team, one plan, one contract: design-build kitchens, baths and basements from Homewood's ELM Construction, founded in 2008.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Homewood from One Design-Build Team
hero.subheadline: ELM Construction designs, prices and builds your kitchen under one contract, led by founder Elliott Pike, the 2023 NAHB Remodeler of the Year.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Homewood design-build firm ELM Construction: Indian Springs kitchen with a long dark wood island, white upholstered stools, brass pendants and an arched range hood

intro.h2: Kitchen Remodeling in Homewood, Designed and Built Under One Roof
paragraphs: ELM Construction has handled kitchen remodeling in Homewood and the Over the Mountain towns since 2008. The firm is design-build: the same company draws your plans, picks finishes with you, checks your wiring and plumbing with its trade partners, and runs construction. One team, one plan, one contract.

That setup changes how pricing works. After the design and selections phase, ELM hands you a contract with a detailed scope of work and a guaranteed fixed price, so the big decisions are made before demolition. Hank P. put it simply after his master bath: they stayed on schedule and on budget.

services.h2: Kitchens, Baths and the Rest of the House

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full kitchen gut and redesign, often taking down walls or borrowing space from a dining room. ELM's designers plan stone and quartz counters, built-in professional appliances, custom storage and lighting. Past kitchens include Vestavia, Hoover, Mountain Brook, Cahaba Heights and Edgewood projects.

image.alt: Mountain Brook kitchen remodel with white shaker cabinets, dark-topped island, lantern pendants, stainless double ovens and a planked ceiling

items.name: Bathroom Renovations
items.blurb: Primary suites, guest baths, Jack and Jill baths and small-bath makeovers. Projects range from heated floors and freestanding soaking tubs to custom tiled showers and wet rooms. Plumbing can be moved to fit the room you want, not the one the builder left you.

image.alt: Homewood bathroom renovation with frameless glass shower in marble tile, white vanity, scalloped black mirror and brass sconces

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Unfinished or dated basements turned into living space: guest suites, home offices, gyms or a lower-level kitchen. ELM handles water management when needed, new framing, insulation, air conditioning, a bathroom and new flooring, so the space stays dry and usable year round.

image.alt: Vestavia Hills basement renovation with long dark-topped island, natural wood cabinets, open shelving and brass pendant lights

items.name: Additions and Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Upstairs additions, covered porches and outdoor rooms tied into your existing roofline. Recent work includes a Hoover porch with a stacked stone fireplace and outdoor kitchen. ELM also takes on whole-home renovations and restoration work, including fire damage repair.

image.alt: Hoover covered porch with cedar ceiling, stacked stone fireplace with mounted TV, ceiling fans and an outdoor grill station

why_choose_us.h2: Why Homewood Homeowners Hire ELM

items.title: A guaranteed fixed price
items.text: Design and detail come first. Trade partners check your electrical, plumbing and structure, then you sign a contract with a detailed scope and a guaranteed fixed price.

items.title: Two years of written coverage
items.text: ELM backs its work with a written warranty that covers you for two years, which the company notes is double the industry standard.

items.title: Certified kitchen and bath design
items.text: Designer Liz Kennedy holds the Certified Kitchen and Bath Designer (CKBD) credential from NKBA. Reviewers name her for helping them make decisions without feeling overwhelmed by choices.

items.title: Your project online, 24/7
items.text: Every client gets an online job portal with the construction schedule, contracts, payment history, change orders and progress photos, open around the clock.

about.h2: Elliott Pike, Homewood High Grad and Founder
about.text: Elliott Pike and his wife, LeArden, started ELM Construction in 2008. The company prospered through the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression, growing mostly through referrals and repeat clients. Elliott graduated from Homewood High School and Troy University, then worked for a firm that remodeled apartment complexes and a national building materials distributor. He was named the 2023 NAHB Remodeler of the Year and is the 2026 Chair of NAHB Remodelers. He still oversees day-to-day operations, alongside production manager Adam Martz, who joined in 2011.

image.alt: Elliott Pike, founder of ELM Construction in Homewood, AL

process.h2: ELM's Four-Step Design-Build Process

steps.title: Let's Talk
steps.text: Call (205) 273-2773 or fill in the contact form to tell the ELM team about the kitchen, bath or addition you have in mind.

steps.title: Let's Meet
steps.text: A one to two hour discovery meeting in your home, with a real talk about cost and timeline. Everyone with a say should attend.

steps.title: Let's Design and Plan
steps.text: Your space is measured into Chief Architect for floor plans, elevations and 3D renderings, then selections with the designer and a fixed-price contract.

steps.title: Let's Renovate
steps.text: ELM sets the construction schedule, applies for building permits, confirms timing with trade partners and starts work.

service_area.h2: Serving Homewood and the Over the Mountain Communities
service_area.text: ELM works from its office on Oxmoor Circle in Homewood and serves the Over the Mountain communities, including Homewood, Vestavia Hills, Mountain Brook and Hoover, plus the greater Birmingham metro area. Recent portfolio projects include kitchens in Indian Springs, Cahaba Heights and Edgewood, and a whole-house fire damage repair in The Preserve in Hoover. faq.h2: Questions About Remodeling with ELM

items.q: What does a complete kitchen remodel cost with ELM?
items.a: ELM's budgeting guide lists a complete kitchen remodel starting at $125,000. That covers gutting the old kitchen, possibly changing walls and layout, solid wood cabinets with soft-close drawers, quartz counters, new appliances, flooring and recessed lights. The price includes permits, project management, taxes, final inspection and cleaning.

items.q: What does design-build mean for my project?
items.a: Design and construction happen under one roof, with one team, one plan and one contract. ELM measures your space, draws floor plans and 3D renderings, guides your selections and checks existing systems with trade partners, so the design is buildable and priced before work begins.

items.q: Will my price change once construction starts?
items.a: At the end of the design phase, ELM presents a contract with a detailed scope of work and a guaranteed fixed price. Checking electrical, plumbing and structure with trade partners first lowers the chance of big surprises. Changes you request later go through a change order you can see in your online portal.

items.q: Is ELM licensed, insured and covered by a warranty?
items.a: Yes. ELM is licensed by the State of Alabama as a Residential Home Builder and Remodeler (AL Home Builders License #21942) and carries general liability and workers compensation insurance. Its work is backed by a written warranty that covers you for two years.

items.q: What does a primary bathroom remodel cost?
items.a: The budgeting guide lists a master bathroom remodel starting at $95,000. That typically means gutting the room, moving plumbing for the shower, tub, toilet and sinks, new solid wood cabinetry, quartz counters with two undermount sinks, recessed lighting and custom mirrors.

intro.h2: Where the designer and the builder share a last name
paragraphs: Elite Kitchen & Bath has offered luxury kitchen remodeling in Manhasset and across Long Island's North Shore since 1984. It is a design-build firm and a licensed, insured general contractor, so design, engineering, permits, construction and installation all run through one team and one point of contact.

That team is still a family. Yeheskel Sharbani, an electrical engineer, started the company. His son David grew up on its job sites and now leads it as president. Most work comes from referrals and repeat clients, and the owners stay involved in every project, from a new quartz countertop to a full gut kitchen.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths and whole homes, designed and built in-house

items.name: Luxury Kitchen Design-Build
items.blurb: Space planning, custom or semi-custom cabinetry, stone counters, appliance integration and lighting design, then construction by the same team. Popular requests include large entertaining islands, walk-in pantries, coffee and beverage stations and smart home features. The firm also designs Kosher kitchens and chef-style cooking spaces.

image.alt: South Shore Long Island open kitchen remodel with walnut-toned cabinets, a long island with counter stools and pendant lights

items.name: Primary Bathrooms
items.blurb: Spa-style primary baths with curbless and steam showers, large-format tile, skylights and wall-hung Italian vanities. Elite handles the plumbing, tile and glass as well as the design, and several of its Great Neck master baths were full extensions of the home rather than simple updates.

image.alt: Great Neck, NY master bath with a curbless steam shower, gray large-format tile and pebble shower floor

items.name: Custom and Imported Cabinetry
items.blurb: American and European cabinetry, including RUTT and Italian lines, plus appliances and finishes from partner manufacturers. Cabinet choices range from semi-custom to fully custom and imported luxury. Built-in wall units, hutches and bars are designed to the inch, and Elite won a Cesar Italian Cabinetry award for outstanding design.

image.alt: Custom white RUTT cabinetry hutch with glass upper doors, marble backsplash and display counter

items.name: Whole-Home, Co-op and Extension Renovations
items.blurb: Full-home remodels, Manhattan co-op apartments, extensions and interior and exterior work, all managed from the Manhasset office. Elite coordinates filing, zoning and permits in-house. Clients have stayed in their apartments during major remodels while the crew kept the work area neat.

image.alt: Whole-floor renovation with a long dining table facing an open kitchen with two islands and wood flooring

service_area.h2: North Shore towns, the Hamptons and Manhattan
service_area.text: The showroom sits at 983 Northern Blvd in Manhasset, just off the LIE at Lakeville Road and Community Drive, with free parking behind the building. From there the team works across Long Island and New York City, from Great Neck and Glen Head to Southampton and Sag Harbor, and in Manhattan co-ops on the Upper East Side, Upper West Side and in Tribeca.

faq.h2: Common questions about a Long Island luxury kitchen

items.q: What does a luxury kitchen remodel cost on Long Island?
items.a: Elite publishes these ranges: a cosmetic update runs about $35,000 to $60,000 and up, a full kitchen renovation $75,000 to $150,000 and up, a luxury custom kitchen $150,000 to $300,000 and up, and estate-level kitchens $300,000 and up. Cabinetry is usually the largest part of the budget.

items.q: Can I walk into the Manhasset showroom?
items.a: Yes. Walk-ins are welcome Tuesday through Saturday. Hours are Tuesday to Friday 10:00 am to 6:00 pm and Saturday 10:00 am to 5:00 pm, with Mondays by appointment and Sundays closed. You can also book a private design consultation at a time that suits you.

items.q: Do I need to hire a designer and a contractor separately?
items.a: No. Elite Kitchen & Bath is the design side and Express Contracting is the licensed, insured builder. Together they handle design, engineering, filing, zoning, permits, construction and installation, so you have one point of contact and one source of accountability for the whole job.

items.q: How do deposits and cabinet orders work?
items.a: After your first meeting you see a preliminary design and budget. If you go ahead, a design retainer is typically due and is often applied toward your cabinetry. Cabinets are ordered only after the final design is approved, generally with a 50% deposit. Appliances must be chosen before that point.

items.q: Do you renovate co-op apartments in Manhattan?
items.a: Yes. Co-ops are part of the firm's regular work, and its service list includes the Upper East Side, Upper West Side, Midtown, Gramercy Park, Soho, Noho and Tribeca. One client's small co-op kitchen was gutted, the sink moved and three kinds of lighting added in about two months.

final_cta.text: Call (516) 365-0595, walk into the Manhasset showroom Tuesday through Saturday, or book a complimentary design consultation.

intro.h2: One bath specialist, one owner on every job
paragraphs: Golden Era Remodel does one thing: bathroom remodeling across Dallas-Fort Worth, run from a shop in Mansfield, TX. Owner Anthony Brown started the company to focus on baths alone. When you call, you reach the person who will manage your project, not a salesperson who hands you to a crew you have never met.

The craft is tile. Showers are built on Schluter, wedi or goboard systems with real cement or epoxy grout, never premixed. You get a detailed written estimate before work begins. If rot or an old leak turns up behind the wall, Anthony stops, shows you what he found and writes a change order before doing more.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling services across Dallas-Fort Worth

items.name: Master Bath Transformations
items.blurb: Full primary baths with custom vanities, tile, lighting, fixtures and flooring, from double vanities to heated floors and soaking tubs. Golden Era handles demo, plumbing, tile and finish work under one contract. A master bath with a walk-in shower and custom tile usually takes 4 to 6 weeks.

image.alt: Master bathroom with dark onyx-look porcelain shower walls, pebble shower floor and a floating double vanity with arched mirrors

items.name: Walk-In and Curbless Showers
items.blurb: Floor-to-ceiling tile, frameless glass, niches, benches and grab-bar blocking on request. Curbless showers get a correct pre-slope, a bonded Schluter membrane and a linear or point drain. Curbless typically adds $1,500 to $4,000 over a curbed build, and most walk-in builds take 1 to 2 weeks.

image.alt: Walk-in shower with large blue-green hexagon wall tile, a recessed niche and a sand-colored tile floor with center drain

items.name: Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: The unused tub comes out and a custom tile walk-in shower goes in, with Schluter waterproofing, new valve, fixtures and drain, and curb or curbless entry. Most conversions run $9,000 to $20,000 and take 1 to 2 weeks, depending on tile, glass and whether plumbing moves.

image.alt: Glass-enclosed walk-in shower with handmade-look beige wall tile, a built-in bench and a raised tiled step

items.name: Custom Tile Installation
items.blurb: Ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite and travertine set with flat layouts and tight grout lines. Golden Era installs shower walls, tub surrounds, large-format and natural stone, herringbone and mosaic patterns, heated tile floors and backsplashes. Full shower tile inside a larger remodel runs about $3,500 to $9,000 or more.

image.alt: Custom tub surround in large-format marble-look porcelain with a long recessed niche and matte black fixtures

why_choose_us.h2: Why DFW homeowners call Anthony

items.title: You deal with the owner
items.text: Anthony writes the estimate, manages the job and is on site for demo, waterproofing, tile layout and the final punch list. There is no rotating crew or project manager filter between you and him.

items.title: Real tile, not acrylic
items.text: Every shower is custom tile on a Schluter, wedi or goboard system with cement or epoxy grout. Google reviewers most often tag tile work, shower rebuilds and master bathroom remodels.

items.title: Prices in writing first
items.text: You get a detailed line-item quote after a free in-home visit. Unexpected problems are photographed and priced on a written change order before any extra work starts.

items.title: A year of workmanship cover
items.text: Golden Era gives a 1-year installation warranty on its workmanship and carries general liability and workers' comp on every job, with certificates of insurance on request.

about.h2: Anthony Brown, the owner who picks up the phone
about.text: Anthony Brown founded Golden Era Remodel to do one thing very well: bathroom remodeling. Working from a shop in Mansfield, Texas, the company has been in business since 2020 and serves two kinds of clients. Golden Standard homeowners in places like Garland, Arlington and Richardson want quality work at a fair, honest price. Golden Luxury homeowners in Frisco, Plano, Southlake and Colleyville want premium stone and flawless finish work. Anthony gives both the same thing: he is on the job site every day and the project is not done until you are happy.

process.h2: How a Golden Era bathroom gets built

steps.title: Free in-home estimate
steps.text: Anthony visits, measures, listens to your goals and sends a detailed written, line-item quote, usually within 48 hours of the visit.

steps.title: Design and materials
steps.text: You pick tile, fixtures and finishes yourself or with help, including visits to tile showrooms, to fit your style and budget.

steps.title: The build
steps.text: Demo, waterproofing, tile and finish work are managed start to finish by the owner, and work does not start until materials are on hand.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: You walk the finished bath together. The job is not called done until you are happy, and the 1-year workmanship warranty begins.

service_area.h2: From Mansfield to every corner of the Metroplex
service_area.text: Golden Era works out of Mansfield and takes bathroom projects within about 45 minutes of the shop, across Tarrant, Dallas, Collin, Denton, Kaufman and Rockwall counties. The site names town pages for Westlake, Colleyville, Allen, Coppell and Flower Mound, where Anthony also handles city permits and HOA submissions when a project needs them. faq.h2: DFW bathroom remodel questions, answered by Golden Era

items.q: Are estimates really free?
items.a: Yes. All in-home consultations and estimates are free and carry no obligation. Call or text (469) 586-6478 to set a time, and evenings and weekends are fine. Anthony measures, talks through your goals and usually sends a detailed line-item quote within 48 hours of the visit.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost in Dallas-Fort Worth?
items.a: Most Golden Era bathroom remodels fall between $15,000 and $45,000. A guest bath refresh with new tile, vanity and fixtures is typically $15,000 to $22,000. A master bath with a walk-in shower, custom tile and stone usually lands at $30,000 to $45,000 or more. Your written quote is line by line.

items.q: How long will my bathroom be out of service?
items.a: A guest bathroom typically takes 2 to 3 weeks once work starts. A master bath with a walk-in shower and custom tile takes 4 to 6 weeks, and a full primary suite with custom millwork or natural stone takes 6 to 8. Work does not begin until all the materials are on hand.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: Golden Era provides a 1-year installation warranty on its workmanship. If something it installed fails because of the craftsmanship, the team comes back and makes it right. Tile, fixtures, cabinets and appliances carry their own manufacturer warranties, which typically range from 1 year to lifetime depending on the product.

items.q: How do payments and financing work?
items.a: You pay a deposit at contract signing, progress payments at set milestones such as demo, rough-in and tile, and the balance on completion. Golden Era accepts credit and debit cards, checks and NFC mobile payments. It does not offer in-house financing but can point you to HELOC and home-improvement loan options.

final_cta.h2: Book a free in-home bathroom estimate
final_cta.text: Call or text Anthony at (469) 586-6478. Evening and weekend visits are fine, and most quotes go out within 48 hours.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Lake Worth Beach, Led by Tristan Dankert

intro.h2: Built down the road on North Federal Highway
paragraphs: H&H Signature Renovations is the owner-led team for bathroom remodeling in Lake Worth Beach, working from 1730 N Federal Hwy. One crew handles demolition, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, cabinetry and finish work, and the same people run the job from day one to the walkthrough. The company takes full renovations only, not small repairs.

Before anyone opens a wall, you get a measured scope and a fixed price, not an allowance that grows later. The team checks whether your home sits in one of the city's six historic districts, handles the permit process and builds any review into the schedule. services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Lake Worth Beach, and the rest of the house

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and powder rooms taken back to the studs. Pan slope, corners and every penetration are waterproofed before tile is set. Fixtures can move, including toilets and shower drains rerouted through the slab, and the crew finishes tile, glass, vanities and trim in house.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel with a freestanding tub, polished marble-look floor, dark vanity and backlit mirrors under a tray ceiling

items.name: Tub-to-Shower Conversion
items.blurb: The tub nobody uses comes out and a walk-in shower goes in. The work covers drain relocation, a new pan with curb or curbless entry, full waterproofing, tile, niche, bench and frameless glass. Grab-bar blocking goes into the wall while it is open.

image.alt: Frameless glass walk-in shower with marble tile and brass fixtures, built where an unused tub used to be

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Layout, cabinetry, countertops, islands, lighting, plumbing and electrical under one crew. Because most county homes sit on a concrete slab, the team checks early whether a sink or island can move. Salt air and humidity shape hardware and cabinet box choices too.

image.alt: Palm Beach Gardens kitchen remodel with white shaker cabinetry, a black quartz waterfall island and a cascading pendant cluster

items.name: Custom Closets and Built-Ins
items.blurb: Closets built as millwork to the opening you have, plus media walls, bookcases, window seats and fireplace surrounds. Wiring and venting are solved before the carpentry closes in. One Google reviewer said a fireplace bookcase with window seats beat the work of dozens of earlier contractors.

image.alt: Open living area with white built-in bar cabinetry, wine storage and a row of glass pendant lights in a Palm Beach County home

why_choose_us.h2: Why Palm Beach County homeowners pick H&H

items.title: A scope, not an allowance

items.title: The owner is on the job

items.title: Local permit know-how

items.title: Insured, with paperwork ready
items.text: H&H is insured in Florida and sends certificates of insurance to condo associations and property managers on request, so building approval does not hold up your start date.

about.text: Tristan Dankert founded H&H Signature Renovations in 2018, though his work in the building trades started well before that. He still owns each project from the first walkthrough to the final reveal, with no string of subcontractors to juggle. His standard is simple: proper waterproofing, quality materials and skilled tile work, finished by a clean crew that protects your home. Reviewers notice. One homeowner watched him renovate her kitchen and her neighbor's at the same time, and another says he was the first contractor recommended to her.

service_area.h2: From Lake Worth Beach to Boca Raton
service_area.text: Every city H&H serves is inside an hour of the shop at 1730 N Federal Hwy, and the team keeps it that way so a question asked on Tuesday gets answered on Tuesday. In Lake Worth Beach that covers downtown and Lake Avenue, the beach and Casino area, Bryant Park and the neighborhoods west toward Lake Osborne. Beyond the city, crews work across Palm Beach County.

faq.h2: Lake Worth Beach bathroom questions, answered

items.q: Is the estimate free?
items.a: Yes. H&H offers a free in-home estimate with no obligation. The team walks the bathroom, measures it and talks through what is not working. You then get a written scope and a fixed price, set after selections are made, so the number does not creep up through allowances once work starts.

items.q: My house is in a historic district. Can I still remodel the bathroom?
items.a: Usually yes. Lake Worth Beach has six local historic districts, and the city requires a Certificate of Appropriateness before exterior work. A bathroom is interior, so most projects skip that step. If your plan changes a window or an exterior door, or vents through an outside wall, review applies and H&H builds it into the schedule.

items.q: Florida changed the permit law. Do I still need a permit?
items.a: Most likely. Under Florida House Bill 803, some residential projects under $7,500 may qualify for a permit exemption from July 1, 2026, but the city says it is not automatic and owners must apply first. A full bathroom renovation usually costs well above that, and H&H handles the permitting process either way.

items.q: Do you take small repair jobs?
items.a: No. H&H does full renovations only: primary baths, guest baths, powder rooms, tub-to-shower conversions, kitchens, closets and built-ins. Small repairs, maintenance and urgent repair calls are not offered, which keeps the crew focused on the projects it has scheduled and on finishing them well.

items.q: Can you work in my condo building?
items.a: Yes. H&H is insured in Florida and sends certificates naming your association or property manager on request. The team prepares the approval packet, reserves the service elevator and plans work around building hours. Shared waste stacks can limit how far a wet wall can move, so that gets checked at the first walkthrough.

final_cta.h2: Tell us what is not working in your bathroom
final_cta.text: Call (561) 888-4488 to book a free in-home estimate. Tristan's team will walk the room, confirm what review it needs and put a real scope and price in writing.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Berkeley, plus baths, ADUs and whole homes

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom kitchens planned around how you cook and gather, from galley kitchens in Berkeley bungalows to open kitchens with islands in Oakland. HDR's NARI award list includes Regional Contractor of the Year kitchen wins in 2020 and 2023.

image.alt: Berkeley kitchen remodel with blue-painted cabinets, white subway tile, a range hood in the same blue and an island with black stools

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and new bathrooms added where none existed. Designers handle tile, vanities and fixtures, and the build team installs them to the approved plans. Recent baths range from Berkeley and Albany to Piedmont, Oakland and Kensington.

image.alt: Berkeley bathroom remodel with teal glossy wall tile, frameless glass shower, walnut vanity and floating orange shelves

items.name: Whole-Home and Historic Remodels
items.blurb: Kitchen, dining, living and bedroom remodels that open older floor plans while keeping original details. The design team specializes in historic Bay Area homes and works with an in-house California licensed architect to solve technically challenging layouts.

image.alt: Oakland whole-home remodel joining the kitchen and dining room, with a round wood table, black spindle chairs and an open staircase

items.name: ADUs and Garage Conversions
items.blurb: Backyard ADUs, studio offices and garage conversions planned with HDR's in-house architect, designers and builders. HDR won a Chrysalis Award for an ADU in 2019, and a recent blog post covers a Berkeley garage turned into a multi-use room.

image.alt: Backyard office ADU in Oakland with navy siding, white French doors and a wood ceiling over the entry

items.name: Basements, Attics and Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Unused basements and attics turned into living space, plus decks, patios and outdoor kitchens from HDR's landscape design-build team. Each one follows the same design, permit and build steps HDR uses for a kitchen or bath.

image.alt: Oakland attic conversion bedroom with exposed wood beams, a skylight, a paper pendant lamp and a wood bed frame

why_choose_us.h2: How HDR keeps East Bay remodels on track

items.title: No start until materials arrive
items.text: HDR orders materials once you sign and does not begin construction until every item is on the job site and inspected, so you are not living in a construction zone any longer than needed.

items.title: Someone on site every day
items.text: Your Lead Carpenter is on site daily unless you are told otherwise. The Head of Production reviews progress about every other day and always on Friday, and you get weekly progress reports.

items.title: A long record of NARI awards
items.text: The awards page lists NARI Regional Contractor of the Year wins for kitchens and baths in 2020 and 2023, an addition in 2024, a Chrysalis Award and a GuildQuality Guildmaster with Distinction.

items.title: A warranty past the industry standard
items.text: HDR's Peace of Mind warranty coverage extends well beyond the industry-standard warranty period, and every job ends with a thorough walkthrough before you sign off.

about.h2: Led by President Chris Fellows
about.text: Chris Fellows is President of HDR Remodeling and has been with the company since 2009. He brings 25 years of construction experience and holds California B General Building and C-6 Cabinet and Finish Carpentry licenses. He is a NARI Certified Remodeling Project Manager, Lead R&R certified and C2 asbestos safety certified. Chris directs HDR's trades, vendors and suppliers alongside Vice President Kevin Mond, who is usually the first person new clients meet. Licensed architect Milton Tong and design manager Tamar Nachshon lead design, and production manager Alberto Navarro Ruiz runs the build crews.

image.alt: Chris Fellows, President of HDR Remodeling in Emeryville, CA

process.h2: The HDR start-to-finish process

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: A complimentary visit to review your wish list and walk the project. HDR suggests starting a Houzz ideabook to share the looks you like.

steps.title: Studio meeting
steps.text: A complimentary meeting at the office and design studio to explore options and estimated cost ranges, and sign a design agreement if you both agree.

steps.title: Design and permits
steps.text: A Design + Build Coordinator schedules design meetings, schematic drawings and cost estimates. After the contract, HDR files for building permits and zoning approval.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Materials arrive and are inspected first. A Pass the Baton meeting hands your job from design to production, then your Lead Carpenter works on site daily.

steps.title: Walk-through and photos
steps.text: A personal post-production walk-through lets you review and sign off on the work, followed by a professional photo shoot of the finished space.

service_area.h2: Serving Berkeley, Oakland and the inner East Bay
service_area.text: HDR works from its office and design studio on Horton Street in Emeryville. The site names Alameda, Albany, Berkeley, El Cerrito, Kensington, Oakland and Piedmont as its core service area. The project gallery shows kitchens and baths on Berkeley streets like Virginia, Hopkins and Grizzly Peak, Oakland homes in Rockridge, and finished work in Alameda, Albany, El Cerrito, Kensington and Piedmont.

faq.h2: Common questions from Berkeley and Oakland homeowners

items.q: Is the first meeting free?
items.a: Yes. HDR starts with a complimentary visit to your home to review your wish list and walk the space. Next comes a complimentary meeting at its office and design studio, where you look at design options and estimated cost ranges. Most clients sign a design agreement at that meeting if both sides want to go ahead.

items.q: Why won't construction start right after I sign?
items.a: HDR orders your materials once the contract is signed and the deposit is in, and it does not start work until all of them are on the job site and inspected. That way your kitchen or bath is not torn apart while you wait on a late cabinet or tile delivery.

items.q: Who will be at my house during the build?
items.a: Your assigned Lead Carpenter is on site every day unless you are told otherwise. The Head of Production visits about every other day and always on Friday. You also get weekly progress reports and access to HDR's project management software to track milestones and selections.

items.q: Can you update an older home without losing its character?
items.a: That is a focus for HDR. Its design team specializes in historic Bay Area homes and aims to keep each home's character while adding modern function. One Berkeley client wrote that the team kept the style and sensibility of their bungalow while bringing in new ideas.

items.q: Do you handle permits and offer a warranty?
items.a: Yes. After the construction contract is signed, HDR files for building permits and zoning approval. When the job is done, a walkthrough confirms every detail, and HDR's Peace of Mind warranty coverage extends well beyond the industry-standard warranty period for your remodel.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Lee's Summit, Designed by the Owners
hero.subheadline: Lorna McCartney and Mel Kelly own Haven Reno KC, and they lead the design and the project management on every remodel. From demo to clean-up, you deal with the people whose names are on the company.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Lee's Summit project: spa-style primary bath with freestanding tub, sage green double vanity and wood-look tile floor

intro.h2: Two designers who also run the job site
paragraphs: Haven Reno KC does bathroom remodeling in Lee's Summit with a small, hands-on team. Lorna McCartney manages projects and designs. Mel Kelly is the general contractor and a designer. You sit down with them to pick layout, tile and fixtures, and then they stay with the job from demo through the final clean-up.

Their recent work shows the range: a 1990s bath turned into a retreat with a freestanding soaking tub, heated tile floors and a walk-in shower, and a spa bath with sage green accents and a warm wood ceiling. Kitchens, basements, laundry rooms and offices get the same care.

services.h2: Bathroom Remodeling in Lee's Summit, Plus Kitchens and Basements

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites, hall baths and small bathrooms, often with a freestanding tub, a frameless glass walk-in shower, a custom vanity and heated floors. Haven typically uses 3000K lighting in its bathrooms so tile and paint look bright and clean without turning yellow.

image.alt: Lee's Summit primary bathroom with frameless glass shower, freestanding tub and tongue-and-groove wood ceiling

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full kitchen gut-and-remodels and refreshes, including two-tone custom cabinets, new counters, refinished hardwood floors and islands sized for how your family eats. Lorna and Mel walk you through layout and materials so the finished room fits your routine and your style.

image.alt: Lee's Summit kitchen remodel with natural maple cabinets, white island, leather counter stools and open wood shelves

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Unfinished or dated basements turned into family rooms, playrooms and music rooms. In Grain Valley, the team gave a log cabin basement a modern update while keeping its cedar paneling and adding a light made from reclaimed church wood.

image.alt: Finished basement family room in the Kansas City area with gray sectional, wood-look plank floor and recessed lights

items.name: Laundry & Mudrooms
items.blurb: Laundry rooms and mudrooms with custom cabinetry, open shelves and durable tile, often remodeled alongside a kitchen or bathroom. One Lee's Summit client had a kitchen, laundry room and bathroom gutted and rebuilt in a single project managed by Lorna.

image.alt: Laundry room remodel in Lee's Summit with sage green upper cabinets, open wood shelf and white washer and dryer

items.name: Offices & Whole-Home Updates
items.blurb: Home offices, bedrooms, playrooms, entries and whole-home remodels. A recent Lee's Summit lake house got warm, personalized design with mid-century modern pops of color, planned so the home looks and feels as great as it functions.

image.alt: Home office remodel in Lee's Summit with built-in bookshelves, board-and-batten wall, walnut desk and woven pendant light

why_choose_us.h2: What sets Haven apart

items.title: The owners are your designers
items.text: Lorna and Mel both design. Lorna also manages projects and Mel is the general contractor, so the people who drew your bathroom are the ones checking it on site.

items.title: A calendar you can see
items.text: Scott M. wrote on Google that his family had a calendar on their phones that was updated daily, and that Lorna was one of the most organized people he had met.

items.title: Design help is part of the job
items.text: Haven manages the remodel start to finish, including help with design. Clients describe the planning as fun instead of overwhelming, with layouts and materials reviewed together.

items.title: Local and on the record
items.text: 5.0 stars from 21 Google reviews, a member of the Lee's Summit Chamber, and quoted by Redfin with tips for getting bathrooms ready for an open house.

about.h2: Meet Lorna McCartney and Mel Kelly
about.text: Lorna McCartney has loved design since renovating her first home in 2006. She left a career as a nurse practitioner to create spaces that lift people up, and as a mother of two she designs rooms that are beautiful and work for real families. Her style leans toward clean, efficient spaces with calm, coastal colors. Mel Kelly is a contemporary artist turned interior designer and general contractor. She caught the remodeling bug in 2011 on her own first home and later ran a home decor business, Not Boring Home, from 2019 to 2022, with work featured in The World of Interiors and House & Garden.

image.alt: Lorna McCartney, owner, project manager and designer at Haven Reno KC

process.h2: Plan, schedule, build, enjoy

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Haven swings by for a free estimate, then works with you on design, materials and layout so the room fits your needs and reflects your style.

steps.title: Schedule
steps.text: Your project gets a clear calendar before demo day. One client described a calendar on their phones that was updated every day.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: The team handles demo, construction and finish work, with Lorna or Mel as your point of contact and the trades coordinated for you.

steps.title: Enjoy your space
steps.text: After the final clean-up you get the room back, finished and ready to use, with the same team a phone call away for the next project.

service_area.h2: Lee's Summit and the towns around it
service_area.text: Haven Reno KC works out of 2 SE 5th St in downtown Lee's Summit, and most of its projects are in Lee's Summit itself. Clients have also hired the team in Raymore, Greenwood, Lone Jack, Grain Valley, Grandview, Peculiar, Kansas City and Overland Park, Kansas. If you live in the Lee's Summit area and are not sure whether your home is in range, call or send a message and ask.

faq.h2: Questions Lee's Summit homeowners ask Haven

items.q: Is the estimate free?
items.a: Yes. Send a few quick details through the contact form or call (816) 607-4099, and the team will swing by your home to look at the space and give you a free quote. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 9 am to 4 pm.

items.q: Who manages my bathroom remodel day to day?
items.a: One of the owners. Lorna McCartney manages projects and Mel Kelly is the general contractor, and reviewers also name Faye as a main contact. Clients mention a shared calendar on their phones that was updated daily, so they knew who was coming and when.

items.q: Do you help with design, or do I need a designer?
items.a: Design help is part of what Haven does. Both owners are designers, and you work with them to review layout, materials and finishes that fit your needs and your style. For bathrooms the team typically uses 3000K lighting, which keeps tile and paint looking bright without feeling harsh.

items.q: Should I remodel my bathroom before I sell?
items.a: Usually not. In advice shared with Redfin, Haven said a full bathroom remodel rarely pays back before a sale. Fresh paint on walls, trim and ceiling, matching light bulbs, an updated light fixture if budget allows, and new caulk with clean grout tend to do more for buyers.

items.q: Do you only do bathrooms?
items.a: No. Bathrooms, kitchens and basement finishing are the main specialties, and Haven also remodels laundry rooms, mudrooms, offices, bedrooms, playrooms, garages and whole homes. Several clients have hired the team for a second or third room after the first one was done.

final_cta.h2: Ready for a bathroom you love?
final_cta.text: Call Haven Reno KC or send a few details, and Lorna or Mel will swing by for a free estimate.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Grand Rapids With the Owner on Site
hero.subheadline: JBJ Building & Remodeling is a family-owned West Michigan builder founded in 2002. Owner Jamie Simmons meets every customer, and his crew is known for level, exact tile work.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Grand Rapids area: master bath with dark double vanity, marble countertop, gold faucets and black-framed mirrors

intro.h2: Tile-first remodels from a Comstock Park crew
paragraphs: JBJ Building & Remodeling has handled bathroom remodeling in Grand Rapids and the towns around it for more than 20 years. The office is on 6 Mile Court in Comstock Park, and the work runs from attic baths and master suites to kitchens, basements, additions and decks.

Tile is where this crew stands out. They set complex patterns, large-format tile and in-floor heating, with careful subfloor prep so grout lines stay true for decades. One Google reviewer came to Jamie on a referral from The Tile Shop for a fireplace wall in 16 by 24 inch natural slate. Another said the level of the tile impressed him most.

services.h2: What the JBJ crew builds

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: From growing a cramped master bath into a full suite to refreshing a small guest bath, JBJ handles the plumbing, electrical and finish work. Popular features include curbless walk-in showers with built-in niches, freestanding soaking tubs and custom double vanities.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with a blue and white patterned tile shower under a sloped ceiling, gold fixtures, wood vanity and dark floor tile

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Jamie looks at your kitchen's current footprint to work out the best flow. The crew installs custom cabinetry, granite or quartz counters, lighting and fixtures, and handles everything from the first teardown to the final coat of paint, in modern or traditional styles.

image.alt: White kitchen remodel with a black and brass gas range, curved white hood, marble counters and a brass faucet over a farmhouse sink

items.name: Custom Tile
items.blurb: Kitchen backsplashes, waterproof tile shower enclosures, mudroom and entry floors, and heated tile floors. The crew specializes in complex patterns and large-format tile, with proper subfloor prep, precise cuts and straight grout lines so the finish does not crack or shift.

image.alt: Vintage-style bathroom with white subway tile walls, mint green upper walls, black and white penny tile floor and a pedestal sink

items.name: Additions and New Builds
items.blurb: Extra bedrooms, mother-in-law apartments, home offices, room additions and custom homes built from the ground up. JBJ pulls the permits, coordinates trades, deliveries and inspections, and matches the new space to your house. Jamie oversees the structural work himself.

image.alt: Home addition under construction in West Michigan with new roof framing and white weather barrier

items.name: Custom Decks
items.blurb: Multi-level decks in premium wood or composite with modern railing systems. Recent builds include a two-story deck with black metal railings and stairs on a brick home, and a wood deck built right up to an above-ground pool.

image.alt: Wood deck with steps and metal railing built beside an above-ground pool at a West Michigan home

why_choose_us.h2: Why homeowners choose JBJ for bathroom remodeling in Grand Rapids

items.title: The owner stays involved
items.text: Jamie Simmons meets with every customer and stays involved in every project. On additions and new builds he oversees the structural work himself, so you are never handed off to a stranger.

items.title: Detail you can see in the tile
items.text: One Google reviewer said the level of the tile and a built-in linen cabinet, nailed, puttied and sanded, were 'so perfect.' Another was sent to Jamie by The Tile Shop.

items.title: No corners cut
items.text: A master bath client wrote that Jamie refused to cut corners and built the room exactly as designed, even when that took a little longer. His ideas kept the budget in check and matched the house.

items.title: Permits and product warranties covered
items.text: JBJ is licensed and insured, pulls every needed permit and builds to code. The company also stands by the manufacturer's warranty on all the products it supplies.

about.h2: Meet owner Jamie Simmons
about.text: Jamie Simmons leads JBJ Building & Remodeling Inc., a family-owned company rooted in Western Michigan since 2002. He built it on a simple idea: a home should reflect the people who live in it, so each project is tailored from quote to completion. Jamie meets with all customers himself, and reviewers often name him for ideas that stay within budget and suit the style of the house. Clients name his crew too, like Don, praised for a bath and a built-in linen cabinet, and Kevin, who set a natural slate fireplace wall.

image.alt: Jamie Simmons, owner of JBJ Building & Remodeling in Comstock Park, MI

process.h2: From first call to final coat of paint

steps.title: Free consultation
steps.text: Call or send the form with your project type, address and estimated budget. The team aims to respond promptly to every inquiry.

steps.title: Walkthrough with Jamie
steps.text: Jamie meets you at the house, looks at the current layout and talks through ideas that fit your budget and the style of your home.

steps.title: Permits and scheduling
steps.text: JBJ pulls the permits and lines up the trades, deliveries and inspections so the job keeps moving once work begins.

steps.title: Build and finish
steps.text: The crew handles demolition, plumbing, electrical, tile and trim through to the final coat of paint, with Jamie involved the whole way.

service_area.h2: Serving Comstock Park, Ada, Rockford and greater Grand Rapids
service_area.text: JBJ works from its Comstock Park office across the north and east sides of Grand Rapids and into the southwest suburbs. The company has served Ada, Rockford and East Grand Rapids for more than 20 years, and its own list adds Cascade, Belmont, Cannonsburg, Grandville, Byron Center and the lower east corner of Sparta. If your town is close to these, call and ask.

faq.h2: Answers for West Michigan homeowners

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. JBJ offers a free consultation and free quote. Call 616-862-8778 or fill out the contact form with your name, project type, project address and estimated budget. The team aims to respond promptly, and Jamie meets with every customer before any work is planned or priced.

items.q: Are you licensed and insured?
items.a: Yes. JBJ Building & Remodeling Inc. is fully licensed and insured. The company handles all aspects of permitting for your project, pulls every permit the job needs and builds strictly to code. It also stands by the manufacturer's warranty on all products it supplies.

items.q: How long does a bathroom remodel take?
items.a: It depends on the size of the room and the scope, and Jamie sets the plan at your walkthrough. For reference, one Google reviewer's complete attic bathroom took 8 weeks against a 6-week plan, and the owner still called the result fantastic. Jamie would rather take a little longer than cut corners.

items.q: Can you install heated tile floors?
items.a: Yes. In-floor heating is part of the custom tile service, along with complex patterns, large-format tile, waterproof shower enclosures and backsplashes. The crew starts with proper subfloor preparation, then makes precise cuts and keeps grout lines straight so the floor holds up for decades without cracking or shifting.

items.q: Will you finish a project another contractor left?
items.a: JBJ has done it. A Google reviewer hired Jamie and his crew after a previous contractor walked away midway through their kitchen remodel. She wrote that they were responsive and professional, did great work, and that she only wished she had called them first. Call to talk through where your project stands.

final_cta.h2: Book a free consultation with Jamie
final_cta.text: Call 616-862-8778, or send the form with your project and budget and the team will get back to you promptly.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Scottsdale, AZ, Planned in Our Showroom
hero.subheadline: Premier began in 1994 as a kitchen and bath specialist. One licensed team designs and builds your remodel under one contract, backed by a 10-year labor warranty.

intro.h2: Design first, then build, all under one Scottsdale roof
paragraphs: Premier Design-Build-Remodel has handled kitchen remodeling in Scottsdale, AZ and across the Valley since Greg Heden founded the company in 1994. It started as a kitchen and bath specialist. Today in-house designers also plan whole-home remodels, room additions and casitas, and the same team builds what they draw.

Your project starts at the showroom on North 80th Street, where you can touch cabinet doors, countertop slabs, tile and fixtures before you choose. You see 3D renderings and get a fixed-price proposal before construction starts. Google reviewers point to the designers by name and to steady communication on permits, updates and quality.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Scottsdale, AZ, and beyond the kitchen

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Layout comes first: traffic flow, appliance placement, island seating, storage and lighting. Then come custom cabinetry, pull-out pantries, stone counters and, when you want an open plan, wall removal with structural beams. Premier handles the permits and engineering inside the same process.

image.alt: Paradise Valley, AZ kitchen remodel from mid-century to modern, with marble-look quartz island, gray lacquer cabinets and double wall ovens

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Spa-style primary suites, walk-in showers with frameless glass, freestanding tubs, steam showers, heated floors and custom vanities. For smaller baths the team uses floating vanities, tub-to-shower conversions and vertical storage. Designers, project managers and installers work as one team from day one.

image.alt: Central Scottsdale transitional bathroom with a freestanding tub under an arched wood-slat niche and glass block window

items.name: Whole Home Remodeling
items.blurb: Connected rooms planned together, with matching flooring, lighting and finishes. Whole-home work can include moving a kitchen or bath, opening a dated floor plan and upgrading electrical or plumbing, all engineered, permitted and phased by one accountable team.

image.alt: Downtown Tempe whole-home remodel with a herringbone wood floor, black built-in cabinetry, round dining table and starburst chandelier

items.name: Casitas and Home Additions
items.blurb: Detached guest casitas, primary suite expansions and new living space. Planning covers utility connections, zoning, structural needs and permits, so the new space fits the property and the existing house. Premier's Terravita casita shows the desert-contemporary style in practice.

image.alt: Terravita desert-contemporary guest casita with stucco walls, French doors, paver walkway and saguaro landscaping

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons Scottsdale homeowners pick Premier

items.title: Three trade licences
items.text: Premier lists General B-135167, Electrical R-11-301243 and Plumbing R37R-318793 on every page of its site, so the work behind your walls is covered by its own licences.

items.title: A price before you commit
items.text: After design reviews and 3D renderings, you receive a fixed-price proposal. You know what the remodel costs before you sign the construction agreement.

items.title: Ten years of labor coverage
items.text: Construction workmanship is warranted for 10 years or until the home is sold, whichever comes first. Products keep their own manufacturer warranties.

items.title: Seasoned people you can name
items.text: Production VP Kent Redmond has 33 years in residential project management. Interior designer Stephanie Olesen-Bute is NCIDQ certified with more than 25 years of experience.

about.h2: Led by founder Greg Heden since 1994
about.text: Greg Heden founded Premier in 1994 and still leads it as president. The company began as a kitchen and bath specialist and grew into a full design-build firm with showrooms in Scottsdale and Mesa. Greg built the team around design, craftsmanship and project management under one roof. He is joined by Kent Redmond, VP of Production and Operations, Kym Davis, VP of Sales and Design with 45 years in remodeling, and designers such as Rachel Herrera, who came up through the tile trade, and Chris Ebert, who began his career in Chicago.

image.alt: Greg Heden, president of Premier Design-Build-Remodel in Scottsdale

process.h2: The Premier six-step design-build process

steps.title: Complimentary consultation
steps.text: A one-hour meeting with a designer, usually in the showroom, about your goals, style and budget window. Call, Zoom or in person.

steps.title: Discovery and measurement
steps.text: The team photographs and measures your home, sketches simple floor plan options and narrows the investment range.

steps.title: Design and renderings
steps.text: Guided selection meetings, full 3D renderings and several revision sessions lead to a fixed-price proposal you can review.

steps.title: Contract and production
steps.text: You sign the construction agreement, meet your project manager at an in-home review, and the build begins with regular site visits.

steps.title: Completion
steps.text: A final walkthrough, punch-list work, professional photos of your new space and follow-up support from the Premier team.

service_area.h2: Where Premier works in the Valley
service_area.text: The Scottsdale showroom sits at 16035 N 80th St, Suite D, and a second showroom is on Baseline Road in Mesa, giving East Valley homeowners two places to see materials in person. From those two bases the team remodels homes in Scottsdale, Paradise Valley, Phoenix, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert and Ahwatukee. Recent portfolio projects include Troon, McCormick Ranch, Greyhawk, Terravita, Arcadia and Downtown Tempe.

faq.h2: Scottsdale remodeling questions, answered

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Premier offers a complimentary one-hour design consultation, usually in the showroom. You can also book it as a phone call or a Zoom meeting. You see materials and the portfolio, talk about investment ranges, and leave with clear next steps for the discovery phase.

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Scottsdale?
items.a: It depends mostly on cabinetry level, structural changes, appliances and finishes, not square footage alone. Rather than quote a rough number up front, Premier narrows the range after measuring your home and then gives you a fixed-price proposal once the design and selections are done.

items.q: Do I need permits to remodel?
items.a: Often, yes. Premier notes that in Mesa, structural, electrical and plumbing changes require permits, and its Scottsdale page lists experience with city permitting requirements. Permits and engineering are managed inside the design-build process, so you do not have to file them yourself.

items.q: What does the warranty cover?
items.a: Premier's construction workmanship warranty lasts 10 years or until the home is sold, whichever comes first. The products installed in your home, such as appliances and fixtures, carry their manufacturers' own warranties with separate terms. Follow-up support continues after the final walkthrough.

items.q: Can I visit the showroom before I decide?
items.a: Yes. The Scottsdale showroom displays custom cabinetry, countertop materials, designer tile, lighting, plumbing fixtures and hardware. Meeting a designer there lets you compare finishes side by side. You can schedule a visit online or call (480) 573-7182 to set a time.

final_cta.h2: See your kitchen in 3D before anyone swings a hammer
final_cta.text: Book a complimentary one-hour consultation at the Scottsdale showroom.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling Minneapolis Families Can Budget For
hero.subheadline: Red Fox Remodeling designs and builds kitchens, baths and basements across the Twin Cities, with starting prices posted on its site and one team from first sketch to final inspection.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Minneapolis area: St. Paul kitchen with navy island, butcher block top, brass pendants and white upper cabinets

intro.h2: Design, permits and build under one Minneapolis roof
paragraphs: Red Fox Remodeling handles kitchen remodeling Minneapolis and St. Paul homeowners plan around, along with bathrooms, basements and additions. Founder Denny Meints started the company in 2022 after years in remodeling and construction management, and built it on integrity, transparent pricing and quality craftsmanship.

Many of the projects on its site are older St. Paul homes, where new hardwood, millwork and siding were matched to the original so the work looks like it was always there. Each service page lists a starting price, so you can tell early whether your budget fits. Google reviewers keep using the same words: communication, integrity and craftsmanship.

services.h2: What Red Fox builds, with starting prices

items.name: Kitchens
items.blurb: Custom kitchens designed around how your family cooks and gathers, from walnut cabinetry and marble tops to butcher block and brick floors. Kitchens start at $75,000 and typically run $90,000 to $200,000. Most full kitchen remodels take about 10 weeks of construction.

image.alt: Garden Cottage kitchen in St. Paul with sage green cabinets, butcher block counters, open shelves and brick floor

items.name: Bathrooms
items.blurb: Primary baths, family baths and tight powder rooms, with features like heated floors, wet rooms that pair tub and shower behind glass, and marble or handmade tile. Bathrooms start at $65,000, typically range up to $150,000, and take about 6 to 8 weeks of construction.

image.alt: Family bathroom in a historic St. Paul home with walnut vanity, brass fixtures and a freestanding tub in a glass wet room

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Rec rooms, guest suites, offices and bathrooms, from waterproofing to final trim. A full basement with a bathroom, bedroom and living space tends to cost around $100,000, with basements starting at $95,000. Design takes 1 to 2 months and construction 3 to 4 months.

image.alt: Finished basement with a sectional sofa, wet bar with white cabinets, open shelves and wood-look floor

items.name: Additions
items.blurb: Additions designed to disappear into the original house, with matched siding, windows and roofing. Additions start at $200,000. Expect nine to twelve weeks of design, four to six weeks of preparation, and four to eight months of building, depending on size.

image.alt: Executive Craftsman addition project in St. Paul with a new kitchen island and peninsula, white cabinets and brass pendants

items.name: Whole Home Remodels
items.blurb: Every room reworked into one plan, from structural changes to finish details. Whole-home projects start at $350,000. Without structural changes they can finish in four or five months, while larger scopes run eight or nine months. Red Fox can also price a house before you buy it.

image.alt: Burnsville whole-home remodel living room with skylights, white brick fireplace and wall of windows

why_choose_us.h2: Why Twin Cities homeowners hire Red Fox

items.title: Prices you can see first
items.text: Red Fox posts starting prices for kitchens, baths, basements, additions and whole homes, and promises transparent pricing through the whole project so you always know where you stand.

items.title: A team with named roles
items.text: Lead designer Mai See Thao, project manager Asher Webb, site supervisor Wade Kyllonen and estimator Chad Torp each bring years of experience to a defined part of your job.

items.title: You always know what is next
items.text: An app-based customer portal and a dedicated project manager keep you informed. One reviewer wrote that Red Fox "communicates clearly and honestly and delivers the promised outcome."

items.title: Award-winning, licensed work
items.text: Red Fox holds a NARI Minnesota Silver award for a residential kitchen, a Minnesota's Best Readers' Choice Bronze for 2025 and a Chrysalis Award. It is licensed (BC799282), a NARI member and EPA lead certified.

about.h2: Meet Denny Meints and his team
about.text: Denny Meints founded Red Fox Remodeling in 2022 after years of experience in home remodeling and construction management. He runs operations and leads a team based on 16th Avenue SE in Minneapolis. Reviewers mention him by name, saying Denny walks you through the process and makes sure the work is done right. Writing about a historic St. Paul addition, Denny said the team "especially loved the challenge of carrying the original home's historic details into every part of the addition."

image.alt: Denny Meints, founder of Red Fox Remodeling in Minneapolis

process.h2: Four steps from first call to finished room

steps.title: Free consultation
steps.text: Tell Red Fox about your project and budget by phone or through the consultation form, and the team sets up a first conversation.

steps.title: Discovery and design
steps.text: The team learns your vision and budget, then builds an initial design and estimate and refines it with you until it is approved.

steps.title: Prepare and plan
steps.text: Red Fox pulls the permits, coordinates trade partners and sources every material so all of it is ready before construction starts.

steps.title: Build and celebrate
steps.text: Your project manager keeps you updated through the app-based portal, with walkthroughs and final touch-ups before the finished space is yours.

service_area.h2: Remodeling across Minneapolis and St. Paul
service_area.text: Red Fox works out of an office at 1153 16th Ave SE in Minneapolis and serves homeowners across the Twin Cities. Its featured projects, including Executive Craftsman, Sophisticated Living, Garden Cottage and Emerald Retreat, are all in St. Paul, many in historic homes on established blocks. If you are weighing a house in a particular neighborhood, the team can give general price guidance before you buy.

faq.h2: Kitchen remodeling Minneapolis questions, answered with real numbers

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost with Red Fox?
items.a: It depends on scope, design and selections. As a general guide, Red Fox says kitchen remodels typically range from $90,000 to $200,000, with projects starting around $75,000 for a more basic scope. Pricing stays transparent through design and construction, so you know where the project stands at each step.

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: Most full kitchen remodels take about 10 weeks of construction. Counting design, selections, permits and ordering, the whole process often runs 6 to 8 months from the first consultation. Red Fox suggests you start planning 3 to 6 months before you want construction to begin, because custom cabinets can have long lead times.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost, and how long does it take?
items.a: A bathroom remodel with Red Fox typically ranges from $65,000 to $150,000. Construction usually takes 6 to 8 weeks. Larger primary bathrooms with layout changes, custom tile or specialty materials can take longer, and specialty materials can have long lead times, so plan ahead.

items.q: Can we live at home during the work?
items.a: For kitchens, in most cases yes, though you may need to move out for part of the project depending on scope. For a bathroom, you can stay throughout if the house has more than one bathroom. For a whole-home remodel, plan to relocate for at least part of the work, which also shortens the schedule.

items.q: Do you work on older and historic homes?
items.a: Yes. Most featured projects are historic St. Paul houses. In one, new hardwood floors and custom millwork were matched to the original home, and an addition used matching siding, windows and roofing. Another restored character lost in a 1990s renovation with new millwork, butcher block counters and a brick floor.

final_cta.h2: Talk with Red Fox about your kitchen
final_cta.text: Call (612) 208-2794 or start a free consultation online. Share your budget and the team will tell you what it can build.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Redmond, WA, Built Around Careful Tile Work
hero.subheadline: Remont Remodeling is a licensed and bonded Eastside contractor that takes on a limited number of projects, so each shower, tub and tile wall gets close attention. Expect daily photo updates and a written warranty.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Redmond WA by Remont: navy subway tile walk-in shower with brass-framed glass door, pebble floor, wood slat wall and heated towel rail

intro.h2: A small Eastside crew with a bath-first focus
paragraphs: Remont Remodeling handles bathroom remodeling in Redmond, WA and the nearby Eastside from a suite in the Overlake Office Center on NE Bel Red Road. Owner Viktor Chirkin keeps the company small on purpose. It takes a selected number of projects at a time, so every job gets his direct oversight from consultation to final walkthrough.

Most calls are about showers. The team converts tubs to walk-in showers, builds barrier-free entries with grab bars and built-in seats, and sets custom tile over full waterproofing. Kitchens and whole-house projects are on the list too. Clients hear from the crew every day by text, email or phone, with progress photos.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Redmond, WA, from tubs to tile

items.name: Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: The old tub comes out and a custom shower goes in, with options like a barrier-free entry, grab bars and a built-in seat. The design phase takes about 2 to 3 business days, and every conversion carries a 5-year parts and labor warranty.

image.alt: Walk-in shower conversion with white handmade-look tile, rainfall head, grab bar and a frameless glass panel

items.name: Walk-In Shower Installation
items.blurb: Barrier-free entries, custom tile and frameless glass, with ADA-compliant options if you plan to age in place. Installation usually takes 2 to 3 weeks after a 5 to 10 day design phase, with a dedicated project manager and a written warranty of up to 5 years.

image.alt: Gray tile walk-in shower with a built-in bench, twin wall niches and a frameless glass enclosure

items.name: Full Bathroom Renovation
items.blurb: Complete tear-outs, layout changes, new plumbing and electrical, and high-end finishes. Renovations take about 2 to 4 weeks of work and include a three-year written warranty on labor and materials. Remont reports more than 300 bathroom renovations completed across the Eastside.

image.alt: Bathroom renovation with a long dark wood double vanity, gray quartz top and backlit oval mirrors

items.name: Bathroom Additions
items.blurb: For a growing family, a new bathroom starts with a space assessment, permits, and plumbing and electrical tie-ins. Most additions take 3 to 6 weeks, depending on structural work. Remont reports more than 200 additions in Bellevue, Kirkland, Redmond and Seattle.

image.alt: Long bathroom with white double vanity, lighted mirror and a sliding glass shower at the far end

items.name: Custom Tile Work
items.blurb: Porcelain, mosaic or natural stone set over professional waterproofing, in bathrooms and kitchens. Reviewers single out the tile: one called it perfection, and another wrote that every tile was perfectly aligned and every grout line flawless.

image.alt: Tub surround in large blue and gold marble-look porcelain tile with matte black shower fixtures

why_choose_us.h2: Why Eastside homeowners call Remont

items.title: Written estimates within two days
items.text: After a 60 to 90 minute in-home consultation, a written estimate with materials, labor and timeline arrives within 24 to 48 hours. Up to two revisions are included at no extra charge.

items.title: Licensed, bonded and insured
items.text: Washington GC License REMONRL761D5, bonded through CBIC (67000453) and insured through CBIC (G11FE2683), with workers' compensation coverage on every project.

items.title: Daily updates with photos
items.text: You hear from the team every day by text, email or phone, and milestones are documented in photos. Reviewers who were away during the work say the updates kept them informed.

items.title: Set hours, clean site
items.text: Crews work 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, protect floors with coverings and dust barriers, and clean the job site before leaving each day.

about.h2: Meet owner Viktor Chirkin
about.text: Viktor Chirkin owns Remont Remodeling and is a Washington State licensed general contractor (License REMONRL761D5). He brings more than a decade of bathroom and kitchen experience and has overseen hundreds of projects across the Eastside. He knows local codes, permits and inspections, and he keeps direct contact with clients through every job. As a local homeowner himself, he takes on only the projects he can supervise closely. The company rule is quality over quantity, and reviews back it up with praise for tile alignment, cleanup and staying on schedule.

process.h2: Our five-step remodeling process

steps.title: Free consultation
steps.text: A 60 to 90 minute visit to measure and photograph your space, check conditions and talk through goals, timeline and budget, with no sales pressure.

steps.title: Written estimate
steps.text: Within 24 to 48 hours you get a breakdown of materials, labor, timeline and permit costs. Two revisions are included at no charge.

steps.title: Contract and design
steps.text: The contract is ready in one to two business days. Final materials and fixtures are confirmed, permits are submitted and a start date is set.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Work runs 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM behind dust barriers, with daily progress photos and multi-point quality checks along the way.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: You review every detail against a quality checklist and receive warranty papers and care guides. The project closes only when you are satisfied.

faq.h2: Questions about your Redmond bathroom project

items.q: Is the estimate free?
items.a: Yes. The first consultation is free and lasts 60 to 90 minutes in your home. Within 24 to 48 hours you receive a written estimate with materials, labor, timeline and any permit costs, and up to two revisions are included at no additional charge. There is no obligation to sign.

items.q: What warranty comes with a new shower?
items.a: Coverage is in writing and depends on the service. Tub-to-shower conversions carry a 5-year parts and labor warranty, walk-in showers carry up to 5 years, full bathroom renovations include three years on labor and materials, and bathroom additions get 2 years on labor plus the manufacturer warranties on materials.

items.q: Do I need a permit for a bathroom remodel in Redmond?
items.a: Many projects that move plumbing, change electrical or add a room need one. Remont identifies the required permits during the estimate, explains the costs, then submits and tracks the applications for you and schedules the inspections. Viktor knows the code and inspection process in each city the company serves.

items.q: Can you remodel my kitchen too?
items.a: Yes. Bathrooms and kitchens are the company's two specialties. Kitchen work covers cabinetry, countertops, plumbing, electrical and appliance coordination. The design phase usually takes 7 to 14 days, and installation runs 4 to 8 weeks depending on size. Remont reports more than 250 completed kitchen renovations.

items.q: How do you protect my home during the work?
items.a: Floors get coverings, work areas get dust barriers, and materials are stored securely and staged in an organized way. Crews keep an 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM schedule and clean the job site before they leave each day, so the rest of the house stays livable while your bathroom is rebuilt.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Kansas City, Designed by Our Own Team

intro.h2: Designers and builders working from one Lenexa office
paragraphs: Renovating KC handles kitchen remodeling in Kansas City from concept to completion, with its own designers, project managers and construction managers on staff. The firm works from an office in Lenexa, Kansas, and takes on homes on both the Kansas and Missouri sides of the metro.

Every kitchen starts with a conversation about what matters most to you. The design team then builds floor plans, mood boards, curated design boards and 3-D renderings, so you see the room before demolition. Licensed contractors and trusted subcontractors take it from there, and clients often thank their designer and construction manager by name in reviews.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Kansas City and the rooms around it

items.name: Kitchen Remodels and Renovations
items.blurb: Layout changes, removed walls and relocated plumbing or electrical, or a lighter renovation that swaps cabinets, counters, flooring and appliances in the same footprint. Renovating KC does both and helps you choose. Its kitchens won 2025 REMY Gold and Silver awards for Residential Kitchen Remodel.

image.alt: Kansas City kitchen remodel with an arched tile range alcove, stained wood base cabinets, white quartz island and farmhouse sink

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Spa-style primary baths, guest baths and powder rooms, large or small. In-house interior designers help you pick fixtures, tile, lighting and paint colors, and a Renovating KC bath took 2024 REMY Gold for a Residential Bathroom Remodel Under $40,000.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with a black freestanding tub inside a glass-enclosed wet room, white stacked tile and a wood-tile accent wall

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Home theaters, playrooms, guest suites, gyms and custom bars that turn unfinished square footage into living space. Most families stay in the house during the work. Basements earned a 2025 REMY Silver, and one recent lower level added a climbing wall, ball pit and stage.

image.alt: Finished basement bar in the Kansas City area with blue-gray cabinetry, honed black counters, under-cabinet lighting and a wall-mounted TV

items.name: Whole-Home Remodels
items.blurb: Modernizing an older house, opening the floor plan or making room for a growing family. The team coordinates every room and system on one schedule, and a whole-home project won 2024 REMY Gold for Entire House Remodel in the $200,000 to $300,000 class.

image.alt: Family room in a Renovating KC remodel with a linear fireplace, stone-look surround and navy built-in shelving

items.name: Additions and Attic Build-Outs
items.blurb: Additions and attic conversions add space you can use every day. One Google reviewer had upstairs guest rooms and an unfinished attic turned into a primary suite with vaulted ceilings, a large walk-in closet and a bath. A Renovating KC addition won 2025 REMY Gold and All-Star honors.

image.alt: Primary bathroom with a freestanding tub, checkerboard marble floor, wood vanity and arched shower opening under a vaulted ceiling

faq.h2: Kitchen remodel questions from Kansas City homeowners

items.q: What is the difference between a kitchen remodel and a renovation?
items.a: A renovation updates what is already there, such as cabinets, counters, flooring or appliances, without changing the layout. A remodel changes the layout itself by removing walls or moving plumbing and electrical. Renovating KC offers both and helps you pick the approach that fits your goals, budget and the way your family uses the room.

items.q: What budget should I plan for?
items.a: The kitchen and bathroom inquiry form starts at a $25,001 to $50,000 budget band, and the general consultation form starts at $50,001, with bands up to $500,000 and more for whole homes. Share your range when you reach out, and the team will build the scope of work and preliminary estimate around it.

items.q: Can we stay in the house during the work?
items.a: For basement finishing, yes: most homeowners keep living at home while the crew works efficiently and keeps the area clean. On bigger jobs it depends on scope. One client family lived in the house for the last couple of months of a near-complete gut remodel and said the crew was friendly and respectful the whole time.

items.q: What warranty comes with a project?
items.a: Every completed Renovating KC project includes a full 12-month warranty. It is the final step of the same process that starts with your consultation and runs through design and construction, and the company states plainly that it stands behind its work. Ask your project manager to walk you through what it covers.

items.q: Which areas do you serve?
items.a: Renovating KC works across the greater Kansas City metro from its Lenexa office, including Overland Park, Leawood, Olathe, Shawnee, Prairie Village and Mission Hills in Kansas and Brookside, Waldo, Lee's Summit, Liberty and Independence in Missouri. Call (913) 481-1236 if your town is not listed and the team will tell you.
