intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Lake Oswego without the runaround
paragraphs: Straight Line Design and Remodeling has handled kitchen remodeling in Lake Oswego and the Portland west side since 2010. The pitch is simple: one team takes your project from the first sketch through engineering, permits, construction and any warranty repairs, so you are not managing five companies at once.

You also know where you stand early. The first step is a phone call with owner Matt Williams, who gives rough timeline and pricing estimates before anyone visits. Kitchen packages are published in tiers, and the 5% design retainer is credited to your contract if you build with the team. Google reviewers point to crews that kept the schedule and an owner who listened.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths, additions and ADUs

items.name: Kitchen Remodel
items.blurb: Better traffic flow, smarter storage and cabinets, counters, flooring and appliances picked with a designer. Updated wiring and plumbing come with it. Recent kitchens in Southwest Portland, Beaverton, Cedar Hills and West Linn have earned NARI and Oregon Home awards.

image.alt: Portland kitchen and living room remodel with navy island, white shaker cabinets, black dome pendants and leather counter stools

items.name: Bathroom Remodel
items.blurb: Bigger showers, tile that is easy to clean, heated floors and touchless faucets. Walk-in showers, grab bars and non-slip floors are built in for kids or aging parents, and designer Alicia Warming has specialized Aging in Place training.

image.alt: Lake Oswego bathroom remodel with navy vanity, white herringbone tile wall, brass faucet and frameless glass shower

items.name: Home Additions
items.blurb: New square footage designed to look like it was always part of the house, from primary suites to family rooms. The team's structural designer and architectural design manager work out the framing and permits before construction begins.

image.alt: Lake Oswego home addition with primary bedroom, wood ceiling beam, linear gas fireplace and green accent wall

items.name: ADU Design and Build
items.blurb: Backyard units for family, rental income or a quiet workspace, matched to your house or styled on their own. One Google reviewer had a detached garage torn down and replaced with a 600 square foot ADU that he now rents out.

image.alt: Portland ADU with dark green siding, shed roof, covered wood entry and horizontal cedar fence

items.name: Basement and Attic Conversions
items.blurb: Unused space under the floor or under the roof turned into bedrooms, baths and living areas. Past projects include a Portland basement with a new bathroom and a Southeast Portland attic conversion, both designed and permitted in-house.

image.alt: Portland basement bathroom remodel with vertical wood-look slat tile wall, glass shower and black fixtures

why_choose_us.h2: Four reasons west-side families call Straight Line

items.title: An owner who leads the trade group
items.text: Matt Williams holds degrees in construction technology, construction management and kitchen and bath design, and serves as president of the NARI Pacific Northwest board.

items.title: Prices you can see first
items.text: Kitchen tiers start at $75,000 to $90,000 for the Builder package and $90,000 to $110,000 for Semi-Designer, so you can budget before the first meeting.

items.title: Awards every year since 2023
items.text: Two 2026 NARI Pacific NW Remodeler of the Year awards, a 2025 Chrysalis Award, and NARI regional CotY kitchen awards in 2024 and 2025.

items.title: Lead-safe and licensed
items.text: Licensed, bonded and insured under CCB# 195218, with an Oregon Lead-Based Paint Renovation license and EPA certification for work in older homes.

about.h2: Meet owner and general manager Matt Williams
about.text: Matt Williams started Straight Line in 2010 and still runs the first conversation on every project. He studied building construction technology, construction management and kitchen and bath design, and today he serves as president of NARI Pacific Northwest. Off the clock he does fine woodworking. His view is that a remodel should stand the test of time and make daily life better. He works with interior design manager Nikki Ditterick, designer Alicia Warming, architectural design manager Steve Griffin, an Army veteran, and production manager Nick Johnston, who keeps communication steady once crews arrive.

image.alt: Matt Williams, owner of Straight Line Design and Remodeling in Lake Oswego, OR

process.h2: How your remodel moves from call to keys

steps.title: Call with Matt, then a site visit
steps.text: A phone call for rough timeline and pricing, then a free on-site consultation to check structure, layout options and a general estimate.

steps.title: Design retainer and concepts
steps.text: A 5% design retainer starts design. The designer shows 1 to 3 layout options, refined over 2 to 5 meetings.

steps.title: Selections, contract and permits
steps.text: You choose tile, cabinets and fixtures, review the final proposal, sign the contract and the team pulls the trade permits.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Zipper walls and weatherproofing contain dust while crews build. Most projects take 6 to 16 weeks of construction, depending on scope.

steps.title: Walk-through and photos
steps.text: A return visit for touch-ups after you settle in, a client survey, and professional after photos from the in-house photographer.

service_area.h2: Lake Oswego, Portland and the west-side suburbs
service_area.text: Straight Line is based in Lake Oswego and meets clients by appointment. Since 2010 the team has worked across the Portland metro area, with most projects in Lake Oswego, Portland, Beaverton, Cedar Hills, Hillsboro, Aloha, King City, Tigard, Tualatin and Sherwood. If you live nearby and are not sure you are in range, ask on your first call.

faq.h2: Before you call: common questions

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost with Straight Line?
items.a: The site publishes kitchen tiers. The Builder package runs $75,000 to $90,000 and the Semi-Designer package runs $90,000 to $110,000. Matt gives rough numbers on the first call, then a more accurate estimate after he walks your home. Both of those steps are free.

items.q: What is the design retainer and do I get it back?
items.a: The design retainer is typically 5% of the project estimate and is paid up front to start design. If you go ahead and build with Straight Line, the full amount is applied to your contract price. If you do not, it is kept as a fee for the design work.

items.q: How long will my remodel take?
items.a: Construction usually runs 6 to 16 weeks depending on scope, after design and permits. Design itself takes 2 to 5 concept meetings depending on how quickly decisions get made, and contract signing is set within 1 to 2 weeks of the final proposal meeting.

items.q: Do you handle permits?
items.a: Yes. Engineering and permitting are part of the service, and the team knows the Portland permit process well. A structural designer joins the final proposal meeting, and the team secures the trade building permits before construction starts so you do not deal with the city yourself.

items.q: Can we stay home while you work?
items.a: Most families do. Before demolition the area is prepped to prevent damage, and zipper walls plus weatherproofing hold back dust and debris through construction. A detailed checklist closes out the job, and the team comes back after you settle in for any touch-ups.

final_cta.h2: Start with a 15-minute call to Matt
final_cta.text: Tell Matt about your kitchen, bath or addition and get rough timing and pricing on the first call.

intro.h2: A Cary company that remodels bathrooms and nothing else
paragraphs: The Bath Remodeling Center, known for years as Portofino Tile, focuses on bathroom remodeling in Cary, NC and across the Triangle. That focus shows in the numbers: more than 2,000 bathroom remodels, over $15 million in completed projects and more than 25 years in the trade.

You work with an interior designer and licensed general contractor from the first measurement, and the company's own full-time employees handle every installation. The showroom on Ward Street in downtown Cary lets you compare tile, quartz and granite tops, vanities, shower glass and heated floors side by side before anything is ordered, with a designer beside you to explain how each choice performs.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Cary, NC, from primary suites to hall baths

items.name: Primary and Master Bathrooms
items.blurb: Full primary bath remodels that start with layout: room at the vanity, how the shower opens, where towels go and whether the tub still earns its space. Master bath remodels are the most common topic in the firm's Google reviews, with 20 reviews tagged for it.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel in the Triangle with navy double vanities, built-in makeup desk, brass sconces and gray marble-look floor tile

items.name: Walk-in Showers and Tile
items.blurb: Custom showers with frameless glass, niches, benches and porcelain, glass or stone tile. Plenty of Triangle owners now trade a bulky soaking tub for a roomier shower that is simpler to clean and safer to step into. Glass enclosures are measured after tile and installed about three weeks later.

image.alt: Frameless glass shower with bench and marble-look porcelain walls beside a wood double vanity with arabesque tile wall and black fixtures

items.name: Tubs and Soaking Baths
items.blurb: Freestanding soakers, built-in tubs, jetted tubs and clawfoot styles, planned together with the shower so the room still works. If the household no longer needs a tub, the team talks through a conversion and what the existing plumbing connections allow.

image.alt: Freestanding white soaking tub next to a glass-enclosed shower with marble-pattern walls and plantation shutters in a remodeled bathroom

items.name: Vanities, Storage and Finishes
items.blurb: Custom-built vanities with drawers sized for daily items, quartz or granite tops, faucets, mirrors and medicine cabinets chosen together. A double vanity is planned to leave real counter space, not just a second sink. Heated floors can be added during design.

image.alt: Wood bathroom vanity with white top, backlit mirror, black towel warmer and frameless shower in a remodeled Triangle bathroom

service_area.text: The showroom sits in downtown Cary, and most projects are in Cary, Apex and Raleigh. The team also travels to Holly Springs, Wake Forest, Rolesville, Clayton and Zebulon, and west to Durham, Chapel Hill, Carrboro and Hillsborough. Weekend and evening showroom visits are available by appointment. If your town is not listed, share your street address and the office will tell you if the crew can get there.

faq.h2: Bathroom remodeling questions we hear in Cary

items.q: How many days will we be without the bathroom?
items.a: The process page lists 12 to 14 business days for installation, including all inspections. Frameless shower glass is custom cut after tile is set and goes in about three weeks later. Your exact schedule depends on scope and product availability, and it is confirmed in writing before work begins.

items.q: What does the first visit cost me?
items.a: Nothing. The first in-home visit, the first showroom appointment and a complimentary remodeling estimate are all free. If you need more extensive design consultations beyond those steps, the site says a consultation fee may apply, so ask about it at your first meeting.

items.q: What affects the cost of a bathroom remodel?
items.a: Room size is only one factor. Moving the layout, the amount of plumbing and electrical work, cabinetry, tile and fixture choices all change the estimate. The team suggests listing your must-have changes first, then comparing alternatives together before you approve the scope.

items.q: Can you design a bathroom for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. Options include low-threshold or walk-in showers in place of a tub, room for a shower chair, a handheld showerhead and grab bars that match the other fixtures. Raise access needs early so entry design, clearances and fixture placement are part of the plan, not an add-on.

items.q: What should I bring to the showroom?
items.a: Bring photos of your current bathroom, rough room measurements if you have them, a list of priorities and pictures of styles you like. Mention whether easy access, storage, cleaning or keeping a bathtub matters most. Those details let the designer make the visit about your house.

intro.h2: Bathroom Remodeling in Sacramento That Holds Up to Six Kids
paragraphs: Andrey Tsushko started Thrive, a family-owned firm focused on bathroom remodeling in Sacramento, after years of replacing cheap fixtures in his own house. He and his wife are raising six homeschooled kids, so their bathrooms get slammed doors, endless showers and the odd experiment. That is the test he builds to: easy-to-clean surfaces, sturdy hardware and materials that last.

The other half of the pitch is accountability. Every job runs behind sealed work zones with dust control and daily cleanup, carries a 3-year no-questions-asked warranty on installation workmanship, and comes with an On-Time Promise. If the crew is late, you get $100 back for each delayed day.

services.h2: Showers, Tubs, Vanities and Full Bath Remodels

items.name: Complete Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: From a new layout down to the final finishes. Thrive handles planning, demolition, installation and final inspection, so you are not managing separate trades. Primary baths can include freestanding soaking tubs, dual vanities and custom tile showers for a calmer, spa-like room.

image.alt: Remodeled primary bathroom with freestanding white tub, wood-look tile floor, white vanities and a large window

items.name: Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: Swap an old tub for a walk-in shower that is easier to step into and easier to clean. Options include slip-resistant shower floors, built-in niches, frameless glass doors and waterproof wall panels. A Citrus Heights conversion added bench seating and a handheld shower.

image.alt: Walk-in shower with frameless glass door, white marble-look walls and a dark pebble shower floor

items.name: Small Bathroom and Vanity Upgrades
items.blurb: Tight hall baths get smarter layouts, floating vanities, backlit mirrors and better lighting. Thrive uses nonporous, mold-resistant surfaces that stand up to Sacramento's hard water, so the room stays looking new with less scrubbing and fits a busy morning routine.

image.alt: Small bathroom with floating black vanity, under-cabinet lighting, round backlit mirror and glass globe pendants

items.name: Bathtub Replacement
items.blurb: An outdated, damaged or hard-to-clean tub can be replaced without a full gut. Most shower and bathtub replacements can be finished in just a few days, so your household is not stuck without a working bathroom for weeks.

image.alt: Hall bathroom with new alcove tub, sliding glass doors, marble-look surround with niche and dark tile floor

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: The same guarantees now cover kitchens: custom cabinetry, quartz or granite counters, islands, backsplash tile and full layout changes. One point of contact and one schedule cover cabinets, counters, tile and electrical from demo day to the final walkthrough.

image.alt: Remodeled kitchen with white shaker cabinets, wood island with open shelving, quartz counters and gray tile floor

faq.h2: Sacramento Bathroom Remodel Questions

items.q: How long does a bathroom remodel take?
items.a: Most full bathroom projects finish in 5 to 8 weeks, depending on scope, and smaller conversions can be faster. Most shower and bathtub replacements are done in just a few days. With the On-Time Promise, you get $100 back for each day the project runs late.

items.q: What does the 3-year warranty cover?
items.a: Thrive offers a 3-year warranty on its installation workmanship with no questions asked. If something is not right with the installation after your remodel, the team will make it right, fast, fair and hassle-free. That promise covers both bathroom and kitchen projects, giving you peace of mind long after the final walkthrough.

items.q: Do you pull permits?
items.a: Yes. Thrive handles the required permits and follows local building codes on your behalf. On its Carmichael page, the company notes it manages all Sacramento County permits so homeowners do not have to deal with that paperwork themselves. Ask during your consultation which permits your project needs.

items.q: Will the materials hold up to Sacramento's hard water?
items.a: Thrive uses durable, nonporous surfaces that resist mold, mildew and the hard water buildup common in the Sacramento area. That means less scrubbing and a shower or vanity that keeps looking new, which matters in a busy family bathroom used many times a day.

items.q: Is the consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Thrive offers a free in-home consultation with no obligation. The team looks at your space, talks through how you use it and what bothers you, and gives you straightforward pricing before any work begins. Call (916) 308-4575 or send the quote form to book.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Norwell, MA, Designed and Built by One Team
hero.subheadline: Transitions is a family-owned design-build firm. Its own employees handle design, demolition, carpentry and installation, and founder Craig Ricciarelli prices every remodel himself before you sign.
trust_badges: Free visit, measure and first design

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Norwell MA project: white perimeter cabinets, a deep navy island, leather counter stools and glass pendant lights

intro.h2: The people who draw it are the people who build it
paragraphs: Transitions has handled kitchen remodeling in Norwell, MA and across the South Shore since 2006. Many firms call themselves design-build and then hand the job to subcontractors. Here, design, material selection, project management, demolition, carpentry and installation are all done by Transitions employees.

The licensed trades, plumbing, electrical and tile, come from the same crews on every job, and they have worked with the firm for years. Craig Ricciarelli, the founder, still estimates each remodel himself before the contract. Because one team owns the design and the build, the full scope is priced up front and change orders are rare and the budget holds.

services.h2: Four ways to work with Transitions

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Floor plans, elevations and 3D renderings, then demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, tile, cabinets and finish carpentry by the in-house team. A dedicated project manager handles permits and inspections, with daily cleanup and dust containment. The team has completed more than 800 kitchens.

image.alt: Two-tone Milton, MA kitchen with an Indigo navy Mouser island, white Divinity perimeter cabinets and brass hardware

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, hall and family baths, powder rooms and new bathroom additions. The team redesigns from the studs out or refreshes the existing footprint, covering layout, shower and tub design, vanities, tile and stone, plumbing fixtures, lighting and mirrors. More than 400 bathrooms are complete.

image.alt: Braintree, MA primary bath with a rift sawn white oak floating vanity, Arctic White quartz and LED mirrors

items.name: First Floor Remodels
items.blurb: For homes remodeled piece by piece over the years, the whole main level is designed as one: kitchen, baths, mudroom, pantry and laundry, with bump-outs where needed. One designer and project manager stay with you from the first sketch to the final walkthrough.

image.alt: Marshfield, MA first floor remodel with a white quartz island, leather counter stools, white oak pantry cabinets and a linear pendant

items.name: Custom Cabinetry, Supplied or Installed
items.blurb: Working with your own contractor? Transitions can design your kitchen and deliver the cabinetry, countertops and hardware, or supply and install them. Lines include Mouser, Tedd Wood and Diamond. Local builders use the same service through the firm's Builder Partnership Program.

image.alt: Builder partnership kitchen in Norwell, MA with walnut base cabinets, glass-front gray uppers and white subway tile

why_choose_us.h2: What sets this South Shore firm apart

items.title: The founder prices your job
items.text: Craig Ricciarelli estimates every remodel himself before you sign and stays involved from the first showroom visit to the final walkthrough. Reviewers note he is quick to answer a phone call.

items.title: Employees, not a rotating cast of subs
items.text: Design, project management, demolition, carpentry and installation are done by Transitions staff. The crew has worked together for over ten years, so the people who built your neighbor's kitchen build yours.

items.title: A line-item budget before the contract
items.text: You see a complete design, full material selections and a detailed line-item budget, with the timeline set, before you sign anything. Clients describe pricing that is clear, with no hidden costs.

items.title: Recognized on the South Shore
items.text: South Shore Magazine gave Transitions its Star of Excellence in 2024 and 2025, and the firm was named Best Bathroom Remodeler in the 2024 Best of the South Shore awards.

about.h2: A Norwell family business since 2006
about.text: Craig Ricciarelli has run his own businesses for nearly 40 years. He founded Transitions in 2006 and still oversees every project that comes through the door. Linda Ricciarelli handles accounting, payroll and job costing, and Nick Ricciarelli came back to the family business from a career in tech to run operations. Designers John Donahue, a Braintree native designing kitchens since 1999, Karen King, with the firm since 2008, and Scituate native Veronica Dee Amelang guide selections, while project manager PJ Mottola runs the build. Clients return for second projects and refer friends.

image.alt: Craig Ricciarelli, founder of Transitions Kitchens, Baths and Remodeling in Norwell, MA

process.h2: Free through design, then one team builds it

steps.title: Showroom visit
steps.text: Tour 5,000 square feet of displays, meet your designer and compare cabinets, counters, tile and fixtures side by side. The visit is free.

steps.title: In-home measure
steps.text: Your designer measures your space, confirms the scope and photographs site conditions. This step is also free.

steps.title: Design and budget appointment
steps.text: See initial concepts and a preliminary budget. A design agreement with a 5% deposit then secures your full design package.

steps.title: Final design and line-item budget
steps.text: The construction team reviews the design in your home, then you get a line-item budget and timeline before signing the contract.

steps.title: Build and walkthrough
steps.text: Permits, demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, cabinets, counters and trim follow in order, ending with a final punch list walkthrough.

service_area.h2: From Hingham to Plymouth and west to Wellesley
service_area.text: Transitions is based on Washington Street in Norwell and works with homeowners across the South Shore and Greater Boston. Crews are regularly in Hingham, Cohasset, Scituate, Marshfield, Duxbury, Hanover and Plymouth, and inland in Milton, Canton, Needham, Wellesley and Newton. Materials-only orders have gone as far as Martha's Vineyard. Not sure about your town? Call, because the team would rather talk about fit than turn you away by zip code.

faq.h2: Before you plan a South Shore remodel

items.q: Is the first showroom visit really free?
items.a: Yes. Your first showroom visit and conversation cost nothing and carry no obligation, and the in-home measure and first design and budget meeting are free too. You pay a 5% design deposit only when you sign the design agreement, so you see a full estimate before any real commitment.

items.q: How far ahead should I start planning a kitchen?
items.a: Transitions recommends reaching out 2 to 3 months before your ideal start date. Design, material selection and ordering all take time, and cabinets and other materials can have long lead times. Starting early makes for a smoother schedule once construction begins.

items.q: Do I need an appointment to visit the Norwell showroom?
items.a: No. Walk-ins are welcome Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 5:00 pm and Saturday 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Booking ahead just makes sure a designer is free to give you full attention. After you send the online form, you can pick a showroom time right away.

items.q: Can I buy cabinets only and use my own contractor?
items.a: Yes. With the materials-only service, Transitions designs the kitchen, selects and orders cabinetry, countertops and hardware, inspects them and delivers to your home. You or your contractor install. A materials-and-installation option adds installation by the Transitions team without the full remodel.

items.q: Do you build additions with a kitchen or bath?
items.a: Smaller additions and bump-outs, yes, especially when they support a kitchen or bath layout already being remodeled. A Marshfield family moved its pantry and laundry into a new rear addition to bring light into the kitchen. Larger additions are taken case by case, usually as part of a bigger remodel.

final_cta.h2: Come see it in person on Washington Street
final_cta.text: Call (781) 871-0881 or stop by 433 Washington St in Norwell, and meet a designer the same day.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in St. Paul for Homes With Character

intro.h2: Old houses, new kitchens, one team
paragraphs: Wise Design & Remodel is a design-build firm for kitchen remodeling in St. Paul and across the Twin Cities, with its office and showroom at 2327 Wycliff Street. The firm specializes in homes with character, from century-old Craftsmen to 1920s Tudors, keeping original woodwork and charm while making the kitchen fit how you live now.

Design, architecture, project management and carpentry sit under one roof. You handle cabinet doors, hardware, flooring and fixtures in the showroom before you choose, and a client portal shows your schedule, plans, contracts and financials day by day. Kitchens are the most common project Google reviewers mention.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in St. Paul, plus baths and lower levels

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Space planning, 3D renderings, custom cabinetry and final installation are all handled in-house. The team balances historic details, like original woodwork in a Craftsman, with modern appliances and storage. The portfolio runs from a Kenwood Scandinavian kitchen to the Hale Tudor family kitchen and the Montcalm whole-home kitchen in St. Paul.

image.alt: Montcalm whole-home kitchen remodel in St. Paul with white cabinets, glass-front uppers, subway tile and a cherry island

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites, guest baths and powder rooms, with layout, plumbing, cabinetry, tile and lighting planned together. Popular features include glass walk-in showers, freestanding tubs and heated tile floors, a comfort Minnesota winters reward. The firm is especially at home in older bathrooms where character matters.

image.alt: Lake Nokomis primary bathroom remodel with sage green walls, a floating wood double vanity, backlit mirrors and a brass towel warmer

items.name: Basement Remodeling
items.blurb: Lower levels turned into family lounges, guest suites with private baths, home gyms with saunas, wet bars and home offices. Past projects include a Highland Park basement retreat, a basement bar and sauna, and a Shoreview golf and fitness basement, all designed to feel like part of the house.

image.alt: Finished basement home gym with a cedar infrared sauna, treadmill and exercise bike in a St. Paul area home

items.name: Whole Home and Living Spaces
items.blurb: When several rooms no longer fit, one coordinated plan covers design consultation, space planning, material selections, 3D visualization, construction planning and installation. The Montcalm whole-home remodel in St. Paul and the South Lake Owasso multi-room remodel show how kitchens, baths and living areas can be redone together.

image.alt: Montcalm whole home remodel in St. Paul showing a refinished front hall, white staircase and view into the living room

why_choose_us.h2: What sets this St. Paul team apart

items.title: An architect on staff
items.text: Architect Jason Miskowiec has over 15 years of residential design experience and a Master's in Architecture from the Illinois Institute of Technology. He works beside the designers and builders on your plans.

items.title: A showroom you can touch
items.text: The Wycliff Street showroom carries Zonavita and Decor cabinets, Karndean flooring, Warmup floor heat and Top Knobs hardware, plus a working kitchen with taps from neighborhood breweries.

items.title: A portal for every project
items.text: Project management software shows which trades are coming, any schedule change, and your contracts, plans, scope of work and financials in one place, updated daily.

items.title: Recognized and licensed

about.h2: From North London row houses to Twin Cities bungalows
about.text: Philip Hide was born and raised in North London, where he started his own remodeling business. Many homes there date from the 1800s, so Phil learned to design smart, creative fixes for old houses without losing their charm. He met his wife, Julianne, while she was studying abroad in London. They married in 2007, lived in London for 9 years and moved their family to Minneapolis in 2014, where Phil founded Wise Design soon after. Today he is the founder and general contractor, and Julianne runs the showroom as a design consultant.

image.alt: The Wise Design & Remodel team together at the St. Paul office and showroom

process.h2: How a Wise Design remodel comes together

steps.title: Start with a conversation
steps.text: Most projects begin with a talk with founder Phil about what you love about your home and what no longer works.

steps.title: Design and space planning

service_area.h2: St. Paul neighborhoods and Twin Cities suburbs we serve
service_area.text: The office and showroom sit on Wycliff Street in St. Paul, and most work happens in St. Paul and Minneapolis. The firm names Highland Park, Union Park, Macalester-Groveland, Summit-University and Summit Hill among its regular St. Paul neighborhoods. Portfolio projects also come from Lake Nokomis, Kenwood, Edina, Shoreview and South Lake Owasso, so call if your home is nearby and you are not sure.

faq.h2: Questions about a St. Paul kitchen remodel

items.q: Can you update my kitchen without losing my older home's character?
items.a: That is the firm's specialty. Founder Phil Hide learned his trade on 1800s houses in London, and the team routinely works in Craftsmen, Tudors and other character homes around St. Paul. Original woodwork and details are kept where they matter, while the layout, cabinetry and appliances are brought up to date.

items.q: Do you design the kitchen or only build it?
items.a: Both. Wise Design & Remodel is a design-build firm with a general contractor, an architect, kitchen and bath designers, project managers and carpenters on staff. Space planning, 3D renderings, custom cabinetry and installation are handled in-house, so you are not coordinating a separate designer and builder yourself.

items.q: Can I see materials before I choose them?
items.a: Yes. The showroom at 2327 Wycliff Street, Suite 110 has cabinetry, countertops, hardware, flooring, shades and fixtures to see and touch, from lines such as Zonavita, Decor, Karndean, Warmup, Top Knobs, Fleurco and Nantucket Sinks. The firm is a dealer for several of them.

items.q: How will I know what is happening during construction?
items.a: Every client gets access to the firm's project management software. It shows which contractors are expected on site, flags any schedule change, and keeps your contracts, plans, scope of work and financials in one hub. Reviewers also mention clear communication and quick answers when issues came up.

items.q: Are you licensed in Minnesota?
items.a: Yes. Wise Design & Remodel holds Minnesota License # BC738242, printed on every page of its site. It is also a BBB A+ Accredited Business, an EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm, and a member of NARI Minnesota and the NKBA, with Best of Houzz awards for 2024 through 2026.

final_cta.text: Call (612) 849-2515 or tell us about your project, and plan a visit to the Wycliff Street showroom to start your design with Phil and the team.

From the owner
Drafty doors and windows in Michigan homes, and why they show up every fall - The first cold morning of October tells you a lot about your house. You notice the chill by the front door, the curtain that moves on its own and the bedroom that never quite warms up. Drafty doors and windows are the most common comfort complaint we hear from Southeast Michigan homeowners, and most of them can be fixed with carpentry rather than a replacement quote. Our draft sealing service exists because the fix is usually smaller than people fear. This guide walks through every place cold air gets past a door or a window, what you can check yourself on a Saturday and what calls for a trained set of hands. It covers entry doors, storm doors, patio doors, double-hung sashes, sills, trim and the caulk lines that hold it all together. When a section points to a job our Wright’s Repairs division handles, we link to it so you can see exactly what the visit includes. We are a design-build firm based in Ypsilanti, and over the years our crews have worked in older plaster-wall homes in Ann Arbor, postwar ranches in Westland and newer colonials in Canton. The draft problems look different in each, but the causes repeat. Worn seals, doors that moved out of square, sills that rotted from the bottom and caulk that gave up years ago account for nearly everything we find on a winterizing visit for Michigan homes. How Michigan housing stock shapes the problem...

hero.h1: Design-Build Remodeling in Ann Arbor, From Sketch to Last Coat
hero.subheadline: Wright's Renovations designs, prices and builds kitchens, baths, basements and additions out of its Ypsilanti shop. One project manager stays with your house from contract to warranty visit.

image.alt: Design-build remodeling Ann Arbor area kitchen by Wright's Renovations: navy cabinets, white quartz counters, gray subway tile backsplash and stainless appliances

intro.h2: Renovation without the runaround
paragraphs: Wright's Renovations offers design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti and four more Southeast Michigan counties. Design, permits, construction and finish work stay under one roof. Six specialized crews work out of one shop on Platt Road, and every house gets one project manager from contract to the warranty visit.

The team plans around the age of your house. Pre-1920 homes in the Old West Side bring balloon framing and knob-and-tube wiring. Royal Oak bungalows often need a flush beam to open the kitchen, and 1960s ranches may hide aluminum branch wiring. Those known issues go into the proposal from the start instead of turning up later as change orders.

services.h2: Design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, room by room

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full gut renovations, layout reworks and kitchen additions, starting from $75K. Cabinet orders go in the week you sign selections, so the longest-lead item never holds up the build. Most kitchens take 6 to 10 weeks, and recent ones run from Ann Arbor to Belleville.

image.alt: Remodeled kitchen with navy island, white quartz top, wood and leather stools, brass faucet and a single pendant light

items.name: Bathroom Renovation
items.blurb: Primary suites, wet rooms and half baths, from $40K. Every shower pan sits on a bonded membrane and gets a flood test before tile goes up. Heated floors are a common add in Michigan. Bathrooms carry a five-year craftsmanship warranty.

image.alt: Dexter, MI bathroom remodel with green wall tile, brass fixtures, soaking tub and wood vanity

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Family rooms, theaters, in-law suites, wet bars and steam showers, from $70K. Before framing, the crew checks the perimeter drain, the sump and the grade outside. Any basement bedroom gets a code-compliant egress window cut in.

image.alt: Finished basement home theater with sectional sofa and wall-mounted TV built by Wright's Renovations

items.name: Home Additions
items.blurb: Second-story builds, primary suite additions, ADUs and in-law suites, from $185K, with engineered drawings and full permitting handled. In-law suites with a first-floor bath are the fastest-growing request across all six counties the firm serves.

image.alt: Ann Arbor, MI home office addition with deep green walls and a desk by the window

items.name: Decks and Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Composite and hardwood decks, three-season rooms and covered patios, from $45K. Footings go below the frost line, and framing is sized for Michigan snow load rather than for the 70-degree day it was built on.

image.alt: Composite deck and patio with outdoor dining set beside a navy blue sided house

items.name: Whole-Home Renovation
items.blurb: Down-to-studs rebuilds, historic restoration and full-floor reworks, from $350K. Work is phased so families can often stay home. On Craftsman and Victorian houses around Ann Arbor, the crew mills trim profiles to match what is already there.

image.alt: Plymouth Township, MI whole-home renovation with new hardwood floors, oak and metal railings and an open kitchen

why_choose_us.h2: Why six-figure clients sign with Wright's

items.title: A fixed number before the contract
items.text: You get a fixed-scope proposal with line-item materials and labor before you sign. Change orders run under 5%, and most projects close at the original signed number.

items.title: See it before demolition
items.text: An in-house designer measures your home, builds 3D renderings and sources materials as part of the scope. You see the finished room and every line item before you commit.

items.title: Daily photos in JobTread
items.text: Your project manager posts site photos to JobTread every day, along with the schedule, documents and invoices. You can check progress from a meeting without making a phone call.

items.title: A clean, livable house
items.text: Zip-wall dust barriers, ram board floor protection and daily cleanup come on every job. Google reviewers call out the punctual crew and the tidy workspace.

about.h2: Started at 19 with one pickup truck
about.text: Connor Wright founded Wright's Renovations in 2021 at age 19, with one pickup truck. More than 550 projects later, the company ranked No. 610 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 and No. 2 in Ann Arbor. Connor is still the founder who walks sites and answers the phone. He also says no to a finish that will look dated before the warranty runs out. Will Sujek, Chief Revenue Officer since 2021, runs discovery calls and proposals. Katherine Anderson, Chief Administrative Officer since 2024, handles permits and insurance certificates. Clients name crew leads Charles and Chile and designers MacKenzie and Nick in their reviews.

process.h2: Four phases, documented the same way every time

steps.title: Week 1: Discovery call
steps.text: A working call about scope, budget and what the space must do. If your number and wish list do not meet, you hear it then.

steps.title: Weeks 2 to 3: Design and proposal
steps.text: In-home measure, 3D renderings, material selections and a fixed-scope proposal with real numbers, so you see the room and every line item first.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Zip walls up, ram board down and daily photos in JobTread. Permits are pulled on every job, and Wright's deals with the building department.

steps.title: Walkthrough and warranty
steps.text: Punch list, final inspection, care guide and warranty packet. Your one-year warranty visit is booked before the last truck leaves the driveway.

service_area.h2: About an hour from the Platt Road shop
service_area.text: Every crew leaves from one building at 7101 Platt Rd in Ypsilanti. The firm draws its line at about an hour on the road, so a crew that leaves at 6:45 is working by 8:00. Washtenaw County is home base. Wayne County runs about 25 minutes out, Livingston 30, Oakland 45 and Macomb 55. Monroe is about 25 minutes away. The company holds its license in all six counties.

faq.h2: What Ann Arbor homeowners ask before signing

items.q: What does a kitchen or bathroom remodel cost with Wright's?
items.a: The company publishes starting points. Kitchens start from $75K, bathrooms from $40K, basements from $70K, decks and outdoor work from $45K, additions from $185K and whole-home renovations from $350K. Your actual number comes as a fixed-scope proposal with line-item materials and labor after the in-home measure and design phase.

items.q: How long will my kitchen take?
items.a: Wright's lists a 6 to 10 week build timeline for kitchens. Before that, the discovery call happens in week one, and design and the proposal take weeks two and three. Cabinet orders go in the week you sign your selections, so the long-lead item does not hold up the schedule.

items.q: What happens if you find a problem behind the walls?
items.a: When a wall hides something, you get photos, three priced fixes and a recommendation within 24 hours. Known issues for your era of house are written in up front. For example, aluminum branch circuits in mid-1960s to early-1970s homes get pigtailed with approved connectors as a proposal line item, not a change order.

items.q: My house is in an Ann Arbor historic district. Can you still work on it?
items.a: Yes. Exterior changes inside Ann Arbor's historic districts go to the Historic District Commission before the building department, and Wright's budgets four to eight weeks for that review. The team designs to the commission's expectations from the start instead of appealing later, and mills trim to match original profiles on older houses.

items.q: Will you take a small job, like a door or a drywall patch?
items.a: Yes, through Wright's Repairs, a separate division with its own technicians and van under the same builder's license. Repairs are quoted in writing from photos and a short video, with a not-to-exceed ceiling. Each job gets before and after photos and one year on workmanship. It covers about 30 minutes from the Ypsilanti shop.

final_cta.h2: Book your discovery call
final_cta.text: Call Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm, or request a free consultation. You will get a straight answer on scope and budget on the first call.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Houston You Can Plan in Our Showroom
hero.subheadline: Your Dream Remodeling designs and builds bathrooms and kitchens from its Showroom and Design Center at 1718 N Fry Rd. You hold the tile and open the vanity drawers before anything is ordered.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Houston project with a frameless glass walk-in shower, marble-look porcelain tile, charcoal vanity and stone-look floor

intro.h2: Design first, then build, from one Houston team
paragraphs: Your Dream Remodeling has handled bathroom remodeling in Houston and nearby cities since 2010, according to its About page. The company began with one idea: design the room around the family before anyone talks about demolition. Design consultants meet you at home or at the N Fry Rd showroom, where you compare tile, quartz and vanities in person.

Every proposal names the waterproofing system, lists each fixture by brand and model, and includes permits where required. If the crew finds hidden damage behind a wall, they show you and price it before doing the extra work. A production manager checks each stage, and you get warranty paperwork at the end.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Houston, plus kitchens and floors

items.name: Walk-In Showers and Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: Custom walk-in showers with benches, niches, frameless glass and low or curbless entries, built over the Schluter-KERDI waterproofing system. One reviewer had a standing shower and Jacuzzi tub turned into a zero curb walk-in shower, finished within the estimated time.

image.alt: Walk-in shower with gold-veined porcelain tile, corner bench, black shower panel and frameless glass

items.name: Master Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Bigger showers, double vanities, freestanding tubs and better storage, planned as one room instead of separate upgrades. You choose custom vanities, quartz tops and lighting at the showroom with your designer, and the in-house crew builds it.

image.alt: Master bath with two charcoal shaker vanities, quartz tops, black-framed mirrors and a glass shower between them

items.name: Aging-in-Place Bathrooms
items.blurb: The CAPS certified team designs curbless showers, installs walk-in tubs and adds grab bars, seats and slip-resistant floors. One client needed a master bath made ADA friendly, and a Jacuzzi tub he could not get out of became a wheelchair accessible walk-in shower.

image.alt: Bathroom with a long gray vanity, white quartz top, black faucets and a glass-enclosed shower with marble-look tile

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Layouts and work zones, custom and semi-custom cabinetry, quartz and stone counters, backsplash tile and layered lighting, priced as one system before construction. One client's total kitchen remodel included removing a load bearing wall, adding beams, a large island and a new pantry.

image.alt: High-gloss white kitchen with a veined charcoal quartz island, stainless chimney hood and linear pendant lights

items.name: Flooring, Countertops and Custom Cabinets
items.blurb: Smaller projects stand on their own too: all types of flooring, countertop replacement, tile and custom cabinetry. Brands installed include Silestone and Dekton surfaces, Wilsonart, J&K Cabinetry, Wolf Cabinetry, and Emser and American Olean tile.

image.alt: Open family room with gray wood-look plank flooring, tray ceiling, ceiling fan and a marble-look fireplace wall

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons Houston homeowners choose Your Dream Remodeling

items.title: A showroom you can visit
items.text: The Showroom and Design Center at 1718 N Fry Rd, Suite 330, is open Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM. You walk full displays and compare cabinet doors side by side.

items.title: In-house crew, licensed trades
items.text: The firm's own crew does the remodeling. Where required, plumbing goes to plumbers licensed by the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners and electrical to TDLR-licensed electricians.

items.title: Written warranty, no deductible
items.text: Labor is covered by a one-year craftsmanship warranty on work done with materials the firm supplies, with no deductible. Installed brands also carry their own manufacturer warranties.

items.title: Recognized and reviewed
items.text: The firm won Best of Houzz in 2023 and an Angie's List Super Service Award in 2020, holds 4.9 stars from 89 Google reviews, and belongs to NAHB, GHBA and NTCA.

about.h2: Led by Ike Dadabhoy, built around design
about.text: Ike Dadabhoy is President of Your Dream Remodeling, and his writing on remodeling ran in the Houston Chronicle on September 25, 2022. The company started in 2010 because too many remodels looked fine in a brochure but were never designed for the family living in them. It grew from a small Houston team into a firm with its own Showroom and Design Center. Reviewers mention Ike by name for tracking down a hard-to-find tile, and Garrett for detailed quotes and renderings delivered on the date he promised.

steps.text: Reach the office at (281) 550-8900 during business hours, or book a visit online. Bring photos, ideas and room sizes if you have them.

steps.title: Free in-home visit
steps.text: A design consultant measures the room, checks plumbing and existing conditions, and talks through your goals and budget.

service_area.h2: Seven Greater Houston cities, one N Fry Rd showroom
service_area.text: Your Dream Remodeling works across Greater Houston from its showroom in the 77084 zip code. Bear Creek and Park Ten are under ten minutes away, Katy and the Energy Corridor about 10 to 20 minutes, and Fort Bend cities about 25 to 35. Scheduling moves fastest closest to the showroom. The About page lists the seven core cities below, and Google posts add Fulshear.

faq.h2: Houston bathroom remodel questions

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost in Houston?
items.a: The firm publishes planning ranges, not quotes. A 5x8 hall bath typically runs $8,000 to $15,000, an 8x10 guest bath $14,000 to $25,000, a 10x10 small master $18,000 to $35,000, and a full master suite $30,000 to $75,000 or more. Moving plumbing, tile, custom vanities and glass drive the final number.

items.q: Is the consultation free?
items.a: Yes. The first in-home visit is free. A design consultant measures the room, checks plumbing and existing conditions, and talks through your goals and budget. You can also bring ideas, photos and room dimensions to the showroom for free help with design and planning before you commit to anything.

items.q: What warranty do I get?
items.a: Your Dream Remodeling gives a one-year workmanship warranty on labor for work done with materials it supplies, and the site says there is no deductible. Products such as Silestone, Schluter-KERDI, J&K Cabinetry and Emser tile carry their own manufacturer warranties. Full terms are on the firm's warranty page.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. The site says financing is available for qualified homeowners, with monthly payment plans and zero-interest promotional periods for approved credit. Ask about current offers at your free consultation, since terms change over time and approval depends on your credit.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom safer for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. The team is CAPS certified and designs curbless or low-threshold showers, installs walk-in tubs, and adds grab bars, shower seats, handheld heads, comfort-height toilets and slip-resistant floors. Curbless showers need careful slope and drain planning, which is worked out during design.

final_cta.text: Call (281) 550-8900, Monday to Friday from 9 AM to 6 PM, or book a free in-home visit online. Saturday showroom visits are by appointment.

From the owner
Why the most detailed bid often matters more than the lowest one A local costumer recently left Alpha General Construction a 5-star review after we converted his shower and tub area into a true wet room. From the finished space, the project may look straightforward. Behind the walls and below the floor, it required demolition, framing adjustments, slab work for a zero-curb entry, drain relocation, waterproofing, tile, plumbing, electrical, drywall, paint, and careful coordination between each phase. That is why a contractor should not be chosen by price alone. The lowest bid may exclude important steps that return later as change orders. The highest bid is not automatically the best value, either. What matters is whether the proposal clearly explains the work: what is included, what is excluded, who supplies materials, how waterproofing will be completed, how hidden conditions are handled, and what warranty supports the finished project. The number matters, but the scope behind the number matters more. A detailed proposal creates accountability before construction begins and gives the homeowner a fair way to compare contractors. We are truly grateful to all our customers for trusting our team and for the 5-star reviews. Planning a bathroom remodel in Midland or Odessa? Compare the details—not just the total. intro.h2: One owner, one written scope, every room
paragraphs: Alpha General Construction offers bathroom remodeling in Midland, TX, along with kitchens and whole-home renovations. Owner Joel Gomez manages each project himself, from reviewing the property and writing the scope to coordinating trades and walking the finished work with you.

Joel also writes Alpha's Behind the Build advice column, and his message is steady: compare the details, not just the total. Your written scope spells out the work, the selections and who is responsible for what, so the price you approve matches the job you get. One wet-room client noted that Alpha gave the highest quote, but it was worth it.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Midland, TX, plus kitchens and whole homes

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Full bathroom renovations that cover shower and tub layout, waterproofing and tile, vanities and countertops, and the plumbing, ventilation and electrical behind them. Glass, fixtures and finish details are planned in the same written scope, so nothing is left to guesswork.

image.alt: Castor Residence bathroom in Midland with a double vanity and makeup desk, round backlit mirrors, wood storage towers and a freestanding tub

items.name: Wet Rooms and Curbless Showers

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Each kitchen starts with a review of the layout and existing conditions. From there the scope covers cabinetry and finish selections, countertops and backsplash, plumbing, electrical and appliance hookups, then flooring, paint and the final details.

items.name: Whole-Home Remodeling

why_choose_us.h2: Why Midland homeowners hire Alpha

items.title: The owner runs your job
items.text: Joel reviews the property, coordinates trades, talks through selections and keeps you informed until the last walkthrough. One reviewer wrote that Joel was great to work with and kept them very informed.

items.title: Showers built not to leak
items.text: Alpha builds the shower pan to code and flood-tests it, then applies a continuous surface waterproofing such as RedGard to walls, niche, bench and curb. Waterproofing is documented and backed by a written labor warranty.

items.title: Everything in writing
items.text: Your written scope defines the work, selections and responsibilities before construction starts, and changes are documented along the way. That gives you a fair way to compare Alpha against other bids.

items.title: Help with financing larger jobs
items.text: For bigger renovations, Alpha works alongside PrimeLending loan originator Stephanie Hecke. Alpha prepares the construction estimate your lender needs, while PrimeLending makes every credit decision.

about.h2: Meet Joel Gomez, owner and project manager
about.text: Joel Gomez owns Alpha General Construction and manages its projects personally. He reviews each property, writes the scope, coordinates the trades, talks through selections and stays involved through the final walkthrough. Under his full name, Joel Gomez Rivas, he writes Alpha's Behind the Build articles on comparing bids, planning a kitchen and the questions to ask before a shower demo. Alpha leans on trusted local partners, including Yates Flooring Center for tile and Ferguson for plumbing fixtures, so orders arrive right the first time. Reviewers describe Joel as nice, patient and good at keeping them informed.

image.alt: Joel Gomez, owner and project manager of Alpha General Construction in Midland, TX

process.h2: The Alpha approach in four steps

steps.title: A conversation
steps.text: Book a time online or call. You talk through your home, your priorities and what you want to change, with a rough budget and photos if you have them.

steps.title: A defined scope
steps.text: Existing conditions, selections, responsibilities and budget are worked out and written down, so you know what is included before work begins.

steps.title: A coordinated build
steps.text: Trades, materials, schedules and any changes are managed as one project, with Joel coordinating each phase and keeping you updated.

steps.title: A final walkthrough
steps.text: You and Joel review the agreed work together, and any completion items are addressed before the project is closed out.

service_area.h2: Remodeling homes in Midland, Texas
service_area.text: Alpha is rooted in Midland and currently accepts projects in Midland, Texas. Every project in its portfolio is a Midland home, from the Highland, Castor, Driftwood and Normandy bathrooms to the Wydewood, Humble, Ward and Farmhouse Road kitchens and the Michigan, Camarie and Ryburn whole-home remodels. When you book, have your project location, the rooms you want to change, a rough budget and any inspiration photos ready.

faq.h2: Questions to ask Alpha before you remodel

items.q: Can you turn my tub and shower into a wet room?
items.a: Yes. Alpha has converted a shower and tub area into a true wet room with a zero-curb entry. That work involved demolition, framing changes, slab work for the curbless entry, drain relocation, waterproofing, tile, plumbing, electrical, drywall and paint. Curbless designs need this planning up front, so it goes into your written scope.

items.q: How do you keep a new shower from leaking?
items.a: Alpha builds the shower pan to code and flood-tests it, then applies one continuous surface waterproofing system, such as RedGard, to the walls, niche, bench and curb. Tile is set with lasers and long levels. The waterproofing is documented, and the work is backed by a written labor warranty.

items.q: How should I compare remodeling bids?
items.a: Look past the total. A useful proposal states what is included and excluded, who supplies materials, how waterproofing will be done, how hidden conditions are handled and what warranty backs the work. The lowest bid can leave out steps that come back later as change orders.

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost in Midland?
items.a: Alpha's kitchen planning guide gives these ranges: semi-custom cabinets about $12,000 to $25,000 or more, custom from about $30,000, and quartz, granite or quartzite at $50 to $100 or more per square foot installed. Set aside 10 to 15 percent for surprises. A full kitchen typically takes 6 to 10 weeks.

items.q: Can I finance a larger renovation?
items.a: You can talk with PrimeLending loan originator Stephanie Hecke about renovation loan programs, where costs may be included in a purchase or refinance mortgage depending on the program. Alpha prepares the construction estimate and project details the lender asks for. PrimeLending makes all credit decisions, and Alpha does not.

final_cta.text: Call (432) 250-7940, Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, text Joel, or pick a consultation time online.

intro.h2: Three ways to change a kitchen, one shop on JVL Industrial Park Drive
paragraphs: Most homeowners call about kitchen remodeling in Marietta, but not every kitchen needs to be torn out. If the layout and cabinet boxes still work, Creative Cabinets and Fine Finishes can refinish them or reface them with new doors and drawer fronts. If the room needs to change, its design team plans a full remodel.

The difference is the shop. Professional sprayers work in a controlled paint booth, so finishes come out clean and smooth. An on-site CNC machine cuts custom cabinets, doors and drawer boxes in-house. On refacing jobs the doors and cabinet frames get the same paint, so they age the same way instead of a veneer peeling with heat and wear.

service_area.text: The shop and design center are at 4225 JVL Industrial Park Drive in Marietta. faq.h2: Refinish, reface or remodel: your questions

items.q: Should I refinish, reface or remodel my kitchen?
items.a: If the layout and cabinet structure still work, refinishing or painting gives a new look at a fraction of the cost of new cabinets. Refacing keeps the boxes but adds new doors, drawer fronts and hardware. If the layout itself is the problem, a full remodel with new cabinets and counters makes sense.

items.q: How is this different from hiring a painter?
items.a: CCFF has professional sprayers on staff and sprays in a controlled paint booth, which gives a clean, smooth finish. Over the years the team has tested many products and uses only the paints and stains it trusts for cabinets. It can also swap in new hardware or hinges as part of the job.

items.q: Will refaced doors match my cabinet frames?
items.a: Yes. Many refacing companies add veneers that can peel over time from heat and wear, leaving doors that no longer match. CCFF finishes both the doors and the cabinets with the same paint so they age together, and builds doors and drawer boxes in-house on its CNC machine.

items.q: Can you work with my own contractor?
items.a: Yes. If you already have a third-party contractor or handyman involved, CCFF will gladly work alongside that team. On full projects, a dedicated project manager communicates with you daily and keeps the workspace clean and organized so your home stays livable.

items.q: Do you come to my part of Atlanta?
items.a: Yes, most likely. The team works throughout metro Atlanta from its Marietta shop, including Kennesaw, Roswell, Alpharetta, Woodstock, Canton, Smyrna, Sandy Springs, Buckhead, Dunwoody and Decatur. Call (770) 693-1896 or book online to set up your first appointment and talk through what your kitchen or bath needs.

final_cta.text: Book an appointment and the CCFF team will tell you whether to refinish, reface or remodel.

intro.h2: New cabinet faces without the tear-out
paragraphs: Cabinet refacing in Wilmington, NC is the main service at Newberry Home Improvement, the parent company of Kitchen Restylers. Installers apply a new veneer to the fronts and sides of your existing cabinet boxes, then swap in new doors, drawer fronts and hardware. Your countertop and sink can stay where they are.

You choose from more than 50 colors and 15 door styles, and the work usually takes 1 to 2 days. The company says refacing can cost 25 to 50 percent less than new cabinets. The same crews also handle new cabinets, Silestone quartz counters, and tub and shower updates from its North Kerr Avenue showroom.

services.h2: Kitchen and bath work, most of it finished within a week

items.name: Cabinet Refacing and Restyling
items.blurb: A new factory-finish surface goes over your cabinet sides and fronts, and every door and drawer front is replaced to match. Trim, crown and shoe molding can be added. Most jobs take 1 to 2 days, and a free inspection tells you whether your cabinets qualify.

image.alt: Kitchen refaced in Shaker style doors in Fashion Grey and White Satin with a dark island and bar stools

items.name: New Cabinets
items.blurb: When refacing is not the right fit, Newberry tears out the old cabinets and installs new custom-made ones with soft-close hinges and glides. Add rollout shelves, trash rollouts or lazy Susans. New cabinets with a countertop can be done in as little as 3 days.

image.alt: Replacement cabinets in Cottage style White Satin with glass-front uppers and a granite island with stools

items.name: Tub to Shower Conversion
items.blurb: Your old bathtub comes out and a low-threshold acrylic shower pan and wall surround go in, in 2 days. Seating, shelving and grab bars can be added. Acrylic resists cracking, chipping and mildew, and it is easier to step into than a tub.

image.alt: Tub to shower conversion with Calcutta stone-look acrylic walls, a low-threshold pan and chrome grab bar

items.name: Shower and Tub Replacement
items.blurb: Replace an old, moldy or leaking shower or a dated tub with Bellastone acrylic in earth tones, white, subway or marble looks. Representatives bring samples to your home, and full-size displays of a few colors are set up in the showroom.

image.alt: Replacement shower with subway tile-look acrylic walls, a glass door and black grab bar

items.name: Full Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Start with the tub or shower, then add a vanity, vanity top, sink, faucet, flooring, wainscoting and toilet as a package. Most full bath remodels take 4 to 5 days. You can also do the shower first and the rest later to spread out the cost.

image.alt: Beach house bathroom remodel with a subway-look acrylic shower, sliding glass door, wood vanity and blue walls

items.name: Countertops, Sinks and Faucets
items.blurb: As an authorized Silestone provider, Newberry installs quartz and granite counters along with sinks, faucets and tile backsplashes. When you also reface or replace cabinets, one crew coordinates the whole install so your kitchen is out of use for less time.

image.alt: Complete kitchen remodel with Shaker style cabinets in Almond, new countertops and stainless appliances

why_choose_us.h2: Why Cape Fear homeowners call Newberry

items.title: Two days, with the water tested overnight
items.text: Newberry will not rush a bath into one day. Its employee installers and plumbers test the water overnight before finishing, which is why tub and shower installs take 2 days.

items.title: The price you hear is the price you pay
items.text: You get exact pricing up front, with no hidden or tacked-on charges, and you know the final price before work starts. One reviewer said Newberry had the best price of three quotes.

items.title: A 7-year warranty backed by labor
items.text: Work comes with a 7-year warranty. If a product turns out to be defective, Newberry matches the manufacturer's warranty with full labor coverage, so you are not billed for the crew's time.

items.title: Back-to-back local award
items.text: WECT named Newberry Best of the Cape Fear in Kitchen and Bath Remodeling for both 2024 and 2025. The company is also BBB Accredited and holds 5.0 stars across 242 Google reviews.

about.h2: Led by Barry Dyer, staffed by installers clients name
about.text: Owner Barry Dyer has spent more than three decades in home improvement. He runs Newberry Home Improvement as the parent company of Kitchen Restylers, and keeps the company focused on kitchens and baths. Showrooms in Wilmington and Myrtle Beach let you see door styles and shower colors in person. The crews are employees, and Google reviewers name them often: JT, Austin and Jacob on cabinets, Kevin on a master bath, and Michael and Eric on a tub-to-shower swap. Clients mention punctuality, tidy work areas and a walkthrough of the warranty at the end.

service_area.h2: Two showrooms covering coastal North and South Carolina
service_area.text: The Wilmington showroom on North Kerr Avenue serves southeastern North Carolina, from Wilmington up to Emerald Isle and New Bern and west to Lumberton. The Myrtle Beach office at 1732 US-501, (843) 970-2743, covers South Carolina from Florence to Murrells Inlet and up through Little River to Calabash. Wherever you live in that stretch of coast, a representative can bring door and shower samples to your home.

faq.h2: What Wilmington, NC homeowners ask about cabinet refacing

items.q: Can my cabinets be refaced?
items.a: Most kitchens can be refaced without major issues. Sometimes one cabinet has to be fixed or replaced. A Newberry kitchen expert inspects your cabinets for free during the in-home visit. If the savings over new cabinets would be small for your kitchen, the inspection is also where they tell you replacing is the better choice.

items.q: Why does a shower install take 2 days instead of 1?
items.a: Newberry does not want to be in a hurry. Its employee installers and plumbers want the water tested overnight before the job is finished, so a new tub or shower is installed over 2 days. The company sees that extra night as a check that protects your home, not a delay.

items.q: How long does a full bathroom remodel take?
items.a: Most full bathroom remodels with a new tub or shower, vanity, top, sink, faucet, flooring, wainscoting and toilet take 4 to 5 days. Large bathrooms can take a day or two longer. You can also have the tub or shower done first and the rest later to split up the cost.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. Financing is offered through Medallion Bank, with payments listed as low as $110 a month and other options available. Approval depends on credit, the loan terms are set directly between you and the lender, and rates vary with the size of the job. Ask about current terms at your consultation.

items.q: What does the warranty cover?
items.a: Projects are backed by a 7-year warranty. Newberry also matches the manufacturer's product warranty with a full labor warranty. If a product turns out to be defective, its suppliers trust Newberry to confirm the defect and replace the material, and you are not billed for the labor to swap it.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Puyallup, WA, Built Right Behind the Walls
hero.subheadline: Brad Zemke is a third-generation carpenter and Air Force veteran. His own crew handles demo, plumbing, waterproofing and tile, and you get a fixed price before work starts.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Puyallup WA: primary bath with a freestanding soaking tub, frameless glass corner shower, skylight and wood-look plank floor

intro.h2: The work behind the walls matters
paragraphs: Pacific Remodeling has offered bathroom remodeling in Puyallup, WA since Brad Zemke started the company in 2018, after five years as a B-52 crew chief in the Air Force. His grandfather and father were carpenters too. Brad says he has renovated hundreds of bathrooms across Pierce County, from 40-square-foot guest baths to 120-square-foot master suites.

What sets his bathrooms apart is the part you never see. Every shower gets a full waterproofing membrane, Schluter KERDI or equivalent, floor to ceiling, and it is inspected before tile goes on. His team does the demolition, plumbing, electrical, tile and finish work in-house, so no stranger subcontractors show up at your door.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Puyallup, WA, plus kitchens and counters

items.name: Full Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Master suites with dual vanities, soaking tubs and heated floors, plus hall baths and powder rooms. Brad publishes real ranges: about $16,000 to $35,000 and 2 to 3 weeks for a hall bath, and $33,000 to $72,000 and 4 to 6 weeks for a mid-range master bath.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with a white double vanity, quartz top, two framed mirrors with sconces and dark tile floor

items.name: Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: The most requested job: about 7 in 10 of Brad's bathroom remodels include one. The old tub comes out, the drain moves, and a custom tile walk-in shower goes in with niches and frameless glass. A standard conversion runs $10,000 to $24,000 and takes 1 to 2 weeks.

image.alt: Tub-to-shower conversion with marble-look porcelain walls, recessed niche, rain head and sliding frameless glass door

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Open layouts, real-wood cabinetry, quartz counters and new flooring. Brad prefers maple for painted cabinets because it resists warping in the damp Pacific Northwest. Cabinetry for a typical Puyallup kitchen with 25 to 35 linear feet runs about $20,000 to $56,000.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with sage green beadboard cabinets, herringbone marble backsplash, stainless hood and granite counters

items.name: Countertops
items.blurb: Granite, quartz, marble and butcher block, templated, cut and installed with tight seams and solid support. A straightforward replacement takes 2 to 3 weeks from consultation to install, and sinks and faucets are reconnected the same day so you have a working kitchen by evening.

image.alt: White shaker kitchen with speckled quartz counters, subway tile backsplash, open shelves and dark wood floor

why_choose_us.h2: Why Pierce County homeowners hire Brad

items.title: Prices on the page
items.text: Brad lists real cost ranges and timelines for powder rooms, hall baths, master baths and conversions, and his written proposal is fixed-price with every line item spelled out.

items.title: One crew, no strangers
items.text: Demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, tile and finish work are done by Pacific Remodeling's own crews, which means fewer scheduling gaps and one person accountable.

items.title: Waterproofing is not optional
items.text: Every shower gets a Schluter KERDI or RedGard membrane on every wall, floor, curb and niche. Brad has torn out five-year-old showers that leaked because someone skipped this step.

items.title: Reviewers trust Brad
items.text: Google reviewers mention Brad by name, a respectful crew and an easy process. One couple chose him after interviewing five companies for their bathroom remodel.

about.h2: Meet Brad Zemke, owner and carpenter
about.text: Brad Zemke comes from a family of carpenters: his grandfather and his father both worked the trade. He spent five years as a B-52 crew chief in the Air Force, then started Pacific Remodeling in Puyallup in 2018 and brought that same discipline to every job. With more than 20 years in the trades, Brad still runs projects himself and walks every finished room with the homeowner. His rule for every job is simple: if this were his mom's house, how would he want it done? Pacific Remodeling is licensed, bonded and insured in Washington.

image.alt: Brad Zemke, owner of Pacific Remodeling in Puyallup, WA

process.h2: From first call to final walkthrough

steps.title: Free in-home consultation
steps.text: Brad visits, measures and talks through what you want and what you can spend. It usually takes 45 to 60 minutes, with no sales pitch.

steps.title: Fixed-price proposal
steps.text: Within about a week you get a detailed proposal with materials, labor, scope and timeline spelled out line by line.

steps.title: Selections
steps.text: Brad helps you pick tile, vanity, fixtures, counters and hardware, and will visit showrooms with you if needed.

steps.title: Build with daily updates
steps.text: Dust barriers go up on day one. Rough-in and waterproofing are inspected before walls close, and the crew cleans up every day.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: Brad walks every inch of the finished room with you. If anything is not right, it gets fixed before the job is called done.

service_area.h2: Puyallup home base, all of Pierce County
service_area.text: Puyallup is home base, and Brad has done more projects here than anywhere else. The crew also works across Pierce County, from Tacoma's North End and West Side to newer homes around Lake Tapps and Bonney Lake, the growing developments in Sumner, larger lots in Edgewood and the neighborhoods of South Hill. The service menu also lists Orting, Buckley, University Place, Lakewood, Fife, Milton and Spanaway.

faq.h2: Puyallup bathroom remodel FAQs

items.q: How much does a bathroom remodel cost in Puyallup?
items.a: Brad's published ranges are $6,500 to $16,000 for a powder room, $10,000 to $29,000 for a tub-to-shower conversion, $16,000 to $35,000 for a full hall bath and $33,000 to $72,000 for a mid-range master bath. These include materials, labor, plumbing, electrical and finish work. Permits are extra when required.

items.q: How many weeks will we be without that bathroom?
items.a: A powder room update takes about 1 to 2 weeks and a tub-to-shower conversion 1 to 2 weeks. A guest or hall bath runs 2 to 3 weeks, and master baths take 4 to 8 weeks depending on whether the layout changes. Your proposal includes a timeline for your specific project.

items.q: Do I need a permit?
items.a: Layout, plumbing and electrical changes usually do. Brad pulls permits from the City of Puyallup and schedules the inspections. Permit fees typically run $250 to $800 and are added to the project price when required. Rough-in work and waterproofing are inspected before any walls are closed or tile is set.

items.q: Can Brad build a curbless shower for a parent or for later years?
items.a: Yes. Brad builds curbless, zero-threshold showers with a linear drain by recessing the shower pan into the subfloor, though some older homes need a slight ramp instead. He also adds solid wood blocking behind the drywall so grab bars can be mounted securely now or years later.

items.q: Is the estimate really free?
items.a: Yes. Brad comes to your home, measures, and talks through materials and budget at no cost and with no obligation. Within about a week you receive a written fixed-price proposal. Call (253) 392-9266, Monday through Saturday from 8 AM to 6 PM, to set a time.

final_cta.h2: Get a straight number on your bathroom
final_cta.text: Book a free in-home estimate and a fixed-price proposal within about a week.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling Blacksburg VA Homeowners Can Price Up Front
hero.subheadline: Renovations & Dependable Building is a small, locally owned design-build company led by Joey Ritenour. It takes a limited number of projects at a time and gives you a fixed price and defined scope before construction starts.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Blacksburg VA: Preston Forest primary bath with black double vanity, white quartz top, lighted mirror and sage walls

intro.h2: A small crew that stays close to every bathroom
paragraphs: Renovations & Dependable Building, also known as RenoDB, handles bathroom remodeling Blacksburg VA homeowners plan for, plus kitchens, basements and other spaces across the New River Valley. It is intentionally small. The company limits how many projects it runs at once, so Joey stays involved from planning and selections through the final walkthrough.

Bathrooms are the heart of the work: guest baths, primary suites and tubs swapped for walk-in showers in Blacksburg, Christiansburg and Riner. Prices are posted online from recent local jobs, and once the design is set you get a fixed price and a defined scope. Reviewers mention prompt replies, crews that show up when scheduled and a tidy job site.

services.h2: Remodeling services across the New River Valley

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Guest baths, primary suites and full layout changes, from tile, cabinetry and lighting to waterproofing and shower glass. Licensed plumbers and electricians join when required. Posted starting prices: $12,500 for a small bath, $24,000 for a mid-size bath and $46,000 for a large primary suite.

image.alt: Large walk-in shower with marble-look tile, built-in bench, grab bar and handheld shower in a Blacksburg primary bath

items.name: Kitchen Renovations
items.blurb: Layout planning, cabinetry, countertops, tile, lighting and appliance installation, managed as one plan with trusted local trade partners. Kitchens start at $55,000 for a small space, $85,000 for a mid-size kitchen with an island, and $125,000 for a large kitchen.

image.alt: Preston Forest kitchen remodel in Blacksburg with white shaker cabinets, stained wood island, marble-look counters and tile backsplash

items.name: Aging in Place Updates
items.blurb: Features that keep a home easy to use for years, built into projects you already want: walk-in showers with benches and grab bars, wider walkways and better lighting. In Pembroke, a new two-level deck was built with an accessible ramp alongside a kitchen remodel.
