why_choose_us.h2: Why Blacksburg and Christiansburg homeowners pick RenoDB

items.title: Prices before you call
items.text: The pricing guide lists starting costs for small, mid-size and large bathrooms and kitchens, based on recent jobs in the area. After design, you get a fixed price and a defined scope.

items.title: One point of contact
items.text: RenoDB works with the same vetted plumbers, electricians, tile setters and cabinet specialists project after project, and you deal with one person who coordinates them all.

items.title: Clean, respectful job sites
items.text: Drop cloths, shoe covers and daily clean-ups are standard. One Google reviewer said the crews showed up when scheduled and the project area was kept very neat and tidy.

items.title: Everything in one portal
items.text: Your JobTread customer portal holds updates, photos, estimates, change orders and invoices. You can sign proposals and make payments there without chasing emails.

about.h2: Meet Joey Ritenour and Ginny Ayers
about.text: Joey Ritenour is the owner and lead general contractor, with eight years of hands-on remodeling and construction experience. Before remodeling, he worked at Virginia Tech in hazardous materials management and lab inspection, which shaped his focus on safety and careful planning. He is a Virginia Tech graduate and a longtime member of the New River Valley community. Operations manager Ginny Ayers, who spent 14 years in Virginia Tech Alumni Relations, runs client communication, marketing and the systems behind each job.

image.alt: Joey Ritenour, owner of Renovations and Dependable Building in Blacksburg, VA

process.h2: How a RenoDB project runs

steps.title: 10-minute discovery call
steps.text: Book a short call online or call or text Joey. You talk through your goals, timeline and whether RenoDB is the right fit.

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: Joey visits to review your space, walk through ideas and budget, and outline the next steps for your project.

steps.title: Design and finalize
steps.text: Layouts and selections are settled with design partners such as Reico Kitchen & Bath and DeHart Tile Co., then you receive a fixed price and defined scope.

steps.title: Build and deliver
steps.text: A dedicated team manages construction, keeps the jobsite clean and posts updates to your JobTread portal as work moves forward.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: When the work is complete, you walk through everything together to make sure it meets your expectations before the job is closed out.

service_area.h2: Towns we serve in the New River Valley
service_area.text: RenoDB works throughout the New River Valley. Recent projects include primary baths in Blacksburg, Christiansburg and Riner, a basement hobby room in Radford, a guest bath in Christiansburg's Highland Park, and a 1919 Sears kit house kitchen in Pembroke. Pulaski and Shawsville are on the service list too. The company is now scheduling for late winter and early spring of 2027.

faq.h2: Bathroom remodeling Blacksburg VA questions, answered

items.q: How much does a bathroom remodel cost in the New River Valley?
items.a: RenoDB's pricing guide is based on its most recent local jobs. A small bathroom under 50 square feet starts at $12,500. A mid-size full bath of 50 to 80 square feet starts at $24,000. A large primary suite over 100 square feet, with room for a soaking tub and walk-in shower, starts at $46,000.

items.q: Will I know the final price before work starts?
items.a: Yes. Layouts, materials and finishes are settled during design, before construction begins. With that detailed plan in place, RenoDB gives you a fixed price and a defined scope of work. If you have a firm budget, share it up front so the team can suggest options that fit it.

items.q: Can you replace my tub with a walk-in shower?
items.a: Yes. Replacing an outdated tub with a walk-in shower is one of the bathroom projects RenoDB lists. In the Wyatt Farms bathroom in Blacksburg, an unused soaking tub made way for a spacious walk-in shower with Blue Onyx accent tile, a coordinating blue vanity and custom rolling glass.

items.q: How will I know what is happening during the project?
items.a: Every client gets a JobTread customer portal. It shows real-time updates, documents and photos, and holds estimates, change orders and invoices in one place. You can review and sign proposals and pay invoices there, and Joey remains your main point of contact the whole way through.

items.q: How do I get started, and when can you begin?
items.a: Schedule a 10-minute discovery call online, or call or text Joey at (540) 418-2130. You will get an email to pick a time, then a 10 to 15 minute call about your goals and timeline. The company is currently scheduling projects for late winter and early spring of 2027.

final_cta.h2: Talk with Joey about your bathroom
final_cta.text: Call or text (540) 418-2130, or book a 10-minute discovery call to see if RenoDB is the right fit for your home.

hero.h1: Kitchen and Bath Remodeling in Sarasota, FL, Planned in a Showroom

intro.h2: Design and construction under one Sarasota roof
paragraphs: S&W Kitchens offers kitchen and bath remodeling in Sarasota, FL from a design showroom on 5th Street in the Rosemary Design District. The company has worked in Florida since 1977 and now runs seven showrooms, from Winter Park to Tampa. In Sarasota, the design and construction teams share one building, so the people who draw your plan also build it.

The promise is predictability. Each project is mapped in a detailed Project Book, and the company reports that 96% of its projects finish on budget and on schedule. Cabinets are made in the USA, everyone who works in your home is background-checked, and 0% financing is available through trusted local lenders.

services.h2: Kitchen and bath remodeling in Sarasota, FL, plus the spaces around them

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Choose a refresh that keeps your layout, a full remodel that changes function and flow, or a luxury remodel. Designers show realistic renderings before construction, and your project manager coordinates S&W's in-house installers from demolition to the final tile.

image.alt: Clearwater kitchen remodel with warm wood shaker cabinets, a quartz island with seating and a wood-wrapped ceiling beam

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: From a tired hall bath to a primary suite that moves plumbing and expands the footprint. Recent work near Sarasota includes primary bath updates in Venice and Bradenton. Designers plan storage, lighting and tile, and the same team handles installation.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with natural wood vanity, dark green tile accent wall, freestanding tub and glass shower

items.name: Aging in Place
items.blurb: Designers with the Certified Aging-in-Place Specialist (CAPS) designation plan curbless showers, wider clearances and non-slip floors that still look good, so a forever home stays safe for decades. One Lock Street project paired a zero-entry shower with the tub.

image.alt: Aging-in-place bathroom with a zero-entry shower behind a black grid glass panel and a long vanity with a seated makeup area

items.name: Outdoor Kitchens
items.blurb: Covered outdoor kitchens built for Florida entertaining, with built-in grills, vent hoods, stone or tile backsplashes and bar seating. The Sarasota showroom page features one of these projects as an outdoor entertainer's space. S&W keeps a separate outdoor kitchen portfolio you can browse before you visit.

image.alt: Covered outdoor kitchen with built-in grill, blue stone backsplash, black vent hood and bar stools under a wood ceiling

items.name: Custom Cabinets and Closets
items.blurb: USA-made cabinetry in warm white oak, walnut or clean contemporary finishes, plus luxury lines from Poggenpohl and Bentwood. Closet designers plan wardrobes, islands and lighting around what you own, and laundry rooms and home bars are on the list too.

image.alt: Custom walk-in closet in Orlando with frosted glass-front wardrobes, a stone-topped island and a crystal chandelier

about.h2: The people behind the Sarasota design center
about.text: S&W Kitchens is family owned and operated and has served Florida homeowners since 1977. Joe Steenbeke Jr. leads the company as President and CEO. In Sarasota, Regional Manager Larissa Hicks heads a design center where designers, project managers and construction staff work side by side. The company has grown to seven showrooms and 33 national awards, yet it still runs each remodel as a team job: everyone who touches your home knows the plan, from first sketch to final walkthrough.

service_area.h2: Sarasota, Manatee and the barrier islands
service_area.text: The Sarasota showroom serves the metro area and communities through Southwest Florida, from Anna Maria and Holmes Beach down to Venice and North Port. Portfolio work spans coastal kitchens in West of Trail neighborhoods and bath updates in Venice and Bradenton. Six more S&W showrooms cover Tampa Bay, Orlando and the Space Coast, and the zip code on your estimate form routes you to the nearest designer.

faq.h2: What Sarasota clients ask before a remodel

items.q: When is the Sarasota showroom open?
items.a: The showroom at 1421 5th St is open Monday to Friday, 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, and Saturday, 10:00 am to 2:00 pm. It is closed Sunday. A designer is always on hand, but calling (941) 274-3552 ahead is the surest way to get a full sit-down about your project.

items.q: What does the free estimate include?
items.a: After you send the form, a designer reaches out within 1 to 2 business days. At your complimentary design consultation they measure your space, talk through your goals and style, and begin your free estimate and design plan. Your zip code helps route you to the closest showroom.

items.q: Can I finance a kitchen or bath remodel?
items.a: Yes. S&W has partnered with GreenSky to offer deferred-interest promotional plans and affordable monthly payments, and it works with trusted local lenders on 0% financing. Some clients use financing to finish several projects at once, which limits the disruption in the home.

items.q: Do you design bathrooms for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. S&W holds the Certified Aging-in-Place Specialist (CAPS) designation. Designers plan curbless showers, wider clearances and non-slip flooring that do not give up style, so a forever home stays safe and comfortable. The Lock Street project, for example, combined a zero-entry shower with a tub.

items.q: Where are your cabinets made?
items.a: S&W offers a wide selection of cabinets made in the USA, from warm white oak and walnut to contemporary finishes. For homeowners who want the finest materials, the company also works with the luxury brands Poggenpohl and Bentwood. You can compare styles and colors in the Sarasota design center.

final_cta.h2: See your new kitchen before it is built
final_cta.text: Call the Sarasota showroom at (941) 274-3552 or request a free estimate, and a designer will reply within 1 to 2 business days.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Pleasant View, TN, From Showroom to Install
hero.subheadline: Owner Mike Guthrie and his design team help you choose cabinets, countertops, tile and flooring in a 7,000 square foot showroom, then design and build the remodel or simply order the products.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Pleasant View TN: gray shaker cabinets, white subway tile backsplash, farmhouse sink and a quartz-topped island

intro.h2: Pick it in person, then let the same team build it
paragraphs: Guthrie Kitchen & Bath Plus offers kitchen remodeling in Pleasant View, TN from its own 7,000 square foot showroom on Industrial Drive. You can handle cabinets, countertops, plumbing fixtures, hardware, tile and flooring before you commit, and work through the layout with a designer on the spot.

Then you decide how much help you want. Services range from complete designs and end-to-end design/build to simply selecting and ordering products, and smaller updates like new countertops or a refreshed vanity are welcome. Guthrie is also the local authorized dealer for The Galley Ideal Workstation, with a full working display in the showroom.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Pleasant View, TN and the rooms beyond it

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Cabinetry, countertops, flooring, lighting and a layout that works, planned with a designer trained on 20/20 design software. When a dishwasher leak stripped one client's kitchen to the subfloor, Guthrie rebuilt it from flooring to countertops to electrical and plumbing.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with white shaker cabinets, a large white quartz island on a dark base, wood-look floor and stainless appliances

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Spacious showers, custom vanities and finishes you can see in the showroom first. A Springfield bath paired a freestanding tub with a custom alcove shower, Delta showerhead, recessed niche with glass shelves, built-in bench and green glass wall tile from Lia.

image.alt: Spa-style bathroom in Springfield, TN with a freestanding tub, blue-green glass subway tile shower and built-in linen shelves

items.name: Countertops
items.blurb: Granite, quartz, Corian, laminate, cultured marble, soapstone, butcher block, stainless steel, tile and glass. The team takes the mystery out of measurements, materials and money, and one client wrote that a free estimate from Guthrie made granite countertops affordable after all.

image.alt: Clarksville, TN kitchen with a speckled granite peninsula, white shaker cabinets, black range hood and navy counter stools

items.name: Multi-Space Remodeling
items.blurb: Projects that cross several rooms or add on to the house. One client's remodel covered two and a half baths, the kitchen, the dining room and the laundry, with walls opened up along the way. Guthrie coordinates the products and trusted subcontractors so every room finishes as one design.

image.alt: Primary bathroom from a multi-room remodel with white veined tile, a frameless glass shower enclosure, freestanding tub and dark wood vanity

items.name: Closets, Laundry Rooms and More
items.blurb: The design team works on any room that benefits from cabinetry, storage, lighting, flooring and an efficient layout. That includes walk-in closets and pantries, mudrooms, laundry rooms, garages, home offices, fireplace surrounds and outdoor spaces, with the same showroom products to choose from.

image.alt: Walk-in closet with light wood shelving, stacked drawers, an illuminated vanity mirror and a built-in seat

why_choose_us.h2: Why homeowners from Clarksville to Franklin come to Pleasant View

items.title: Touch it before you buy it
items.text: The 7,000 square foot showroom displays cabinets, countertops, tile, plumbing fixtures and hardware, plus a flooring store, so you choose with your own eyes instead of from a catalog.

items.title: An owner who knows cabinets
items.text: Mike Guthrie has worked in construction since 1982 and fell for cabinetry and countertops at a millwork company. Reviewers describe him as honest, detail-oriented and knowledgeable about granite.

items.title: Crews you can let in the house
items.text: Guthrie is a fully licensed contracting firm, and its employees and tradespeople are licensed, insured and have all passed background checks before they work in your home.

items.title: Start at any size
items.text: Swap a vanity, replace countertops or remodel several rooms at once. Free design consultations and available financing let you start the conversation where your budget is.

about.h2: Meet owner Mike Guthrie
about.text: Mike Guthrie went to work for a convenience store chain right after high school and rose from clerk to district manager within four years. In 1982 he moved into construction, and a winter job offer from the owner of a millwork company changed his direction: he was hooked on cabinetry, countertops and woodworking. Today he runs Guthrie Kitchen & Bath Plus from its Pleasant View showroom with designer Heather Dickson, who trained on 20/20 Design Software and is studying for NKBA certification, plus purchasing and accounting staff and a team of trusted subcontractors.

image.alt: Guthrie Kitchen & Bath Plus storefront and showroom entrance in Pleasant View, TN

process.h2: How a Guthrie remodel comes together

steps.title: Showroom consultation
steps.text: Start with a free design consultation at the Pleasant View showroom, talking through your needs, style and budget among real displays.

steps.title: A design that fits
steps.text: A designer works with you on layout and product selections to create a plan that realizes your vision and fits your needs and budget.

steps.title: Clear budget and communication
steps.text: You get effective communication through design and remodeling, including a transparent budgeting process, so you know what each choice costs.

steps.title: Installation to completion
steps.text: Guthrie's team and trusted subcontractors install your products and carry the project from concept to completion.

service_area.h2: Six Middle Tennessee counties, one Pleasant View showroom
service_area.text: Guthrie's showroom at 1040 Industrial Dr in Pleasant View sits in Cheatham County, and the team also works across Davidson, Robertson, Sumner, Montgomery and Williamson counties. faq.h2: Questions to ask before your showroom visit

items.q: Can I just buy cabinets or countertops from you?
items.a: Yes. Guthrie's services range from complete design and end-to-end design/build to simply selecting and ordering products. One Google reviewer bought cabinetry, countertops and flooring for a 1980s home and was pleased from start to finish. Tell the design team what you need and they will match the level of help to your project.

items.q: Is the design consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Guthrie offers free design consultations, and you can book one from any page of the site or by calling (615) 247-5091. You talk through the space, your style and your budget with the design team while looking at real cabinets, countertops, tile and fixtures on the showroom floor.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. Financing is available for kitchen, bath and other remodeling projects, and the showroom works with a home improvement loan partner. Ask about current terms during your free consultation so the budget conversation covers both the design you want and how you would like to pay for it.

items.q: Are your installers licensed and insured?
items.a: Yes. Guthrie describes itself as a fully licensed contracting firm, and its employees and tradespeople are licensed and insured and have all passed background checks. The company also lists NAHB and National Tile Contractors Association memberships and BBB accreditation among the organizations it works with.

items.q: Do you only work on kitchens and baths?
items.a: No. The team designs any space that benefits from cabinetry, storage, lighting, flooring and an efficient layout, including closets and pantries, mudrooms, laundry rooms, garages, home offices, fireplace surrounds and outdoor spaces. Partial updates count as well, such as new countertops, new flooring or a refreshed bathroom vanity.

final_cta.text: Visit 1040 Industrial Dr, Ste 114 in Pleasant View, Monday to Friday 8am to 5pm or Saturday 9am to 2pm, or call (615) 247-5091 to book a free design consultation.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Ventura, Drawn, Built and Finished by One Team
hero.subheadline: Jeff King has owned Kitchen Places since 1993. His designers draw your kitchen in CAD, and project managers supervise every install from the Callens Road showroom.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Ventura: Sea La Vie kitchen with walnut-stained Nickels cabinets, a Calacatta Gold quartz island, blue majolica tile range alcove and terracotta floor

intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Ventura that shows you the picture first
paragraphs: Kitchen Places has handled kitchen remodeling in Ventura since 1993 from its showroom at 1500 Callens Road. It is a full-service design-build firm, so the same team designs your kitchen and supplies and installs the cabinetry, countertops, plumbing, appliances, tile, flooring, lighting, glass and hardware.

Clients keep mentioning one thing: they saw the kitchen before it was built. One Ventura homeowner wrote that Jeff could create pictures of the proposed remodel, and her kitchen looked like the picture, only better. Then a detailed workflow chart shows when each stage starts and ends, so you know what to expect each day.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths and whole homes from Kitchen Places

items.name: Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: From a small galley to a full layout change with walls moved and plumbing relocated. One past client gained a walk-in pantry after the team moved plumbing and appliances in a 35-year-old kitchen. Cabinet lines include Nickels, Bellmont and Medallion.

image.alt: Simple + Serene kitchen in Ventura County with a rift-cut white oak island, honed quartzite counters, white cabinets and woven-seat counter stools

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and powder rooms, with tile, glass, plumbing fixtures and lighting chosen in the showroom. Radiant heating from WarmlyYours is available for floors, mirrors and towel racks. Repeat clients often come back for the bath after the kitchen.

image.alt: Scalloped Waves bathroom with a white clawfoot tub, teal fish-scale tile wall, wood bath caddy and a wall-mounted tub filler

items.name: Whole-House and Guest House Remodels
items.blurb: Kitchen Places brings designers, architects, engineers, craftsmen and technicians to larger projects. Its portfolio includes a coastal guest house, living rooms, laundry rooms and multi-room remodels that tie the kitchen and baths together into one consistent look.

image.alt: Coastal Guest House kitchen with a white waterfall-edge island, rattan bar stools, white cabinets and ocean artwork

items.name: Townhomes, Condos and Mobile Homes
items.blurb: Small spaces get the same design attention as big ones. The portfolio includes a Ventura tri-tone townhouse and a full mobile home makeover, and one client said her small kitchen job still made her feel like an important customer.

image.alt: Mobile home kitchen makeover with gray lower cabinets, white uppers, a white quartz peninsula, woven stools and open shelving

items.name: Cabinets, Counters and Windows
items.blurb: As an authorized dealer, Kitchen Places supplies and installs Nickels, Bellmont and Medallion cabinets, Cambria, Caesarstone and Silestone quartz, and Pella windows and doors. You can see and compare them at the Callens Road showroom before choosing.

image.alt: English Charm kitchen with Bellmont alabaster cabinets, a sand-colored tile backsplash and a diamond checkerboard Marmoleum floor

why_choose_us.h2: Why Ventura County homeowners pick Kitchen Places

items.title: The owner on the job
items.text: Clients describe Jeff King managing day-to-day project activities, answering questions and making sure jobs are done right. He has owned the company since 1993.

items.title: A schedule you can read
items.text: A detailed workflow chart shows when work starts and finishes. One Ventura client said the staff kept to the schedule and left the site immaculate.

items.title: Designers with real range
items.text: Crickett Kinser holds a BFA in Interior Architectural Design and did historic preservation design at Paramount Studios. Megan Paulson founded 22 Design House in 2016.

items.title: Financing through Cambria
items.text: Finance by Cambria bundles your remodel with up to $75,000, with no application fees, no prepayment penalties and no closing costs.

about.h2: Jeff King: Coast Guard veteran, UCSB graduate, Ventura craftsman
about.text: Jeff King has owned Kitchen Places since 1993. He served four years in the U.S. Coast Guard, then earned a B.A. in Environmental Studies at UC Santa Barbara. Ventura's coastline and the Channel Islands brought him here after college. Jeff is a creative craftsman who loves working out the smallest details so the fit and finish are never compromised. One Google reviewer called him a master craftsman with a phenomenal staff. He leads a team of designers, a design assistant and project managers who supervise every installation.

image.alt: Kitchen Places showroom building with a stone tile facade at 1500 Callens Road in Ventura, CA

process.h2: Six steps, from the showroom to the celebration

steps.title: Visit the showroom
steps.text: Your first meeting is a chance to see the team's work in person and try the cabinet, counter and fixture brands they carry.

steps.title: Getting to know you
steps.text: The team visits your home to see the space firsthand and hear how you cook, store and gather before any planning starts.

steps.title: Broad strokes
steps.text: Designers put preliminary concepts on paper and in the CAD system, so you can see the layout before committing to it.

steps.title: The finishing details
steps.text: Hardware, finishes, lighting and every special detail get filled in, and the final plans are set before installation.

steps.title: Build and celebrate

items.name: Lori S.
items.text: After quite a bit of investigating, we settled on Kitchen Places to remodel our 35-year-old kitchen. They were wonderful. We moved plumbing, created a walk-in pantry, and moved appliances to create a much more efficient and beautiful kitchen.

service_area.h2: Remodeling homes across Ventura County
service_area.text: The Callens Road showroom sits in Ventura, and most Kitchen Places projects are in Ventura County. Past clients write in from Ventura, Camarillo, Thousand Oaks and Oak View, and project names point to East Ventura, Midtown and Surfer's Point. Since 1993 the team has designed and installed kitchens and baths across southern and central California, so call if you live farther out.

faq.h2: Questions Ventura homeowners ask before they remodel

items.q: Will I see my kitchen before it is built?
items.a: Yes. After the team visits your home, designers sketch preliminary concepts and develop them in a CAD system. Clients say this is what they value most: one wrote that her kitchen looked like the picture, only better, and another said there were very few surprises during construction.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes, through Finance by Cambria. You can bundle Cambria quartz surfaces with other remodel products and services for up to $75,000. The application is paperless and takes under 10 minutes, with no prepayment penalties, no application fees and no closing costs. Ask the team how to get approved.

items.q: How do I know the job will stay on schedule?
items.a: You get a detailed workflow chart that shows when each stage starts and finishes, and installation runs on a flow-chart based system. Clients have said the staff stuck to the schedule, cleaned the work area every day and finished on time.

items.q: Which brands can I choose from?
items.a: Kitchen Places is an authorized dealer for Nickels, Bellmont and Medallion cabinetry, Cambria, Caesarstone and Silestone quartz, Pella windows and doors, and WarmlyYours radiant heating. You can compare door styles, slabs and finishes side by side at the Ventura showroom before deciding.

items.q: When is the showroom open?
items.a: The showroom at 1500 Callens Road is open Monday through Friday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Saturdays by appointment. It closes for major holidays, including Thanksgiving weekend and Christmas. Call (805) 658-0440 to schedule your visit with a designer.

final_cta.text: Call to set a time, meet the designers and see the cabinet and counter lines in person.

hero.eyebrow: St. Charles and St. Louis design-build
hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in St. Charles That Opens Up Your Main Floor
hero.subheadline: Aptitude Design & Build removes walls, reworks layouts and builds the kitchen in one contract, with the people who build it in the room while it is designed.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling St. Charles: open-concept kitchen with light shaker cabinets, stained wood island with seating, veined counters and stainless built-in refrigerator

intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in St. Charles, from the wall out
paragraphs: Aptitude Design & Build does kitchen remodeling in St. Charles and across the St. Louis area from its shop on South 5th Street. Many of their kitchens start with a structural question. On one St. Charles home, the wall between kitchen and family room held up the whole second floor. The crew shored it up, set a new beam, and built an oversized island with a second prep sink where the wall used to be.

Because the builders sit in on design, layout ideas get priced and checked for structure early, not after demolition. That matters in older St. Louis houses, where plaster walls, old wiring and earlier remodels can hide behind the cabinets. Google reviewers describe excellent service, great communication and attention to detail from bid to final walk-through.

services.h2: Remodeling services for St. Charles and St. Louis homes

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom cabinetry, islands, wall removal and open-concept layouts, walk-in pantries, custom range hoods, coffee bars, lighting and plumbing updates. The team asks first whether your current layout works, so you only pay to move what needs moving. Most kitchens take 8 to 12 weeks of construction.

image.alt: St. Louis area kitchen remodel with white veined waterfall island, brass lantern pendants and stained wood upper cabinets

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites, hall baths and guest baths with walk-in showers, frameless glass, soaking tubs, double vanities, heated floors and aging-in-place features. Most St. Louis area bathroom remodels run $15,000 to $80,000 and take 4 to 8 weeks of construction.

image.alt: Ballwin primary bathroom remodel with Italian quartzite floor and shower, deep soaking tub under a window and white vanity cabinets

items.name: Basement Remodeling
items.blurb: Finished lower levels with home theaters, wet bars, guest suites, home gyms, offices and added bathrooms, plus egress windows, insulation and drywall. One wellness basement featured in St. Louis Magazine has a sauna, cold plunge, golf simulator and guest quarters. Most take 6 to 12 weeks.

image.alt: Basement remodel for a golf enthusiast with indoor golf simulator, stone-clad column, dartboard cabinet and wood-look floor

items.name: General Home Remodeling
items.blurb: Whole-home and main-floor renovations, structural wall removal, mudrooms, laundry rooms, home offices, built-ins and second-story additions. Larger projects are planned so trades, schedule and quality control stay with one project manager from start to finish.

image.alt: Two-story home with yellow siding and black shutters after a second-story addition that added three bedrooms

why_choose_us.h2: Why homeowners from Ballwin to Ladue pick Aptitude

items.title: Comfortable with structural work
items.text: Load-bearing walls, new beams, moved plumbing and relocated doorways are routine here. The St. Charles open-concept kitchen required temporary shoring for the whole second floor before the wall came out.

items.title: Builders in the design meetings
items.text: The people who build your project help plan it, so feasibility, selections and budget are weighed together before work begins instead of being discovered during demolition.

items.title: Noticed by local press
items.text: Aptitude has been featured in the St. Louis Business Journal, St. Louis Magazine, Ladue News and St. Louis Magazine's Faces of Exceptional Remodeling.

items.title: Clients come back
items.text: Reviewers on Google include returning clients, and the owner's reply to one review thanks a family for trusting the team again with another interior transformation.

about.h2: A word from founder Matt Mierek
about.text: Matt Mierek founded Aptitude and serves as its president. He describes his team as craftsmen who want long-term relationships with clients, not one-and-done jobs, and says that mindset has been part of the company's DNA from the start. In an interview with Ladue News he explained the goal of simplifying remodeling so it is enjoyable for clients. Homeowners on Google say Matt was helpful and knowledgeable through the bid process, and they mention foreman Terry by name. The firm also handles commercial build-outs, offices and apartment remodels across the region.

image.alt: Matt Mierek, founder and president of Aptitude Design & Build in St. Charles, MO

process.h2: The Aptitude kitchen process, step by step

steps.title: Consultation
steps.text: Talk through what is not working, what you want to change and your expected investment, so goals and budget line up from day one.

steps.title: Design and layout planning
steps.text: Explore layouts, islands, cabinetry, appliance placement and lighting, and answer the big question of how the kitchen can work better.

steps.title: Selections and budgeting
steps.text: Choose cabinets, counters, flooring, fixtures and appliances with the budget in view, since design and construction are priced together.

steps.title: Pre-construction and permits
steps.text: Plans, scheduling, trade coordination, ordering and permits are lined up before demolition so the build runs smoothly.

steps.title: Build and final walk-through
steps.text: A dedicated project manager runs construction from demolition to finish carpentry, then a final walk-through closes out remaining details.

service_area.h2: Working across St. Charles and St. Louis County
service_area.text: Aptitude is based at 912 S 5th St in St. Charles and remodels homes on both sides of the Missouri River. Recent and listed communities include St. Charles, St. Louis, Clayton, Ladue, Frontenac, Chesterfield, Kirkwood, Town & Country, Creve Coeur, Des Peres, Webster Groves, Richmond Heights, Wildwood, Ballwin, the Central West End, Holly Hills and South City.

faq.h2: St. Charles remodeling questions, answered

items.q: Can you take out a wall to open up my kitchen?
items.a: Often, yes. On a St. Charles kitchen the wall between kitchen and family room carried the entire second floor. The team temporarily supported the structure, installed a new beam and support system, and turned two closed rooms into one open space with a large island.

items.q: How long will my kitchen be out of commission?
items.a: Most kitchen remodels take about 8 to 12 weeks once construction begins. Keeping the existing footprint usually takes less time than moving plumbing or walls. Design, selections, cabinet ordering and permits happen before demolition, so starting those talks early helps the schedule.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost around St. Louis?
items.a: Aptitude says most bathroom remodels in the St. Louis area range from $15,000 to $80,000. Guest bath updates sit near the low end. Primary baths with custom tile, freestanding tubs, heated floors or expanded layouts need a larger budget. Construction usually takes 4 to 8 weeks.

items.q: Do you handle permits and inspections?
items.a: Yes. Permitting is part of pre-construction planning, and the team manages permits and inspections for projects throughout St. Louis, St. Charles and surrounding communities. Plans, trade scheduling and material orders are coordinated at the same time so work can start cleanly.

items.q: Can you remodel an older St. Louis home without losing its character?
items.a: Yes. Older homes may hide uneven floors, old wiring, plaster walls or earlier renovations, and the team plans for those. Cabinetry, millwork, flooring, lighting and proportions are chosen so the new kitchen still fits the architecture of the house.

final_cta.h2: Ready to open up your kitchen?
final_cta.text: Call Matt's team in St. Charles to talk through your layout, structure and budget.

items.q: What do Kent bathroom remodels usually run?
items.a: Big Build lists bathroom remodels from about $10,000 for a cosmetic refresh to $50,000+ for a full luxury primary bath. items.q: How many weeks should I plan around?
items.a: Plan on 3 to 6 weeks for a typical bathroom. Simple cosmetic updates can wrap up in 1 to 2 weeks, while gut remodels that move plumbing and add a custom shower can take 6 to 8 weeks. You get a start date, a completion date and weekly progress updates.

items.q: What if the crew uncovers rot or bad wiring?
items.a: Older homes often hide worn supply lines, old wiring or rot once things are opened up. Big Build flags every one of those issues in writing the moment it is found, with the cost, so you decide before anything changes. There are no surprise invoices at the end.

faq.h2: Ames Kitchen Remodel Questions

items.q: How long does a countertop replacement take?
items.a: After you pick your material and color, the team comes out within about a week to make a digital template so the slab is cut to size. Install is usually about four to five weeks later. A plumber disconnects the sink, and the crew removes your old counter the day before the new one goes in.

items.q: Which countertop material should I choose?
items.a: Laminate is the most budget-friendly but the least durable. Granite resists scratches but needs sealing every year. Quartz is the most popular choice and needs no sealing, though it is not heat resistant. Dekton by Cosentino is heat proof and extremely strong. You can compare all four in the showroom.

items.q: Can I see materials before I decide?
items.a: Yes. That is the point of the showroom at 204 Airport Road in Ames. You can walk through cabinet displays and look through hundreds of countertop samples. Hours are Monday to Friday, 10am to 5pm, and Saturday by appointment only. The showroom is closed on Sunday.

items.q: Do you offer free estimates?
items.a: Yes. Call (515) 233-1470 for a free estimate, or email showroom@completelykitchens.com to schedule a free walkthrough and consultation of your kitchen or bathroom project. A designer will visit your home, take measurements and talk through what you want before any design is drawn up.

items.q: What can I update if my budget is tight?
items.a: Smaller updates still change how a kitchen feels. Under-cabinet lighting can be installed in an afternoon. A new sink, new knobs or pulls, a fresh backsplash, painted cabinets or new quartz countertops can all refresh the room without the cost of brand new cabinets. Ask the showroom which fits your budget.

intro.h2: Richmond families keep calling the same company back
paragraphs: Custom Kitchens has been doing kitchen remodeling in Richmond, VA for over 65 years, and the Hendrick family still runs it. The work covers kitchens, bathrooms and built-in cabinetry, planned by certified designers and installed by experienced craftsmen.

Many of its clients are not on their first project. One Google reviewer had the firm remodel his kitchen, then came back years later for the primary bath. A Libbie and Grove client wrote that every time they move, they call Custom Kitchens for the renovation. The company's promise has not changed in decades: listen, do it right and do it on time.

services.h2: What Custom Kitchens designs and installs

items.name: Kitchen Renovations
items.blurb: Full kitchen renovations planned from layout to hardware by a certified designer, then installed by the CKI team from tear-out to final install. The showroom carries brands such as Wolf, Sub-Zero, Bosch and Omega Cabinetry, so you can compare appliances and cabinets you won't find at a big box store.

image.alt: Old Meets New on Hanover kitchen in Richmond with a navy island, white cabinetry, stainless built-in refrigerator and long open floor plan

items.name: Bath Renovations
items.blurb: Primary baths and powder rooms designed with the same care as a kitchen, from vanity cabinetry and tile to fixtures and lighting. Recent work ranges from a sparkling primary retreat with a freestanding tub and walnut vanity to a powder room with patterned wallpaper and brass fittings.

image.alt: Richmond primary bathroom remodel with a walnut vanity, white quartz top and freestanding soaking tub

items.name: Built-In Cabinetry
items.blurb: Home offices, bars and other built-in cabinetry, designed by the same certified designers who plan kitchens. Clients go through the same process for every project, which the firm says lowers stress, shortens construction time and produces the best result.

image.alt: Built-in home office in Tarrington with gray-stained cabinetry, open shelves, a desk with under-cabinet lighting and a black counter

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons Richmond homeowners give for choosing CKI

items.title: Three generations in one showroom
items.text: Richard Hendrick took over from his father, the founder, in 1986. His sons Kyle, Carter and Curtis now work as designers and managers, so the family name is on every job.

items.title: Certified designers on staff
items.text: The team includes Certified Kitchen Designers such as Richard Hendrick and Allison Stowers, along with licensed contractors and experienced craftsmen. A certified designer is always on site at the showroom.

items.title: A price you can hold them to
items.text: A North Chesterfield client wrote that designer Kyle offered layout and price options, then 'We determined a price and worked to it and stuck to it!' The expected price creep never came.

items.title: Recognized by local peers
items.text: The firm lists Contractor of the Year honors for 2017 through 2020 and 2023 and PRO Awards from 2022 to 2025, and it belongs to the Central Virginia PRO chapter and the NKBA.

about.h2: Meet Richard Hendrick, president since 1986
about.text: Richard Hendrick has spent his whole career in the family business. He started as a carpenter's helper in high school and college, learning how kitchens are actually built. His father, the founder of Custom Kitchens, was his mentor and taught the client-first approach the company still runs on. Richard became president in 1986 and is a Certified Kitchen Designer known for award-winning designs. He has since brought in the third generation: Kyle as vice president and designer, Carter as designer and Curtis, a former installation manager, as vice president of operations.

image.alt: Richard Hendrick, CKD, president of Custom Kitchens Inc in Richmond, VA

process.h2: Planning, design and installation, in that order

steps.title: Visit the showroom
steps.text: Stop by Horsepen Road to get inspired and meet a designer. No appointment is needed, and a private design session is free.

steps.title: Planning
steps.text: Your designer listens to your needs, discusses the project and budget, proposes ideas and explains your options.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: After a design deposit, you get drafts and concepts, pick finishes and colors, review perspective drawings and make revisions.

steps.title: Installation
steps.text: Once the contract is signed, materials are ordered and received before construction, a temporary kitchen is set up, then demo and installation begin.

steps.title: Start living
steps.text: The finished room is yours to enjoy, and the team stays available for warranty service after the job.

service_area.h2: Where we handle kitchen remodeling in Richmond, VA and nearby
service_area.text: The showroom is at 6412 Horsepen Road in Richmond. Client stories on the site come from the Near West End, Windsor Farms, Libbie and Grove, Rothesay Circle and Stratford Hills in the city, from Henrico and the Wellesley area, and from Chesterfield and North Chesterfield. Recent projects include a Tarrington kitchen and a farmhouse by the Rappahannock. If your neighborhood is not listed, call and ask.

faq.h2: Questions we hear in the Horsepen Road showroom

items.q: Do I need an appointment to visit the showroom?
items.a: No. The showroom is open to the public Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, and a certified designer is always on site. After-hours appointments are available on request. If you want private time with a designer, leave your details and the team will set up a complimentary design session.

items.q: Which brands can I see in person?
items.a: The showroom features many high-end finishes and hardware lines plus brands such as Wolf, Sub-Zero, Bosch and Omega Cabinetry. These are products you usually cannot find at a big box store, and seeing them side by side makes choosing cabinets and appliances much easier.

items.q: When do I pay a deposit?
items.a: Planning comes first: your designer listens, discusses the project and budget and explains your options. A design deposit starts the design phase of drafts, finish selections, perspectives and revisions. You sign the construction contract only after the design is done, and materials arrive before demolition starts.

items.q: Will I have a working kitchen during the remodel?
items.a: Custom Kitchens sets up a temporary kitchen as part of the installation phase, so you can still make coffee and simple meals while the old kitchen comes out. Ordering and receiving materials before construction begins also keeps the time without a kitchen as short as possible.

items.q: What happens if something needs fixing later?
items.a: The company handles warranty claims. One Google reviewer bought a home with a kitchen Custom Kitchens had recently renovated, and said Curtis and Blake went above and beyond when a warranty issue came up. Ask your designer for the written warranty terms for your project.

intro.h2: Cabinets, counters and crews under one roof
paragraphs: Modern Kitchen has offered kitchen remodeling in Elkhart since 1946, from a showroom at 30513 Old US 20 West. What began as cabinets built by hand in a garage is now a full design, selection and installation team for kitchens and baths across Northern Indiana and Southwest Michigan.

Projects start at the showroom. A designer looks at how you cook, store and gather, then draws a plan around those needs and your budget. Cabinetry, Cambria countertops and appliances are picked in one visit, and Modern Kitchen's own staff carries the job from planning to completion, whether it is new cabinets or a full renovation.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Elkhart and the services around it

items.name: Kitchen Design
items.blurb: Every project starts as an empty canvas. Modern Kitchen's design professionals work out function and storage, colors and style, and the difference between necessities and wish lists, then build a plan around those needs and your budget. Large projects or small, complete renovations or new cabinets.

image.alt: Loft-style kitchen design with a dark island, warm under-counter lighting, open pipe shelving and tall windows

items.name: Cabinetry
items.blurb: Aristokraft for affordable kitchens and baths, semi-custom Diamond, and premium KitchenCraft. Choose contemporary or French Country, dark woods or light, natural wood finish or painted. The team helps you match door style, finish and features to the way you live and the look you like.

image.alt: Goshen area kitchen with navy lower cabinets, white upper cabinets, butcher block counters and a marble-look waterfall island

items.name: Countertops and Appliances
items.blurb: Cambria countertops, with a Roomvo visualizer on the site to preview styles in your own room, plus natural stone and laminate options. Modern Kitchen has also sold appliances for over 60 years, including Amana, KitchenAid, Maytag and Whirlpool, matched to your layout and budget.

image.alt: Kitchen with charcoal cabinets, a waterfall quartz island with seating, professional range and black pendant lights

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Bathroom cabinetry, countertops and fixtures, designed and installed by the same team that does the kitchens. Past clients have asked for everything from a claw foot tub to a master bath redo after their kitchen was finished, and many come back for the guest bath next.

image.alt: Elkhart bathroom remodel with a floating black double vanity, white vessel sinks, black framed mirrors and marble-look tile

why_choose_us.h2: Why Elkhart families keep coming back

items.title: Three generations, one philosophy
items.text: Mark's grandfather Lance started out building cabinets by hand. Mark's father Steve joined in 1964 and Mark in 1986. Grandpa's rule, be honest and give exceptional service, still runs the business.

items.title: Recognized at 75 years
items.text: State Representatives Doug Miller and Dale Devon presented Mark Jones with greetings and congratulations from Governor Eric Holcomb when Modern Kitchen marked its 75th anniversary.

items.title: Real people you can name
items.text: Google reviewers thank designers Tammy and David by name. Tammy Case, Dave Flock and Michael Lang handle sales and design, and Willis Roberts is the finish carpenter.

items.title: Repeat clients
items.text: One Granger interior designer says Modern Kitchen has remodeled her last three kitchens. A South Bend couple had their kitchen done, then their master bath, with the guest bath next.

about.h2: Mark Jones and a cabinet shop that started in a garage
about.text: Modern Kitchen began with Mark Jones's grandfather, Lance, building cabinets by hand in his garage, and the business has served the area since 1946. Mark's father, Steve, joined him in 1964, and Mark followed in 1986. A lot has changed since then, from cabinet brands to appliances, but the family says one thing has not: Lance's belief in being honest and giving exceptional customer service. Today Mark is president, and the showroom team serves homeowners, builders and remodelers. In Mark's own words, the goal is to help you redesign, remodel and relax.

service_area.h2: Serving Northern Indiana and Southwest Michigan
service_area.text: The showroom is on Old US 20 West in Elkhart, and the team works across Northern Indiana in South Bend, Granger, Mishawaka, Elkhart and Goshen, plus Southwest Michigan. Past clients quoted on the site live in South Bend, Granger, Elkhart and Cassopolis, Michigan. If you are close to the state line, call and ask whether your address is in range.

faq.h2: Questions Elkhart homeowners ask Modern Kitchen

items.q: Which cabinet brands do you carry?
items.a: Modern Kitchen sells Aristokraft cabinetry for affordable kitchens and baths, semi-custom cabinetry by Diamond, and premium KitchenCraft cabinets. Styles run from contemporary to French Country, in dark or light woods, natural wood finishes or paint. A designer helps you narrow the choices to the right door, finish and features.

items.q: Can I see a countertop in my own kitchen before I buy?
items.a: Yes. Modern Kitchen offers Cambria countertops, and its products page includes the Roomvo room visualizer, which lets you try different countertop styles in a photo of your own room or in sample rooms. The showroom also has natural stone and laminate countertop samples to compare in person.

items.q: Do you remodel bathrooms as well as kitchens?
items.a: Yes. The same design and installation team handles bathroom cabinetry, countertops and fixtures. One Elkhart client got the claw foot tub she always wanted, and a South Bend couple had Modern Kitchen remodel their master bath after their kitchen, with the guest bath next on their list.

items.q: Do you sell appliances too?
items.a: Yes. Modern Kitchen has been in the appliance business for over 60 years and carries brands including Amana, KitchenAid, Maytag and Whirlpool. Because appliances are the first step in a kitchen design, the team matches them to your layout, needs and budget, and also sells laundry pairs like washers and dryers.

items.q: When is the showroom open?
items.a: The showroom at 30513 Old US 20 West in Elkhart is open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 5 PM. The contact page also lists Saturday hours of 9 AM to noon, and evening appointments are available. Call (574) 674-9989 to confirm a time with a designer before you drive over.

final_cta.h2: Bring your kitchen ideas to the showroom
final_cta.text: Call Mark and the design team at (574) 674-9989 to set up a visit, or send a message and they will reach out to plan your kitchen or bath.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Martinsburg, WV, Planned in Our Showroom
hero.subheadline: Pick cabinets, counters and vanities in person at our 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive. Our own in-house team then installs everything, from toe-kicks to hardware.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Martinsburg WV: Petrasek family kitchen with Muted Moss green base cabinets, Wicker-finish wood uppers and island, Tyrol quartz counters and a chimney range hood

intro.h2: A Martinsburg showroom with 31 years behind it
paragraphs: Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths has handled kitchen remodeling in Martinsburg, WV and across the Eastern Panhandle since 1995. You start in a 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive, where you can open cabinet doors, compare countertops and stand at real vanities. Then the in-house team builds it.

The firm leans on American-made cabinetry from makers such as KraftMaid. Its project write-ups list each door style and finish, like a Muted Moss and Wicker two-tone kitchen in Martinsburg or a load-bearing wall moved four feet in Harpers Ferry. Reviewers praise the guidance through layouts and selections, and the clear communication.

services.h2: Kitchens and baths, from design to the last cabinet pull

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full tear-outs, wall removals and layout changes, carried out by Mountaineer's own team. In Harpers Ferry, the Jackson kitchen gained an open plan when a load-bearing wall moved four feet on two LVL beams. It was finished with Woodhaven Shaker cabinets and Calacatta Arno quartz.

image.alt: Harpers Ferry, WV kitchen remodel with walnut-tone Shaker cabinets, white quartz counters, brass faucet and gas cooktop

items.name: Cabinets and Countertops
items.blurb: Choose semi-custom or traditional cabinetry in the showroom, with brands like KraftMaid and Brighton Cabinetry. Counters come in quartz, stone, wood, solid surface, laminate or concrete. In Falling Waters, the Wiggins kitchen paired Shortbread maple base cabinets with wood accents.

image.alt: Falling Waters, WV kitchen with white KraftMaid cabinets, wood-tone island with seating, glass pendant lights and a French door

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and powder rooms, planned around your budget, timeline and style. The team handles layout changes, new windows, closets and knee walls. A Charles Town family came back after their kitchen to have the bath gutted and rebuilt.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel with freestanding white soaking tub, wood-look tile wainscot and frameless glass walk-in shower

items.name: Custom Tile Showers
items.blurb: Showers are built on Schluter pans and wrapped in Kerdi waterproofing membrane before any tile goes up. In Harpers Ferry, the Reap master bath got a 72-inch curbless shower in 12x24 tile, two niches and Ditra-Heat floor heating with a 10-year manufacturer warranty.

image.alt: Harpers Ferry, WV curbless walk-in shower with large white 12x24 tile in a brick pattern, tiled niche and glass door

items.name: New Construction Kitchens and Baths
items.blurb: Building a new home? Mountaineer draws the floor plan for the new kitchen or bath and installs the cabinets, fixtures and lighting. Kitchen styles range from traditional and Craftsman to cottage, Mediterranean, transitional and modern, all on view in the showroom.

image.alt: Cottage-style kitchen with white cabinets, open wood shelves, wood range hood, butcher block island and retro green refrigerator

why_choose_us.h2: Why Eastern Panhandle families choose Mountaineer

items.title: See it before you buy it
items.text: The 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive is the only one of its kind in the area. You can open the cabinets and feel the countertops before you decide.

items.title: Our own crew installs
items.text: Every project is handled in-house from start to finish. That includes demo, plumbing changes, drywall, trim and hardware, with no hand-off to strangers halfway through.

items.title: American-made materials
items.text: Cabinetry and materials on every job are American-made. Recent kitchens used all-plywood boxes and soft-close hardware from lines such as KraftMaid and Woodhaven.

items.title: A team that has stayed
items.text: Owner Ben DeOms has worked alongside most of the crew for five, ten or more years. Google reviewers name Brandon and Eric for patient, careful design guidance.

about.h2: From summer job at 16 to owner
about.text: Ben DeOms first walked into Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths at 16. He worked summers, evenings and weekends through high school and learned the trade beside skilled craftsmen. He eventually took over the business, which has served Martinsburg for more than 31 years. Ben says he wants to keep the quality and integrity the previous owners built, with American-made materials on every job. Under his ownership the company opened its new showroom and is taking on more higher-end projects. Project manager Buck Day, sales and design lead Brandon Cooley, salesman Patrick Carter and office manager Heidi Shank round out the team.

image.alt: Ben DeOms, owner of Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths in Martinsburg, WV

process.h2: How a Mountaineer project comes together

steps.title: Start at the showroom
steps.text: Stop in or book a time to talk through your goals, needs and inspiration while you look at cabinets, counters and vanities in person.

steps.title: Layout and selections
steps.text: The designer reviews layout options, whether galley, L-shaped or U-shaped, and guides your choices of materials, finishes, fixtures and paint colors.

steps.title: Ordering and scheduling
steps.text: Planning, design, ordering and scheduling make up most of the 3 to 6 months a kitchen project takes from start to finish.

steps.title: In-house installation
steps.text: Once work starts, a typical kitchen takes about 2 to 3 weeks. Mountaineer's own team handles demo, trades, cabinets, trim and hardware.

steps.title: The reveal
steps.text: You walk into the finished room. For the team, seeing a client's reaction to the start-to-finish change is the best part of the job.

service_area.h2: Berkeley, Jefferson and Morgan counties
service_area.text: Mountaineer is based in Martinsburg and works for homeowners across Berkeley, Jefferson and Morgan counties in West Virginia's Eastern Panhandle. Recent projects include kitchens in Martinsburg, Falling Waters, Charles Town and Harpers Ferry. There are also custom tile baths in Harpers Ferry and Charles Town, and a church kitchen in Hedgesville. Not sure if you are in range? Call the showroom.

faq.h2: Martinsburg kitchen and bath questions

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: The whole process of planning, designing, ordering, scheduling and installing can take 3 to 6 months. Most of that time comes before work begins. Once the project starts, a typical Mountaineer kitchen remodel takes about 2 to 3 weeks. Material choices, the size of the job and its complexity all affect the timing.

items.q: When can I visit the showroom?
items.a: The showroom at 1950 Rock Cliff Dr in Martinsburg is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Saturday and Sunday visits are by appointment only, which helps if you cannot get there during the workday. Call (304) 267-6262 to set a time, or just stop in during the week for ideas.

items.q: Do you do all the work yourselves?
items.a: Yes. Mountaineer's in-house team handles every project from start to finish. On recent kitchens that meant demolition, plumbing changes for a new stove, vent ducting, drywall, cabinet installation, trim, toe-kicks and hardware. On one Harpers Ferry kitchen it also meant the engineering coordination for a load-bearing wall.

items.q: How do you keep a shower from leaking?
items.a: Recent showers are built on Schluter shower pans, with Kerdi waterproofing membrane on the walls before tile goes up. The Reap master bath in Harpers Ferry used a 72-inch Schluter pan with a curbless entry. The Dagg shower in Charles Town used the same system, plus a built-in bench and dual niches.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. Mountaineer offers financing through Acorn for customers who would rather not pay the full cost up front. Ask about it when you visit the showroom or call (304) 267-6262. Terms and approval come from the lender, so the team can point you to the application while you plan your kitchen or bath.

final_cta.h2: Come see it in person on Rock Cliff Drive
final_cta.text: Visit the showroom weekdays 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, or call to book a weekend appointment with Ben's team.

intro.h2: A design studio that also runs the build
paragraphs: OKC Kitchen & Bath offers kitchen remodeling in Oklahoma City for homeowners who want design and construction under one roof. The team works from an office in Midtown at 12 NW 13th St., and projects reach across the metro, including Edmond and Nichols Hills. Full interior design is part of every job, not an add-on.

The firm is upfront about fit: projects include full interior design services and begin at $40,000. That lets the team spend real time on each home, from mood boards to a cabinet meeting held in your own kitchen. Reviewers name the crew members and say communication stayed clear from the first call to the last day.

service_area.h2: Serving Oklahoma City, Edmond, Nichols Hills and Norman
service_area.text: The team completes full-service projects across the Oklahoma City metro from its Midtown office. The site names Oklahoma City, Edmond and Nichols Hills, and past clients quoted on the home page live in Newcastle, Edmond and Norman. Proposal meetings happen at the Midtown office and design meetings are held in person, so most work stays within driving range of downtown.

faq.h2: Before you book a discovery call

items.q: What is the minimum project size?
items.a: Projects include full interior design services and begin at $40,000. The contact form asks you to pick a budget range, from $40,000 to $60,000 up to $200,000 and more, and a start window of as soon as possible, three to six months, or six months or later. That helps the team prepare for your call.

items.q: Is design included or extra?
items.a: Design is included. OKC Kitchen & Bath works as a design-build firm with an in-house designer, so you meet in person to review inspiration, build mood boards and pick materials. The same company then builds what you approved, which keeps the plan and the construction lined up.

items.q: What is the cabinet meeting?
items.a: It is step five of the process. Before construction begins, the team meets at your home to review cabinet sizing, spacing and function. The goal is a layout that works for daily life, from where appliances sit to how storage and traffic move through the room.

items.q: Can you keep some of my existing features?
items.a: Often, yes. One Norman client asked to keep the original cabinets in both her kitchen and master bathroom, and the team worked them into the final design while replacing the flooring through most of the house. Mention anything you want to keep on your discovery call.

items.q: Where do meetings take place?
items.a: The discovery call is by phone. The team then visits your home for a consultation and invites you to the Midtown Oklahoma City office at 12 NW 13th St., Suite 1E, to review the proposal and an early visual direction with the in-house designer.

intro.h2: More than glass: full bathrooms and kitchens for 30+ years
paragraphs: Specialty Kitchens and Baths, LLC handles bathroom remodeling in Warren, MI and across Oakland, Macomb and western Wayne County. Many homeowners know the company by its other name, Designs in Glass, because owner Howard Emmer built his reputation on frameless and euro glass shower doors.

The company does far more than glass. Howard's crews tear out and rebuild whole bathrooms and kitchens, then finish them with custom cabinets, granite or quartz counters, tile and lighting. Almost everything is custom built for your space, and you get one-on-one service from Howard from the first visit to the final install. Reviewers say the crew treats your home like their own.

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Major and minor bathroom renovations, from a new shower to a full remodel down to the studs. Work covers custom bathroom design, vanities and cabinets, countertops, custom tubs, glass shower doors, tile and lighting, all built to fit your space.

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling

Howard's team can also help you pick hardware, sinks and faucets. Gallery projects include kitchens in Novi, Troy, Farmington Hills, Birmingham and Bloomfield.

about.h2: Meet owner Howard Emmer

In his own words: "I love seeing my customers happy with the service we provide for them. faq.h2: Answers before your free consultation

items.q: Do you only install glass?
items.a: No. Many people assume so because of the Designs in Glass name, but Specialty Kitchens and Baths is a full-service remodeling company. Howard's team handles complete bathroom and kitchen remodels, basements, custom cabinets, granite and quartz countertops, floor tile and lighting, as well as glass shower doors.

items.q: Is the estimate free?
items.a: Yes. Howard will meet with you for a free consultation and write up a proposal for your project. Visits are by appointment only, so call (248) 798-1000 or send an email to set a time. The office is open weekdays from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm and Saturdays from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm.

items.q: Can you just replace my shower door and update the shower?
items.a: Yes. You can upgrade an existing shower with a new frameless or euro glass door, or add new tile and fixtures at the same time. One Google reviewer had a real tile floor laid over the old one and worn glass replaced with high-quality glass that has a coating to help prevent water stains.

items.q: Should I choose granite or quartz counters?
items.a: Both can last well over 25 to 30 years. Granite is cut from a solid piece of stone, is more prone to chipping and needs to be sealed and resealed over time. Quartz is made from crushed quartz bound with resin and does not need sealing. Howard will walk you through both.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: All remodeling and renovation projects come with a two-year workmanship warranty, so your new bathroom, kitchen, floors or glass stay covered well after installation. The company is also BBB accredited with an A+ rating, and it has more than 30 years of remodeling experience in Metro Detroit.

intro.h2: Know the number before the hammer swings
paragraphs: Kitchen remodeling in Denton, TX usually goes wrong in the gap between a quick bid and the real bill. Wreedone closes that gap up front. On the first visit the team listens, looks at the space and gives you a budget range built from real numbers on its last four similar projects.

From there you walk through the design in photoreal 3D, choose every finish, and sign a pre-construction agreement with an itemized price. If you change something later, you see the cost before work goes ahead. Most Wreedone kitchens run $60,000 to $150,000 or more, depending on size, layout changes and finishes.

services.h2: Kitchen Remodeling in Denton, TX, and Bathrooms Built the Same Way

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: One team handles tear-out, layout and structural changes, custom soft-close cabinetry, countertops, lighting, electrical, appliances and paint. Walls come out and beams go in when the plan calls for it, and every structural change is engineered and permitted.

image.alt: White kitchen with cabinets extended to the ceiling, charcoal island, patterned tile backsplash and pendant lights

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Full and primary bath remodels with freestanding soaking tubs, custom vanities, large-format tile and heated floors, even inside the shower. You approve the layout, tile and fixtures in 3D, and the team pulls permits and orders everything up front.

image.alt: Desert Willow primary bathroom in Denton, TX with freestanding tub, frameless glass shower and pebble shower floor

items.name: Walk-In Showers & Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: Curbless and glass-enclosed showers tiled floor to ceiling, with waterproofing done right. In one Wreedone remodel an unused jetted tub and an old shower became a single large frameless shower with a pebble floor, a custom bench and niches.

image.alt: Persimmons primary bathroom in Denton, TX with frameless glass walk-in shower, sage green vanity and brass sconces

items.name: Whole-Home & Multi-Room Remodels
items.blurb: Kitchens that open into dining rooms, pantries, wet bars, mudrooms and laundry rooms, planned and built as one project. Recent Denton work includes the Kashmiri Walnut whole-house renovation and the Tamarack kitchen, dining, pantry and laundry remodel.

image.alt: Kashmiri Walnut whole-house renovation in Denton, TX with walnut island, waterfall countertop and a timber ceiling beam

why_choose_us.h2: Four reasons Denton homeowners call Wil

items.title: Priced before demo day
items.text: You get a cost range on the first visit and an itemized price in a pre-construction agreement before work starts. Your price only moves if you choose to change something.

items.title: Best of Houzz eight years running
items.text: Wreedone has won Best of Houzz for service every year from 2019 through 2026, and holds a 5.0 rating across 79 Houzz reviews alongside 4.9 stars on Google.

items.title: One project manager, daily updates
items.text: A dedicated project manager runs your build with daily updates and clean job sites. Client experience manager Keith Gumera guides you from the first call to the final walkthrough.

items.title: A warranty that sells with the house
items.text: Every remodel carries a 5-year workmanship warranty that transfers to the next owner, with check-ins at 3, 6 and 11 months. The same team handles any fix directly.

about.h2: Wil Reed and the Wreedone team
about.text: Wil Reed founded Wreedone in Denton in 2017 on a simple belief: a home renovation should not be a nightmare. After seeing firsthand how most contractors operate, he set out to do it differently, with a refined process, thorough communication and work the team is proud to sign. More than 150 North Texas homes later, he is the standard every project is held to. Spencer Stewart builds your estimate and 3D renderings, project managers Justin Hamel and Chase Kubiak run the build, and Keith Gumera looks after you from first call to final walkthrough. Every photo on the site is real Wreedone work.

process.h2: Six steps, laid out before you start

steps.title: Listen and capture the vision
steps.text: The team comes to your home, listens and assesses the space. The visit is free and carries no commitment.

steps.title: A data-driven cost range
steps.text: In the same visit you get a realistic budget range, built from real numbers on Wreedone's last four similar projects.

steps.title: Pre-construction agreement
steps.text: A full photoreal 3D design, a detailed scope and a clear price that you approve before any work begins.

steps.title: Construction and walkthrough

steps.title: Follow-up and warranty

service_area.text: Wreedone is based in Denton and works across Denton County and nearby North Texas towns. faq.h2: What Denton homeowners ask before they remodel

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost in Denton?
items.a: Most Wreedone kitchen remodels run $60,000 to $150,000 or more, depending on size, layout changes and finishes. At the first in-home visit you get a budget range built from the team's last four similar projects, then an itemized price in the pre-construction agreement before any work starts.

items.q: Will I see my kitchen or bathroom before it is built?
items.a: Yes. Every project starts as a photoreal 3D design. You walk through the exact layout, cabinets, tile and fixtures, refine them with the team and choose every finish. What you approve on screen is what gets built in your home, so there are no surprises on demo day.

items.q: What does the 5-year warranty cover?
items.a: Wreedone gives a full workmanship warranty on every project for five years, in writing. If something is not right, the team makes it right with one call. The coverage transfers to the next owner if you sell, and scheduled check-ins happen at 3, 6 and 11 months.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Wreedone does not lend money itself and earns no fee from financing. If monthly payments suit your family, two independent marketplaces are built into the estimate: HFS, with home improvement loans up to 20 years and no equity required, and Acorn Finance, which compares 30+ lenders. Prequalifying is a soft credit check.

items.q: Can you fix a shower another contractor ruined?
items.a: Yes. Google reviewer Anna C. hired a sub to retile her shower, and the job ended up destroying both shower and tile. It turned into a complete overhaul with new walls and a new pan, and she called Wil's team to do it. She later wrote that the company is truly unlike any other.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Boardman, OH, Most Showers Done in One Day
hero.subheadline: When you call Your New Baths, you talk to the people who do the work. Owner Brandon Moore swaps tubs for showers, replaces surrounds and builds custom tile baths across the Mahoning Valley.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Boardman OH: walk-in shower with white marble-look solid surface walls, black fixtures, fold-down seat and glass door

intro.h2: A small local crew that answers its own phone
paragraphs: Your New Baths does bathroom remodeling in Boardman, OH and across Northeast Ohio and Western Pennsylvania, from Youngstown and Niles to New Castle. Most tub-to-shower conversions and shower replacements are finished in a single day, so your family is not without a bathroom for weeks.

Owner Brandon Moore is the name you see in nearly every review. He shows up on time, explains the plan for each day and cleans up before he leaves. Showers use Samuel Mueller solid surface panels, which are non-porous, so there are no grout lines to scrub. For bigger jobs, he also builds full tile showers with waterproofing behind every wall.

services.h2: Showers, tubs and full baths

items.name: One-Day Tub to Shower Conversion
items.blurb: The old tub comes out and a low-threshold shower goes in, usually in a single day. Add a fold-down seat, a grab bar, corner shelves and a sliding glass door. It is a common pick for homeowners who want easier, safer footing in the bathroom.

image.alt: Tub to shower conversion in Lowellville, Ohio with marble-look walls, fold-down seat, grab bar and sliding glass door

items.name: Tub and Shower Replacement
items.blurb: Worn surrounds and dated tubs are replaced with Samuel Mueller solid surface walls. The color runs all the way through the material, so small scratches buff out, and the non-porous surface wipes clean without trapped moisture or hidden mold.

image.alt: Bathtub replacement with marble-look solid surface surround and sliding glass doors with black hardware

items.name: Custom Tile Showers
items.blurb: For homeowners who want tile, the crew does proper substrate prep, waterproofing and careful layout. A recent bathroom in Southington, Ohio got tile from floor to ceiling, waterproofing behind it all and a linear drain in the floor.

image.alt: Custom tile shower with large marble-look tile, a recessed niche, built-in corner bench and black shower valve

items.name: Full and Master Bath Remodels
items.blurb: Complete remodels cover the shower or tub plus flooring, vanities, lighting and plumbing fixtures, with the price set before work begins. These take longer than a one-day shower; one reviewer's full remodel was finished in 4 days, as promised.

image.alt: Remodeled walk-in shower with gold-veined marble-look walls, black rainfall shower head, glass doors and fold-down seat

why_choose_us.h2: Why neighbors pick Your New Baths for bathroom remodeling in Boardman, OH

items.title: You deal with the installer
items.text: This is not a franchise or a call center. When you phone Your New Baths, you speak to the people who will do the work, and reviewers name Brandon on almost every job.

items.title: Lifetime workmanship warranty
items.text: Every project is backed by a lifetime workmanship guarantee, and the company is licensed and insured. It also promises 100 percent satisfaction on the work it completes.

items.title: Clear price before work starts
items.text: You get a fair, upfront price at the free in-home estimate and it does not change. One reviewer called the result a really good price for the quality of work.

items.title: Water damage repairs, too
items.text: After a burst pipe flooded a basement bathroom in New Castle, PA, the homeowner said that by the end you couldn't tell anything had happened.

about.h2: Meet Brandon Moore, founder and owner
about.text: Brandon Moore founded Your New Baths and still does the work himself. Google reviewers describe him the same way again and again: on time, quick, clear about the plan for each day, and careful to clean up. His company focuses on one-day showers and full bathroom transformations using Samuel Mueller solid surface materials, plus custom tile for clients who want it. Your New Baths is locally owned, licensed and insured, and the site says it has more than 10 years of experience serving Ohio homeowners. Jobs range from a surround shower in Niles to a full tile bath in Southington.

image.alt: Brandon Moore, founder and owner of Your New Baths in Boardman, OH

process.h2: Four steps to a new bathroom

steps.title: Free in-home estimate
steps.text: Call or fill out the form. The team schedules a no-obligation, no-pressure visit to your home at a time that works for you.

steps.title: Pick your design and price
steps.text: You walk through wall, base and door options and get a clear, upfront price with no surprises before anything is ordered.

steps.title: Install day
steps.text: The crew measures carefully, protects nearby floors and furniture, keeps the work area contained and installs your new shower or tub.

steps.title: Clean-up and final walkthrough
steps.text: Everything is cleaned up before the crew leaves, and you walk through the finished bathroom, backed by the lifetime workmanship warranty.
