service_area.h2: Mahoning Valley, Greater Cleveland and Western PA
service_area.text: Your New Baths is based in Boardman and covers the Mahoning Valley and beyond. Its own list runs from Youngstown, Cortland and Champion north to Ashtabula and west to Akron, Cleveland, Solon and Chagrin Falls, plus New Castle across the line in Pennsylvania. Recent jobs and reviews also come from Niles, Lowellville and Southington. Call to check whether your town is on the schedule.

faq.h2: Before you book: common bath questions

items.q: Is it really done in one day?
items.a: Most tub-to-shower conversions and shower or tub replacements are finished in a single day, so you are not without a bathroom for long. Full and custom tile remodels take longer because they include flooring, vanities, plumbing and tile work. One Google reviewer's full remodel was completed in 4 days, exactly as promised.

items.q: What does a project cost?
items.a: The company's offer page says projects start at $8,500. Your exact price depends on the size of the space and the materials you pick, and you get a clear, upfront number at the free in-home estimate. That price is set before any work begins, with no gimmicks or surprise charges added later.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. The site lists three plans: 12 months same as cash with no interest if paid in full, a 60-month plan at 8.99 percent from about $199 a month, and a 144-month plan at 9.99 percent from about $125 a month. Ask about financing at your free estimate; approval depends on credit.

items.q: Why solid surface instead of tile or acrylic?
items.a: Samuel Mueller solid surface is non-porous, so water cannot soak in, mold has nowhere to hide and soap scum wipes off. The color runs through the whole panel, so minor scratches can be buffed out. If you still prefer tile, Your New Baths builds custom tile showers with full waterproofing.

items.q: Can you fix a bathroom after water damage?
items.a: Yes. One Google reviewer in New Castle, PA hired Your New Baths after a burst pipe sent water into a basement bathroom. He praised the communication and said that once the work was done you couldn't tell anything had happened. Call to describe the damage and set up a visit.

final_cta.h2: Talk to Brandon about your bathroom
final_cta.text: Call 330-980-8398 or fill out the form for a free, no-pressure in-home estimate anywhere from Boardman to Akron and New Castle.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Raleigh, NC, Priced by the Owner in Person
hero.subheadline: For more than 15 years Affordable Remodeling Solutions has focused on kitchens and baths around Raleigh and Cary. President Jonathan Doering visits your home and builds the estimate himself.

intro.h2: Kitchens and baths are the whole focus
paragraphs: Affordable Remodeling Solutions has handled kitchen remodeling in Raleigh, NC and nearby towns for more than 15 years, with bathrooms as the other half of the business. The name describes the goal: good materials and careful work at a fair price, with budget-friendly options when you need them.

When you call or text, you talk with Jonathan Doering, the company's president. Google reviewers describe him spending over an hour looking at every detail of a home before he prices a job, then returning a detailed estimate within days. They also mention Susanne by name for keeping projects organized and on schedule.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Raleigh, NC and bathroom updates

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full kitchen remodels, from galley kitchens that gain counter space to layouts opened up by removing a wall. Recent work includes a Blue Dunes granite galley in Raleigh, a navy-island kitchen in Cary and kitchens in Clayton, Knightdale and North Raleigh. Transparent timelines and cost breakdowns come with every project.

image.alt: Raleigh, NC kitchen remodel with a separating wall removed, white quartz island, stainless appliances and pendant lights

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, hall baths and condo baths, including showers with frameless glass, freestanding tubs, custom vanities and tile work. After a leak damaged one Raleigh primary bath, the team rebuilt it with soft-green tile, a pebble-stone shower floor and niche, and a warm wood vanity.

image.alt: Raleigh primary bathroom with soft green shower tile, pebble-stone shower floor and niche, frameless glass and a wood vanity

items.name: Garden Tub to Sauna Conversions
items.blurb: That big garden tub nobody uses can become something you will. Affordable Remodeling Solutions has replaced an outdated garden tub and shower with an in-bathroom sauna, a project it describes on its blog for homeowners who want a primary bath that works harder.

image.alt: Cedar sauna built into a primary bathroom in place of a garden tub

why_choose_us.h2: What Raleigh clients notice about ARS

items.title: An estimate built from a real look
items.text: One reviewer said Jonathan spent over an hour at the house, checking the basement and attic, and had a very detailed estimate ready within a few days.

items.title: Help with the choices
items.text: Clients say Jonathan suggests materials, tile positioning and colors, and stays in tune with the details while remaining easy to talk to.

items.title: On time and on budget
items.text: A recent Google reviewer had an outdated bathroom redone top to bottom and wrote that the project was completed on time and on budget.

items.title: Flexible on how you take part
items.text: One Raleigh client supplied many of the materials and did much of the demolition. The ARS team stepped in from there and finished the tile work.

about.h2: Talk with Jonathan Doering, President
about.text: Jonathan Doering leads Affordable Remodeling Solutions, INC as president, and he answers the phone himself. Call or text and you will reach him directly. Over more than 15 years the company has kept its focus on kitchen and bathroom remodeling in the Raleigh-Cary area, with courteous, clean and experienced tradesmen. Reviewers describe Jonathan as detail-minded and personable, and they often thank Susanne alongside him for steady communication. The trades he brings in for drywall, plumbing and electrical work earn their own praise in reviews for being competent and reliable.

image.alt: Jonathan Doering, President of Affordable Remodeling Solutions in Raleigh, NC

steps.title: Reach Jonathan

steps.title: Detailed estimate

steps.title: Build and updates

If your home sits a little outside that map, ask anyway: one reviewer's small bathroom was outside the usual range, and Jonathan took it on.

faq.h2: Answers for Raleigh homeowners

items.q: Who will I talk to when I call?
items.a: You will usually reach Jonathan Doering, the president, directly. The contact page invites you to call or text (919) 607-5467 to speak with him, or to fill out the consultation form. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 to 5:00, and the company is closed on weekends.

items.q: How detailed is the estimate?
items.a: Very. One client wrote that Jonathan spent over an hour at the house, looking at every detail including the basement and attic, and delivered a very detailed estimate within a few days. The company says it provides clear timelines and cost breakdowns, so there are no surprises later.

items.q: Can I supply materials or do some of the work myself?
items.a: It has been done. One Raleigh client supplied many of the materials and did a lot of the demolition, and the ARS team took it from there and finished the tile work. Ask Jonathan during the visit which parts make sense for you to handle on your own project.

items.q: How should I prepare for a kitchen remodel?
items.a: The company's planning guide on its blog lists eight decisions to make before demolition, such as what is not working now, whether the layout should change, how storage should match daily habits and choosing appliances early. You can also download the free Project Planning Guide from the website.

items.q: Do you only do full remodels?
items.a: Most projects are full kitchen or bathroom remodels, but reviewers also describe small bathroom jobs, a laundry room and a shower remodel. The consultation form lets you upload photos of your space and of projects you like, which helps Jonathan understand the scope before he visits.

final_cta.h2: Start your Raleigh kitchen with a conversation
final_cta.text: Call or text Jonathan to set up a visit, or grab the free Project Planning Guide first.

Our new Design Center on Hillside Drive has displays featuring Kohler, Starmark Cabinetry, Infinity by Marvin, ProVia and HomeStory doors. The original Design Center and office in Muskego is still open, too.

Two brothers started Callen in 1986. Michael and Christiane Wood took over in 2023 with a plan to keep the company's standards while adopting newer building science and installation methods. Kitchens and baths are planned as complete rooms, with layout, storage, lighting, cabinetry and surfaces chosen together, and every project carries a lifetime workmanship warranty.

services.h2: Callen services, kitchens and baths first

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full kitchen designs, not partial updates. Your Sales • Design Consultant draws detailed plans and 3D views, then helps you choose cabinets from lines such as Starmark and Ultracraft, Kohler faucets and the surfaces that suit how you cook and entertain.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with white and stained wood cabinets, quartz peninsula, open wood shelves and glass pendants

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Bathrooms planned as one system, covering layout, moisture control, durable materials and comfort. Callen uses high-performance surfaces like Onyx for clean lines that last, and offers accessible features, spa-style showers and freestanding tubs. Your consultant shows 3D views of the room before any work starts.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel with a freestanding tub, sage green tile shower and black grid fluted glass partition

items.name: Interior Spaces
items.blurb: Main floors, laundry rooms, mudrooms and attic conversions, designed to match the rest of the house. The focus is on flow, organization and storage, with finishes carried from room to room so new spaces blend with the old ones.

image.alt: Laundry and mudroom remodel with gray and walnut cabinets, quartz folding counter, built-in bench and coat hooks

items.name: Replacement Windows
items.blurb: Infinity by Marvin windows made from Ultrex fiberglass, rated 8 times stronger than vinyl and backed by a limited lifetime warranty. Callen is an Infinity by Marvin Platinum Dealer and can cut new openings when a design calls for it.

image.alt: White farmhouse with black Infinity by Marvin replacement windows, covered porch and stone walkway

items.name: Entry, Storm and Patio Doors
items.blurb: ProVia entry and storm doors, HomeStory interior doors and patio doors, all installation-only. HomeStory doors are laser-measured for a precise fit, and storm doors help protect your entry from Wisconsin wind and cold while adding ventilation and curb appeal.

image.alt: Charcoal ProVia entry door with glass sidelites and white trim on a gray-sided home with brick steps

why_choose_us.h2: Why Lake Country homeowners choose Callen

items.title: Nearly four decades in Wisconsin
items.text: Callen has served Southeastern Wisconsin since 1986. Production manager Steve Turzinski started as a carpenter helper 25 years ago, and designer Paulette Sodemann has been with Callen for nearly 20 years.

items.title: Certified kitchen and bath designers
items.text: The kitchen and bath team includes Jennifer Earhart, CKBR, Paulette Sodemann, CKBR, CRD, and Danni Maddison, CRD, UDCP, plus Ryan Rieck as project manager and estimator.

items.title: Two design centers to visit
items.text: See products in person at the Muskego Design Center and office or the new Delafield Design Center. Both are open weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Saturdays 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.

items.title: Backed for the long run
items.text: Every project comes with a lifetime workmanship warranty. Google reviewers describe the work as "meticulous from sales to ordering to install" and praise the honesty of the first estimate visit.

about.h2: A 1986 company under new ownership
about.text: Two brothers founded Callen in 1986, and for almost four decades it has remodeled homes across Southeastern Wisconsin. Since 2023 the company has been owned by Michael Wood, its president and director of sales and business development, and Christiane Wood, vice president. Their stated aim is to respect Callen's legacy while embracing progress in building science and installation methods. In 2026 they opened a second Design Center in Delafield to bring that experience closer to Lake Country homeowners, where clients work directly with Sales • Design Consultants, project managers and the carpentry team.
about.owner_role: President, Director of Sales and Business Development

process.h2: Design, Build, Live: how a Callen remodel works

steps.title: Meet at the Design Center
steps.text: Your project starts with a collaborative conversation with a Sales • Design Consultant at the Muskego or Delafield Design Center.

steps.title: Plans and 3D views
steps.text: After a retainer agreement, your consultant creates detailed plans, drawings and 3D views and guides finish, color, layout and fixture choices.

steps.title: Accurate estimate
steps.text: Because the same team designs and builds, it knows how each design choice affects cost and prices your project from the finished design.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Once the design is final and the budget is agreed, the same design-build team handles construction with professional project management.

steps.title: Live with it
steps.text: Your finished kitchen or bath is backed by a lifetime workmanship warranty, and the service team stays available after the job is done.

service_area.h2: Serving Lake Country and Southeastern Wisconsin
service_area.text: With Design Centers in Delafield and Muskego, Callen serves homeowners across Southeastern Wisconsin. Lake Country towns like Delafield, Oconomowoc, Hartland, Pewaukee and Dousman are minutes from the Hillside Drive Design Center. The Muskego office covers Waukesha, Brookfield, New Berlin and Milwaukee County, and the team also works north to Mequon and Cedarburg and south to Racine and Burlington. If your town is not listed, ask; the list is 'including but not limited to'.

faq.h2: Questions about kitchen remodeling Delafield WI homeowners ask

items.q: Where can I see materials before I decide?
items.a: Visit either Design Center. The new Delafield location is at 2736 Hillside Drive, and the original Design Center and office is at S63W13131 Janesville Road in Muskego. Both are open Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Saturday, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., with displays from Kohler, Starmark Cabinetry and Infinity by Marvin.

items.q: How does pricing work with design-build?
items.a: Design starts after a retainer agreement. Your consultant then produces plans, drawings and 3D views and helps you select finishes. Because the same team designs and builds, it can tie each choice to its cost and give an accurate estimate. Construction begins once the design is final and the budget is agreed.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. Through Regions Bank, on approved credit, Callen offers a 12-month same-as-cash loan, with interest waived if repaid within 365 days, and a traditional installment loan with fixed APRs starting at 8.99%. For Wisconsin residents the APR will not exceed 17.99%. Your Sales • Design Consultant can help you choose.

items.q: What warranty comes with a Callen remodel?
items.a: Callen provides a lifetime workmanship warranty on its remodeling work. Infinity by Marvin windows and patio doors also carry a limited lifetime warranty from the manufacturer. Callen's service team, including a service manager and service technician, handles follow-up after the project is complete.

items.q: Which cabinet and fixture brands do you use?
items.a: Kitchens often feature Starmark Cabinets or Ultracraft Cabinets with Kohler faucets, and bathrooms use high-performance surfaces like Onyx. For windows and doors, Callen installs Infinity by Marvin, ProVia entry and storm doors and HomeStory interior doors. Consultants can show past projects to help you choose.

final_cta.text: Call (414) 529-5509 or request a consultation, then stop by 2736 Hillside Drive to see cabinets, counters and fixtures in person.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Temecula, CA, With Cabinets Built by Hand
hero.subheadline: Owner Joel Cervantes designs your layout, builds your cabinets and leads the crew that moves walls, reroutes gas, plumbing and electrical, and sets the tile. One craftsman, from first sketch to final fixture.

intro.h2: One artisan with every trade under his eye
paragraphs: JC Custom Cabinets handles kitchen remodeling in Temecula, CA the way a furniture maker would. Owner Joel Cervantes designs the layout, builds the cabinetry and supervises every phase himself. You talk to the person whose hands are on your project, not a sales rep or a stack of disconnected subcontractors.

Because he controls design, fabrication and installation, his crew can take a kitchen down to the studs. On a Meadowview Estates remodel they moved interior walls, raised the ceiling, rerouted gas, water and electrical lines and swapped small windows for panoramic ones. When the budget is tight, Joel offers quality prefab cabinets from a local maker.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Temecula and the rooms around it

items.name: Full Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: Turnkey work from layout to appliances: wall and window changes, plumbing and electrical updates, tile backsplashes, lighting and new flooring. Joel personally handles design, fabrication and installation, so cabinets, counters and trim fit the way they were drawn.

image.alt: Crowne Hill Estates kitchen in Temecula with white Shaker cabinets, quartzite counters and an oversized island wrapped in reclaimed lumber

items.name: Custom and Prefab Cabinetry
items.blurb: Handcrafted cabinets built to your layout, or high-quality prefabricated Shaker cabinets from a trusted local manufacturer when the budget is tight. Prefab units get custom finessing and accents, so the finished run reads as one built-in piece.

image.alt: White Shaker kitchen in Temecula with frosted glass uppers, black chimney hood, quartz island and black saddle stools

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Master suites and vanity overhauls from concept to completion: tile walls and floors, electrical rewiring, fixture placement, frameless glass showers and custom storage. Vanities range from prefab white Shaker units with Bianco Swan quartz to fully custom double vanities.

image.alt: Temecula bathroom with white Shaker double vanity, black hardware, framed mirrors and a frameless glass shower in marble-look tile

items.name: Built-Ins and Media Walls
items.blurb: Media walls, fireplace cabinetry, home office bookcases, closet systems, mudroom benches, laundry rooms and dining buffets, finished with accent lighting, framing and clean wire management. Recent built-ins went into homes in Temecula, Murrieta, Riverside and La Cresta.

image.alt: Custom white Shaker entertainment center with open side shelving built for a Temecula client

items.name: ADU Interiors
items.blurb: For a Temecula Wine Country ADU, Joel designed, built and installed the kitchen, bathroom, laundry room and a cabinetry nook. The finish: golden-toned birch Shaker cabinets, brushed gold hardware and Calacatta De Oro quartz with a 2-inch square edge.

image.alt: Temecula Wine Country ADU kitchen with golden-toned birch Shaker cabinets, brushed gold pulls, Calacatta De Oro quartz and a farmhouse sink

why_choose_us.h2: Why Temecula homeowners hire Joel

items.title: You talk to the builder
items.text: Joel is the designer, the cabinetmaker and the lead on site. Reviewers call him a master carpenter who can build anything, and one wrote that the price quoted was the price paid.

items.title: Licensed, in business since 2015
items.text: JC Custom Cabinets, LLC holds California license #1038035. Joel started as an apprentice and has more than 20 years in the trade.

items.title: Fewer markups
items.text: Design, carpentry, tile, plumbing and electrical stay under Joel's supervision, which he says removes subcontractor markups. Google reviewers often mention his fair pricing.

items.title: Called in to fix other jobs
items.text: Anthony hired JC after missed deadlines with an original contractor, and Joel's reply to Royal R. describes stepping in to correct a hidden Murphy door's alignment.

about.h2: Meet Joel Cervantes, owner and craftsman
about.text: Cabinetry has been Joel Cervantes's lifelong passion. He started as an apprentice when he was young, spent more than 20 years in the trade, and has run JC Custom Cabinets since 2015. As owner, designer and craftsman, he plans each layout, builds the cabinets and directs a trusted crew of specialists on site. His aim is to add hundreds of thoughtful details so the room fits your style and the way you live. He offers a free consultation in your home, and the business serves clients in Spanish too.

image.alt: Black and white portrait of Joel Cervantes, owner of JC Custom Cabinets in Temecula

process.h2: How a JC Custom Cabinets project comes together

steps.title: Free in-home consultation
steps.text: Joel meets you at home, for a small project or a large one, to look at the space and talk through layout, cabinet options and budget.

steps.title: Design and written contract
steps.text: He designs the layout and puts materials, costs, timeline and any outside tradespeople into a professional written contract before work begins.

steps.title: Cabinet fabrication
steps.text: Custom cabinets are built to your layout, or quality prefab units from a local cabinetmaker are prepared with custom details to match.

steps.title: Build and install
steps.text: Under Joel's supervision the crew handles walls, gas, plumbing, electrical, tile, flooring and lighting, then installs appliances, fixtures and hardware.

service_area.h2: Southwest Riverside County, close to home
service_area.text: JC Custom Cabinets is based in Temecula and works across southwest Riverside County. faq.h2: Temecula kitchen questions, answered by the craftsman

items.q: Do you build custom cabinets or install stock ones?
items.a: Both. Joel designs, builds and installs fully custom cabinets for kitchens, baths, entertainment centers, laundry rooms and closets. When the budget is tight, he offers quality prefabricated cabinets from a trusted local manufacturer and adds custom touches, like a wine rack sized so wall and base cabinets line up.

items.q: Can your crew move walls, plumbing and gas lines?
items.a: Yes. The crew handles structural wall and window changes and reroutes natural gas, water and electrical lines under Joel's supervision. On one Meadowview Estates kitchen they also raised the ceiling and added panoramic windows, then installed the cabinets, quartzite counters and appliances.

items.q: Is the in-home consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Joel offers a free in-home consultation and estimate for projects small or large. Call (951) 816-7809 to set a time. He will look at your space, talk through layout and cabinet options, and explain which parts of the job his own team will handle.

items.q: Can we plan the project in Spanish?
items.a: Yes. The contact page says "Se habla español," so you can plan your kitchen, bath or built-in project in Spanish or English. The business also identifies as Latino-owned on its Google profile, and it serves families across Temecula, Murrieta and Menifee.

items.q: Will you build cabinets outside the kitchen?
items.a: Yes. Joel builds media walls, fireplace cabinets, home office bookcases, closet systems, mudroom benches, laundry room cabinets and dining room buffets. Prefab units are often blended with custom pieces, and media walls can include accent lighting, framing and clean wire management for the TV.

final_cta.h2: Talk directly with the craftsman who will build it
final_cta.text: Call Joel at (951) 816-7809 to book a free in-home consultation and estimate. Se habla español.

seo.og_title: Schock Construction and Design: Eastside remodels at a fixed bid
seo.og_description: Owner Steve Schock's Issaquah firm publishes its kitchen and bath prices, scans your room in 3D and locks the budget before demolition.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Issaquah With a Fixed Bid Before Demo Day
hero.subheadline: Schock Construction and Design has remodeled Eastside homes for more than 30 years. Owner Steve Schock walks your kitchen, the estimate is explained line by line, and the price is locked before construction starts.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Issaquah: Modern Moment kitchen with a quartz waterfall island, full-height slab backsplash, white cabinets and brass pendants

intro.h2: Prices on the page, decisions made before demolition
paragraphs: Schock Construction and Design has handled kitchen remodeling in Issaquah and across the Eastside for more than 30 years. It is locally owned and operated, works only east of Lake Washington and has completed more than 100 projects there.

Its approach is unusual for the trade: the site publishes real numbers. A kitchen runs $150,000 to $180,000 before appliances, and every scope item, allowance and selection is settled during design so the bid can be fixed before demo day. Anything truly hidden behind a wall goes through a written change order that you see, price and approve before any work on it begins.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Issaquah, plus baths, additions and whole homes

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Plywood cabinet boxes, 3/4-inch solid wood dovetail drawers and soft-close everything come standard, and range hoods over 300 CFM get the code-required makeup air. Expect about three months of design, four to six weeks of preparation and two and a half to three months of construction.

image.alt: Squak Mountain Retreat kitchen remodel in Issaquah with wood shaker cabinets, a quartzite island, black range hood and stone fireplace beyond

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths average around $150,000 all-in and hall baths run $80,000 to $100,000. In-floor heat runs into the shower floor and bench, walls get Durock board with Laticrete waterproofing, and humidity-sensing fans are sized to the room. Construction takes about two and a half months.

image.alt: Elegant and Timeless bathroom remodel in North Bend with a long quartz vanity, brass sconces, checkerboard tile floor and glass shower

items.name: Whole-Home Remodeling
items.blurb: Main floors opened, systems replaced and every room designed as one vision. The Squak Mountain Retreat in Issaquah got a new furnace, a full rewire, rerouted plumbing, new windows and a full-height stone fireplace, and the Lake Sammamish View owners came back for three phases over three years.

image.alt: Squak Mountain Retreat great room in Issaquah with a full-height stone fireplace, wood-trimmed windows and the open kitchen beyond

items.name: Home Additions
items.blurb: Space that looks like it was always part of the house. At Beaver Lake in Sammamish, Schock enclosed a rear patio into the family room, adding 232 square feet of conditioned space without growing the footprint. Additions on Mercer Island and in Sammamish also appear in the firm's portfolio.

image.alt: Modern on Mercer home addition on Mercer Island with a light oak vanity, open shelving, black fixtures and a lit mirror

why_choose_us.h2: Why Eastside homeowners trust Schock with the big projects

items.title: Published prices, fixed bids
items.text: Real price ranges are on the site and your budget is fixed before demolition. Hidden conditions go through a written change order that you see, price and approve.

items.title: The owner at your walkthrough
items.text: Steve Schock comes to the on-site visit with the project coordinator and estimator, and the team 3D-scans the room into an as-built blueprint on the spot.

items.title: A crew you will get to know
items.text: A Schock site superintendent runs each job with subcontractors who have worked with the firm for 10+ years, and a live online schedule shows who is coming and when.

items.title: Recognized and licensed
items.text: Eight Best of Houzz awards for design and service since 2016, membership in the Master Builders Association, NAHB and NARI, and licensed and insured in Washington.

about.h2: Steve Schock and the people who run your job
about.text: Steve Schock owns Schock Construction and Design, and in his words remodeling homes is a way of life: he likes seeing the potential in every house, old or new, big or small, then working out the plan, budget, design and build. He comes to the first on-site walkthrough for kitchen and bath projects. His team includes project coordinator Lisa Howard, estimator and general manager Chris Dederer, office manager Michelle Winterstein, construction manager Mike Krajewski and site supervisors Doug Cetina and Elijha Shibkiy. Interior design comes through a partnership with Kristi Sparks of Canyons Design.

image.alt: Steve Schock, owner of Schock Construction and Design in Issaquah, WA

process.h2: Five stages from first call to finished kitchen

steps.title: A real conversation (day 1)
steps.text: A phone call about scope, budget and timeline. If the numbers and the vision line up, a site visit is booked; if not, you hear so honestly.

steps.title: On-site walkthrough (weeks 1 to 2)
steps.text: Steve, the project coordinator and the estimator watch how your kitchen works, then 3D-scan the room into an as-built blueprint.

steps.title: Line-item estimate (within 2 weeks)
steps.text: An estimate built from decades of real historical costs, walked through line by line over Zoom, with a projected construction start date.

steps.title: Design with guardrails (about 3 months)
steps.text: The interior designer works with your scope and allowances already built in, so the design stays beautiful and on budget.

steps.title: Preparation and construction
steps.text: Four to six weeks of job preparation, then about two and a half to three months of construction run by a Schock site superintendent.

service_area.h2: Working only on the Eastside of Lake Washington
service_area.text: Schock works exclusively east of Lake Washington, from its office on NW Gilman Blvd in Issaquah. That covers lakefront Medina and Clyde Hill, Bellevue, Kirkland, Redmond, Sammamish, Newcastle and Mercer Island, and the foothill towns of North Bend, Snoqualmie and Fall City. The team knows the local permitting offices and housing stock, from Sammamish hilltop homes to Kirkland craftsmans and Mercer Island mid-century houses.

faq.h2: Straight answers on Issaquah kitchen remodels

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost with Schock?
items.a: Schock's Eastside kitchens run $150,000 to $180,000 before appliances, which you buy yourself; plan on about $30,000 for a typical appliance package. Kitchens that open into the living space start around $250,000. The bid is fixed before demolition, so the number on page one of your estimate is the number you pay.

items.q: How long from first call to a finished kitchen?
items.a: Plan on about three months of design with the interior designer, four to six weeks of job preparation, then two and a half to three months of construction. A bathroom takes about two and a half months to build once its design is locked. Your estimate shows a projected construction start date.

items.q: What happens if you find something behind a wall?
items.a: It goes through a written change order. You see the problem, you see the price and you approve it before anyone touches it. Because scope, allowances and selections are all settled during design, very few surprises are left by the time demolition starts, which is how Schock keeps budgets and finish dates.

items.q: What comes standard that others charge extra for?
items.a: In kitchens: plywood cabinet boxes, 3/4-inch solid wood dovetail drawers, soft-close doors and drawers, and undermount sinks with real allowances. In primary baths: in-floor heat that runs into the shower and up the bench, a full Durock and Laticrete waterproofing system, and humidity-sensing Panasonic fans.

items.q: Is the consultation really free?
items.a: Yes. The first conversation is free and carries no obligation. It starts as a discovery call about your scope, budget and timeline. If the project is a fit both ways, Schock schedules an in-home walkthrough and then delivers a full build estimate with a room-by-room breakdown and material allowances.

final_cta.h2: Get a number you can hold Schock to
final_cta.text: Call (425) 620-6318 or book a free in-home consultation and estimate. It starts with a no-pressure discovery call about your kitchen, bath or whole home.

seo.meta_description: Kitchen remodeling in Elkhorn, WI by a family firm founded in 1972. Fixed-price contracts and a 5-year workmanship warranty. Call (262) 723-7232 to get started.
seo.og_title: Stebnitz Builders: three generations of kitchen and bath remodeling in Elkhorn, WI
seo.og_description: Founded by Stan Stebnitz in 1972 and run today by his grandson Chris, with a 34-person team and a five-year workmanship warranty.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Elkhorn From a Third-Generation Builder
hero.subheadline: Stebnitz Builders plans every detail of your kitchen or bath before construction, signs a fixed contract, then backs the work for five years instead of the usual one.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Elkhorn area: lake-view kitchen with long white quartz island, walnut base cabinets, black geometric pendants and wall of windows

intro.h2: Fifty years of listening to Walworth County homeowners
paragraphs: Stebnitz Builders has offered kitchen remodeling in Elkhorn and across Walworth County since Stan Stebnitz started the company in 1972. His sons bought it in 1986, and his grandson Chris runs it today from the office at Highways 43 and 67. The firm is best known for lake homes, but it also takes on first-time remodels and small bathroom updates.

The method is careful, not fast. Before any demolition, a Project Development Agreement covers 60 to 120 days of planning where cabinets, quartz tops, fixtures and paint colors are all chosen and priced. You then sign a fixed contract, so the budget does not drift once the crew shows up. A five-year workmanship warranty covers what they built after they leave.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Elkhorn and everything around it

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Layout changes that fix the work triangle, islands and opened walls for entertaining, pantries and deep drawers for storage, and new lighting and floors. Your budget is checked early with an Opinion of Probable Cost, then every selection is locked before construction.

image.alt: Remodeled kitchen with white inset cabinets, navy island with wood top, dark wood ceiling beam and glass pendant lights

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suite and guest bath updates, plus master bath additions. Expect walk-in showers with custom tile, heated floors, double vanities, soaking tubs and steam showers, with fixes for poor ventilation, tight layouts and aging plumbing worked out before demolition.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with white double vanity, brass faucets and sconces, transom window and frameless glass shower

items.name: Aging in Place
items.blurb: Universal design that does not look clinical: curbless showers, comfort-height toilets, blocking for grab bars, wider doorways, lowered counters and main-floor primary suites and laundry. Past work includes a mid-century bath and a Geneva Landings remodel by the lake.

image.alt: Bright bathroom with freestanding soaking tub, brass floor-mounted filler, corner windows and gray tile floor

items.name: Whole Home Remodeling and Additions
items.blurb: Full-house resets, lake home renovations and additions that go up or out. The team plans structure, trades and finishes together and uses 3D design and virtual walkthroughs, so the new space reads as one home rather than a series of patches.

image.alt: Whole home remodel with green kitchen cabinets, wood plank vaulted ceiling with white beams and a large quartz island

items.name: Lower-Level and Exterior Remodeling
items.blurb: Lower levels finished as media rooms, gyms or retreats, and exterior work including siding, window replacement, roofing and gutters. Restoration projects repair and update older homes while preserving the historic architecture that gives them their character.

image.alt: Remodeled home entry with timber-frame gable porch, stone columns, wood front door and green siding

why_choose_us.h2: What three generations of building gets you

items.title: Five years of workmanship coverage
items.text: Most builders offer one year. Stebnitz covers carpentry, installation, plumbing, electrical and HVAC work, exterior finishes and structural changes for five years after completion.

items.title: A fixed contract after full planning
items.text: The 60 to 120 day Project Development phase settles every selection and cost first, which is how the firm replaces budget creep with a fixed price.

items.title: One production manager on your job
items.text: A dedicated production manager coordinates trade partners and keeps your household running. A GuildQuality client wrote that production manager Ryan Hibl always returned calls and followed through.

items.title: Rooted in Walworth County
items.text: A 34-person team based in Elkhorn that coaches local youth sports, volunteers with Habitat for Humanity and supports the United Way and SMILES.

about.h2: Chris Stebnitz and the family business
about.text: Stan Stebnitz founded the company in 1972, doing general carpentry and small additions. In 1986 his sons Dave, Gary and Dan bought the business and moved it to Delavan. Dave's son Chris Stebnitz became the third-generation owner, and in 2015 he moved headquarters to Elkhorn to sit in the middle of the county. Chris leads 34 people today, from remodeling consultants and designers to field carpenters and apprentices. The company still runs on three rules from the start: always do what is right, serve others as you expect to be served, and never walk away from a project.

image.alt: Chris Stebnitz, owner of Stebnitz Builders in Elkhorn, WI

process.h2: From first conversation to final walkthrough

steps.title: Listen and align the budget
steps.text: A first conversation about your goals, followed by an Opinion of Probable Cost so ideas and budget match before design goes far.

steps.title: On-site review
steps.text: A remodeling consultant visits the house to see the space, check existing conditions and talk through what is possible.

steps.title: Project Development Agreement
steps.text: Over 60 to 120 days, every cabinet, countertop, fixture and paint color is chosen and priced, then a fixed contract is signed.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Your production manager coordinates carpenters and trade partners on a set schedule while respecting the parts of the house you still use.

steps.title: Walkthrough and warranty
steps.text: A final walkthrough closes the job, and the five-year workmanship warranty starts so you can simply call if anything is not right.

service_area.h2: Elkhorn, the lakes and beyond
service_area.text: Stebnitz works out of 204 Commerce Ct in Elkhorn, near the center of Walworth County. The team serves the county's lakefront communities, with recent work around Lake Geneva, Williams Bay, Lake Beulah and Whitewater Lake, along with select parts of Rock, Jefferson and Racine counties. If you are unsure whether your town is covered, call the office.

faq.h2: Questions Elkhorn homeowners ask before remodeling

items.q: What does your five-year warranty cover?
items.a: It covers defects in workmanship and installation by Stebnitz and its subcontractors for five years after completion. That includes cabinets, trim, windows, doors and framing, plumbing, electrical and HVAC work under the contract, siding, roofing and flashing, and any structural changes. Product warranties from manufacturers are passed to you separately.

items.q: Why does planning take 60 to 120 days?
items.a: During the Project Development phase the team chooses and prices everything, from cabinets and quartz countertops to plumbing fixtures and paint colors. Finishing those decisions before construction is what makes a fixed contract possible and keeps the project on budget and on schedule once crews start.

items.q: Will you take on a smaller project?
items.a: Yes. Kitchen and bath updates, single-room projects and first-time remodels are part of the mix. One Google reviewer wrote that her $15,000 job got the same degree of personal attention as the firm's larger work, and that nobody treated it as small potatoes.

items.q: Can you help us stay in our home as we age?
items.a: Yes. Aging-in-place projects can move the primary suite and laundry to the main floor, add curbless walk-in showers and comfort-height toilets, reinforce walls for grab bars, widen doorways and halls, and lower counters, all designed to look like a normal, attractive remodel.

items.q: Can I visit your office?
items.a: The studio and office is at 204 Commerce Ct #3 in Elkhorn, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM according to the website. Call (262) 723-7232 or email remodel@stebnitzbuilders.com to set up a time so the right consultant is there to meet you.

final_cta.text: Tell the Stebnitz team what you want your kitchen or bath to do, and they will start with an honest look at cost.

intro.h2: A design-build team that draws your Irvine kitchen first
paragraphs: USA Home Remodeling offers kitchen remodeling in Irvine as a design-build contractor, so one team handles the consultation, 3D design, permits, construction and final walkthrough. service_area.h2: Irvine and the cities around it
service_area.text: The main office is in Irvine, with a second office in La Jolla for North San Diego County. In Irvine the team works from Woodbridge and Turtle Rock to Northwood, University Park and Great Park. Recent projects also span Newport Beach, Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Santa Ana, Orange, Placentia, Laguna Hills, Laguna Niguel and Mission Viejo, plus Carlsbad and Oceanside to the south.

faq.h2: What Irvine homeowners ask before remodeling

items.q: Is the estimate really free?
items.a: Yes. In-home estimates are free with no obligation to hire. The company has a $10,000 per-project minimum, and the home being estimated must be owned by you or at least in escrow. The 3D design is also included at no extra charge with every project.

items.q: How much do Orange County homeowners spend on a kitchen?
items.a: The company's own blog describes kitchen remodels in the $25,000 to $50,000 range and says most of its Orange County bathroom remodels land between $20,000 and $30,000. Your price depends on layout changes, cabinets, counters and appliances, and the detailed estimate spells it out line by line.

items.q: Will my HOA need to approve the remodel?
items.a: Often, yes. Many Irvine neighborhoods, such as Northwood, have HOA architectural review, and larger jobs need permits through Irvine Permit Services. USA Home Remodeling prepares the submissions, handles plan review and schedules inspections, so you do not have to manage the city process yourself.

items.q: What does the warranty cover?
items.a: You get a written 3-year labor and workmanship warranty at the final walkthrough, covering the work the team performs. The company describes that as about three times longer than most contractors offer. Ask during your estimate for the warranty wording so you know exactly what is included.

items.q: Can I pick my own materials?
items.a: Yes. Cabinets, countertops and tile are chosen with you during the 3D design stage, and you can change them on screen until the room looks right. The company also passes its contractor pricing on finished materials directly to you. Countertop options include quartz, granite and marble.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Lakeville, Designed and Built by One Team
hero.subheadline: White Birch Design is a boutique design-build firm run by co-owners Steve McDonald and Angela Barnhart, with award-winning kitchens across Lakeville, Eagan and the South Metro.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Lakeville MN by White Birch Design: white cabinets, navy island with leather counter stools, glass pendants and wood-trimmed windows

intro.h2: Kitchen Remodeling in Lakeville with a Boutique Design-Build Team
paragraphs: White Birch Design handles kitchen remodeling in Lakeville and the South Metro as a full-service design-build company. One team takes your kitchen, bath or lower level from first idea through design and construction, so you are not passing plans between a designer and a separate contractor. Its stated goal is simple: you feel part of the process and get the result you wished for.

The firm calls its approach boutique: the experienced design and project management of a big design-build company, without the big price tag or impersonal communication. Co-owners Steve McDonald and Angela Barnhart bring a combined 30+ years in design, construction and real estate, which also helps homeowners weigh return on investment.

services.h2: Kitchens, Baths, Lower Levels and Mudrooms

items.name: Kitchen Design and Remodeling
items.blurb: Every kitchen starts with a consultation about your goals, your ideas and the existing space. White Birch promises it will never come back with an outrageous estimate or a design that does not fit your lifestyle. Many projects open up the whole main floor.

image.alt: Eagan main floor kitchen remodel with natural maple cabinets, gray island with seating, wood range hood and beverage fridge

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and powder rooms. Recent work swapped an unused jetted tub in Lakeville for a walk-in shower with a built-in bench, frameless glass and grab bars, plus a makeup station and illuminated mirrors hung in front of the window.

image.alt: Lakeville primary bath remodel with walk-in shower, quartz bench, brass handle and dark cherry vanity with illuminated mirrors

items.name: Lower Level Finishing
items.blurb: Basements designed for relaxing, hosting and gathering, from bars to family rooms. White Birch guides you through design, finishing and remodeling, and holds a 2025 RotY basement award. A Rosemount lower level features painted beams, bar seating and a dining area.

image.alt: Rosemount basement remodel with painted ceiling beams, dining table, bar seating and modern black chandelier

items.name: Mudrooms and Main Floors
items.blurb: The hardworking rooms get design attention too. A Lakeville mudroom gained green cabinetry, stained maple shelving, custom shoe storage and a family command center after a wall came out between the closet and garage entry.

image.alt: Lakeville mudroom remodel with palm-pattern wallpaper, open coat hooks, wood shoe shelves under a bench and green cabinets

about.h2: Meet Co-Owners Steve McDonald and Angela Barnhart
about.text: White Birch Design is owned by Steve McDonald and Angela Barnhart, who bring a combined 30+ years in the design, construction and real estate industries. Angela leads design as owner and designer, and clients credit Steve's experience for showing them what is actually possible. Together they take homeowners from concept to design to construction, and help them choose options that maximize return on investment. Their team includes construction manager Dane Mueller, job supervisors Mike Leahy and Kevin Lerdon, and designers Alicia Czech and Nicole Breyfogle. The company also supports Ronald McDonald House.

service_area.h2: South Metro Towns We Remodel In
service_area.text: White Birch Design is based in Lakeville. Its main focus is kitchen, bath and basement remodeling in the South Metro communities of Lakeville, Eagan, Apple Valley, Burnsville, Rosemount, Prior Lake and Savage, and it also works with homeowners across Minneapolis and St. Paul. Past projects reach Shakopee, Bloomington, Hopkins, Northfield, New Prague and Owatonna, so ask even if your town is not listed.

faq.h2: Questions Lakeville Homeowners Ask Before a Remodel

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: For a full remodel, plan on about 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track. A cosmetic refresh with new countertops, hardware, paint and lighting can move faster.

items.q: Do I need a finished design or start date before I call?
items.a: No. Whether you have just started researching or want to begin next week, White Birch invites you to reach out. No start date or final design is needed, just a conversation about your ideas, your space and what you want to change. Call 952-686-8443 or use the contact form.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom safer as we age?
items.a: Yes. In a recent Lakeville primary bath, an unused jetted tub came out and a spacious walk-in shower went in, with a built-in bench, frameless glass and shower grab bars. Those aging-in-place features were worked into the design so the room still looks contemporary rather than clinical.

items.q: Is White Birch Design licensed?
items.a: Yes. The company lists its Minnesota license as BC# 736504 on its contact page. It also shows 2025 NARI RotY awards for residential kitchens and a basement, and it has exhibited at the Parade of Homes Remodelers Showcase. Ask for references from past clients near you during your consultation.

items.q: Which towns do you serve?
items.a: The main focus is the South Metro: Lakeville, Eagan, Apple Valley, Burnsville, Rosemount, Prior Lake and Savage. The team also takes projects across Minneapolis and St. Paul, and its portfolio includes work in Shakopee, Bloomington, Hopkins, Northfield, New Prague and Owatonna. Call to confirm your address.

final_cta.h2: Start the Design Conversation for Your Kitchen
final_cta.text: Share your ideas with Steve and Angela's team; a final design or start date is not needed.

seo.meta_description: Employee-owned kitchen remodeling in Jacksonville since 1983: design, cabinets, quartz and granite cut in-house, flooring. 4.5 on Google. Call (904) 641-8336.

seo.og_description: Design, cabinets, in-house quartz and granite fabrication and flooring from one Beach Blvd showroom, owned by the people who do the work.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Jacksonville From an Employee-Owned Team
hero.subheadline: Woodsman designs kitchens, installs cabinets, cuts quartz and granite countertops in its own Jacksonville shop and lays new floors. Since 2023 the company has been 100% owned by its employees.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Jacksonville area project in Ponte Vedra: soft blue Shiloh shaker cabinets, brass hardware, a white quartz island and wood counter stools

intro.h2: The parts of a kitchen that matter most, done in-house
paragraphs: Woodsman Kitchens & Floors has offered kitchen remodeling in Jacksonville since 1983, starting as a small cabinetry supplier on the First Coast. The company is not a full-service general contractor. It focuses on design, cabinets, countertops and flooring, and it does those parts itself.

Quartz and granite tops are cut and polished in the company's own Jacksonville warehouse, which keeps quality and lead times in local hands. In September 2023 the business became 100% employee-owned, so the designer, the fabricator and the installer in your home are all part owners. The goal is a custom-looking kitchen without a custom price tag.

services.h2: Design, cabinets, counters and floors from one showroom

items.name: Kitchen Design
items.blurb: In-house designers plan your layout and cabinets, pair countertops with backsplashes, coordinate flooring and help choose colors. The service also covers bathrooms, laundry rooms and new builds. Design support is included when you choose products through Woodsman, with no third parties or commissions.

image.alt: Warm transitional kitchen in Coastal Oaks with stained wood and eggshell painted cabinetry and a large island

items.name: Cabinets and Installation
items.blurb: Cabinet lines include Shiloh, Aristokraft, Eclipse, Diamond Vibe and Kitchen Craft, in custom and budget-friendly options. Installers tear out old cabinets, then set kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities and built-ins level and aligned, working hand in hand with the designers who drew the plan.

image.alt: Ponte Vedra kitchen with black Shiloh inset cabinets, a reeded walnut island, arched details and gold-veined quartz

items.name: Quartz and Granite Countertops
items.blurb: Woodsman offers quartz and granite only, measured, cut and polished at its local fabrication facility and installed by its own team. Keeping fabrication in-house gives the company control over quality and scheduling, which makes the countertop install smoother and lead times more consistent.

image.alt: White shaker kitchen with a marble-look quartz island, stainless appliances and beaded globe pendant lights

items.name: Flooring
items.blurb: Hardwood, luxury vinyl plank, laminate and tile for kitchens and living spaces, chosen from the showroom displays and installed by the same company that builds your kitchen. Matching floors to the cabinets and counters is part of the design work, so the whole room is planned together.

image.alt: Bright open-concept Jacksonville home with new light wood-look flooring running from the dining area into the kitchen

items.name: Bathroom Vanities and Baths
items.blurb: Bathroom remodeling and vanities with the same cabinet lines, quartz and granite tops and design help used in kitchens. Finished projects include a primary bath in Julington Creek, a bathroom refresh in Ponte Vedra Beach and coastal baths with built-ins in Atlantic Beach.

image.alt: Bright primary bathroom with light wood vanities, white countertops, a freestanding tub and a glass walk-in shower

why_choose_us.h2: Why First Coast homeowners pick Woodsman

items.title: Owned by the people who do the work
items.text: Since September 2023 the company has been 100% employee-owned through an ESOP. The people designing, cutting and installing your kitchen are owners with a stake in getting it right.

items.title: Countertops cut in Jacksonville
items.text: Quartz and granite slabs are fabricated in the company's own local warehouse, not shipped out. That gives Woodsman direct control of quality and keeps lead times consistent.

items.title: Design help without a designer fee
items.text: In-house designers guide every selection, and their support is included when you buy your products through Woodsman. The company promises prices below big box stores on expert design and quality materials.

items.title: Techs who treat your home with care
items.text: Google reviewers praise service techs like Joel, Jimi and Curtis for arriving on time, wearing shoe covers, and showing owners how to care for their cabinets after the job.

about.h2: A Jacksonville company owned by its employees
about.text: Woodsman began in Jacksonville in 1983 as a small cabinetry supplier and grew into one of Northeast Florida's known names in kitchens, baths and flooring, with more than 200,000 jobs completed. In September 2023 it became 100% employee-owned. Brad Mangold serves as president and Ira Cloud as vice president, and designers such as Ann-Marie Kallio, with the company since 2014, guide clients through selections. Woodsman belongs to the Jacksonville Chamber of Commerce, the Northeast Florida Builders Association, the Florida Home Builders Association and the NAHB, and local builders rely on it too.

image.alt: Woodsman Kitchens & Floors employee-owners gathered in the company's Jacksonville warehouse

process.h2: How kitchen remodeling in Jacksonville works with Woodsman

steps.title: Visit the showroom
steps.text: Look for the big purple W on Beach Blvd. Full kitchen vignettes, cabinet lines, slabs and flooring are on display six days a week.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: A designer learns your needs, style and budget, then plans the layout, cabinets, countertops and flooring around how you live.

steps.title: Fabricate
steps.text: Your materials are ordered to the approved design, and countertops are cut and finished for your space in the local fabrication shop.

steps.title: Install
steps.text: Installers tear out old cabinets, then set new cabinets, countertops and floors with careful attention to fit, function and detail.

steps.title: Service after the job
steps.text: Service techs come back for adjustments and repairs, and reviewers say they explain how to clean and care for your cabinets.

service_area.h2: Five counties across Northeast Florida
service_area.text: From the showroom at 11732 Beach Blvd, Woodsman serves homeowners and builders in Duval, St. Johns, Clay, Nassau and Baker counties. That covers Jacksonville and the beaches, Ponte Vedra, St. Augustine, Amelia Island and Yulee. Recent finished projects sit in Ponte Vedra, Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach, San Marco, Julington Creek and Coastal Oaks. Not sure your area is covered? Call and the team will check.

faq.h2: Good to know before you visit Beach Blvd

items.q: Is Woodsman a general contractor?
items.a: No. Woodsman says plainly that it is not a full-service general contractor. It handles kitchen design and layout, cabinet installation and tear-outs, quartz and granite fabrication and installation, and flooring. That covers everything from a cabinet-only upgrade to a complete kitchen transformation within that scope.

items.q: Where are the countertops made?
items.a: Woodsman offers quartz and granite only, and many tops are fabricated locally in the company's Jacksonville warehouse. items.q: Which cabinet brands can I see in the showroom?

intro.h2: A Capital Region remodeler with roots in a Delmar garage
paragraphs: Bennett Contracting handles kitchen remodeling in Albany, NY and across the Capital Region from its offices, showroom and warehouse at 693 South Pearl Street. The company traces back to 1915, when Dan Bennett opened a plumbing shop in a rented garage in Delmar. Today it is a full-service remodeler with more than 80 employees.

Design moved in-house in 2016, when Bennett also became a dealer of cabinets and countertops. Designers, project managers, carpenters and trades now work inside one company, so the team that plans your kitchen is the team that builds it. Estimates come from experienced professionals, not commission-driven salespeople.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Albany, NY and the rest of the house

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: In-house designers plan layout, cabinetry, countertops, lighting and appliances, then Bennett's own carpenters and trades build it. Older Capital Region homes are a specialty, from Victorian kitchens in Schenectady to lake-view kitchens in Saratoga. Its kitchen and bath business grew 1000% after the 1984 move to Albany.

image.alt: Award-winning modern Saratoga kitchen with dark flat-panel cabinets, black counters, glass pendant lights and lake-view windows

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Full bathroom renovations with tile, vanities, shower enclosures, water-saving fixtures and aging-in-place planning. Bennett's bathrooms have won a Qualified Remodeler Master Design Silver Prize in 2026 for a $75,000 to $100,000 bath, and recent jobs include Delmar, Slingerlands and Saratoga Springs.

image.alt: Ballard Blue bath in Saratoga Springs, NY with a blue-gray double vanity, granite top and oval silver mirrors

items.name: Additions and Whole-Home Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suite additions, family rooms, in-law spaces, expanded kitchens and multi-room remodels, with walls moved and structure reinforced where older homes need it. Project managers run each phase, from permitting to the final walkthrough. Bennett won CRBRA's Best Addition award in 2025.

image.alt: Bright room with arched dark wood windows, sliding patio doors and a stone wall opening onto a deck

items.name: Windows, Doors and Decks
items.blurb: Replacement windows, entry and patio doors, siding, decks, porches and seasonal rooms. Bennett's vinyl windows are made in the Northeast from American-made parts and carry a lifetime warranty, and installers are trained employees, not piece-rate subcontractors.

image.alt: Gray composite deck with black railings and Adirondack chairs off the back of a brown-sided home

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons Albany homeowners pick Bennett

items.title: Owners who know the history
items.text: Andrew and Kevin Gutman took over in 2019 from Paul Gutman and Greg Jackson, who ran the company for over 40 years. Their transition plan aims at a second hundred years in business.

items.title: Award-winning remodeler
items.text: CRBRA Remodeler of the Year in 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2022, and number 159 on the 2025 Qualified Remodeler Top 500 list of the nation's largest remodeling firms.

items.title: Safety taken seriously
items.text: Bennett won the NAHB SAFE Remodeler Safety Program of the Year for firms with 50+ employees in 2023 and 2024, with best-in-class training for every crew.

items.title: No pressure, financing available
items.text: Consultations are led by experienced professionals, not commission-driven sales. Financing is offered through a trusted lending partner for larger projects, as a convenience rather than a sales tool.

about.h2: A third-generation family business on South Pearl Street
about.text: Dan Bennett opened a plumbing shop in a rented garage in Delmar in 1915. After World War II his sons-in-law grew it into DA Bennett Plumbing & Heating. In the late 1970s grandson Greg Jackson and his friend Paul Gutman started an insulation business, which became Bennett Contracting, Inc. in 1984 and moved to 693 South Pearl Street in Albany. In 2019 Andrew Gutman, now President, and Kevin Gutman, Vice President, became the owners. Andrew calls it a 100-plus-year tradition of quality and integrity.
about.owner_role: President & Co-Owner (with Kevin Gutman, Vice President & Co-Owner)

process.h2: Bennett's five-phase remodeling process

steps.title: Conversation and evaluation
steps.text: Bennett learns about your goals, your home and the scope you have in mind, then sorts out feasibility, priorities and next steps.

steps.title: Design and planning
steps.text: Designers, and engineers where needed, settle layouts and structural details so decisions are made before construction starts, not during it.

steps.title: Pre-construction and permitting
steps.text: The team guides you through permits and scheduling so the project meets local codes before any work begins.

steps.title: Construction and project management
steps.text: A project manager coordinates trades, materials and timelines, and keeps you posted as the work moves forward.

steps.title: Completion and walkthrough
steps.text: You review the finished work together with the team, final details are addressed, and the job closes when it meets expectations.

service_area.h2: Albany, Schenectady, Troy, Saratoga and the towns between
service_area.text: Bennett is headquartered on South Pearl Street in Albany and lists 27 Capital Region communities it serves, from Delmar and Bethlehem, where the business began, to Clifton Park, Niskayuna, Troy and Saratoga Springs. Showroom staff can confirm whether your street is covered, and recent kitchen and bath projects have also been completed in Castleton, Slingerlands and Johnsonville. If your town is not on the list, call and ask.

faq.h2: Albany kitchen remodel questions for Bennett

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Bennett's FAQ invites homeowners to contact the office for a free consultation, and its project pages describe no-pressure consultations led by experienced professionals rather than commission-driven sales. You can call (518) 462-6731 or send a project inquiry with photos or plans attached.

items.q: Who designs my kitchen?
items.a: Bennett brought design in-house in 2016 and became a dealer of cabinets and countertops at the same time. Its FAQ says a quality kitchen contractor should offer an NKBA certified designer with full CAD drawings, architectural plans when structure changes, lighting design and a full line of appliances with installation.

items.q: Do you offer financing?
items.a: Yes. Bennett Contracting offers financing options through a trusted lending partner to help make larger projects more manageable. The company treats financing as a convenience, not a sales tool, and the team will walk you through the options if it helps line up your project timing with your budget.

items.q: Will my kitchen remodel need a permit?
items.a: Many projects do, depending on the scope and the municipality. Bennett advises you early in planning and handles the permitting steps as part of the process when they are required. Permitting and scheduling are a set phase before construction, so the project is compliant with local codes before work starts.

items.q: Can you work on an older Capital Region home?
items.a: Yes. Bennett lists deep experience in older Capital Region homes, where walls may need to move, structure may need reinforcing and layouts often date from a different era. Its portfolio includes a Victorian kitchen in Schenectady and a retro 1950s bathroom in Albany updated without losing its character.

final_cta.h2: Plan your kitchen with a team that has done it for generations
final_cta.text: Call (518) 462-6731 to talk with Bennett's office, or visit the showroom at 693 South Pearl Street, Monday to Friday.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Columbus, Ohio, With the Owner on Every Job
hero.subheadline: Michael Freed designs your kitchen with you, shows it in 3D before demo and fits it with custom cabinets built to order by Amish craftsmen in Ohio.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Columbus Ohio project in Upper Arlington: long white quartz island with woven stools, charcoal pantry cabinets, white range hood and white oak floors

intro.h2: A small Columbus team, from first sketch to final walkthrough
paragraphs: Elevate Remodeling is a design-build company offering kitchen remodeling in Columbus, Ohio, along with baths, basements and whole-home work. Owner Michael Freed founded it in 2016. He is a Columbus native and Ohio State graduate who has worked in remodeling since 2012, starting with hands-on construction.

Most remodeling companies pass a project from a salesperson to a designer to a crew of subs. At Elevate, the same small team stays with you from the first conversation to the keys. Clients often mention the communication. One Westerville homeowner wrote that the communication was outstanding from the initial consultation to the final walkthrough.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths, basements and Amish-built cabinets

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full remodels, layout changes and lighter refreshes, from a 1960s Clintonville ranch to an Upper Arlington colonial. Recent kitchens added waterfall islands, white oak shelving and a 36-inch Wolf range. Most Upper Arlington kitchens take six to ten weeks from demo to walkthrough.

image.alt: Upper Arlington, OH kitchen remodel with large white island and wood stools, stainless refrigerator and sliding door to the yard

items.name: Amish Custom Cabinetry
items.blurb: Cabinets are built to order by an Amish cabinet maker in Ohio. They use plywood boxes, solid wood face frames, hand-cut dovetail drawers and soft-close hardware, in maple, oak, mahogany or alder. Any Benjamin Moore or Sherwin-Williams color is available, or a custom stain.

image.alt: Upper Arlington, OH wet bar with white custom cabinets, marble-look counter, brass faucet, floating wood shelves and wine cooler

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites, hall baths, powder rooms, tub-to-shower conversions and aging-in-place updates. Expect frameless glass, custom tile, heated floors and Amish-made vanities. Most Upper Arlington bathrooms run three to five weeks, depending on the plumbing and tile scope.

image.alt: Dublin, OH primary bathroom remodel with marble-look tile shower, wood vanity with gold pulls, arched mirror and brass sconces

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Family rooms, guest suites, gyms, offices and wet bars. The team handles framing, electrical, egress windows and full bathrooms, including trenching the slab for plumbing. Most basements take 6 to 10 weeks of construction after design and permits.

image.alt: Finished basement in Upper Arlington, OH with open living area, recessed lighting, new carpet and white utility room doors

items.name: Whole-Home Renovation
items.blurb: Kitchen, baths, living spaces, flooring, trim and finishes handled as one design by one team. Michael helps you decide which walls can move, where storage belongs and how the house should flow. Work is phased so you can plan around living at home.

image.alt: Columbus, OH living room refresh with painted white brick fireplace, wall-mounted TV, light wood floors and new lighting

why_choose_us.h2: What you get when you hire Elevate

items.title: An exact quote, not a range
items.text: After the consultation, you get a 3D rendering and a real number tied to a real plan. The price changes only if you add scope, with no change-order-later routine.

items.title: The owner on site
items.text: Michael leads design with you, manages trade coordination and stays on the job to the final punch list. You are never handed to someone who missed the design talks.

items.title: Permits built into the schedule
items.text: Columbus, Upper Arlington, Dublin and Worthington each run their own permit reviews. Elevate pulls the permits and plans those timelines in from the start.

items.title: Licensed trades and a warranty
items.text: Licensed tradespeople do all mechanical work, which is inspected before walls close. Elevate is insured and gives a one-year workmanship warranty on top of vendor coverage.

about.h2: Meet Michael Freed
about.text: Michael Freed started Elevate Remodeling with a simple idea: homeowners deserve a remodel built on transparency, communication and craftsmanship, not surprises and excuses. He has worked in remodeling since 2012, moving from hands-on construction to leading full design-build renovations. That field time means he knows what is likely behind your walls and what a realistic timeline looks like. Michael lives in Upper Arlington and leads design with each homeowner using in-house 2D and 3D renderings. The team's site supervisor is Waffles, a dog who makes sure every project is up to snuff, always in his best bowtie.

process.h2: Five stages for every Columbus kitchen

steps.title: In-home consultation
steps.text: Michael comes to you, walks the space, asks how you cook and gather, and gets a clear read on your budget before designing anything.

steps.title: Design and selections
steps.text: Layout drawings and 3D renderings come first, then cabinets, counters, tile, appliances and lighting. Approving the shop drawings locks your design and price.

steps.title: Permits
steps.text: Elevate pulls permits and schedules inspections with your city, building each jurisdiction's review time into the plan instead of finding it mid-project.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Demo through final clean with one team and one point of contact. The jobsite is left organized at the end of every day.

steps.title: Walkthrough
steps.text: You walk the finished kitchen with Michael and the punch list is closed out before the project is called done.

service_area.h2: Older homes and newer builds around Columbus
service_area.text: Elevate works mainly in Columbus and its suburbs, from its base on Pemberton Drive. Older homes in Upper Arlington, Bexley and Clintonville often have plaster walls, cast iron drains and galley kitchens worth opening up. Newer homes in Dublin, Powell and New Albany usually have good floor plans with builder-grade finishes ready for an upgrade. Don't see your town below? Call and ask.

faq.h2: Before your Columbus kitchen remodel

items.q: Is the consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Elevate offers a free design consultation with no pressure and no obligation. It is an in-home visit, not a showroom appointment. Michael walks your space, talks about how you cook and gather, and gets a read on your budget range. After you reach out, expect a reply within one day.

items.q: How long will my kitchen be out of commission?
items.a: Most Upper Arlington kitchen remodels take six to ten weeks from demo to final walkthrough, depending on scope. Design, selections and permits come before that. Bathrooms usually run three to five weeks, and basements take 6 to 10 weeks of construction after design and permitting. Projects with a bathroom or egress window run toward the longer end.

items.q: Where are your cabinets made?
items.a: In Ohio, by an Amish cabinet maker, built to order for your kitchen. Boxes are full plywood with solid wood face frames, hand-cut dovetail drawers and soft-close hinges and glides. You can choose maple, oak, mahogany or alder, painted in any Benjamin Moore or Sherwin-Williams color or finished with a custom stain.

items.q: Will the price change after we start?
items.a: Only if you choose to add scope. After the consultation, Elevate creates a 3D rendering of the proposed layout and gives you an exact number tied to that plan. For fully custom cabinets, shop drawings are produced, and your approval locks in both the design and the price before anything gets built.

items.q: Do you work on older homes in Upper Arlington and Bexley?
items.a: Yes, often. Pre-war homes in Clintonville, Bexley and Old Arlington usually have plaster over wood lath, cast iron waste lines and one small original bathroom. Michael's construction background helps him plan for what is behind those walls. Elevate pulls permits with the City of Upper Arlington, including egress and electrical inspections for finished basements.

final_cta.h2: Talk to Michael about your kitchen
final_cta.text: Call Monday to Saturday, 8 am to 6 pm, or request a free in-home consultation. You will hear back within one day.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Santa Cruz, From Design to Final Walkthrough
hero.subheadline: Elite Construction pairs in-house interior designers with its own lead carpenters, so your kitchen, bath or ADU is planned and built by one team. Owners Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates have remodeled Santa Cruz County homes for more than two decades.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Santa Cruz project with a black and white geometric tile backsplash, white custom range hood, brass drum light and black-framed windows

intro.h2: An engineer and a Kiwi carpenter, building in Santa Cruz
paragraphs: Elite Construction has provided kitchen remodeling in Santa Cruz County for more than twenty years, along with bath renovations, additions and ADUs. The firm works from 347 Soquel Ave in Santa Cruz and knows the coastal conditions, permit processes and neighborhood styles from Aptos to Scotts Valley.

The partnership began on a rugby field. Eric Lamascus was an engineer in high-tech automation, and Craig Yates had finished a four-year building apprenticeship in his native New Zealand. They set out to make remodeling less stressful and more transparent, which shows in bids that break out labor, materials and subcontractors, plus an online portal for every job.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Santa Cruz, plus baths, whole homes and ADUs

items.name: Kitchens
items.blurb: Smart layouts and standout finishes, from a navy and walnut kitchen to a Pleasure Point remodel and a custom kitchen in the Santa Cruz Mountains. 'Better' kitchens add soft-close drawers, quartz or granite tops and upgraded fixtures. 'Best' brings custom cabinetry and can move walls or plumbing.

image.alt: Santa Cruz Mountains kitchen with a hammered copper apron sink, knotty alder cabinets, open shelves and a wide window onto the trees

items.name: Bathrooms
items.blurb: Relaxed, refined bathroom remodels with curbless showers, soaking tubs, Fireclay tile and custom vanities. Recent work includes a Pleasure Point bath with ocean views, a Pasatiempo update that traded a tub for a curbless walk-in shower, and a rustic primary bath with a hammered metal double sink.

image.alt: Pasatiempo bathroom remodel with a wood double vanity, black hex tile floor and curbless walk-in shower with a black granite bench

items.name: Whole Home Remodels
items.blurb: Transformational work across a whole house or condo, such as a coastal condo remodel in Santa Cruz and a Santa Cruz Mountains hideaway with a steel-clad fireplace. Each job runs on an online portal that tracks material deadlines, install dates and a running total of costs.

image.alt: Santa Cruz Mountains home remodel with a riveted steel fireplace surround, arched firebox door and reclaimed wood mantel

items.name: ADUs and Additions
items.blurb: Detached ADUs and additions built for Santa Cruz County lots. One rustic detached ADU in Santa Cruz has reclaimed wood siding, a pitched metal roof and French doors. A permit and estimate coordinator on staff keeps the paperwork moving while the design is finished.

image.alt: Rustic detached ADU in Santa Cruz with reclaimed wood siding, a pitched metal roof and French doors under oak trees

why_choose_us.h2: Why Santa Cruz County homeowners hire Elite

items.title: Pricing you can read

items.title: Carpenters on staff
