items.text: California Lic. #773506 is printed on every page. The site shows a Best of Houzz 2021 Service badge and a Santa Cruz Sentinel Readers Choice 2020 win.

about.h2: Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates, partners since the rugby field
about.text: Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates met playing rugby. Eric, now CEO, was a former engineer from Oklahoma working in high-tech automation. Craig had just finished a demanding four-year building apprenticeship in New Zealand, where construction standards are high. They formed Elite to make remodeling less stressful and more transparent, and they stay selective about the projects they take on. Today the owners lead a team of designers, coordinators, project managers and carpenters. Their own tagline sums up the goal: proof that you can love your contractor.

image.alt: Headshots of Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates, owners of Elite Construction in Santa Cruz, CA

process.h2: How an Elite remodel moves, step by step

steps.title: Share your ideas
steps.text: Call or email with photos and Pinterest or Houzz boards so the team can give a ballpark cost and judge whether it is a good fit.

steps.title: Design consultation at home
steps.text: A designer visits to learn your taste, wishes and budget so the bid that follows is accurate.

steps.title: Line-by-line estimate review
steps.text: You go through the bid line by line, with design and construction options to fit the scope to your budget.

steps.title: Finalize the design
steps.text: After pricing appliances and fixtures, you lock the layout. The online portal then shows material deadlines, install dates and running costs.

steps.title: Build, then relax
steps.text: Crews build the project and keep you in the loop. If an issue comes up after you move back in, the Elite guarantee covers you.

service_area.h2: Where Elite works in Santa Cruz County
service_area.text: Elite serves Santa Cruz County from its office in the Soquel Ocean Center at 347 Soquel Ave. The footer names Aptos, Soquel, Capitola, Santa Cruz and Scotts Valley, and finished projects sit in Pleasure Point, Pasatiempo, Seabright, Midtown and the Santa Cruz Mountains. Clients quoted on the site also live in Ben Lomond. Twenty-plus years here means the team knows coastal conditions and local permit processes.

faq.h2: What Santa Cruz homeowners ask Elite

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Santa Cruz?
items.a: Elite's pricing page lists a standard kitchen at $55,000 and up at its 'Better' level and $65,000 and up at 'Best.' Large kitchens start around $65,000 for 'Better' and $100,000 for 'Best.' Elite does not take 'Economy' work, which it describes as a typical rental-property remodel.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost?
items.a: A medium bathroom starts around $25,000 at the 'Better' level and $35,000 at 'Best.' A large bathroom starts around $35,000 for 'Better' and $60,000 for 'Best.' 'Better' covers quartz or granite tops and upgraded fixtures, while 'Best' adds custom cabinetry, designer fixtures and possible plumbing moves.

items.q: Is the estimate free?
items.a: Yes. Elite offers a free, no-obligation preliminary estimate for any project you are considering. Sending photos of your space and your Pinterest or Houzz boards helps the team give you a ballpark cost early, so you can decide whether Elite is a good fit before the design visit.

items.q: How will I know where my project and budget stand?
items.a: Each client gets access to an online portal. It shows detailed timelines for the materials you need to choose, such as tile and fixtures, the install dates for every phase, and a running total of expenses. Reviewers also praise steady communication from the bid through the build.

items.q: Do you build ADUs?
items.a: Yes. Elite builds ADUs and additions as well as kitchens, baths and whole-home remodels. Its gallery includes a rustic detached ADU in Santa Cruz with reclaimed wood siding, a pitched metal roof and French doors. A permit and estimate coordinator on staff helps keep the approvals on track.

final_cta.h2: Get a straight number on your remodel
final_cta.text: Call (831) 234-5052 or email Eric at EL@DiscoverElite.com for a free, no-obligation preliminary estimate.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Malden, MA, With Cabinets Built by Halco
hero.subheadline: Halco designs your kitchen or bath, builds it with cabinetry from quick ship to its own fully custom Halco Cabinet line, and backs every project with a 5-year warranty.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Malden MA and Greater Boston: Halco's Brookline kitchen with white inset cabinets, glass-front uppers, a quartz island with blue-gray stools and a skylight

intro.h2: A Malden remodeler that builds its own cabinets
paragraphs: Halco Kitchen & Bath handles kitchen remodeling in Malden, MA and across the Boston area north to southern New Hampshire. The team designs the space, supplies the cabinetry and manages construction, so the plan, the boxes and the install all come from one company. You can begin with a discovery call or an in-home consultation.

Cabinets are where Halco stands apart. You can choose quick ship, semi custom or full custom lines, or the company's own fully custom Halco Cabinet, in overlay, inset or frameless styles at any price point. Every project carries a 5-year warranty, and cabinetry adds a limited lifetime warranty.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Malden, MA, baths, cabinetry and additions

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full kitchen renovations planned with Halco's design team, from layout and cabinetry to counters and lighting. Recent kitchens include a navy-island kitchen in Ipswich, a two-tone kitchen in Beverly, a walnut kitchen in Wakefield and a custom-color kitchen in Melrose.

image.alt: Ipswich, MA kitchen with a navy island, orange counter stools, wood ceiling beams, blue tile backsplash and white cabinets

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and condo bathrooms with custom vanities, tile and fixtures. Portfolio work includes a primary bath in North Reading, contemporary bathrooms in a South End condo and a bath in Cambridge, each paired with Halco cabinetry.

image.alt: North Reading, MA primary bathroom with a charcoal double vanity, white quartz top, oval mirrors and light blue walls

items.name: Custom Cabinetry
items.blurb: Quick ship, semi custom, full custom and Halco's own fully custom Halco Cabinet, in overlay, inset or frameless construction. Beyond kitchens, the team builds pantries, built-ins, bar cabinetry and mudroom benches, all with a limited lifetime warranty on cabinetry.

image.alt: Lynnfield, MA built-in pantry with navy cabinetry, a butcher-block counter, farmhouse sink and brass faucet

items.name: Additions and Mudrooms
items.blurb: Expanding the existing home, attached or detached garages, sunrooms, porches and decks, plus mudrooms, basements and attics. Halco lists 12 to 16 weeks for a typical addition, project dependent, and recent work includes an addition in Middleton.

image.alt: Middleton, MA home addition with sage siding, a dark roof, a covered front porch and an attached garage

items.name: New Construction
items.blurb: Design and building of new homes, typically 6 months to a year depending on the project. The home page features a two-story new home with a full-width front porch, and the portfolio includes new construction in Middleton.

image.alt: Front view of a two-story new construction home with greige siding, white columns, a black front door and fall mums on the steps

why_choose_us.h2: Why North Shore homeowners call Halco

items.title: Cabinets at every price point
items.text: Halco designs with quick ship, semi custom, full custom and its own Halco Cabinet line, so you can match the look you want to your budget without changing contractors.

items.title: Warranties in plain numbers
items.text: Every associated project carries a 5-year warranty, and cabinetry comes with a limited lifetime warranty. Both are stated on the site, not hidden in a contract.

items.title: Timelines you can plan around
items.text: Interior remodels typically run 5 to 7 weeks, additions 12 to 16 weeks and new construction 6 months to a year, each project dependent, so you can plan around the work.

items.title: A contained, clean job site
items.text: The crew lays floor protection and plastic walls to keep dust in the work area, and you track the schedule and documents in an online project portal. Google reviewers note a clean workspace and a project that stayed on schedule.

about.h2: The team behind Halco
about.text: Halco is led by co-owners Tyler Procopio, Vice President of Construction, and Tim Procopio Jr., Vice President of Operations. Ally Procopio directs operations and Kelly Procopio directs marketing. Designer Amanda Rivera works with clients on layouts and finishes, project manager Erin Roe keeps jobs on track, and carpenters Wesley Oliveria, Blad Martins and Felipe Ferares do the build. One Google reviewer described setting up a consultation with Jarod and Tyler, who came out to the house to take measurements before designing her new kitchen.

image.alt: Tyler Procopio, co-owner of Halco Kitchen & Bath in Malden, MA

process.h2: What happens from first call to final inspection

steps.title: Discovery call or home visit
steps.text: Start with a discovery phone call or an in-home consultation so the team understands your project, explains the process and answers early questions.

steps.title: Contract and scheduling
steps.text: After the contract is signed and the deposit is placed, a team member sets your anticipated start date and opens your online project portal.

steps.title: Prep and protection
steps.text: You clear the work area of furniture, decor and cabinet contents. The crew lays floor protection and builds plastic walls to keep dust contained.

steps.title: Demo, framing and inspection
steps.text: The crew completes demolition, framing and rough mechanicals, and the town inspector signs off before any walls are closed up.

steps.title: Finishes and final sign-off
steps.text: Board is hung, finished materials and mechanicals are installed, and any final inspections take place before the project wraps up.

If your town sits inside that range, the team can likely help.

faq.h2: Before you book: common Halco questions

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: Halco lists 5 to 7 weeks for interior remodeling such as a kitchen or bath, project dependent. Additions typically take 12 to 16 weeks, and new construction runs 6 months to a year. A team member gives you an anticipated start date once the contract is signed and the deposit is placed.

items.q: What warranty do I get?
items.a: Every associated project comes with a 5-year warranty. Cabinetry also carries a limited lifetime warranty. Both terms are printed on Halco's own FAQ, so you know the coverage before you sign, and your project documents stay in your online portal.

items.q: What cabinet options do you offer?
items.a: Halco works with quick ship, semi custom and full custom cabinetry, plus its own fully custom Halco Cabinet line. It can design in overlay, inset and frameless styles at all price points, and the same cabinetry shows up in built-ins, pantries, bars and mudrooms across its portfolio.

items.q: What should I expect once work starts?
items.a: You clear the work area of furniture, decor and cabinet contents. Halco protects floors and puts up plastic walls to contain dust, then completes demo, framing and rough mechanicals for the town inspector to sign off. After that come board, finishes and final inspections, all tracked in your online project portal.

items.q: Do you work outside Malden?
items.a: Yes. Halco covers the Boston area north to southern New Hampshire. Recent projects include Melrose, Wakefield, Lynnfield, North Reading, Peabody, Beverly, Middleton, Topsfield, Boxford and Ipswich, along with city projects in Cambridge, Brookline, the South End and Beacon Hill. Not sure about your town? Ask on the discovery call.

hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Buford, GA, Led by Owner Taylor Scalera
hero.subheadline: Taylor Scalera started as a project estimator and built Integral Renovations around fair pricing and a hassle-free job. His crew handles master baths, showers and kitchens, and you can see the plan in 3D first.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Buford GA project: white subway tile walls, freestanding tub, black double vanity and brass chandelier

intro.h2: A master bath done right, often in days
paragraphs: Integral Renovations handles bathroom remodeling in Buford, GA from its shop on Braselton Highway, and master baths are among the projects its Google reviewers mention most. Reviewers say owner Taylor Scalera visits often to check on progress, and they name his crew members, like Carlos and Juan, in their reviews.

The work starts with a free design consultation about your goals and budget. From there the team can build a 3D rendering so you can walk through the room before anything is torn out. Depending on scope, many of its bathroom remodels are finished in just a few days, so you are not without a bathroom for long.

services.h2: Remodeling services from the Buford shop

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Full renovations, master baths and small-bathroom remodels that make the most of tight space. The team installs custom showers and tubs, vanities and countertops, storage and tile, with project managers keeping each job on track and within budget.

image.alt: Freestanding soaking tub under a picture window framed by dark marble-look wall tile

items.name: Showers, Tile & Flooring
items.blurb: Walk-in showers with frameless glass, multi-jet systems and tiled niches, plus tile and flooring for bathrooms, kitchens and the rest of the house. Reviewers mention new floors finished on tight timelines, with the old flooring ripped out and replaced fast.

image.alt: Walk-in shower with marble-look tile, frameless glass enclosure and rain showerhead beside a window

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling & Installation
items.blurb: Complete kitchen remodels or targeted upgrades: custom cabinetry or cabinet refacing, quartz, granite, marble or butcher block counters, new backsplash tile, lighting, flooring and appliance integration. The crew handles the plumbing, electrical and cabinet installation too.

image.alt: White kitchen with wood-stained island, stainless gas cooktop, glass pendant lights and built-in shelving

items.name: Basement Remodels
items.blurb: Unfinished basements turned into living space, game rooms and bars. Basement renovation is one of the topics Google reviewers mention most, and one finished basement even includes a golf simulator room with turf, an impact screen and a wall-mounted TV.

image.alt: Finished basement golf simulator room with green turf, impact screen and wall-mounted TV

items.name: Complete Home Remodels
items.blurb: Whole-house updates, from opening up a floor plan to adding an extra bedroom for a growing family. Designers, contractors and project managers work as one team, and the company also builds decks and screened porches when the project heads outdoors.

image.alt: Two-story living room with built-in shelving, fireplace, ceiling fan and hardwood floors after a home remodel

why_choose_us.h2: Why Buford homeowners hire Integral

items.title: An owner who started as an estimator
items.text: Taylor Scalera learned pricing as a project estimator before running a growing remodeling company. He founded Integral to give homeowners quality work with extremely fair pricing.

items.title: You know when the crew is coming
items.text: Reviewer Shari H. wrote that Integral kept her informed and updated on progress each day, with arrival times given every morning.

items.title: Quick bathroom turnarounds
items.text: Depending on scope, many Integral bathroom remodels are finished in just a few days. Albert F. wrote that his bathroom and new kitchen backsplash were done on time and on budget.

items.title: See it in 3D first
items.text: Integral offers 3D renderings with layouts, colors and finishes you can adjust, so you can walk through the new bathroom or kitchen before demolition and avoid surprises.

about.h2: Taylor Scalera built Integral after years in the field
about.text: Taylor Scalera spent his summers learning the details of residential construction. After a short corporate job out of college, he went back to building, starting as a project estimator for a small handyman business and rising to vice president as it grew to a national presence. After six years there, he founded Integral Renovations. In his words, his goal is to use his knowledge and network to give homeowners a quality, hassle-free experience with extremely fair pricing. Today he leads a team with backgrounds in design, construction and project management, and reviewers say he visits often to check on progress.

image.alt: Taylor Scalera, founder of Integral Renovations

process.h2: Bathroom Remodeling in Buford, GA, Step by Step

steps.title: Free design consultation
steps.text: Sit down with the team to talk through your vision, preferences and budget, and share the bathroom ideas you have been saving.

steps.title: Design and planning
steps.text: Integral builds a custom design plan and helps you choose materials, fixtures and layout. A 3D rendering is available so you can see the room first.

steps.title: Construction and installation
steps.text: The crew handles everything from demolition to installing vanities, showers and flooring, with a project manager keeping the job on schedule and within budget.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: When the work is done, the team walks the new bathroom with you to make sure every detail meets your expectations before they call it finished.

service_area.h2: Based in Buford, working across the Atlanta area
service_area.text: Integral Renovations works out of 2693 Braselton Hwy in Buford, Georgia, and takes on projects for clients across Georgia, including Atlanta and the surrounding areas. The office is open weekdays from 10 am to 4 pm, with evening and Saturday visits available on request. If you are not sure whether your home is in range, call the shop and ask.

faq.h2: Bathroom remodeling questions from Buford homeowners

items.q: How long does a bathroom remodel take?
items.a: It depends on scope, but many Integral bathroom remodels are completed in just a few days, so you get your bathroom back without a long disruption. Larger master bath renovations take longer, so ask for a timeline for your exact scope at the free design consultation.

items.q: Is the design consultation really free?
items.a: Yes. Integral starts every bathroom and kitchen project with a free consultation to talk through your vision, your preferences and your budget. It is also the time to share any bathroom ideas you have saved, so the team can tell you what will work in your space.

items.q: Can I see my new bathroom before work starts?
items.a: Yes. Integral offers 3D renderings that let you walk through the planned room and adjust layouts, colors and finishes in real time. Seeing the space first helps you make decisions with confidence and cuts down on surprises once construction begins.

items.q: Do you remodel kitchens too?
items.a: Yes. Kitchen work ranges from complete remodels to targeted upgrades: custom cabinetry or cabinet refacing, countertops in quartz, granite, marble or butcher block, backsplash tile, lighting, flooring and appliance integration. The crew handles the plumbing, electrical and cabinet installation as part of the job.

items.q: What hours can I reach you?
items.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 10 am to 4 pm. After 4 pm and on Saturdays, appointments are available on request. Call (470) 993-4343 or email taylor@integralrenovations.co, and you can also request a quote through the online form.

hero.h1: Custom Kitchen Cabinetry in Gray, ME, Built by the Laplantes
hero.subheadline: Founder and head craftsman Ryan Laplante builds the cabinets, and lead designer Kevin Laplante plans the layout. One family shop takes your kitchen from first sketch to final install.

image.alt: Custom kitchen cabinetry Gray ME: white cabinets, a dark island with a white top, lantern pendants and a wood plank ceiling by Laplante Cabinetry

intro.h2: A Maine cabinet shop, not a showroom
paragraphs: Laplante Cabinetry has made custom kitchen cabinetry in Gray, ME since 2015. It is a family-owned and operated shop, and the founder is the person who builds your cabinets. More than 50 projects later, every job still starts with a conversation about how you cook, store things and gather in the room.

Not every kitchen needs a full tear-out. Some clients get refinished cabinets, new doors and hardware, or modified boxes that fit a new appliance. Others want a complete custom kitchen with a new island and layout. Recent Google reviewers say Ryan's craftsmanship shows in every single detail of the build.

services.h2: From new doors to a fully custom kitchen

items.name: Custom Kitchen Design
items.blurb: Lead designer Kevin Laplante plans each kitchen around how your family uses it, in modern, traditional or contemporary styles. The work covers functional layout planning, space optimization, appliance integration and material selection, so the design fits both your room and your routine.

image.alt: Custom kitchen with white full-height cabinets, a charcoal island with a white quartz top and black pendant lights

items.name: Bespoke Cabinetry
items.blurb: Cabinets are crafted with precision and close attention to detail, then installed by the same team. Islands can carry special touches, such as a reclaimed wood end panel or a built-in microwave drawer, so the finished kitchen looks made for the house it is in.

image.alt: Custom white kitchen island with a dark reclaimed wood end panel and a built-in microwave drawer

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling and Updates
items.blurb: Remodels range from cabinet refinishing, through partner Eastern Finish, to new doors and hardware, cabinet modifications and complete custom kitchens. One project turned dated orange oak cabinets into a white kitchen with a granite-topped island.

image.alt: Before and after kitchen remodel: dated oak cabinets replaced with white cabinets and a granite island

items.name: Custom Built-ins
items.blurb: The shop also builds custom furniture and built-in pieces for kitchens and living spaces, such as a painted built-in cabinet with open shelves. Each piece is made to match the cabinetry and trim already in your home.

image.alt: Custom painted built-in cabinet with open shelves and closed storage beside a hallway gallery wall

why_choose_us.h2: Why work with a family cabinet shop

items.title: The owner builds it
items.text: Ryan Laplante is the founder and head craftsman. Google reviewer Bruce M. calls him the head craftsman and owner who does exceptional design and work, so you deal with the builder directly.

items.title: Design and build in one family
items.text: Kevin Laplante leads design while Ryan leads the build. Plans are drawn by people who know how the cabinets will actually be made and installed, which keeps the finished kitchen true to the drawing.

items.title: Options short of a tear-out
items.text: If your boxes are sound, refinishing, new doors and hardware, or cabinet modifications can refresh the room. If they are not, the shop builds a complete custom kitchen instead.

items.title: Support after the install
items.text: Project management covers you from initial planning to final installation, and post-installation support is part of the service list, so questions after move-in still have a home.

about.h2: Meet Ryan and Kevin Laplante
about.text: Laplante Cabinetry, also known as Laplante and Sons Custom Cabinetry, is a family-owned kitchen design and custom cabinetry company in Gray, Maine. Ryan Laplante founded it in 2015 and works as head craftsman, building the cabinets himself. Kevin Laplante is the lead designer who turns your wish list into a layout. Together they have completed more than 50 projects. The company says it blends traditional skills with newer techniques, and its stated mission is exceptional design, quality craftsmanship and personal service on every project.

image.alt: Ryan and Kevin Laplante of Laplante Cabinetry in Gray, Maine

process.h2: How a Laplante kitchen comes together

steps.title: Call or write
steps.text: Call 207-513-8440 or send the contact form with a few lines about your kitchen and what is not working today.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: Kevin plans the layout, appliance spots, storage and materials with you, whether you want a refresh or a full custom kitchen.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Ryan crafts the cabinetry and built-ins to your plan, with the precision and attention to detail that reviewers point out.

steps.title: Install and finish
steps.text: The team installs the cabinets, adds the finishing touches and manages the project to the end, with support after installation.

faq.h2: Questions about custom kitchen cabinetry in Gray, ME

items.q: Who actually builds my cabinets?
items.a: Ryan Laplante, the founder and head craftsman. Laplante Cabinetry is family owned and operated, and Ryan leads the build while Kevin Laplante leads design. Google reviewers name Ryan directly, and one calls him the head craftsman and owner who does exceptional design and work.

items.q: Can you update my kitchen without replacing every cabinet?
items.a: Often, yes. Remodels range from refinishing, offered with partner Eastern Finish, to new doors and hardware and modifications to your existing cabinets. If your cabinet boxes are not worth saving or the layout needs to change, the shop designs and builds a complete custom kitchen instead.

items.q: What does the design work include?
items.a: Kevin Laplante plans the layout so the kitchen flows well, fits your appliances and makes the most of the space, whether the room is compact or large. Material selection and finishing touches are part of the plan, and styles range from modern to traditional and contemporary.

items.q: Do you build anything besides kitchens?
items.a: Yes. Along with kitchens, the shop builds custom built-ins and furniture pieces made to match your kitchen and living spaces, such as painted built-in cabinets with open shelving. Ask about a built-in when you plan your kitchen so the woodwork and finish match from room to room.

items.q: What happens after the cabinets are installed?
items.a: The company manages each project from initial planning to final installation and lists post-installation support among its services. If something needs attention after you move back into your kitchen, call 207-513-8440 and talk with the family that built it rather than a call center.

intro.h2: A general contractor that specializes in bathrooms
paragraphs: North2South Renovations offers bathroom remodeling in Delray Beach, FL and across Palm Beach County from its base on Albatross Road. Founder and owner-operator Colby Matheny started the company to bring honesty and real craftsmanship back to South Florida remodeling. The team brings 15 years of hands-on renovation experience to every job, large or small.

Because North2South holds a Florida certified general contractor license, it can take a bathroom down to the studs, move plumbing, pull permits and pass inspections without handing you off. Google reviewers say the same thing in different words: Colby explains what to expect each day, sets clear expectations and follows through.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Delray Beach, FL, plus kitchens and whole homes

items.name: Full Bathroom Renovations
items.blurb: Primary suites, guest baths and full gut renovations with walk-in showers, custom vanities, tile design and lighting upgrades. Materials are chosen to last in Florida's coastal climate. Recent work includes a fully renovated bathroom in Boca Raton with floating vanities and large-format tile.

image.alt: Renovated bathroom in Boca Raton, FL with a floating wood double vanity, arched brass mirrors and large-format beige porcelain walls

items.name: Shower and Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: Old tubs and cramped stalls replaced with custom walk-in showers. The work runs through demolition, rough-in plumbing, waterproofing, tile, glass and fixtures, with GFCI outlets and new lighting circuits brought up to current code along the way.

image.alt: Remodeled bathroom with gray shaker double vanity, backlit mirrors and a marble-look walk-in shower with pebble floor

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling and Custom Cabinets

process.h2: How a North2South bathroom remodel runs

The team remodels bathrooms and kitchens throughout Palm Beach County, including Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, West Palm Beach, Jupiter and Wellington. faq.h2: Delray Beach bathroom remodel questions

items.q: Are you licensed and insured?
items.a: Yes. North2South Renovations is a fully licensed and insured Florida certified general contractor, license CBC1269429. That license lets the company take on structural changes, additions and multi-trade projects, not only cosmetic updates, and it is printed in the footer of every page on the website.

items.q: Will my bathroom remodel need a permit?
items.a: Most bathroom renovations that move plumbing, change electrical or alter the structure need one. In Boynton Beach, for example, permits go through the City of Boynton Beach Building Department. As the general contractor, North2South handles permitting, inspections and code compliance for you.

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. North2South offers a free consultation. During it, the team will also tell you honestly whether your project needs a licensed general contractor or whether a specialty contractor would be enough for a smaller cosmetic job. Call (561) 664-3256 or use the contact form.

items.q: Which cities do you serve?
items.a: All of Palm Beach County, including Delray Beach, Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, West Palm Beach, Jupiter and Wellington. If you are not sure your neighborhood is covered, the company asks you to call and talk through the project anyway.

items.q: What cabinet and countertop options do you offer?
items.a: Full custom shaker cabinets, inset cabinets for a seamless look, and semi-custom white cabinets that cost less and arrive sooner. Countertops come in quartz, quartzite and granite, and North2South says it fabricates them in-house for a precise fit in kitchens and bathroom vanities.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling Jupiter FL, Designed and Built by One Team
hero.subheadline: Palmhouse Design & Build plans, prices and builds your kitchen with one accountable team. You get a line-by-line estimate before work begins and a single point of contact through the final walkthrough.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Jupiter FL: wood shaker cabinets, quartzite waterfall island, brass pendants and stainless range hood

intro.h2: Why Jupiter kitchen remodeling works better with one team
paragraphs: Palmhouse Design & Build has handled kitchen remodeling Jupiter FL homeowners trust since 2005, along with baths, interiors and whole-home renovations across Palm Beach County. Co-founders Oscar and Rosie Barrig lead the company alongside Jonathan and Gabriel Barrig, both Certified General Contractors.

Every project gets a Design Consultant, an Interior Designer and a Project Manager. Design, budgeting, scheduling and construction stay under one roof, so the plan that gets drawn is the plan that gets built. The firm says plainly that it is not the lowest-price option. It is for homeowners who want clear communication and a fully managed process.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths and whole homes across Palm Beach County

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Kitchens reshaped around how your household cooks and gathers, from layout and cabinetry to counters, lighting and appliances. Floor plans, elevations and digital renderings let you see the room first, and the specifications give a complete cost analysis before you sign.

image.alt: Jupiter kitchen remodel with white oak cabinets, glossy white tile, plaster range hood, black pantry wall and woven pendants

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Spa-style primary baths, guest baths and powder rooms, with tub and shower installation, tile, vanities and lighting. Your Interior Designer guides selections in the Palmhouse Design Studio, and the same contracting team that permitted the job builds it.

image.alt: High-end bathroom renovation by Palmhouse with a freestanding soaking tub, navy walls, botanical wallpaper and brass fixtures

items.name: Custom Cabinetry
items.blurb: Custom cabinets for kitchens, baths and storage throughout the home. For kitchen projects where the layout already works, custom cabinets are also offered as a stand-alone service, built to fit your existing footprint without a full remodel.

image.alt: Jupiter kitchen with walnut slab cabinets, integrated refrigerator panels, white quartz waterfall island and globe pendants

items.name: Interior Design and Whole-Home Renovation
items.blurb: Floor plans, material palettes and finish selections handled in-house, from a single room to a full house. The team orders products, tracks deliveries and gives weekly ETAs, and out-of-state owners can run a full remodel virtually by Zoom, Google Meet, email and text.

image.alt: Modern Jupiter interior with white upper cabinets, walnut lower cabinets, dark glass tile backsplash and stainless range hood

items.name: Exteriors and Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Stucco repair, exterior painting, impact windows and doors, reroofing, gutters, pavers and patio summer kitchens, finished for the Florida climate. One Jupiter backyard went from bare lawn to a new pool with a tiled spa and paver deck.

image.alt: Before and after backyard renovation in Jupiter, FL: bare lawn turned into a pool with tiled spa and paver deck

why_choose_us.h2: What Palm Beach County homeowners get with Palmhouse

items.title: Line-by-line pricing
items.text: You get a detailed, line-by-line estimate before work begins, and the construction agreement spells out the timeline, payment schedule, approved specifications, drawings and final budget.

items.title: A home that stays livable
items.text: Daily jobsite cleaning, dust control systems and floor and surface protection are standard. A Google reviewer noted the crew cleaned up the work area at the end of each day.

items.title: Licensed builders on staff
items.text: Jonathan and Gabriel Barrig are Certified General Contractors, and project manager Jason Vassalotti is OSHA certified with more than 20 years in reconstruction.

items.title: Any size, same standard
items.text: From $10K renovations to multi-million dollar projects, the team, structure and process stay the same, whether it is one bathroom in Jupiter or an estate on Palm Beach Island.

about.h2: The Barrigs behind Palmhouse
about.text: Oscar Barrig co-founded Palmhouse and serves as managing partner, bringing more than three decades of contracting and building experience. Co-founder Rosie Barrig has over 30 years in administration and residential space planning and keeps every project organized, so spaces come out both good-looking and highly functional. Jonathan and Gabriel Barrig are Certified General Contractors who manage projects and handle budgeting, local codes, universal design and energy efficiency. Reviewers mention Oscar by name, and one said he and his team are "respectful, timely, and talented at what they do."

image.alt: Oscar Barrig, co-founder of Palmhouse Design & Build in Jupiter, FL

process.h2: How a Palmhouse remodel moves from consultation to keys

steps.title: Complimentary consultation
steps.text: A Design Consultant meets you at home to talk through goals and budget and suggest solutions. Out-of-state owners can start by phone or video.

steps.title: Design and planning
steps.text: Your Design Consultant and Interior Designer photograph and measure the home, then draw a custom plan around the way you live.

steps.title: Presentation and agreement
steps.text: You review floor plans, elevations, renderings and a full cost analysis, then sign a construction agreement with timeline, payment schedule and final budget.

steps.title: Selections and permits
steps.text: You choose finishes in the client-only Design Studio while the team orders products and secures HOA approvals and permits.

steps.title: Construction and finish
steps.text: A weekly schedule keeps you informed during the build. At the end, your design fee is credited to the final bill and a two-year warranty begins.

service_area.h2: From Jupiter Island to Palm Beach
service_area.text: Palmhouse works from its Maplewood Drive showroom in Jupiter across northern Palm Beach County and beyond. That includes Tequesta, Juno Beach and Jupiter Island to the north, and Palm Beach Gardens communities such as BallenIsles, Mirasol, PGA National and Old Palm. It also covers waterfront work in North Palm Beach and historic and oceanfront estates on Palm Beach Island, where HOA review and access coordination are part of every plan.

faq.h2: Kitchen remodeling Jupiter FL questions we hear most

items.q: How will I know what my remodel costs?
items.a: Before construction you get a line-by-line estimate. At the design presentation, the specifications give a complete cost analysis of the plan. Once you approve it, the construction agreement lists the timeline, payment schedule, approved specifications, drawings and final budget, so the numbers are settled before work starts.

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. The first meeting is a complimentary consultation at your home with a Design Consultant to discuss goals, budget and possible solutions. If you move forward, design work begins under a retainer, and your design fee is credited toward your final bill when the project is finished.

items.q: Do you work in gated and golf communities?
items.a: Yes. Palmhouse has completed renovations in Palm Beach Gardens communities including BallenIsles, Mirasol and PGA National. The team prepares construction-ready documents and handles the HOA approvals, permits and access coordination these neighborhoods require, as well as waterfront planning in North Palm Beach.

items.q: Can you manage my remodel while I am out of state?
items.a: Yes. Many clients are snowbirds or own vacation homes in Florida. Palmhouse has completed full house remodels while meeting clients by Google Meet, Zoom, email and text. Each week you get clear ETAs for deliveries and key milestones, so you can follow progress from anywhere.

items.q: What warranty do you offer?
items.a: Palmhouse backs its work with a two-year warranty that starts when your project is complete. The company is a licensed general contractor in Florida, carries insurance, and lists BBB accreditation and memberships in the National Association of Home Builders and the Florida Home Builders Association.

intro.h2: A father-and-son company with its own crew
paragraphs: Rohrer For Construction has offered kitchen and bath remodeling in Lake County, IL since 1989. Adolph Rohrer founded the company, and today he and his son Austin run it together. Most of the work is done by their own crew, a team that has worked together for more than 35 years, which keeps quality and communication in one place.

Kitchens and baths lead the list, but the same crew also finishes basements, builds additions, garages and decks, and handles exteriors. That range helps when a bathroom job uncovers framing or plumbing that needs attention. Permits in towns like Grayslake, Libertyville and Mundelein are handled for you.

services.h2: Kitchen and bath remodeling in Lake County, IL, and beyond

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full renovations, layout fixes, small-kitchen makeovers and open-concept updates, planned around cabinet storage, prep space and traffic flow. A moderate Lake County kitchen typically runs $25,000 to $75,000; custom cabinetry and high-end finishes can run higher.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with gray Shaker cabinets, white quartz counters, stainless appliances and oak floors

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Guest baths to primary suites, built with Schluter waterproofing and fixtures from brands like Delta and Kohler. A typical bathroom takes 2 to 4 weeks, depending on whether it needs new tile, a plumbing move or a full gut renovation.

items.name: Showers and Tub Conversions
items.blurb: Walk-in, curbless and enclosed showers, tub-to-shower conversions and bathtub replacements. For a curbless shower the crew first checks floor depth and the drain route, then builds slope, waterproofing, tile and glass as one project, with blocking for grab bars where needed.

image.alt: Shower with dark-framed sliding glass door, gray wood-look wall tile and a low white shower base

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Unfinished lower levels turned into usable rooms, from open family spaces with new flooring and lighting to specialty features like a basement sauna. Framing, insulation, drywall and flooring are handled by the same crew that does your kitchen.

items.name: Additions, Garages and Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Room additions, second-floor additions, garages, decks, pergolas and screen houses. Planning, permits, construction and the final walkthrough are managed by the same team, so even a larger, multi-phase project still has one point of contact from start to finish.

service_area.h2: About 20 miles around Lindenhurst
service_area.text: Rohrer works within roughly 20 miles of Lindenhurst. That covers northern and central Lake County, from Antioch and Fox Lake down to Libertyville and Mundelein, and south toward Buffalo Grove and Lake Forest. Across the state line, the crew also supports Kenosha, Pleasant Prairie, Salem, Bristol and Twin Lakes. Projects just outside the radius may still qualify, so reach out anyway.

faq.h2: Lake County remodeling questions

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Lake County?
items.a: A moderate kitchen renovation typically runs $25,000 to $75,000, depending on size, materials and scope. Projects with custom cabinetry and high-end finishes can run higher, and moving plumbing or appliances adds work. Rohrer gives free, detailed estimates so you know what to expect before anything starts.

items.q: How long does a bathroom remodel take?
items.a: In Rohrer's experience a typical bathroom takes 2 to 4 weeks. New tile, a relocated drain or a full gut each change the schedule. You get a clear timeline at the start and regular updates while the crew works, so you know when the room will be ready to use again.

items.q: Do I need a permit for my remodel?
items.a: Most structural, electrical and plumbing work and all additions need permits in Lake County towns such as Grayslake, Libertyville and Mundelein. Rohrer handles the permit process for you and builds to local code, with the goal of passing inspection the first time.

items.q: Do you do more than kitchens and baths?
items.a: Yes. The same crew finishes basements, builds room additions, garages and decks, and handles exterior painting and siding. Specialty jobs like a basement sauna, screen houses and pergolas are in the portfolio too. One contractor for a mixed project means fewer hand-offs and clearer accountability.

items.q: Can I finance my project?
items.a: Yes. Rohrer has a referral partnership with RenoFi, a lender focused on renovation loans that, according to the company, often offers better rates than traditional options. The process is simple and carries no obligation, so you can check your numbers while you plan the project.

final_cta.text: Call (847) 668-7183 for a free in-person quote, or post a question in the Rohrer Facebook group if you are still deciding.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Caldwell With a Master Craftsman on the Job
hero.subheadline: Michael Kuhn has spent over 35 years building and remodeling. His family business designs kitchens and baths, builds custom cabinets locally, and starts every project with a free estimate.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Caldwell area: gray shaker cabinets, navy island with white quartz top, gas cooktop, glass pendants and mustard leather stools

intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Caldwell, explained before it is built
paragraphs: Treasure Valley Redesign & Remodel offers kitchen remodeling in Caldwell and across the valley as a small, family-owned company. Founder Michael Kuhn grew up watching his father build cabinets, framed houses with his cousin, and eventually ran his own crew. Today his daughter Becca works beside him.

Their core value is client education. Michael writes openly about why two remodel bids can look so different, how allowances change a price and why picking materials early matters. The aim is simple: you should know what is being built, what is included and what is still open before work starts. Reviewers say they valued the team's knowledge, attention to detail and fair pricing.

services.h2: What the TVRR team builds

items.name: Kitchen Remodel and Renovation
items.blurb: New layouts, smarter storage and quality materials that turn a dated kitchen into a place to cook and gather. One reviewer's kitchen was built hand in hand with her outside designer, so you can bring your own designer or use theirs.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with light oak tall cabinets, navy lower cabinets, white waterfall island and black pendant lights

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Walk-in tile showers, freestanding tubs, new vanities and lighting for primary and hall baths. One Google reviewer has had the team remodel three bathrooms and a kitchen, and says they stand behind everything they do.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with natural wood vanity, brass fixtures, marble-look frameless glass shower and freestanding tub

items.name: Custom Cabinetry
items.blurb: Locally crafted cabinets for kitchens, mudrooms, entertainment walls and office built-ins, designed and built to fit your space exactly. Michael's start in the trade came from watching his father build cabinets, and it still shows in the details.

image.alt: Custom white built-in entertainment wall with lighted open shelves, arched TV niche and shaker base cabinets

items.name: Home and Office Additions
items.blurb: New bedrooms, family rooms, garages and work space that match the existing house in look and function, so you gain room without uprooting your family or business. Basement remodels and attic-bedroom conversions are also on the service list.

image.alt: Rear of a gray-sided home with a single-story addition, new windows, patio door and curved concrete walkway

items.name: Decks, Patios and Covers
items.blurb: As a Trex Pro, Michael builds composite decks along with patios, awnings and outdoor kitchens. The team also offers disaster restoration after flood, fire or storm damage, from the first damage assessment through a full rebuild of your home or business.

image.alt: White pergola-style patio cover over a gray deck on a brick ranch home with solar panels

why_choose_us.h2: Why valley homeowners keep calling TVRR back

items.title: The owner is the craftsman
items.text: Michael Kuhn has more than 35 years of hands-on building and leads every project himself, with a vision of the finished space before the first nail goes in.

items.title: Free consultations, clear bids
items.text: Consultations and estimates are always free, in person or virtual. Proposals spell out scope and allowances so you can compare bids on equal terms.

items.title: Repeat clients
items.text: One family has worked with TVRR for nearly two decades on a custom home and several remodels. A Google reviewer has used them for a kitchen and three bathrooms.

items.title: They solve the puzzle
items.text: The team likes intricate jobs other contractors shy away from, and only sends trusted crew members into your home, people they would welcome into their own.

about.h2: Meet Michael Kuhn, founder and master craftsman
about.text: Michael Kuhn's love for building started when he watched his father craft cabinets. He went on to frame houses with his cousin, ran his own crew, and then started his own company. After more than 35 years, he still approaches each kitchen, bath, addition and deck with precision. Michael is a devoted family man who loves camping, and his daughter Becca recently joined the business, making it a true multi-generation family company. Clients describe him as personable, caring and easy to talk to.

image.alt: Michael Kuhn, founder and master craftsman of Treasure Valley Redesign & Remodel

process.h2: Ten steps, grouped into five stages

steps.title: Free consultation
steps.text: An in-person or virtual meeting to talk through your vision, needs, budget, design ideas, scope and must-have features.

steps.title: Rough estimate and design
steps.text: A rough estimate keeps the budget honest while layouts, materials and finishes are planned together with you.

steps.title: Detailed proposal and contract
steps.text: A written proposal shows what is included and what is still to choose, followed by the contract and a schedule.

steps.title: Prep and construction
steps.text: Pre-construction prep, then the build itself, with regular communication so you are never left guessing what comes next.

steps.title: Quality checks to follow-up
steps.text: Quality checks and a punch list catch the final details, then a walkthrough, warranty and follow-up after you move back in.

service_area.text: Treasure Valley Redesign & Remodel works across the greater Treasure Valley from Caldwell. The team remodels homes in Caldwell, Nampa, Middleton, Star, Eagle, Meridian, Kuna and Boise, with the most work in Eagle, Meridian, Boise and Star. Consultations can happen in person at your home or by video, so tell the team where you live when you reach out.

faq.h2: Treasure Valley remodeling FAQ

items.q: Is the estimate really free?
items.a: Yes. The company says consultations and estimates are always free. The first meeting can be in person or virtual, and covers your vision, needs, budget, design ideas and must-have features. Fill in the short intake form or call, and the team will reach out to schedule it.

items.q: Why might your bid differ from another contractor's?
items.a: Michael has written about this. Two bids can both say kitchen remodel but price different scope, allowances, materials and project management. TVRR's proposals list what is included, what is not, which allowances are assumed and what is still to be selected, so you can compare fairly.

items.q: Can you work with my own designer?
items.a: Yes. One Google reviewer had her kitchen built in close partnership with her designer, Ngenius Design, and wrote that the team worked seamlessly with them and moved quickly on any concern. If you do not have a designer, the team offers design assistance as part of the project.

items.q: Do you build decks and outdoor spaces?
items.a: Yes. Michael is a Trex Pro, and decks are a company specialty. The service list also includes patios, awnings, outdoor kitchens, garage additions and storage sheds, so outdoor living can be planned along with an indoor remodel or as a project of its own.

items.q: Do you help after fire or water damage?
items.a: Yes. The company lists disaster restoration for flood, fire and storm damage, with a certified restoration team that handles everything from the damage assessment to a full rebuild. Call (208) 318-5588 and explain what happened so the team can respond quickly.

final_cta.h2: Book your free kitchen estimate
final_cta.text: Tell Michael and Becca what is not working in your kitchen, and they will come to you.

hero.eyebrow: Showroom and cabinet shop in Anaheim
hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Anaheim, With Cabinets Built in Our Own Shop
hero.subheadline: APlus is a two-generation family business that designs your kitchen, builds every cabinet in its Anaheim factory and installs it with its own team. Owner Alex Tabrizi is both a general contractor and a certified designer.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Anaheim design-build project: white custom cabinets, blue-veined marble waterfall island, metal range hood and glass-front uppers in a Newport Coast kitchen

intro.h2: From a family garage to an Anaheim cabinet factory
paragraphs: APlus handles kitchen remodeling in Anaheim and across Orange County as a design-build firm, with design, construction and cabinet making under one roof. Every cabinet is built in the company's own facility on East La Palma Avenue, so sizes, finishes and inside storage are made for your room, not picked from a catalog.

The business started when Abraham Tabrizi built cabinets in his garage while his young son Alex handed him tools. It grew into an Irvine workshop and then the Anaheim factory, and Alex now runs it. Google reviewers single out cabinet quality, and one client says cabinets bought 13 years ago still please them today.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths and built-ins made to measure

items.name: Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: Full design-build kitchens, from space planning and material selection to demo, plumbing, electrical and install. The designer studies how you cook and gather, then plans the layout, colors and cabinetry around it. A detailed 3D rendering is approved before anything goes into production.

image.alt: Santa Ana kitchen remodel with navy custom island, white quartz top, white shaker perimeter cabinets and brass chandelier

items.name: Custom Cabinetry
items.blurb: Kitchen, bath, closet and entertainment center cabinets are engineered and built in the Anaheim factory. Keeping production in-house lets the team control quality from start to finish and offer custom pieces for less than outside shops charge, according to the company.

image.alt: Custom corner cabinet with two-tier wood lazy Susan shelves holding small appliances, built in the APlus Anaheim cabinet shop

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Bathrooms planned for the space you have, with custom vanities and storage made in the same shop as the kitchens. The design expert works through layout and materials with you and provides 3D renderings, then the construction team builds it to plan.

image.alt: Dana Point bathroom remodel with walnut vanity, white quartz counter, black fixtures and frameless glass shower

items.name: Complete Home Remodels
items.blurb: Whole-house projects that tie kitchens, bathrooms, entertainment centers, living spaces, closets and additions into one design and one schedule. A San Clemente client had APlus rebuild the kitchen, baths, entertainment center and built-ins in a single project.

image.alt: Family room remodel with custom oak built-in shelving, window seat and plaster fireplace surround in an Orange County home

why_choose_us.h2: What sets an APlus kitchen apart

items.title: You can tour the factory
items.text: Your second meeting is at the Anaheim showroom, where you sit down with the designer and lead contractor and walk through the shop where your cabinets will be built.

items.title: Designer and builder in one person
items.text: Alex Tabrizi is a general contractor and a certified designer, so the plan you approve is drawn by someone who knows how it will be framed, plumbed and installed.

items.title: Cabinets that last
items.text: Cabinet quality is the most-tagged topic in APlus's Google reviews. A Laguna Hills client says the custom cabinets are built with old-world craftsmanship and have held up amazingly.

items.title: Most work comes by referral
items.text: More than half of APlus projects come from referrals, and the company reports that over 98 percent of clients interviewed said they would recommend it to friends and family.

about.h2: Meet Alex Tabrizi, second-generation owner
about.text: Alex Tabrizi grew up in the business. His father, Abraham, started APlus in an Orange County garage building cabinets, moved it to a small Irvine workshop and later to the Anaheim factory. Alex joined the family company more than 25 years ago and now leads it as a general contractor and certified designer. That dual role lets him plan a kitchen that looks right and builds right. His team includes designers, project managers, plumbers, electricians, cabinet engineers and other trades as needed, all working from the La Palma Avenue facility.

process.h2: How a remodel moves from your kitchen to our shop and back

steps.title: In-home meet and greet

steps.title: Showroom and factory visit

service_area.h2: Orange County towns we remodel in
service_area.text: The showroom and factory sit on East La Palma Avenue in Anaheim, a short drive from most of Orange County. North county clients come from Fullerton, Orange, Yorba Linda and Tustin. Many recent kitchens are in south county, including Newport Coast, Laguna Beach, Ladera Ranch, Coto de Caza, San Juan Capistrano, Dana Point and San Clemente. Call to confirm a town not shown.

faq.h2: Questions about remodeling with APlus

items.q: Do you really build your own cabinets?
items.a: Yes. All APlus cabinetry is custom built in the company's facility in Anaheim, California. That covers kitchens, bathroom vanities, closets and entertainment centers. You can see the shop during your showroom meeting, and a long-time client notes the cabinets are custom made in their own shop rather than modular units.

items.q: How does the consultation work?
items.a: It is a two-step process. First, someone visits your home to measure and photograph the space. Next, you meet the designer and lead contractor at the Anaheim showroom and factory to talk about goals, space planning and design ideas. The in-home consultation is complimentary.

items.q: Do I need to hire my own designer?
items.a: No. Owner Alex Tabrizi is a certified designer as well as a general contractor, and the team includes designers who handle space planning and material selection. You approve a detailed 3D rendering before your cabinets go into production, so the design and the build come from the same company.

items.q: Who manages the job once work starts?
items.a: A project manager is assigned when your cabinets go into production and leads the job from demolition to completion. Plumbing, electrical, engineering and installation are handled by the APlus team and its specialty trades, so you are not coordinating separate contractors yourself.

items.q: Do you work in my part of Orange County?
items.a: APlus lists more than 30 Orange County communities, from Anaheim, Brea and Fullerton in the north to Mission Viejo, Rancho Santa Margarita and San Clemente in the south. Recent portfolio projects include Santa Ana, Newport Coast, Coto de Caza, San Juan Capistrano and Dana Point.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Waukesha with Prices You See Up Front
hero.subheadline: GMH Construction publishes its kitchen and bath price ranges, designs your project before you sign, and builds most jobs on a fixed-price contract, with owners Greg and Dane on site.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Waukesha County project in Sussex, WI by GMH Construction: walnut island with white quartz top, copper range hood, brass pendants and white cabinets

intro.h2: Kitchen Remodeling in Waukesha, Planned Before It Is Priced
paragraphs: Most homeowners looking at kitchen remodeling in Waukesha want a straight answer on cost. GMH Construction puts its numbers on the site: a standard kitchen remodel runs about $75,000 to $100,000 and up, and a premium remodel about $105,000 to $160,000 and up. Your own price follows a design phase, not a guess.

That design phase is the core of how GMH works. A Design Retainer covers the time with their designers, so the scope, selections and budget are settled before construction. Most projects then move to a fixed-price contract: unless you change the scope or selections, the quoted price does not go up.

services.h2: Remodeling Services Across Waukesha County

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom cabinets, countertops, islands, layered lighting, flooring and storage. Standard remodels may include minor wall changes and moved fixtures over 12 to 16+ weeks. Premium remodels use higher-end materials and can move walls or windows, over 14 to 18+ weeks.

image.alt: Hartland, WI kitchen remodel with dark granite island top, wood cabinets, glass pendant lights and an open sightline to the dining area

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Main baths, primary suites and three-quarter baths with custom cabinetry, showers and tubs, lighting and flooring. Pricing assumes a full gut and remodel, and an interior designer works with you through the whole project. Most baths take 8 to 12 weeks.

image.alt: Three-quarter bathroom remodel with glass walk-in shower, gray subway tile accent, white vanity and granite top

items.name: Basements and Lower Levels
items.blurb: Full lower-level build-outs with three-quarter bathrooms, wet and dry bars, family rooms and home theaters. Projects include utilities, framing, insulation and flooring. A Hartland lower level features a bar with seating beside a brick fireplace.

image.alt: Hartland, WI basement remodel with wet bar, quartz peninsula, glass-front cabinets and brick fireplace

items.name: Additions and Sunrooms
items.blurb: Room additions, three-season and four-season sunrooms, and whole-house remodels that open up older floor plans. One Delafield family wrote that GMH removed walls and staircases that other bidders called impossible, and rebuilt their entire first floor.

image.alt: Brookfield, WI home addition with vaulted ceiling, dark timber trusses, wide windows and wood floor dining area

items.name: Signature Series
items.blurb: A budget-friendly, semi-custom option for kitchens, baths and basements with little to no structural change. You choose from a curated set of popular materials. Published ranges: kitchens $65,000 to $80,000, main baths $35,000 to $48,000, owner baths $50,000 to $65,000.

image.alt: Waukesha, WI bathroom remodel with wood double vanity, white quartz top, black mirrors and black hexagon floor tile

why_choose_us.h2: What Sets GMH Apart

items.title: Owners on your job
items.text: Greg or Dane meets you, plans the project and writes your bid, then stays present at your home through construction. Both are reachable by cell phone.

items.title: Fixed pricing
items.text: Most projects run on a fixed-price contract. Labor and materials are included, and the price holds unless you change the scope or selections.

items.title: A Design Center to see it first
items.text: Explore cabinetry, countertops, fixtures and finishes in person with GMH designers, who also work with the production team so the design can actually be built.

items.title: Clean, connected job sites
items.text: Crews clean up daily, and a client wrote that GMH runs a large HEPA air filter to keep dust out of the house. JobTread keeps schedule, finances and documents in one app.

about.h2: Owner-Run for Over 30 Years
about.text: GMH Construction, Inc. has been remodeling homes in Southeast Wisconsin for over 30 years and is a licensed general contractor in the state. It is owner-run: Greg Perkins and his co-owner Dane meet homeowners, plan projects, write bids and stay on site through construction. Designers Robin and Audrey lead the design phase, and Julie keeps schedules moving behind the scenes. The firm is an active NARI member and holds an A+ rating with the BBB. Many clients come back; one testimonial describes a kitchen, foyer and family room job as a second remodel with GMH.

image.alt: GMH Construction carpenters installing kitchen cabinets in a Waukesha County home

process.h2: How a GMH Project Is Planned and Priced

steps.title: Consultation at your home
steps.text: An owner meets you at home to walk the space, set the scope and explain how pre-construction works.

steps.title: Design Retainer
steps.text: About 2 to 3 weeks later, GMH presents a Design Retainer with the scope, a budget range and estimated designer time.

steps.title: Design and selections
steps.text: Designers guide your choices at the Design Center and finish with a set budget and a detailed scope of work.

steps.title: Construction contract
steps.text: Sign the contract, usually fixed-price, and set your start date. Crews generally work from 7:00 to 4:00.

service_area.h2: Lake Country and Waukesha County Service Area
service_area.text: GMH works from its office on Westmound Drive and remodels homes throughout Waukesha County and Southeast Wisconsin. Its most common service areas are Waukesha, Pewaukee, Brookfield, Elm Grove, Hartland, New Berlin, Delafield, Menomonee Falls, Merton, Sussex, Lake Country and Oconomowoc. Testimonials also come from homeowners in Bayside and Whitefish Bay, so call if your town is a little farther out.

faq.h2: Waukesha Remodeling Costs and Timelines

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Waukesha County?
items.a: GMH lists a standard kitchen remodel at about $75,000 to $100,000 and up, taking 12 to 16+ weeks, and a premium remodel at $105,000 to $160,000 and up, taking 14 to 18+ weeks. The semi-custom Signature Series kitchen runs about $65,000 to $80,000. Final pricing depends on room size and features.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost?
items.a: With standard finishes, a typical 45-square-foot main bath starts around $45,000 and a primary bath around $70,000. Premium finishes start around $60,000 and $90,000. Prices assume a full gut and include labor, materials, flooring, countertops and fixtures. Most baths take 8 to 12 weeks.

items.q: What is the Design Retainer?
items.a: After the first meeting at your home, GMH follows up in about 2 to 3 weeks with a Design Retainer. It outlines the scope of work, a project budget range and the estimated time with their designers. That design work produces an accurate budget and a detailed construction contract, usually at a fixed price.

items.q: Who will supervise my job?
items.a: One of the owners, Greg or Dane, meets you to plan the project and write the bid. Designers Robin or Audrey and their team handle design, specifications and pricing. Once work starts, Greg and Dane are present at your home throughout, and both are always reachable by cell phone.

items.q: What hours do crews work, and how will I stay informed?
items.a: Crews generally start at 7:00 and finish at 4:00, though GMH works with each family on start times. Communication runs through JobTread, which reaches several team members at once and shows your schedule, finances and documents. For emergencies, the team can always be reached by phone.

final_cta.h2: Get Real Numbers for Your Kitchen
final_cta.text: Book a free consultation at your home and see what your project would take.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Ithaca, NY, Priced Before We Build
hero.subheadline: Upscale Remodeling designs and builds kitchens, baths, basements and additions under one roof. You get running estimates during design and a fixed price before construction, backed by a 5-year warranty.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Ithaca NY: home addition kitchen with warm wood cabinets, stainless double wall ovens and a sliding door to the yard

intro.h2: Know the number before the walls come down
paragraphs: Upscale Remodeling has handled kitchen remodeling in Ithaca, NY since 1991 as a full-service design-build firm. The same team draws your kitchen and builds it, so the design is priced against real construction costs as it develops, not after.

The firm is open about money. Its pricing page says most Ithaca-area kitchens it completes start at $70,000 and most bathrooms at $40,000. During design you get running estimates, and before construction starts you get a fixed price. Older Ithaca homes bring plaster walls, aging plumbing and knob-and-tube wiring, so those are checked early, before design decisions are locked in.

services.h2: What the Upscale team designs and builds

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Custom cabinets, quartz and natural stone counters, fixtures, lighting and storage, chosen in the private Design Studio in Freeville. Projects range from updating a dated layout to opening walls into the dining room. Most kitchens are finished in 8 to 14 weeks from the start of construction.

image.alt: Remodeled kitchen with brown leather stools around a marble-topped island with reclaimed wood paneling and white cabinets

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths and half baths, from a leaking tub replaced with new tile, tub, counter and trim to a full redesign with custom vanities. Christie, a Certified Kitchen & Bath Designer, leads design, and most Ithaca-area bathrooms the firm completes start at $40,000.

image.alt: Remodeled bathroom in an Ithaca, NY home with a warm wood vanity, lighted mirror cabinet and built-in linen storage

items.name: Basement Renovation and Finishing
items.blurb: Unfinished basements turned into usable rooms, from entertainment spaces to wet bars, designed and built by the same team as the rest of your house. The firm publishes an honest breakdown of basement remodel costs on its blog, so you can plan the budget before the first meeting.

image.alt: Finished basement in the Finger Lakes region with a dark-cabinet wet bar, bottle shelves and a pub-height table

items.name: Additions and Renovations
items.blurb: Sunrooms, three-season rooms, mudrooms and kitchen additions that fit the house you already have. One South Ithaca project paired an addition with a renovation, and a Cayuga Heights home gained a three-season room. All permits, inspections and subcontractor coordination are handled directly.

image.alt: Three-season room addition on a stone house in the Cayuga Heights neighborhood of Ithaca, NY

why_choose_us.h2: Why Tompkins County homeowners trust Upscale

items.title: A fixed price before construction
items.text: Free pricing guides show typical starting costs, running estimates follow you through design, and the price is fixed before any building starts. Reviewers call it a quality job at a fair price.

items.title: Five years of coverage
items.text: Every project carries a 5-year warranty, and the process ends with post-completion support and anniversary inspections, so someone comes back to check the work after you move back in.

items.title: A+ BBB, zero complaints
items.text: Upscale is accredited by the Better Business Bureau with an A+ rating and reports zero complaints in more than 30 years of service. It was also named to Remodeling magazine's Top 550 list.

items.title: Certified people on your job
items.text: Designer Christie holds the CKBD and CLIPP credentials and is president of the NKBA Central New York chapter. The firm is a Certified Graduate Remodeler, an Aging-in-Place Specialist and EPA Lead-Safe certified.

about.h2: Steve Nash and a family of Ithaca builders
about.text: Founder Steve Nash's ancestors settled the Ellis Hollow and Snyder Hill area in the early 1800s and built some of the region's first homes, and several still stand. Steve started learning the trade at age nine, working beside his father and grandfather. The lesson he kept was simple: never compromise and never cut corners. He founded Upscale Remodeling, and the company has served Ithaca since 1991. Today he leads a team that includes designer Christie, project manager Rich, lead carpenters Caesar and Ken, and estimator Scott, with ongoing training for every role.

image.alt: Steve Nash, founder of Upscale Remodeling in Freeville and Ithaca, NY

process.h2: The four-step design-build process

steps.title: Discovery and getting acquainted
steps.text: An initial call, then a free meeting and site visit at your home. If it is a fit, you sign a Project Development Agreement to start design.

steps.title: Design and development
steps.text: Conceptual design, design development and selections in the Freeville Design Studio, with running estimates, ending in a final design and formal fixed-price proposal.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Permits, material ordering, scheduling and a pre-construction meeting come first. During the build you get constant communication from your project manager.

steps.title: Completion and enjoyment
steps.text: A final walk-through with you, then the 5-year warranty period with post-completion support and anniversary inspections in the years after.

faq.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Ithaca, NY: straight answers

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Ithaca?
items.a: Upscale says most kitchen remodels it completes in the Ithaca area start at $70,000, and most bathrooms start at $40,000. Free pricing guides on its site break down each level. Because every kitchen is custom, you get running estimates during design and a fixed price before construction begins.

items.q: How long will my kitchen be out of service?
items.a: Most kitchen remodels in the greater Ithaca area are finished within eight to fourteen weeks from the start of construction, depending on scope. When a project also takes in a pantry, laundry area or breakfast nook, those parts are scheduled in parallel to shorten the time without a kitchen.

items.q: My house is old. Will that cause surprises?
items.a: Plaster walls, aging plumbing, knob-and-tube wiring and beams in unexpected places are common in Ithaca and Finger Lakes homes. Upscale assesses those conditions early, before design decisions are locked in, so the scope and price reflect what is actually behind the walls.

items.q: What does the warranty cover after the job?
items.a: Upscale backs its work with a 5-year warranty, which it calls industry-leading. The final phase of its process includes a warranty period with post-completion support and anniversary inspections. One reviewer noted the crew came back to adjust cabinets and fix small problems without hesitation.

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Upscale will schedule an initial consultation at no cost, walk through your space, talk about what is realistic for your budget and explain the process from start to finish. Product selections later happen in the private Design Studio in Freeville, which is open by appointment.

intro.h2: Two former teachers running a boutique design-build firm

faq.h2: Marysville remodeling questions, answered

items.q: What is design-build, and why does it matter for my kitchen?
items.a: Design-build puts designers, architects and the general contractor on one team. Instead of hiring a designer, then collecting bids and acting as the go-between, you work with a single point of contact. The budget and buildability are considered from the first sketch, which helps avoid the overruns and delays of design-bid-build.

items.q: Will I know the full price before work starts?
items.a: Yes. During the Development phase VanderBeken prepares concept drawings, 3D renderings, a detailed scope of work and a fixed investment price, using an advanced estimating system. You see the complete picture before production begins, which is meant to give you control and predictability over the cost of the remodel.

items.q: What warranty do you offer?
items.a: Every remodel comes with a two-year warranty. After the final walkthrough, where any concerns are addressed, the team follows up at 90 days and again at 12 months to make sure everything is still performing and meeting the firm's standards. You also keep your dedicated project manager as a contact.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom accessible without it looking institutional?
items.a: Yes. Ron and Jennifer are Certified Aging in Place Specialists, and the firm won the 2025 REX Award for Universal Design Excellence. One Lake Stevens client had a 1981 main bath turned into an ADA bath that, in her words, does not look or feel like it.

items.q: Can I bring my own architect or designer?
items.a: Sometimes. Clients occasionally ask to bring their own architect or interior designer, and VanderBeken evaluates each request individually. The team wants to be sure it can coordinate well with them and still deliver the service and results it promises, so raise it during your first call or office visit.

final_cta.h2: Start with an initial design consultation
final_cta.text: Call (425) 870-8123 to talk with Ron and Jennifer's team about your kitchen, bath or whole-home project and set up an office visit.
