seo.og_description: Plan every detail first, then build at a fixed price. Kitchens, baths and additions within a half hour of Montpelier, with cabinetry made in our own millwork shop.

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Montpelier, VT, Planned Down to the Towel Bar
hero.subheadline: Clar Construction plans every detail of your kitchen or bath up front, then builds it at a fixed price. Cabinets come from its own millwork shop in Montpelier's old clothespin factory.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Montpelier VT area project in Stowe: walnut-stained island with gas range, ceiling-mounted stainless hood, white cabinets and open wood shelves

intro.h2: Why planning comes first at Clar
paragraphs: Clar Construction has offered kitchen remodeling in Montpelier, VT and the towns within a half hour since 2004. Dan Clar started the company as its only employee. Today it is a full team of carpenters working out of a shop on Granite Street. They build kitchens, baths, additions, decks and custom cabinetry.

The firm's motto on surprises is simple: 'You like surprises? We don't.' Before construction starts, you and the team settle everything from the floor plan down to the grout color and towel bars, so the price can be fixed. Google reviewers note that while others may charge less, the quality justifies the price.

services.h2: Built by Clar's carpenters and shop

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Kitchens planned around how you cook and gather, in modern, farmhouse, traditional or mixed styles. Everything is mapped out before a single tool is lifted. Cabinetry, counters and lighting plans come together with custom pieces from the shop when the design calls for them.

image.alt: Vermont farmhouse kitchen remodel with exposed timber beams and posts, wood stove, sage cabinets and painted island

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, three-quarter baths, half baths and brand-new bathrooms. Walk-in showers, glass doors, tiled floors, heated floors, an added window and more storage are all common requests. One Google reviewer had Clar renovate a 50-year-old bathroom after an earlier window job.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with soaking tub and beadboard apron, frameless glass shower, grab bars and slate-look tile floor

items.name: Custom Cabinetry and Built-Ins
items.blurb: In its 2,000 sq. ft. shop, Clar builds kitchen and bath cabinets, vanities with matching mirrors, bookcases, mudroom lockers, benches and closets. Built-ins are made to look like they were always there. One client's bookcase and under-stair drawers did just that.

image.alt: Custom built-in wood bookcases with a rolling library ladder, reading chair and window seat, made in Clar's Montpelier shop

items.name: Additions and Sunrooms
items.blurb: Add a room instead of moving. Clar designs and builds additions, mudrooms and sunrooms lined with airtight, energy-efficient windows that bring in light all year. The same team handles decks and porches made for a Vermont summer.

image.alt: Sunroom addition with a wall of windows, wood ceiling, stained concrete floor and dining table

items.name: Whole-Home, Historic and Aging-in-Place Work
items.blurb: Clar began in 2004 with a focus on preserving Vermont's historic buildings, and still takes on full remodels of older homes. Many clients also plan changes that help them stay in their homes through retirement, from safer baths to better layouts.

image.alt: Whole-home remodel of an older house with arched doorway, shiplap walls, raised reading nook and wood floors

why_choose_us.h2: Is Clar the right fit for you?

items.title: A fixed price you can trust
items.text: Every detail is chosen during the Project Development phase, so the contract is a fixed price. If you change goals along the way, the cost of that change is discussed openly first.

items.title: A lead carpenter you already know
items.text: One of Clar's lead carpenters, someone you meet during planning, runs your job. He or she coordinates the licensed electricians, plumbers and roofers and sends periodic updates.

items.title: Honest about fit
items.text: Clar says it is not for homeowners chasing the cheapest bid or needing work to start tomorrow. It suits people who care more about doing it right than doing it fast.

items.title: Pricing alternatives offered
items.text: One longtime client wrote that you always know where you stand expense-wise and are given pricing alternatives. Projects typically range from $25,000 to more than $1 million.

about.h2: Dan Clar, from steeples to kitchens
about.text: Dan Clar grew up in Rochester, NY and earned a degree in Education. In college he worked for a contractor that restored church steeples. He spent half his time in the millwork shop making parts and the other half hanging 125 feet up in a bosun's chair to install them. That job hooked him on carpentry. In 2004 he started Clar Construction in Montpelier as its only employee. The company now works from the historic National Clothespin Company building on Granite Street, turned into a millwork shop. Dan lives in Montpelier with his family and is trying to figure out how to build a wooden canoe.

image.alt: Dan Clar, owner of Clar Construction in Montpelier, VT

process.h2: Four steps from first talk to warranty

steps.title: Get to know each other
steps.text: Call, email or walk into the office. Clar learns your ideas, explains its design-build process and suggests a price range based on similar past projects.

steps.title: Project Development Agreement
steps.text: Through a series of meetings with in-house staff or partner designers, you settle every detail, from the floor plan to the towel bars.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Your lead carpenter runs the schedule with insured trade partners and keeps you posted on which trades are coming in the weeks ahead.

steps.title: Completion and warranty
steps.text: Near the end, you meet to list any open items, so they get finished while the crew and tools are still at your house.

service_area.h2: Within a half hour of Montpelier
service_area.text: Clar works mostly within a half-hour radius of Montpelier, where its shop and office sit downtown on Granite Street. Recent clients include a Stowe kitchen and repeat customers who came back after window and siding work. The towns it names include Barre, Berlin, Northfield, Middlesex, Worcester, Calais, Marshfield, Plainfield, Duxbury, Waterbury and Stowe. Have a larger project farther out? Ask, because the team sometimes takes on work beyond this area.

faq.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Montpelier, VT: common questions

items.q: What does a kitchen or bath remodel with Clar cost?
items.a: Clar's clients typically invest between $25,000 and $1 million or more, depending on size and scope. At the first meeting, the team compares your budget with similar projects it has finished and suggests a price range. For complex projects, it sets a second meeting within a week to review that range.

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Clar offers a free consultation with no sales pressure. You can call, email or walk into the Granite Street office. The team will ask about your current thinking, may suggest ideas you had not considered, and will explain how its design-build process works so you can decide if it suits you.

items.q: What is the Project Development Agreement?
items.a: It is the planning agreement you sign after the first meeting, once you agree on a target budget. In a series of meetings with Clar's in-house staff or partner designers and architects, you settle every detail of the project. That level of detail is what lets Clar offer a fixed price in the construction agreement.

items.q: Who will be working in my home?
items.a: Clar's own carpenters, led by one of its lead carpenters, whom you will already have met during planning. Licensed trades such as electricians, plumbers and roofers come from trade partners, and everyone on your project is properly insured. Planning also covers dust control, snow clearing and any needs of children or pets.

items.q: Can you build cabinets for my kitchen or bath?
items.a: Yes. In its 2,000 sq. ft. shop in the old National Clothespin Company building, Clar builds kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities with matching mirrors, bookshelves, mudroom lockers, benches, closets, custom doors and built-in seating. The shop also does custom trim details when a project needs them, for homeowners and for other contractors.

final_cta.h2: Start with a conversation on Granite Street
final_cta.text: Call the office or book a free consultation to talk through your kitchen, bath or addition with Dan's team.

paragraphs: Pereira Construction of South FL handles bathroom remodeling in Lake Worth and across Palm Beach and Broward counties. services.h2: What the Pereira crew builds

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling and Shower Conversions

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling

hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Minneapolis With Three Design Options
hero.subheadline: Sicora Design / Build draws every remodel at three price points, then builds it with its own project managers and Rift Sawn cabinet shop. The firm has served the west metro since 2000, now under owner Ron Sonnek.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Minneapolis area project in St. Louis Park with a Cambria island, soapstone perimeter counters, white cabinetry and GE Cafe appliances with champagne bronze handles

intro.h2: One firm for design, cabinets and construction
paragraphs: Sicora Design / Build has offered kitchen remodeling in Minneapolis and the west suburbs since Thomas Sicora founded the firm in 2000. Today owner Ron Sonnek leads a team of interior designers, project managers and cabinetmakers working from 5601 W Lake St. You get one point of contact from the first consultation to the warranty walkthrough.

What sets the process apart is choice. For each project the designers draw three plans, lite, medium and heavy, at different price ranges, with floor plans, renderings and a 3D virtual walk-through. You pick the level that fits, exact costs are set with the trade contractors, and the firm says projects land within 3% of budget on average.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Minneapolis, plus suites, basements and more

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Timeless layouts, smart storage and quality materials, from a 'Refreshed' kitchen with new quartz tops to a full 'Design & Build' plan with a new island. Recent St. Louis Park kitchens pair Cambria and soapstone, and one adds a red oak stained island and a hidden pantry.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel in St. Louis Park, Minnesota with a red oak stained island, white cabinetry, globe pendants and a hidden pantry in modern farmhouse style

items.name: Owner's Suites and Bathrooms
items.blurb: Bedroom, bath and closet planned as one suite, with custom vanities, tile, lighting and storage, and in-floor heat at the top design level. A recent St. Louis Park owners' suite has his and her vanities with white quartz tops and maple cabinetry.

image.alt: Owners' suite bathroom remodel in St. Louis Park, Minnesota with a freestanding tub, glass shower and maple vanity with white quartz top

items.name: Basements
items.blurb: Unfinished lower levels turned into rooms the family actually uses. One case study took a walkout basement and made it the family's everyday hangout area, and other Sicora basements add wet bars, built-in media walls, game tables and wine storage.

image.alt: Finished basement with a quartz-topped game table, coffered wood ceiling, built-in TV wall and wine bar

items.name: Custom Cabinetry and Closets
items.blurb: Rift Sawn, Sicora's own cabinet and woodworking shop, builds kitchen cabinets, entertainment centers, bars, counters, shelving and built-ins, and no project is too big or too small. It also designs and installs custom closet systems at a more attainable price than typical luxury brands.

image.alt: Custom kitchen drawer with wood pan dividers holding skillets and baking sheets, in a St. Louis Park, Minnesota remodel

items.name: Porches, Living Spaces and Whole House
items.blurb: Porches, living rooms and whole-house remodels, including an all-season sun room addition and an Edina fireplace wall with a linear gas fireplace, custom ledge stone and tape lighting. Before-and-after photo pairs on the whole-house page show what a full makeover can change.

image.alt: Fireplace feature wall remodel in Edina, Minnesota with a linear gas fireplace, custom ledge stone blend and tape lighting

why_choose_us.h2: Why west metro homeowners keep coming back to Sicora

items.title: Three plans, three prices
items.text: You see lite, medium and heavy designs side by side, each with its own price range, so you can match your wish list to your budget early.

items.title: Budgets that hold
items.text: Exact costs are set after a site walk-through with the trade contractors, and the firm reports less than a 3% budget variance on average.

items.title: Warranty plus an 11-month visit
items.text: Every project carries a 2-year mechanical and 10-year structural warranty. A walkthrough is scheduled 11 months after completion to handle any repairs.

items.title: Clients who return
items.text: One Google reviewer's family has hired Sicora five times, for two major kitchen upgrades and three bedroom expansions. The firm is also an EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm.

about.h2: Ron Sonnek and the Sicora team
about.text: Thomas Sicora founded the firm in 2000, and it still focuses on timeless, custom design delivered through an engaging, transparent process, which the company calls the Sicora difference. Ron Sonnek now owns the business. His team includes production manager Jim Gill, interior designers Darcy Dickman and Heidi Kinder, project manager Dave Stricker, Tim Nurkka on service and warranty, and four cabinet shop craftsmen. Reviewers name Ron, Darcy and Jim for keeping design wishes and budgets in check and staying on top of progress.

process.h2: From consultation to the 11-month warranty walkthrough

steps.title: Consultation and assessment
steps.text: Book a phone, virtual or in-home meeting at least three days ahead. The team checks whether your project is feasible.

steps.title: Design (2 to 4 months)
steps.text: Designers develop lite, medium and heavy plans with floor plans, renderings and a 3D virtual walk-through of the space.

steps.title: Contract development
steps.text: Trade contractors walk the site, exact costs are set, you choose your options, and the contract is written from them.

steps.title: Construction (2 to 5 months)
steps.text: A pre-construction meeting with your designer and project manager starts the build, and an app shows progress, updates and changes.

steps.title: Warranty
steps.text: A punch list and walkthrough close the job, followed by the 2-year mechanical and 10-year structural warranty and an 11-month check-in.

service_area.h2: Serving St. Louis Park, Edina and the Lake Minnetonka area
service_area.text: Sicora works from 5601 W Lake St, where Minneapolis meets St. Louis Park. The firm names fourteen communities, from Minneapolis, Edina and Golden Valley out to Wayzata, Excelsior, Deephaven and the rest of the Lake Minnetonka area. Recent project photos come from St. Louis Park, Edina, Minneapolis and Minnetonka. If your town is not on the list, call the front desk to ask.

faq.h2: Minneapolis remodeling questions for Sicora

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost?
items.a: Sicora's ballpark guide for a 12 by 12 foot kitchen runs from about $38,000 for a 'Refreshed' kitchen with existing cabinets and new quartz tops, to $55,000 'Refaced,' $89,000 'Transformed' with new custom cabinets, and $102,000 and up for a full 'Design & Build' with a new layout and island.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost?
items.a: For a 6 by 10 foot bathroom, the guide lists about $29,000 for 'Clean,' $32,000 for 'Refresh' with tile flooring and $45,000 for 'Renew' with a custom vanity, granite top and tile surround. A full 'Design & Build' bath with in-floor heat is priced per project.

items.q: How long does a remodel take?
items.a: Design usually takes two to four months, because you review three plans, renderings and a 3D walk-through. Construction runs two to five months depending on the project. Contract development falls between the two, after trade contractors walk the site and exact costs are set.

items.q: What warranty do you offer?
items.a: Sicora provides a 2-year mechanical and 10-year structural warranty. About 11 months after your project is done, the team schedules a walkthrough for any repairs. If something comes up beyond those warranties, the firm asks you to tell them, since the goal is clients for life.

items.q: Is the first consultation free?
items.a: Yes. Sicora offers a free in-home consultation, and you can choose a phone or virtual meeting instead. Please book at least three days ahead. For an earlier slot, call the front desk at (952) 929-0098 and the team will do its best to fit you in.

final_cta.text: Call (952) 929-0098 or book a free in-home consultation online at least three days ahead.

intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Buford, with the prices out in the open
paragraphs: Buford Renovations offers kitchen remodeling in Buford for homeowners who want one person to answer for the whole job. That person is Oscar Tamez, owner and lead contractor, with 20+ years in residential construction and hundreds of kitchen and bathroom remodels managed across Gwinnett, Hall and Forsyth counties.

Custom cabinetry is the craft the company was founded on, so cabinets get planned first: built to the ceiling, fitted around awkward corners and finished with soft-close hardware and pull-outs. Oscar also publishes 2026 cost guides for Buford and nearby towns, so you can see real local price ranges before the free in-home visit.

items.name: Kitchen remodeling
items.blurb: Layout changes, custom or semi-custom cabinets, quartz, granite or butcher block counters, full-height backsplashes, islands with seating and layered lighting. Open-concept projects include the structural engineering, permits and beam work. Most full kitchens take 4 to 8 weeks once materials are on hand.

about.h2: Meet Oscar Tamez, owner and lead contractor
about.text: Oscar Tamez owns Buford Renovations LLC and runs its jobs as lead contractor. He brings 20+ years of hands-on residential construction experience and has personally managed hundreds of kitchen and bathroom remodels across Gwinnett, Hall and Forsyth counties. The company is not a franchise and does not hand everything off to subcontractors, and Oscar stays personally involved in every project. Google lists the business as Latino-owned. Oscar writes the company's cost guides himself, explaining in plain numbers what drives a budget, from cabinets at 30 to 40 percent of a kitchen to the tile and shower package in a bath.

image.alt: Bright primary bathroom with a freestanding tub, a glass walk-in shower and a long white double vanity by Buford Renovations

process.h2: How a Buford Renovations remodel runs

steps.title: Free in-home consultation
steps.text: The team visits your home to measure the space, hear what you want and talk honestly about scope and budget.

steps.title: Fixed written estimate
steps.text: You receive a detailed, fixed written estimate, usually within 48 hours of the visit, with no obligation to go ahead.

steps.title: Design and selections
steps.text: Layout, cabinetry, counters, tile, vanity, glass, fixtures and lighting are chosen with you before anything is ordered.

steps.title: Permits and build
steps.text: The crew pulls permits, works to a written schedule, contains the work zone, protects floors and nearby rooms, and cleans up daily.

steps.title: Walkthrough and punch list
steps.text: The job closes with a final walkthrough and a punch list, so the last details are finished before the crew leaves.

faq.h2: Buford remodeling questions, answered with real numbers

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Buford?
items.a: Oscar's 2026 Buford guide lists four levels: a basic refresh at $10,000 to $20,000, a mid-range remodel at $25,000 to $45,000, a high-end renovation at $50,000 to $80,000 or more, and a gut and rebuild at $75,000 to $120,000 or more. Most full remodels of a standard 10 by 12 foot kitchen land between $30,000 and $50,000.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel or walk-in shower cost?
items.a: The 2026 Buford bathroom guide puts a cosmetic refresh at $3,500 to $8,500, a mid-range full renovation at $15,000 to $28,000 and a high-end primary suite at $30,000 to $55,000 or more. Tub-to-shower conversions with custom tile and frameless glass usually run $8,000 to $15,000 installed. Oscar suggests setting aside 10 to 15 percent for surprises behind the walls.

items.q: How long will my kitchen or bathroom take?
items.a: Most full kitchen remodels take 4 to 8 weeks once materials are on hand. Most full bathrooms take 3 to 5 weeks from demolition to final walkthrough, and shower conversions are often faster. You get a written schedule before work starts. January through March is usually the slower season, which often means you can get on the calendar sooner.

items.q: Do you handle permits in Buford, Sugar Hill and Gwinnett County?
items.a: Yes. As a licensed Georgia general contractor, Buford Renovations pulls and manages permits and inspections through the City of Buford, the City of Sugar Hill, Gwinnett County, Hall County or whichever office covers your address, including structural permits for wall removals. In Gwinnett, plan on 1 to 3 weeks for approval when plumbing is being moved.

items.q: Can we live at home during the remodel?
items.a: Almost all clients do. The crew contains the work zone, protects floors and nearby rooms and leaves the site clean every day. If your home has a second bathroom, daily life goes on around the job. One Google reviewer who had a full bathroom redone said the team was respectful of the rest of the house.

about.h2: Meet Ethan Randle, founder of Ironwood
about.text: Ethan Randle is the founder and CEO of Ironwood Custom Remodels. After his honorable discharge from the United States Marines in 2014, he joined an International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers apprenticeship. About a year in, he wanted work with a more direct effect on people's daily lives. He went to work full-time for a general contractor in Orange County, California, while attending night school for a degree in construction technology, and then started his own company. Today Ironwood focuses on kitchen, bath and whole-house makeovers in the Triangle and Triad. Clients call Ethan organized and thorough, and some have brought him back for a second or third project.

process.h2: How an Ironwood remodel moves from first call to finished room

steps.title: Online form and phone consultation
steps.text: Send the short form, then talk by phone about the work you want, the finished space you picture and estimated pricing.

steps.title: In-person consultation
steps.text: A licensed team member meets you at home to walk the space and get a clear picture of your project and your goals.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: Layout and finishes are designed with Ironwood's design partners, or Ironwood builds from plans you already have, as the Hurdle Mills homeowners did.

steps.title: Project planning
steps.text: Scope, materials and order of work are set before construction begins, backed by a detailed quote so you know what you are paying for.

steps.title: Construction and move-in
steps.text: The crew builds while Ethan keeps you updated. The last of Ironwood's seven stages is simple: enjoy your new space.

service_area.h2: Serving Durham, Chapel Hill, Cary and the Triangle
service_area.text: Ironwood Custom Remodels is based in Durham and works across the Triangle and into the Triad. Its service list covers Durham, Chapel Hill, Carrboro, Hillsborough, Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Morrisville, Creedmoor, Burlington and Greensboro. Recent case studies come from Durham's historic Hope Valley neighborhood, the Cambridge neighborhood in Cary and a classic home in Hurdle Mills. Live close by but not on the list? Call (760) 642-6051 and ask.

faq.h2: Durham kitchen and bath remodeling questions

items.q: How much does a kitchen or bath remodel with Ironwood cost?
items.a: Ironwood has no set price list. Each project is priced on its own materials, labor and other factors, and the estimate is free. Your first phone consultation covers estimated pricing. For scale, Ironwood's 2026 guide puts spa-style primary bath packages in the Triangle at $45,000 to $150,000 or more.

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: It depends on scope. In Ironwood's own case studies, the Legacy Kitchen in Hurdle Mills took 10 to 12 weeks. The Blue Haven kitchen in Hope Valley, which included moving structural walls and new Marvin windows, and the Cambridge kitchen in Cary each took 12 to 16 weeks. Ask Ethan for your own timeline at the consultation.

items.q: Can we keep living at home during the remodel?
items.a: Families have. One Google review describes updating an entire early-90s first floor, removing the dining room and greatly expanding the kitchen while the owners lived in the home with their kids and dogs. Ironwood has also published a guide on phasing a whole-home renovation so you do not have to move out.

items.q: Can Ironwood build a design from my own kitchen designer?
items.a: Yes. The Hurdle Mills homeowners had already finished their design with The Kitchen Specialist and chose Ironwood to build it. On other kitchens, Ironwood partnered with Heather Holcombe Designs in Hope Valley and Chess Kitchen & Interiors in Cary. If you are starting from scratch, design is one of the seven stages of the process.

items.q: Are you licensed, and who handles the permits?
items.a: Ironwood Custom Remodels is a licensed and insured North Carolina contractor. Public permit records list the company as the contractor, for example on a Town of Cary permit issued in August 2026 for a primary bath and kitchen countertop remodel. Ask for the licence number when you book your free estimate.
